remain any fragment of they at this time but the king of Fez on the other side hear that the people of Temesne be come into his dominion make a truce with the tribe of Zenete and bend his great army against the say Temesnites and at length have find they half famish near unto the river of buragrag he so stop their passage on all side that they be constrain to run up the craggy mountain and thicket at last be environ with the king force some of they be drown in the river other be throw down headlong from the rock and the residue be miserable slay by their enemy and for the space of ten month there be such havoc make among the temesnite that a silly remnant of they be leave alive but king joseph prince of the luntune return forthwith to Maroco for the repair of his force to the end he may bid the king of Fez a battle howbeit Temesne be bereave of her people be leave to be inhabit of wild beast neither have that province any new colony or supply of inhabitant till that about one as yet remain do sufficient testify they have also most large and fair garden out of which they gather great abundance of fruit especial of melon and pomecitrons even at this day all which be perfect this great and famous town be build not many year ago by Mansor the king and mahometan patriak of Maroco upon the ocean sea shore by the east part thereof run the river Buragrag beforenamed and there discharge itself into the main sea. the rock whereon this town be found stand near the mouth of the say river have the river on the one side thereof and the sea on the other in build it much resemble Maroco which Mansor will to be a pattern thereof save that it be a great deal less than Maroco some say that the reason why it be build in this place be for that king Mansor possess the kingdom why king Mansor build the town of upon the sea shore of Granada and a great part of Spain beside and consider that Maroco be so far distant that if any war shall happen he can not in due time send new force against the christian determine to build some town upon the sea shore where he and his army may remain all summer time some persuade he to lie with his army at Ceuta a town upon the straits of Giblaltar but Mansor see that by reason of the barrenness of the soil he can not maintain a army royal for three or four month in the town of Ceuta he cause this town of in short space to be erect and to be exceed beautify with temple college palace shop stove hospital and other such building moreover on the south side without the wall he cause a certain high tower like the tower of Maroco to be build save that the wind stair be somewhat large insomuch that three horse abreast may well ascend up from the top whereof they may escry ship a huge way into the sea. so exceed be the height thereof that I think there be no where the like building to be find and to the end that great store of artificer and merchant may hither from all place make resort he appoint that every man accord to his trade and occupation shall be allow a yearly stipend whereupon it come to pass that within few month this town be better store with all kind of artificer and merchant then in any town in all Africa beside and that because they reap a double gain here use Mansor with his troop to remain from the begin of April till the month of September and whereas there be no water about the conduit of fresh water 12. mile town meet to be drink for the sea run ten mile up into the river and the well likewise yield salt-water Mansor cause fresh water to be convey to the town by certain pipe and channel from a fountain twelve mile distant and the conduit he make arch-wise like unto the conduit of Italy in many place and special at Rome so soon as the say water-conduit be derive unto the town he cause it to be divide and send into sundry place as namely some pipe thereof to the temple some to the college other to the king palace and the rest into the common cistern throughout all the city howbeit after king mansor death this town grow into such decay that scarce the ten part thereof now remain the say notable water-conduit be utter fordo in the war between the marin family and the successor of Mansor also king Mansor cause sella to be wall round about and build therein a fair hospital sella and a stately palace into which his soldier may at their pleasure retire themselves here likewise he erect a most beautiful temple wherein he cause a goodly hall or chapel to be set where king Mansor be bury up which be curious carve and have many fair window about it and in this hall when he perceive death to seize upon he he command his subject to bury his corpse which be do they lay one marblestone over his head and another over his foot whereon sundry epitaph be engrave after he likewise all the honourable personage of his family and blood choose to be inter in the same hall. and so do the king of the marin family so long as their commonwealth prosper myself on a time enter the same hall behold there thirty monument of noble and great personage and diligent write out all their epitaph this I do in the year of the Hegeira nine hundred and fifteen in Thagia be visit the sepulchre of one account for a most holy man who be report in the time of Habdulmumen to have wrought many miracle against the fury of lion whereupon sepulchre visit for fear of lion he be repute by many as a great prophet I remember that I read in a certain writer of that nation common call etdedle a whole catalogue of the say holy man miracle which whether he wrought by arte-magicke or by some wonderful secret of nature it be altogether uncertain howbeit his great fame and honourable reputation be the cause why this town be so well fraught with inhabitant the people of Fez have solemnize their easter do yearly pilgrimage far and frequent frequent this town to visit the say sepulchre and that in such huge number that you will esteem they to be a whole army for every principal man carry his tent and other necessary with he and so you shall see sometime a hundred tent and sometime more in that company fifteen day they be in perform of that pilgrimage for Thagia stand from Fez almost a hundred and twenty mile myself be a child go thither on pilgrimage oftentimes with my father as likewise be grow up to man estate I repair thither as often make supplication to be deliver from the danger of lion westward it begin at the river of buragrag and stretch eastward to the river call the territory of Fez. inaven which two river be almost a hundred mile distant asunder northward it up in feat of chivalry they appoint one Rasid a most valiant and skilful captain to instruct he insomuch that while he be but fifteen year of age he grow famous for his valiant act and stratagem and begin wonderful to idris his great valour at fifteen year of age enlarge his dominion wherefore his troop and family increase every day more and more he set his mind upon building of a city and change of his habitation and so he send for cunning builder into all nation who have diligent peruse all place in the region at last make choice of that where the city of Fez now stand for here they find great store of fountain and a fair river which spring forth of a plain not far off run pleasant almost eight mile amidst the little hill till at length it cast itself upon another plain southward of the place they find a wood which they know will be right commodious for the town here therefore upon the east bank of the say river they build a town contain three thousand family neither omit they either town so increase that there be but a small distance between they for the governor of each labour might and main to augment their own jurisdiction a hundred and fourscore year after there fall be worth three duckat a month in this city be more than a hundred bath-stove very artificial and stately build which though they be not of equal bigness yet be they all of one fashion each stove have four hall without which be certain gallery in a high place with five or six stair to ascend unto they here man put off their apparel and hence they go naked into the bath in the midst they always keep a cistern full of water first therefore they that mean to bathe themselves must pass through a cold hall where they use to temper hot water and cold together than they go into a room somewhat hot month together they use for fuel likewise the woman have their stove woman bath apart from the man and yet some hothouse serve both for man and woman but at sundry time namely for man from the three to the fourteen hour of the day and the residue for woman while woman be bathe themselves they hang out a rope at the first entrance of the house which be a sign for man that they may then proceed no far neither may husband here be permit to speak with their own wife so great a regard they have of their honesty here man and woman both after they have do bathe use to banquet and make merry with pleasant music and sing young stripling enter the bath stark naked without any shame but man cover their privity with a linen cloth the rich sort will not enter the common bath but that which be adorn their leg accord to each one estate and ability let we now speak somewhat of their victual and manner of eat the common sort set on the pot with fresh meat twice every week but the gentleman and rich sort every day their manner of eat and drink and as often as they listen they take three meal a day their breakfast consist of certain fruit and bread or else of a kind of liquid pap make like unto frumenty in winter they sup off the broth of salt flesh thicken with course meal to dinner they have flesh salad cheese and olive but in summer they have great cheer their supper be easy of digestion consist of bread melon grape or milk but in winter they have sodden flesh together with a kind of meat call Cuscusu which be make of a lump of Dow be set first upon a kind of meat call Cuscusu the fire in certain vessel full of hole and afterward be temper with butter and pottage some also use often to have roast-meat and thus you see after what sort both the gentleman and common people lead their life albeit the nobleman fare somewhat more dainty but if you compare they with the nobleman and gentleman of Europe they may seem to be miserable and base fellow not for any want or scarcity of victual but for want of good manner and cleanliness the table whereat they sit be low uncover and filthy seat they have none but the bare ground neither knife or spoon but only their ten talon the say Cuscusu be set before they all in one only platter whereout as well gentleman as other take it not with spoon but with their claw five the meat and pottage be put all in one dish out of which every one rake with his greasy fist what he think good you shall never see knife upon the table but they tear and greedy devour their meat like hungry dog neither do any of they desire to drink before he have well stuff his paunch and then will he sup off a cup of cold water as big as a milke-bowle the doctor indeed be somewhat more orderly at meal but to tell you the very truth in all Italy there be no gentleman so mean which for fine diet and stately furniture excel not the great potentate and lord of all Africa as touch their marriage they observe these course follow so soon as the maid the show not so much alacrity among the people of Fez there have remain certain relic of festival day institute of their rite observe upon festival day and their manner of mourn for the dead relic of as touch their feast prescribe by the mahometan law they be at large set down in that brief treatise which we have write concern the same law. the woman have by death lose their husband father or any other of their dear friend assemble forthwith a great multitude of their own sex together who strip themselves out of their own attire put on most vile sackcloth and defile their face with much dirt then call they certain man clad in woman attire bring great foure-square drum with they at the noise of which drum the women-mourner sing a funerall-song tend as much as may be to the commendation of the party decease and at the end of every verse the say woman utter most hideous shriek and out-cry tear their hair and with much lamentation beat their cheek and breast till they be all-imbrued with blood and so these heathenish superstition continue for seven whole day together at which seven day end they surcease their mourn for the space of forty day and then they begin anew to torment themselves for three day together in manner aforesaid howbeit these kind of obsequy be observe only by the base people but the gentleman and better sort behave themselves more modest at this time all the widow friend come about she to comfort she and send diverse kind of meat unto she for in the mourning-house they may dress no meat at all till the dead corpse be carry forth the woman herself that lose her husband father or brother never go forth with the funeral but how they wash and bury the dead corpse and what superstition they use thereabout you shall find record in my little treatise the majesty of the Fezzan kingdom decay of school in Fez for the instruct of child there be almost two hundred every one a description of the grammar school in Fez. two hundred school the Alcoran learn by heart of which be in fashion like a great hall. the schoolmaster teach their child to write and read not out of a book but out of a certain great table every day they expound one sentence of the Alcoran and have read quite through they begin it again repeat it so often till they have most firm commit the same to memory which they do right well in the space of seven year then read they Alcoran his father invite all his son schoolfellow unto a great banquet and his son in costly apparel ride through the street upon a gallant horse which horse and apparel the governor of the royal hand some of which weigh thirty pound these torch be most curious make be torch on mahumet birthday adorn round about with diverse first-fruit of wax which be light betimes in the morning do burn till sun-rise in the mean while certain singer resound the praise of mohammed and so soon as the sun be up all their solemnity cease this day use to be very gainful unto the schoolmaster for they sell the remnant of the wax upon the torch for a hundred duckat and sometime for more none of they pay any rent for his school for all their school be build many year ago and be free bestow for the train up of youth both in these common school and also in the college they have two day of recreation every week wherein they neither teach nor study now let we speak of the fortune-teller and diviner of who there be a great number and the fortune teller three sort of diviner in Fez. three kind for one sort use certain geomanticall figure other pour a drop of oil into a vial or glass of water make the say water to be transparent and bright wherein as it be in a mirror they affirm that they see huge swarm of devil that resemble a whole army some whereof be travel some be pass over a river and other fight a land-battell who when the divine see in quiet he demand such question of they as he be desirous to be resolve of and the devil give they answer with beckon or with some gesture of their hand or eye so inconsiderate and damnable be their credulity in this behalf the foresay glasse-viall they will deliver into child hand scarce of eight year old of who they will ask whether they see this or that devil many of the city be so besot with these vanity that they spend great sum upon they the three kind of diviner be women-witche witch which be affirm to have familiarity with devil some devil they call red some white and some black devil and when they will tell any man fortune they perfume themselves with certain odour say that then they possess themselves with that devil which they call for afterward change their voice they feign the devil to speak within they then they which come to inquire ought with great fear and tremble ask these vild and abominable witch such question as they mean to propound and last offer some fee unto the devil they depart but the wise and honest sort of people call these woman sahacat which in latin signify fricatrice because they have a damnable custom to commit unlawful venery fricatrice among themselves which I can express in any modest term if fair woman come unto they at any time these abominable witch will turn in lust towards they no otherwise then lusty younker do towards young maid and will in the devil behalf demand for a reward that they may lie with they and so by this mean it often fall out that think thereby to fulfil the devil command they lie with the witch yea some there be which be allure with the delight of this abominable vice will desire the company of these wiche and feign themselves to be sick will either call one of the witch home to they or will send their husband for the same purpose and so the witch perceive how the matter stand will say that the woman (...) s possess with a devil and that she can no way be cure unless she be admit into their society with these word her silly husband be persuade do not only permit she so to do but make also a sumptuous banquet unto the damn crew of witch which be do they use to dance very strange at the noise of drum and so the poor man commit his false wife to their filthy disposition howbeit some there be that will soon conjure the devil with a good cudgel effect it be a wonder to see into what reputation they grow thereby but when they can cast forth a devil they say it be a airy spirit their manner of adjure devil be this first they draw certain character and circle upon a ash-heape or some other place then describe they certain sign upon the hand and forehead of the party possess and perfume he after a strange kind of manner afterwards they make their enchantment or conjuration inquire of the devil which way or by what mean he enter the party as likewise what he be and by what name he be call and last charge he to come forth other there be that work by a certain cabalistical rule call Zairagia this rule be contain in many cabalist write for it be think to be natural magic neither be there any other negromancer in all Fez that will more certain and true resolve a doubtful question howbeit their art be exceed difficult for the student thereof must have as great skill in astrology as in cabala myself in time past have attain to some knowledge in this faculty continue I remember a whole day in describe one figure only which kind of figure be describe in manner follow first they draw many circle within the compass of a great circle in the first circle they make a cross at the four extremity whereof they set down the four quarter of the world to wit east west north and south at each end of one of the say cross line they note either pole likewise about the circumference of the first circle they paint the four element then divide they the same circle and the circle follow into four part and every four part they divide into other seven each one be distinguish with certain great arabian character so that every element contain eight and twenty character in the three circle they set down the seven planet in the four the twelve sign of the zodiac in the five the twelve latin name of the month in the six the eight and twenty house of the moon in the seven the three hundred sixty five day of the year and about the convexity thereof the four cardinal or principal wind then take they one only letter of the question propound multiply the same by all the particular aforenamed and the product or sum total they divide after a certain manner place it in some room accord to the quality of the character and as the element require wherein the say character be find without a figure all which be do they mark that figure which seem to agree with the foresay number or sum produce wherewith they proceed as they do with the former till they have find eight and twenty character whereof they make one word and of this word the speech be make that resolve the question demand this speech be always turn into a verse of the first kind which the arabian call Ethavil consist of eight and twelve accord to the meet of the arabian tongue whereof we have entreat in the last part of our arabian grammar and the verse consist a arabian grammar write by John leo. of those character comprehend always a true and infallible answer unto the question propound resolve first that which be demand and then expound the sense of the question itself these practitioner be never find to err which cause their art of cabala to be have in great admiration which although it be account natural yet never see I any thing that have more affinity with supernatural and divine knowledge I remember that I see in a certain open place of observe in the mahometan law. diverse mahometan sect moral philosopher they observe certain rule which Mahumet never prescribe by some they be account catholic or true Mahumetans and by other they be hold for heretic howbeit the great part of the common people reverence they as if they be god notwithstanding they commit many thing unlawful and forbid by the mahometan law as namely whereas the say law forbid any love-matter to be express in any musical ditty or song these moralist affirm the contrary in the foresay mahometan religion be a great number of rule or sect every of which have most learned patron and protector the foresay sect spring up fourscore year after Mahumet the first author thereof be call Elhesen Abilhasen and be bear in the town of Basora this man teach his disciple and follower certain precept but write he leave none behind he about a hundred year after there come another notable doctor of that sect from bagaded call Elharit Ibnu ese who leave volume of write unto his disciple afterwards those that be find to be his follower be all condemn by the mahometan patriarch and lawyer howbeit fourscore year after that sect begin to revive again under a certain famous professor who draw after he many disciple unto who he publish his doctrine this man at length and all his follower be by the patriarch and lawyer condemn to die which he understanding write forthwith unto the patriarch request that he may be license to dispute with the lawyer as touch his doctrine of who if he be convince he will most willing suffer death otherwise that it will be against all equity that so many innocent shall perish upon a unjust accusation the patriarch think his demand to be reasonable condescend whole thereunto but when the matter come to disputation the party condemn soon put all the lawyer to silence which when the patriarch perceive he revoke the sentence as unjust and cause many college and monastery to be erect for the say party and his follower after which time this sect continue about a hundred year till the emperor Malicsach of the turkish race come thither out of Asia the great and destroy all the maintainer thereof whereupon some of they flee unto cairo and the rest into Arabia be disperse here and there for the space of twenty year till the reign of Caselsah nephew unto one of his counsellor and a man of a high spirit be addict unto the say sect so restore erect and confirm the same that by the help of one Elgazzuli a most learned man who have write of the same argument a notable work divide into seven part he reconcile the lawyer with the disciple of this sect conditional that the lawyer shall be call conseruer of the prophet Mahumet his law and the sectary reformer of the same this concord last between they till bagade be sack by the tartar which befall Bagdet sack by the tartar in the year of the Hegeira 756. at what time those sectary so increase that they swarm almost over all Africa and Asia neither will they admit any into their society but such as be very learned and train up in all kind of liberal science to the end they may the better defend their own opinion and confute their adversary but now adays they admit all kind of rude and ignorant person affirm all sort of learning to be needless for the holy spirit say they reveal the knowledge of the truth unto such as be of a clean heart and they allege many reason for the confirmation of this their opinion though not very forcible wherefore despise their ancestor rite and the strict observation of the law they addict themselves to nought else but delight and pleasure feast often and sing lascivious song sometime they will rend their garment either allude thereby to the verse that they sing or be move thereunto by their corrupt and vile disposition say false that they be then ravish with a fit of divine love but rather impute it to their abundance of meat and gluttony for each one of they will devour as much meat as may well suffice three or which be more likely they utter those passionate clamour and out-cry because they be inflame with unlawful and filthy lust for sometime it happen that some one of the principal of they with all his scholar and disciple be invite to the marriage of some gentleman and at the begin of the banquet they will rehearse their devout orison and song but so soon as they be rise from the table the elder of the company be about to dance tear their garment and if any one in the midst of their dance that have drink immoderate chance to fall down he be take up forthwith by one of the scholar and too too lascivious kiss whereupon this proverb grow among the people of Fez the hermit banquet which they use in reproach of those master that make their scholar their minion among these sect there be some that have not only a diverse law but also a different of diverse other rule and sect and of the superstitious credulity of many belief from the residue whereupon by some other they be call heretic some there be also which hold that a man by good work by fast and abstinence may attain unto the nature of a angel which good work fast etc. do say they so purge and free the mind from all discipline or science and although they fall into sin before they be come to the fifty degree yet they say that God will not impute that sin unto they these fellow indeed in the beginning lead a most a great height and every one of the say standard-bearer know most exact always ford of river and passage through wood wherefore they be for the most part appoint to guide the army the drummers of who there be great store in the king host play upon certain drum of brass as big as a great kettle the low part whereof be narrow and the upper broad be cover with a skin these drummers ride on horseback have always on the one side of their horse a great weight hang down to counterpoise the heaviness of their drum on the other side they be allow most swift horse because the moor account it a great disgrace to loose a drum the say drum make such a loud and horrible noise that they be not only hear a far off but also strike exceed terror both upon man and horse and they be beat only with a buls-pizzle the musician be not maintain at the king charge for the city be bind at their cost to send a certain number of they to the war who accord to their demeanour in the war be admit or not admit unto the king table this king have also a certain master of ceremony who sit at his foot in the senate house and command each man to sit down and to speak accord to his dignity all the maid servant in the king family be negro-slave which be partly chamberlain and partly wait maid and yet his queen be always of a white skin likewise in the king of Fez his court be certain christian captive be partly Spanish and partly Portugal woman who be most circumspect keep by certain eunuch that be negro slave the king of Fez have very large dominion but his revenue be small to wit scarce three the king of Fez his revenue then small hundred thousand duckat the five part whereof redound not to the king for the remainder be divide into sundry portion as we have before signify yea the great part of the say revenue be pay in corn cattle oil and butter all which yield but small store of money in some place they pay a ducat and one four part tribute for every acre but in other place a whole family pay but so much in some other region each man above fifteen year of age pay as much tribute also neither be the people of this great city more vex with any thing then with pay of their tribute and imposition here also be to be note that the mahometan governor the priest only except may not exact great tribute how much revenue than those that mohammed have allot unto they namely of every of their subject which possess a hundred duckat in ready money they be to have two duckat and a half for yearly tribute every husbandman likewise be bind to pay for tribute the ten part of all his corne. and tithe pay to mahometan prince because they be priest and by his law none other all the say tribute he appoint to be pay unto the patriarch who shall bestow that which be superfluous for the prince to have upon common use namely for the relieve of poor impotent people and widow and for maintain of war against the enemy but since the patriarch begin to decay the prince as we have before-said exercise tyranny for it be not sufficient for they to exact all the forename tribute and riotous to consume the same but also to urge people unto great contribution so that all the inhabitant of Africa be so oppress with daily exaction that they have scarce wherewithal to feed and apparel themselves for which cause there be almost no man of learning or honesty that will seek any acquaintance note with courtier or will invite they to his table or accept any gift be they never so precious at their hand think that whatsoever good they have be get by theft and bribery the king of field there be certain little cell make be so high that a man may stand upright in they each one of these cell be shut fast with a little door and contain within every of they a arm man who open the door present himself to the view of the lion then the lion see the door open come run towards they with great fury but the door be shut again he wax more furious than before then bring they forth a bull to combat with the lion who enter a fierce and bloody conflict wherein if the bull kill the fight betwixt a lion and a bull. lion that day sport be at a end but if the lion get the victory than all the arm man be ordinary twelve leap forth of their cell and invade the lion each one of they have a javelin with a pike of a and a half long and if these arm man seem to be too hard for the lion the king cause their number to be diminish but perceive they too weak the king with his company from a certain high place where he stand to behold the sport kill the lion with their crossbow and oftentimes it fall out that before the lion be slay some one of the man die for it the residue be sore wound the reward of those that encounter the lion be ten ducat apiece and a new garment neither may conjecture the miserable estate of this people the mountain yield nought but panic whereof they make bread and other victual but at the foot thereof be certain garden replenish with grape date and they frame their iron iron-mine in manner of horseshoe which serve they sometime in stead of money whereof they have great want in this mountain unless the smith by their art keep this money in store the wood both to keep goat and to gather fuel they have neither civility nor learning but live after a brutish manner without all discretion and humanity this woody mountain be full of pinetree and fountain their house be not make of stone but of sea-rush so that they may easy be remove from place to place which be very mount Selelgo commodious to the inhabitant for every spring they leave the mountain and descend into the valley from whence about the end of may they be expel by the arabian which inhabit the desert who by reason of their abundance of goat and other cattle forsake the say hazard of their life especial if the basket or the rope be wear in any place yea and the distance of place be often a occasion of great terror in this mountain there be great store of cattle but unto this place there daily resort certain officer appoint by the senate who view and observe the increase of Nilus declare unto certain child how much it have increase which child wear yellow scarf upon their head do publish the say increase of Nilus in every street of the city and the suburb and receive gift every day of the merchant artificer and woman so long as Nilus increase the foresay device or experiment of the increase of Nilus be this that follow if the water reach only to the fifteen cubit of the foresay pillar they hope for a fruitful year follow but if it stay between the twelve cubit and the fifteen than the increase of the year will prove but mean if it rest between the ten and twelve cubit then be it a sign that corn will be sell ten duckat the bushel but if it arise to the eighteen there be like to follow great scarcity in regard of too much moisture and if the eighteen be surmount all Egypt be in danger to be swallow up by the inundation of Nilus the officer therefore declare unto the child the height of the river and the child publish the same in all street of the city charge the people to fear God and tell they how high Nilus be increase and the people be astonish at the wonderful increase of Nilus whole exercise themselves in prayer and give of alm and thus Nilus continue forty day increase and forty day decrease all which time corn be sell very dear because while the inundation last every man may sell at his own pleasure but when the eighty day be once past the clerk of the market appoint the price of all victual and especial of corn fat and have kill he the say sect of Chenefia come and buy up his flesh handsmooth this sect be rife also among the turk the mameluke and the people of Asia and albeit the turk may free use the food beforementioned yet do they not enure themselves thereunto in Egypt and in the city of cairo there be permit four several sect differ each from other both in canon and civil law all which sect have their original from the religion of Mahumet for there be in time past four man of singular learning who by subtlety and sharpness of wit find out a way to make particular deduction out of mahumet general precept so that each of they will interpret the opinion of Mahumet accord to their own fancy and will every man apply they to his own proper sense and therefore they must needs disagree much between themselves howbeit grow famous among the common people in regard of their diverse canon and precept they be the first author and founder of the say four sect any one of which whatsoever mahometan profess can renounce the same at his pleasure and embrace another sect unless he be a man of deep learning and know the reason and allegation of both part also there be in the city of cairo four principal judge who give sentence only upon matter of great importance under which four be substitute other inferior judge in every street of the city which decide petty contention and brabble and if the party which be at controversy chance to be of diverse sect the plaintiff may summon and convent the defendant before the judge of his street howbeit the defendant may if he will appeal from he unto the high judge of all be place over the four principal judge aforesaid and be governor of the sect call essafichia and this high judge have authority to dispense withal or to disannul the decree of the four principal and of all the other inferior judge accord as he shall see cause whosoever attempt aught against the canon and precept of his own religion be severe punish by the judge of the same religion moreover albeit the priest of the foresay sect differ very much both in their form of liturgy or prayer and also in many other respect yet do they not for that diversity of ceremony hate one another neither yet do the common people of sundry sect fall to mutiny and debate but man indeed of singular learning and much read confer oftentimes together and as in private each man affirm his own sect to be the best so likewise do they confirm their opinion by subtle argument neither may any man under pain of grievous punishment reproach any of the say four ancient doctor and in very deed they all of they follow one and the same religion to wit that which be prescribe in the canon of the principal doctor of the mahometans which canon go for currant over all Africa and most part of Asia except in the dominion of the great sophi of Persia who because he reject the say canon be account by other mahometans a heretic and a schismatic but how such variety of opinion proceed from the four doctor aforesaid it be tedious and troublesome to rehearse he that be desirous to know more of this matter let he read my commentary which I have write concern the law and religion of mohammed accord to the doctrine of Malich who be a man of profound learning and be bear at Medina Talnabi where the body of Mahumet lie bury which doctrine of Malich be embrace throughout all Syria Egypt and Arabia wherewith if any be delight let he peruse my foresay commentary and they will satisfy he to the full upon malefactor they inflict most grievous and horrible punishment especial upon such as have commit any heinous crime in the court. thief they condemn to the halter a murder commit treacherous they punish in manner follow the executioner assistant take the malefactor one by the head and another by the foot and then come the chief executioner with a two-hand-sword and cut his body in twain the one part whereof adjoin a horrible kind of execution to the head be put into a fire full of un-slaked lime and it be a most strange and dreadful thing to consider how the same dismember and half body will remain a live in the fire for the space of a quarter of a hour speak and make answer unto the stander by but rebel or seditious person they flay alive stuff their skin with bran till they resemble man shape which be do they carry the say stuff skin upon camel back through every street of the city and there publish the crime of the party execute than which punishment I never see a more dreadful by reason that the condemn party live so long in torment but if the tormenter once touch his navel with the knife he present yield up the ghost which he may not do until he be command by the magistrate stand by if any the navel be cut be present death be imprison for debt not have kind of eagle be call in the arabian tongue Nesir the african teach their eagle to prey upon fox and wolf which in their encounter cease upon the head of the say beast with their bill and upon the back with their talent to avoid the danger of bite but if the beast turn his belly upward a strange narration the eagle will not forsake he till she have either peck out his eye or slay he many of our african writer affirm that the male eagle oftentimes engender with a she-wolf beget a dragon have the beak and wing of a bird a serpent tail the foot of a wolf and a skin speckle and party colour like the skin of a serpent neither can it open the eyelid and it live in cave this monster albeit myself have not see yet the common report over all Africa affirm that there be such a one the Nesir be the great fowl in all Africa and exceed a crane in bigness though the bill the fowl call Nesir neck and leg be somewhat short in fly this bird mount up so high into the air that it can be discern but at the sight of a dead carcase it will immediate descend this bird live a long time and I myself have see many of they unfeathered by reason of extreme old age wherefore have cast all their feather they return unto their nest as if they be new hatch and be there nourish by the young bird of the same kind the italian call it by the name of a vulture but I think it to be of another kind they nestle upon high rock and upon the top of wild and desert mountain especial upon mount Atlas and they be take by such as be acquaint with those place the best african hawk be white be take upon certain mountain of the numidian hawk desert and with these hawk they pursue the crane of these hawk there be diverse kind some be use to fly at partridge and quail and other at the hare parrot there be as big as a dove of diverse colour some red some black and some ash-coloured parats or poppiniay which albeit they can so fit express man speech yet have they most sweet and shrill voice of locust there be sometime see such monstrous swarm in Africa that in fly the locust they intercept the sunbeam like a thick cloud they devour tree leaf fruit and all green thing grow out of the earth at their departure they leave egg behind they whereof other young locust breed which in the place where they be leave will eat and consume all thing even to the very bark of tree procure thereby extreme dearth of corn especial in Mauritania howbeit the inhabitant of Arabia Desarta and of Libya esteem the come of these locust as a fortunate bode for seethe or dry they in the sun they bruise they to powder and so eat they the great part of Africa have none other salt but such as be dig out of quarry and of mineral and fruit root and first of mineral salt. one pound of salt for half a ducat mine after the manner of marble or freestone be of a white red and gray colour Barbary abound with salt and Numidia be indifferent furnish therewith but the land of Negro and especial the inner part of Ethiopia be so destitute thereof that a pound of salt be there sell for half a ducat and the people of the say region use not to set salt upon their table but hold a crumb of salt in their hand they lick the same at every morsel of meat which they put in their mouth in certain lake of Barbary all the summer time there be fair and white salt congeal or kern as namely in diverse place near unto the city of Fez. antimony grow in many place of Africa in the lead-mine be separate from the lead the mineral call antimony by the help of brimstone great plenty of this mineral be dig out of the bottom of mount Atlas especial where Numidia border upon the kingdom of Fez. Brimstone likewise be dig in great abundance out of other place of Africa euphorbium be the juice or gum of a certain herb grow like the head of a wild thistle between the branch whereof grow certain fruit as big in compass as a green cucumber after which shape or likeness it bear certain little grain or seed and some of of euphorbium the say first-fruit be a ell long and some be long they grow not out of the branch of the herb but spring out of the firm ground and out of one flag you shall see sometime twenty and sometime thirty of they issue forth the people of the same region when the say fruit be once ripe do prick they with their knife and out of the hole proceed a liquor or juice much like unto milk which by little and little grow thick and slimy and so be grow thick they take it off with their knife put it in bladder and dry it and the plant or herb itself be full of sharp prickle of pitch there be two kind the one be natural and take out of certain stone which be in fountain the water whereof retain the unsavoury smell and taste of the same and of pitch the other be artificial and proceed out of the juniper or pinetree and this artificial pitch I see make upon mount Atlas in manner follow they make a deep and round furnace pitch make in mount Atlas with a hole in the bottom through which hole the pitch may fall down into a hollow place within the ground be make in form of a little vessel and put into the say furnace the bough of the foresay tree break into small piece they close up the mouth of the furnace and make a fire under it by the heat whereof the pitch distil forth of the wood through the bottom of the furnace into the foresay hollow place and so it be take up and put in bladder or bag be a fruit grow upon a small tree which bear large and broad leaf of a cubit the fruit call Mau^ or Musa long have a most excellent and delicate taste and spring forth about the bigness of a small cucumber the mahometan doctor affirm that this be the fruit which God forbid our first parent to eat in paradise which when they have eat they cover their nakedness with leaf of the same fruit as be of all other leave most meet for that purpose they grow in great abundance at Sela a town of the kingdom of Fez but in far great plenty in the land of Egypt and especial at Damiata the tree bear cassia be of great thickness have leaf like unto the mulberry tree of cassia they bear a broad and white blossom and be so lade with first-fruit that they be constrain to gather great store before they be ripe lest the tree shall break with overmuch weight and this kind of tree grow only in Egypt the root Tauzarghente grow in the western part of Africa upon the ocean sea shore the root call Tauzarghente yield a fragrant and odoriferous smell and the merchant of Mauritania carry the same into the land of Negro where the people use it for a most excellent perfume and yet they neither burn it nor put any fire at all thereto for be keep only in a house it yield a natural send of itself in Mauritania they sell a bunch of these root for half a ducat which be carry to the land of Negro be sell again for eighty or one hundred duckat and sometime for more the herb Addad be bitter and the root itself be so venomous that one drop of the water distil thereout will kill a man within the space of a hour which be common know the root call addad even to the woman of Africa the root Surnag grow also upon the western part of mount Atlas be say to be very comfortable and preservative unto the privy part of man and be drink in a electuary to the root call Surnag stir up venereal lust etc. neither must I here omit that which the inhabitant of mount Atlas do common report that many of those damosel which keep cattle upon the say mountain have lose their virginity by none other occasion but by make water upon the say root unto who I will in merriment answer that I believe all which experience have teach concern the secret virtue of the same root yea they affirm moreover that some of their maiden be so infect with this root that they be not only deflower of their virginity but have also their whole body puff up and swell these be the thing memorable and worthy of knowledge see and observe by i John Leo throughout all Africa which country I have in * * that be in Barbary Numidia Libya the land of Negro and Egypt all place travel quite over wherein whatsoever I see worthy the observation I present commit to writing and those thing which I see not I procure to be at large declare unto i by most credible and substantial person which be themselves eye-witness of the same and so have get a fit opportunity I think good to reduce these my travel and study into this one volume forasmuch as man desire to read late occurrent and these my labour be intend not to the profit and pleasure alone but to the honour also of the english name and nation I have add this follow discourse of the late war in Barbary not yet pursue they to these time but content myself with the beginning and some year proceed thereof the english have as you shall see yea be no small part therein in the voluntary english adventure in the civil uncivil broil of ice-frozen muscovia of sunne-scorched Barbary of turkish and persian fight by sea the mogul by land the Sweden polish German bohemian belgian and many-headed-italian broil near home the eastern and see you short I take my leave this 24. of june 1600. from the city of Maroco from Maroco in Barbary your love brother in-law Thomas bernhere obtain the sceptre he first provide himself of the grave man he can find in his kingdom to be counsellor of estate then of the most experience and valiant soldier for commander over his camp and garrison town and whereas he be monarch over two nation the larby and brebers he find it requisite to use a twofold government the larby dwell in the most plain champion country of his three kingdom Moruecos the larby be the dweller in the plain the brebers mountainer Sus and Fez be easy govern be of mild and peaceable nature give to thrift and tillage of the ground seek no alteration but receive from he a due form of justice execute by his minister protect they from the montaneir which be robber willing obey his regal authority and yearly pay their ten towards their king maintenance as for the brebers or montaneir be of a untamed and fierce disposition speak the tamiset tongue which be as much different from the Larbee as Welch be from our english dwell in place by nature defensible and almost inaccessible he can not so well govern neither have ever such absolute power over they nor receive the five penny of profit from they as he do from the alarby therefore he seek by all mean to diminish their strength of people draw the greatness of his dominion they always into foreign expedition especial into that war against the negro which continue a long time thereby extend his empire so far that way as by camel it be six month journey from Moruecos to the far part of his dominion likewise he use a Caravan be a company of merchant go together for trade with a great number of horse camel and mule lade with commodity this people to go with the caravans to Gago to fetch home his yearly tribute and custom whereby many be consume in travel over the for any offence or robbery commit by they his sword shall punish severe that the rest may fear divide their country into several division or canton in every of which he place a Alkeid with soldier to suppress any sudden uproar much like our lieutenant set over our several county but that the Alkeid be continual resident and have great power in execute marshal law and last as pledge of their loyalty he will get their chief man son into his hand bring they up in his court to a more civil and delicate kind of life he be always of mind to keep peace with Christendom with Spain who be his next potent neighbour but above all love the english nation and admire the late queen happy government willing to entertain trade with we witness his many letter write to that worthy lady of happy memory and his embassage send unto she 1601. perform by Abdala Wahad anowne and Hamet Alhadg their great traveller to Mecha and other place towards his subject he be not too tyrannical but sweeten his absolute power and will with much clemency by diverse way he get excessive store of gold first by see his ten true pay from the larbee second by trade with the negro take up the salt at tegazza and sell it at Gago have from thence return in good gold third by husband his maseraw or ingenewe where his sugar cane do grow though now all spoil sugar garden with these war for it be sufficient know all of they about Moruecos Taradant and magador be yearly worth unto he six hundred thousand ounce at the least I omit his love he take in entertain foreign artisan the re-edify of his house in Moruecos get italian marble the rich that can be buy for money and workman hire from thence at great wage his sumptuous provision for the sarraile and maintenance of his the place where his woman be keep woman not so much delight in the sin as his predecessor have do before as to Muley Sidan the three son continue in Tedula a province fruitful and situate in the flat of Barbary the midway m. Sidan between Fez and Moruecos as I have tell you who govern those part in great peace and quietness even in the chief time of the tumult that be in the border dominion of his elder brother Sheck whereof you shall read hereafter insomuch that he be general commend and like both of his father and of all the kingdom for his government be strict in see the execution of justice to be do in those part that he govern not spare his kindred or near follower in those case from his infancy he natural hate all manner of thief whatsoever especial those his rob by the highway and without any favour or mercy severe punish they howsoever he carry himself very dutiful to his father while he be live yet from his childhood he be always of a aspire and ambitious nature which can never be bring to subject itself to give any awful respect to his elder brethren but to hazard his whole estate in obtain the kingdom account himself his father lawful heir in that he be his father elder son which he have by any of his marry wife in this point not regard the custom and law of the moor who in title of inheritance or succession respect not the mother whether she be marry wife or concubine buy with money so that her son be the elder in birth but to return again to Muley Sheck the king elder son who after the death of his bassa Mustepha behead by his father command soon show unto all man the want of governgo that be in he for in his latter time give himself over to drunkenness and other detestable vice which amongst the moor common accompany that sin regard not at all the government of his kingdom but suffer his servant follower and soldier to do Muley sheck misgovernment of himself and his country what they will in rob and spoil the good of his honest mind subject without controlment and through want of justice due execute his whole country in a short time swarm so with thief and robber by the high way that there be no travel through his dominion but in Caffilas or company of three hundred and four hundred person at a time and they hardly sometime escape the hand of thief the alarby who continue to this day in tribe and kindred be the husbandman of the country live in the field in tent by till of the ground and breed up of cattle when as they can not quiet gather in and peaceable enjoy the corn and fruit of the ground deny to pay the king their accustom duty and in the field follow the course of Muley sheck servant in the city in rob of all passenger that come within their power and such be the lavish manner of spend and consume of his treasure that in his humour he neither regard what he give nor to who in so much that a jew who be a musician and use to play before he in his drunken rich jew. fit what with the gift give he by the prince and what else he get out of his house have get together in money and jewel in the space of four or five year to the value of four hundred thousand duckat which be about forty thousand pound sterling this dissolute life and careless government of Muley Sheck grieve the old king not a little especial to see such a change or alteration in he who forwardness in former time have be the stay of his age and have move he to upon difference come thither to have their cause decide every one must tell his own tale and plead his own matter when both party have speak then give the their manner of judicature judge sentence so that in one day the cause be bring into court and the same day end if either part have witness to produce than the judge give three day respite to bring they in which be bring the adverse party shall have other three day respite to disprove they and if he can prove the witness either infamous in manner or give to detestable sin as drunkenness adultery or such like and can prove the witness say not his prayer six time allegation against witness due in four and twenty hour then shall he be utter disable to bear witness and thus in seven day the long suit shall be end if a obligation or rather bill of debt be bring into court the obligee must either pay the debt go to prison or to pawn the value of the debt debt or better which pawn may be keep in nine day upon great reason to see if the debtor can redeem it at the nine day end if he do it not then be it sell and the party who shall pay the money must sustain the loss as coadjutor to these judge and next in place to they be the scrivanos who upon death coadjutor to the judge or other remove be common make judge these be talby which make write between party and party short and plain without multiplication of word and they be of opinion in their obligatory bill they put neither forfeit nor condition have for the make thereof two penny english and no more they use no long draught in matter of purchase or these tripartite indenture with such large and long implicit and explicit covenant but thus the people deal in matter of contract and bargain I buy of you manner of contract a uineyard house merchandise at such a price to be pay at such a time call two honest man whereof one shall be a Talbie if I can get he to witness this our bargain we four go to the scrivener who likewise be a Talbie and have this set down in writing and if our bargain be for twenty thousand pound it be set down in ten line and the justice of the country will allow i my bargain with as great reason as if I have a great engross book of conveyance as big as the map of the whole world in the new edition next in this nature to these be the sterye which have small fee to see the execution of law sterye or officer of the court. a sentence of the judge fulfil these likewise fetch man to answer their adversary which will delay and not come before the judge either upon perverseness or badness of their plea or any other cause whatsoever wherefore to be always ready these be continual attendant in the house of the judge and wait upon he whethersoever he go be a officer to see true weight and measure if any be faulty all the ware Muttifeb in such a man shop he give to the poor the party proclaim a unjust man and sore whip the Hackam be the lord Martial in every city who judge upon life and death assoon as Hackam the party delinquent be take and his offence prove present his throat be cut murder there be death so be manifest theft adultery likewise prove by very good witness and sometime it be death for any man to wear a sword who be not a officer yea though he be a soldier other offence accord to the necessity of the time and pleasure of the king by proclamation be make death which the Hackam must see execute upon loss of his own head Muckadens be substitute to the Hackam see his judgement fulfil and in his absence Muckadens have his authority foker or saint dwell in the best place of the country keep great hospitality for all traveller foker whither any man come for a night and be go in the morning much good these do in the country by their example of moral live and bestow their own good in their life time to help the needy and distress comprimise difference betwixt party and repress all disorder win great love and respect for their house be hold sanctuary who privilege the king will not violate but upon great and weighty reason the king nobility and soldier desire to serve on horseback which most common they do for in any army there be three horse for one foot the king will seldom venture to the cause and manner of their fight fight out a battle but as you may perceive by the precedent it be and be the usage amongst the three brethren when they meet in a field whosoever get at the first onset the advantage make the other present leave the field and fly unto some place of strength they fight with no armour except a buff jerkin for the better for it and a leather hide tan for the mean and some coat of male their arm be a horseman staff target and sword or a horseman piece and sword. the alarby serve all upon horse will fight sore battle to maintain their deadly feud deadly feud with the larby than in service of their king insomuch that upon loss of any great lord or chief man of their blood crull battle have ensue wherein ten thousand man have be slay at one time and it be their fashion the fair virgin to ride upon a camel with a flag in her hand deck in all pomp to solicit her kindred to revenge and go foremost in the field encourage they to follow upon which incitement much blood be spill her kindred as loath to lose their virgin and not revenge their injury the other side strive to win she and the field hold that a continue glory to the seven generation when a man be kill his tribe seek not revenge only upon the man which kill the party but the first man of that tribe he meet withal he will he kill if he can and so think he have satisfy his kinsman death the brebers or mountayner likewise maintain this feud who be most shoot and swordman with the brebers upon the day of battle their woman follow hard behind they with a colour in their hand call hanna and if they see any of their side offer to run away or retire present they will throw some of this hanna upon their clothes which will stain and the party ever after be hold for a coward and a dishonour jew. for fear of this infamy few forsake the field but either conquer their enemy or die like man who be present strip and bury by these woman which follow they the trade of the moor into NICHOLAY and how it come into the possession of Barbarossa and also of Malta and Tripoli ALger be a city in Africa very ancient first build by a people of Africa call Mesgana of who she take she first name afterward be call i^^ and be change of name of alger the seat royal of juba in the time when the roman bare dominion in Africa in honour of Caesar it be call julie Caesare and since the moor call it gezeir Arab Eleagair which in their language signify isle because she be cituate near maiorque-minorque jevise and Fro^entierre but the spaniard now do call she alger howbeit she be situate upon the Mediterran sea upon the hang of a mountain environ with strong wall ramperd ditch platform and bulwark in form almost threesquare the largeness which go towards the sea side stretch narrow almost unto the high part whereas there be a great building make in form of a citadel to command the town and entry of the haven as for the building be beyond the palace royal be very fair house belong too particular man with a great number of bath and cook house the place and street be so well ordain that every one in his occupation apart there be about three thousand hearth-steed at the bottom of the city which be towards the north join to the wall which be beat with the surge of the sea in a great place be by great artifice and subtle architecture build their principal and head mosque and a little below that be the arsenal which be the place into which be hail up and trim the galley and other vessel this city be very merchant-like for that she be situate upon the sea and for this cause marvelous people for her bigness she be inhabit of turk moor and jew in great number which with marvelous gain exercise the trade of merchandise and lend out money at usury they have two market day in every week to the which resort a infinite number of people of the mountain plain and valley be neighbour thereabouts which do bring thither all sort of fruit corn and foul of very cheap price for I have see a Partridge sell for a judit which be a small piece of silver money in manner four square and be in furnace fit make for breed of chicken value of our money four penny and a mite but true it be that their partridge be not so big nor delicate as we be the hen and chicken be also very good cheap for that they have in most part of their house furnace make in manner like unto the hothouse or stove of Germany in the which with a small heat they do breed and hatch their egg without help of the hen and therefore it be not to be marvel at though they have great plenty of such pullen they also have a great number of camel and ox which they do shoe lade and ride upon as upon camel and ox shod horse and go through the street because of the multitude of people which there be marvelous they go cry with a loud voice Baluc Baluc which be too say beware beware I have also see diverse moor mount on Barbary horse without saddle bridle stirrup or the moor do ride their horse without saddle or bridle spur have only a string in the mouth to stay they withal and as for the man they be altogether naked have only about their middle part to cover their privity some piece of a white charge or blanket in manner of a apron and about their head a linen cloth roll which they bring about and under their chin their weapon be three dart or long javelin which they carry in their right hand and do weapon of the moor shoot and throw with wonderful dexterity and upon their left arm be fasten a large dagger make a little crooked after the fashion of a woodknife which they call Secquin and use to fight at hand stroke withal and to annoy their enemy come to the close the most part of the turk of Algiers whether they be of the king household or the galley be Christians reny or mahumetise of all nation but most of they spaniard italian and of Provence of the land and coast of the sea Mediterran give ail to whoredom sodometry theft and all other most detestable vice live only of rove spoil and pill at the sea and the island be about they and with their practic art bring daily to Algiers a number of poor christian many reny christian in Algiers a miserable life of the christian slave in Algiers Pleasant garden which they sell unto the mother and other merchant of Barbary for slane who afterward transport they and sell they where they think good or else beat they miserable with staff do employ and constrain they to work in the field and in all other vile and abject occupation and servitude almost intolerable and therefore it be not to be marvel at though these poor christian slave make of it no scruple at all in put of we in danger to set themselves at liberty without the city towards the west be many fair and pleasant garden set and adorn with diverse tree bring forth first-fruit of alsort among other thing there be milons of marvelous goodness and incomparable sweetness they have also another fruit call which the italian call angury be like in bigness and colour to our green citroville in winter which they eat raw without bread or salt and have a taste so delicate and sweet that it melt in one mouth give a water as it be sugar and serve great to refresh and digest about their garden be many well full of good water and the ground there abouts although it be mountain and valley be very fertile for fruit and vine on the other part towards the east without the town run into the sea a small river call which a river serve aswell to drink of as other commodity and also make many mill to grind the course of the sea from the cape of Marfuz where as yet be see the foundation of the ancient city tipasa which in time past be by the emperor of Rome honour in praise of tipasa a old city the country latin do bow and wind like unto a crosebow-lath and all along the river and the shore the moorish woman and maiden slave of Algiers do go to wash their linen be common whole naked save that they wear a piece of Cotten cloth of some strange colour to cover their secret part which notwithstanding for a little piece of money they will willing uncover they wear also for a ornament about their neck arm and leg great collar or bracelet of Latin set with certain false stone but as for the wife of the turk or moor they be not see go uncover for they wear a great Barnuche make of a blanket of white black or violet colour which cover their whole body and the head the second day after our arrival at Algiers I find the mean for money and with fair word too hire a renyed Spaniard to conduct and lead i through all place that I most desire to see so as by his mean I see and learn many thing within four or five day that we be there in quiet and namely bring i upon a high mountain be a mile from the town to see and behold the situation of a very strong and great tower be build upon another mountain there near about and gentle inquire of he what strength the tower may be of he declare unto i that the breadth of the ditch about the same be seventeen brase save about the gate and entry into it towards the north it be only seven fathom broad and two spear length deep moreover he say unto i that within the fortress there be nine great cast piece and eighteen other as well minion as fawconet and other and that in the midst of the tower there be a well of very good water upon the height thereof stand a windmill and another stand without the gate and that thirty ordinary soldier be commit within it to keep the same and to make short that this tower be make to none other intent as also other since have confirm then for the guard and keep of the fountain head which from thence be bring and convey under the water into the city alger be long time under the dominion of the king of Telensin until such time as they of Bugie choose a new king unto who they give and render themselves as his tributary because he be near unto they then the king of Telensin and that he can soon help they if need be but in process of time perceive themselves to be as it be free and out of all doubt arm certain ship to the sea with the which they become such coursaire or pirate that in short time they annoy by their piracy and robbery on the sea not only the coast of Spain but also all the mediterrane land which perceive Ferdinando the king catholic Ferdinando king catholic constrain the moor to a truce send to alger a great army to assiege they and for to keep they in most distress cause with a marvelous readiness a fort to be make in a small island which lie before the city keep they by that mean so straight besiege that in short time they be constrain to require a truce for ten year which be agree unto they upon condition of a certain tribute which they pay until the death of king Ferdinando for than they espy a convenient time and mean to break the truce and to set themselves at liberty call unto they Cairadin barbarosse who after the siege of bone retire to the castle of Gegill stand in the coast of the Mediterran sea upon the top of a high rock seventy mile from bugie who be by they choose to be their chief captain give many fierce assault unto the fortress so as he put the spaniard to flight and incontinent after cause it to be ruin and pull down even to the foundation he then see so happy success of his enterprise can no long abide to be as companion but in a bath traitorous slay a prince of Arabia call Selim who Selim slay by treason declare himself to be lord of the city afterward forsake the name of a captain any long cause himself to be call king and coin money under his name and so well guide his affair that in short time after he bring all his neighbour about he to become contributory unto he such be the beginning of the magnificent estate of Cariedin barbarosse after who death his brother Hariadene the king have not complete power but they enjoy as this author say a kind of commonwealth this Ha^iadene be the famous sea captain admiral of the turk navy mention in the turkish history which affright
