three ship as one of middleburgh undermine and defraud merchant one of Amsterdam and one of Schiedam and that all our ship meet and lie at anchor together to sell our ware the one ship see that the other traffic more and vent more ware then his fellow to find the mean to get the merchant aboard their ship they will the pilot with who they must hold friendship for they carry the merchant aboard to bring they aboard their ship and they will give they something for their labour and the pilot accord to get something bring they aboard that ship which have make they that offer for they be very covetous which the other ship perceive will the pilot to bring the merchant aboard their ship and they will likewise give they something and they make they answer that if they will give they as much as the other do they will come aboard their ship which they promise to do and give they more dache than the other and by that mean drive the merchant pilot and tolken aboard their ship which the other ship see and think that their merchant ware cost they no more than the other give they more dache than the other and by that mean strive one with the other they diminish one and the other gain and in fine their gift grow to such a rate that at this day their dache amount unto six or seven and now it be come to pass that whereas the country people and merchant be wont to pay the litridge and brokeridge to the pilot and tolken to carry they aboard the ship they seek to the merchant and country moor to get they into their canoe for greediness of dache which they get of the factor for their labour to bring the merchant aboard and thereby in stead of pay they for go aboard they give the merchant much dache in regard of the great profit they get thereby many merchant come to the sea side to buy ware some of they a hundred or two hundred mile from within the land bring great store of gold and have diverse slave with they which they lade with the ware which they buy in the ship whereof some have twenty other thirty and some more as they have mean and accord to the trade that they use which merchant or moorish country people know the house or lodging where they use to lie and weigh their money to their tolke or host and tell they what good or ware they will have who come aboard common bring one of the merchant with they for they trust not one the other and leave the rest with their slave upon the land which tell they what ware they desire to have and if it be a merchant that can speak no Portugal speech they will present tell you and will the factor not to speak moorish speech unto they because their merchant be one that dwell far within the land thereby give you to understand that they mean to deceive he and to beguile he of much money the poor merchant be sick and lie in ask my fellow if I be a thief the ship spue like a dog in the mean time the broker make the match for they tell the factor how much ware they desire to have for so much gold for that the ware be common sell all at one price the tolken make not many word with the factor but set certain ware before the merchant as little as they can to content he for his money and the price be make with he he weigh their gold and take the ware and go on land again and the merchant be go home than the pilot and tolken come aboard the ship again to fetch that which they have coozon the merchant off so that oftentimes the merchant be deceive of a three part of their good by such practice other while he look about or turn to spew steal a piece of the merchant gold and put it into their mouth ear or nostril make the merchant believe that his money be too light the merchant for his part see that cozen knave by mean of their the every his money will not reach out because it be too light that it may weigh more than it be blow in the balance which the factor oftentimes perceive not and think that they have their full weight be by that mean deceive and come short of their reckon so that they have a thousand device to steal and to beguile the merchant at first they be wont to be very simple in their deal and trust the netherlander very much whereat we wonder for they be of opinion that white man be god and white devil can hardly make black saint will not deceive they and then take the ware upon their word without reckon it after they whereby they be deceive for that if they buy ten fathom of linen cloth they find but eight and by that mean lose two fathom and other thing after the rate which the factor do so gross that the merchant in the end perceive it and begin to look better to themselves and grow so subtle in their reckon that if they buy one hundred fathom of linen they can reckon it to a fathom and tell whether they have their measure or not so that now if you do they any wrong by measure or reckon they will not come aboard your ship any more and which be more for any bad look or hasty word that you shall give they they will never be friend with you again trouble and war in the Netherlands constrain we to seek traffic here also and to undertake this voyage by that mean to put the portugall from it which in the end we do for ware for these part of Guinea and for what use that since the netherlander come hither to traffic with the negro moor the portugall have best trade and be whole decay first we bring they great store of slight linen cloth whereof there be very much spend in those country for they themselves therewith and it be the chief thing they use for that purpose beside this we carry they great store of basin as little basin barber basin basin to drink in platter of copper flat basin great broad copper pan at the least two fathom about and small posnet without edge the small basin they use to put oil in wherewith they anoint themselves and the great sort of they they set in the grave of the dead and use they to carry diverse thing in the barber basin they use to wash themselves in and when they cut their hair platter they use to lay over other to cover they withal to keep dust and filth from fall into their thing the great broad pan be by they use to kill a goat or a hog in and to make it clean therein in stead of a tub. the possenet they use to dress their meat in which serve they to very good purpose they will not have they with steal as we use they here with we and many other such like basin of copper which our ship bring thither in great quantity and therewith fill the country so full and by mean thereof they be sell as good cheap there unto the negro as they be buy in Amsterdam and although there be so many of those basin bring thither and no ware that wear so much as linen yet you see but few old copper thing there and therefore you must think that there be great store of people inhabit further within the land which use so great quantity of such thing we carry thither great store of kettle which they use to fetch water in out of their pit and valley and some red copper pot tin within wherein they use to put water in stead of a barrel of bear to drink earthen pot they use also to drink out of iron be use by they to make their weapon as assagaie cut knife poniard etc. the assagay and poniard they use for the war the cut knife to till and cut up the ground in stead of spade and some to cut wood withal and to use about their building for they have no other tool they also buy great store of red blue yellow and green cloth which they use for girdle about their middle to hang their knife purse poniard and such like thing at they use white spanish serge to wear upon their body instead of cloak ring of copper and brass which they wear about their arm and foot for a great pride they also use tin thing as ring for their arm but not many they use many knife which we make with we in Holland and call they dock messen. they also use great store of Venice bead of all kind of colour but they desire some colour more than other which they break in four or five piece and then grind they upon a stone as our child grind cherry stone and then put they upon string make of bark of tree ten or twelve together and therewith traffic much those ground coral they wear about their neck hand and foot they also use round bead and special great round counter which they hang and plait among their hair and let they hang over their ear pin they use to make fishhook horse tail they use when they dance and also when they sit still to keep the fly from their body look glass and small copper milk Kans with many such like thing but the chief ware that be utter there and most use among they be linen cloth brass and copper thing basin kettle knife and coral at first we use many time to deceive they not only in measure of linen but in deliver their knowledge in our war and trial thereof they break and patch basin and embrace kettle for their money rot cloth through the which they may have sift bean knife that be so rusty that they can hardly without break pull they out of their sheath with such like ware but now by use and experience they have attain to such skill in our ware that they be almost able to surpass we therein for first when they buy any linen cloth they look if it be not to slight and thin and whether it be white and broad for they be very curious to buy white and broad linen and respect not the strength so much as the breadth of the linen for they use to hang it about their body special the woman which desire to have it hang down from underneath their breast to their knee second they take woollen cloth and hold it up against the light to see if it be thin they draw the knife on it of the sheath to see if they be not rusty they look upon the basin one by one to see if they have no hole in they or whether they be break and the least hole that they spy in they they lay they away and desire to have other for they and also if they be but a little foul or greasy they will none of they and for quantity and quality make trial of all other ware as curious as in Europe be do @. 4 what custom the merchant pay to their king their measure weight scale market also their sabbath Fetissos and superstition the king have their custom dwell upon the sea coast where the ship lie to traffic with the country people and they be place there to see that the custom king lose not their rent and impost and that it may be the better pay they and no deceit use they appoint one of their son or some one of their near friend to be present with they those customer receive the custom of the fish which be take in his precinct or before his haven and to that end he have a measure to measure it withal and if the measure be not full of any fish whatsoever than it pay no custom but if their fish be more than fill that measure than he take the five fish thereof or as much as he think good to take for his custom and that be present send to the king of that quarter by his slave which every morning come thither to fetch the fish such merchant as come thither a great way out of the country pay to the king of the haven where they go to traffic the weight of six penny in gold for their passage through his toll country and whether they intend to buy much or little the passage money be all one and when they have traffic with the factor in the ship and come to land the customer take a part of their good from they which be common a four part of that which they have buy and carry it away with he than the merchant take the rest and carry it to his lodging which do he go back again to the customer who they call within Portugal be the watch and agree with he and pay he as little as they can and so have their good again and if they have bestow less than two ounce of gold upon ware than there be no set custom to be pay for it but they give as much as they can agree upon for it with the customer and that be the customer own profit in stead of his wage but whatsoever they buy above the value of two ounce of gold than they must pay a english of gold for custom thereof those two ounce of gold they call Benda also if they have steal any thing from any of their country people they also pay money for it as the case require and also when they have lie with another man wife than the fines king have a forfeit pay unto he for it and when the country people come to market with their weapon they must leave their weapon in some place or else they must pay a forfeit which be six penny weight in gold if they come with any arm or weapon to their sea-towne and they also that counterfeit false gold with diverse other forfeiture which be all pay to the king whereof the customer every three month make his account and pay it unto the king. they make weight of copper of diverse sort and have little copper scale which be weight and scale round and hollow like a orange peel a Benda be their great weight which with we be two ounce benda-affa be half a Benda which be a ounce assuwa be two Pesos and a half Eggeba be two Pesos or half a ounce Seron be a and a half Eusanno be a or a loot be three quarter of a each Peso be a loot be a quarter of a or a small parcel be half a or half a loot each be a loot so that their weight be all one with we for the name but differ in the pound a and a half which be a loot and a half so that their weight be so much light than we they measue their cloth by two fathom together which they cut one from the other and call it and sell their linen in that sort among themselves and those two fathom after measure our measure be a stork and three quarter and they be very subtle in measure of their linen and can reckon that so many of our stork make so many of their fathom they cut their woollen-cloth in piece not above a handful broad which they use in stead of girdle about their middle and sell the cloth in this sort among themselves in this manner and use no other kind of measure thereunto they be not very subtle nor expert in tell special to reckon for when they have pass the number of ten they rehearse so many word one after the other for one number that they be so cumber that they can tell how to get out of it and so sit buzz tell or number so long till at last they have forget their number and be force to begin to tell again but since they begin to deal with the netherlander and be to reckon above the number of ten for they use no more among they they tell till they come to ten and then take one of their finger into their hand and then tell to ten again and then take another finger into their hand and so proceed till they have both their hand full which in all make a hundred than they mark that up and then begin again to tell to ten and use the same order as before every town have market day special appoint upon the which you find more to be market how they be keep no market on their sabbath buy then upon other day and every town have his market upon such a day as the other have it not and so every one differ upon their day and when their market day come they have two day market one after the other wherein the principal boor or country people come from diverse place to traffic with the ship they have their Sunday also but on that day they do nothing in the morning betimes assoon as it be day the country people come with their sugar cane to the market carry two or three bundle together upon their head which be bind up like faggot and be in the market they unbind they and so lay they down upon the ground which do the inhabitant of that place come to buy they some two other three and some more as they have need of they whereby they have soon sell their sugar cane for they use many of they to eat and assoon as they have sell their sugar cane than the woman come to the market with their ware who bring orange lemon Bannanas Backovens ware potato Indianias Rice Manigette hen egg bread and such like necessary which those that dwell on the seaside have need of and be sell both unto the inhabitant and to the netherlander in the ship which come thither to buy it the inhabitant of the seaside come also to the market with their ware which they buy of the netherlander as linen cloth knife ground coral looking-glass pin arm ring and fish which their husband have get in the sea whereof the woman buy much and carry they to other town within the land to get some profit by they so that the fish which be take in the sea be carry at least a hundred or two hundred mile up into the land for a great present although many time it stink like carrion and have a thousand maggot creep in it those woman be very nimble about their business and so earnest therein that they go at least five or six mile every day to the place where they have to do and be lade like ass for at their back they carry their child and on their head they have a heavy burden of fruit or and so go lade to the market and there she buy fish to carry home with she so that oftentimes they come as heavy lade from the market as they go thither these pay no custom to the king but if they find any in the way as they go which be their idolatrous superstition god they give they some of their fruit or to eat which be as much as if they give they the ten part thereof tithe those woman go seven or eight together and as they pass along the way they be very merry and pleasant for common they sing and make a noise about noon the country people begin to come to the market with their palme-wine which they carry in pot some bring one some two pot as they be able they come arm to the market have a hew knife at their girdle and two or three assagaye in their hand but when they enter into the market than they set their arm in a certain place appoint thereunto and when they have sell and go home again every man take his weapon and go his way not once change one with the other but every man take his own and when the netherlander and the negro have do traffick when the country people come to the market with their wine look what the pilot or rower that carry the merchant aboard the ship have get or that be give they for dache by the factor there with they buy palme-wine and drink it up together they pay for their wine either with gold or linen but for the most part they pay for it with gold which they weigh very narrow one unto the other and when there be many merchant and that the wine be much desire than it be oftentimes dear than spanish wine be with we beside this the market folk know every one their place and where to sit to sell their ware as those with fruit stand in one place they with sugar cane in another place they with wood water and bread by themselves and those that sell wine in a place by themselves but the palme-wine which be bring thither by sea from other place that be never bring to the market for many time when it come in the canoe in the evening when the people have need thereof assoon as it be bring on land the negro stand ready upon the shore watch for it and go to the merchant every one take a pot and carry it away so that they have present sell it and the merchant need not fear that he wine will sour for want of utterance for they be so greedy of it special for to drink that oftentimes they fight and fall together by the ear for it they use no money nor any kind of mint wherewith they pay each other but when they buy any thing they pay for it with gold and that by weight and it be a very small parcel that have not some kind of weight to weigh it withal and they pay each other with four square piece of gold weigh a grain or half a grain the cause why they pay in this sort and have this custom be by mean of the portugal of the castle of Myna which show they this way for before the portugal come thither the negro know no such thing but when they buy any thing they exchange ware for ware but the portugal come thither have no money to pay they when they buy first-fruit or other victual to eat a therefore they desire to pay with kacrawen in stead of money and so it be the custom about the castle of Myna that they have great store of kacrawen which they use for payment more than in other place in place where the portugal be not know the negro use not that kind of mint but sell their gold as it come out of the earth for they know not how to melt or use their gold as the negro do that deal with the portugal and in stead of money pay one the other in small stone they use also small piece of iron of a finger length with a half moon thereon which they use in stead of money and have no other kind of money in the golden coast of Guinea than such as I say before wherewith they pay each other although they be altogether wild rough and uncivil have neither scripture nor book nor any notable law that may be set down or declare to show the manner of their policy and live yet when they have pass the six day of the week in labour and pain take to get their living the seven day they leave work and reckon that to be their day of ease and abstinence from work or their Sunday which they call Dio Fetissos which in our fetissos day a ethnic sabbath speech shall signify Sunday but they observe it not upon our Sunday nor upon the jew sabbath day but hold it upon Tuesday the second work day in the week what law or opinion they have to move they thereunto I know not but they hold Tuesday for their Sunday and that day the fisherman go not to the sea for fish the woman and country people that day bring no wine to the market but all the wine which that day they draw out of the tree they deliver it unto the king which in the evening he give unto his gentleman and they drink it among they that day they do no kind of work nor traffic with other but such as dwell on the seaside refrain not for all that to go aboard the ship and to buy ware of the netherlander in their market they have a square place four foot every way support with four pillar and about two cubit high from the ground flat on the top and cover close with reed and hang round about Wispes or Fetissos of straw whereon they lay with fetissos meat palme-oile or water and give their god that to eat and drink to sustain he withal that he shall not die for hunger or thirst think that he eat and drink it and life by it but the bird of the air eat the grain and drink the water and when it be eat they anoint the altar with oil and set more meat and drink upon it think thereby to do their god great sacrifice and service they have also a priest who in their speech they call a Fetissero he upon their sabbath day the Fetissero or priest. sit upon a stool in the middle of the market before the altar or place whereupon they sacrifice unto their Fetisso than all the man woman and child come and sit round about he and there he speak unto they and they sit still to hear he but what it be or what it mean that can I learn nor perceive neither can you get it from they for I have oftentimes ask they his preach about it but they will not tell but be ashamed to declare it but I have see this Fetissero have a pot with a certain drink wherein there be a snake stand by he and a wisp and some woman with their little child go to he which child he stroke with colour or with some of that drink and so they go away which I guess to be a kind of salve against his blessing their Fetisso for they esteem their Fetissos to be both good and evil and when their Fetissero have make a oration unto they than he stand up and smear the altar with his wisp and drink out of his pot and then the people use certain word and make a great noise among they clap their hand together cry 1. i. and therewith their preach be do and so every one go home to his house they hang many straw Wispes upon their head and think thereby to be free and safe as their matin long as they wear they and that their Fetissos can do they no harm in the morning betimes when they have wash their body clean they stroke their face with white stripe make of earth like chalk which they do in honour of their Fetisso and use it in stead of prayer in a morning when they eat any thing they present their Fetisso the straw Wispes which they wear about their leg the first bit and also the first draught that they drink give he to drink which if they do not they think they shall have no good luck that day for they persuade themselves that their Fetisso will not otherwise suffer they to be quiet when the fisherman take but small store of fish than they think that their Fetisso be angry and therefore appease their Fetisso will give they no fish than they make a great cry among they and go to their Fetissero and give he gold to conjure their Fetisso to send they store of fish this conjurer present go and make all his wife two three or four or as many as he have put on their best apparel and ornament and with they go howl and cry round about the town strike themselves upon their breast and clap their hand flat together and so make a great stir and noise go to the seaside and take bough from the tree hang they about their neck those tree they esteem to be their who they think send they fish then the conjurer or he that shall bewitch the Fetissos come with a drum and play or sound before the tree which they esteem to be good for that purpose which do he go to his wife upon the strand and when they have speak one unto the other a good while he cast into the sea for his meat with other colour think that thereby their god be appease and will let they take fish enough when the king receive not custom enough to maintain himself withal than he go to a tree which he esteem to be his Fetisso and sacrifice unto it carry it meat and drink then the conjurer come and conjure the tree to tell they whether there will any merchant come or not which to do they make a heap of ash in form like a sugarloaf and cut consultation with their oracle a bough from the tree stick that in it than they take a basin of water and drink out of it and therewith sprinkle the bough of the tree which do they speak each to other and then again they sprinkle more upon it after that they take some of the ash and bedaub their face therewith end in that manner use many foolish and vain ceremony and not long after they shall hear a voice which be the devil that say something unto they and therewith they go home again and bring word what their Fetisso have say they hang many of those thing about their child for disease as be say before as also of their drink of jealousy cap. 3. cap. 1. when any man die they also make a Fetisso and desire it to bring the body into the oath world and not to trouble it in the way as it go than the next our near kinsman kill a funeral rite hen and dress it ready to be sodden which do they go and sit in a corner of their house and with he take all his Fetissos and place they in order as their great god in the middle and the rest of mean sort by it than he take certain bead some make of shell some of bean and great pease and other of feather mix with button make of bark of tree and hang they upon the after that they take the blood of the dead hen and therewith spinkle their Fetisso for a dead man must offer blood unto his god than he fetch certain herb out of the field and hang they about his neck like a chain in the mean time while the man be in this sort make ready the hen be sodden and be sod then he bring it and put it in a platter set it in the middle of the Fetissos which do he begin to conjure use many word and cast water or wine of palm upon his Fetisso than he take two or three of the green leaf which he have about his neck and roll they between his hand make a little bowl or bale thereof which he take in the two fore-finger of both his hand and thrust it between his leg twice or thrice one after the other say to his Fetisso aucie which be as much as if he shall say all hail after this he wringe the sap out of that ball and let it drop upon his Fetisso which do he lay the ball upon the ground and take two or three leaf more of the herb he have about his neck and roll they in his hand and have make they in a ball thrust they between his leg speak certain word as aforesaid and then let the sap drop upon his Fetisso and this he do until such time as he have roll and wring all the green herb in that sort which he have about his neck then he take all the ball or leaf together in his hand and thereof make a ball as big as a man fist wherewith he wipe his face and that also be a Fetisso which be do the dead body shall rest in peace and therewith he pack up all his trinket and lay they aside until another time that some other body set he a work this kind of superstition they esteem annulet for a great holiness for their body for when they go to war they hang such bead about their neck arm and leg think that their Fetisso will defend they thereby and preserve they from kill and think that they need not fear any thing they esteem the pittoir also for a god for when they go from one town to another and hear it call they be exceed joyful and glad for they say that it be a Fetisso which speak unto they say Fetisso that all those that then travel in the way shall have no hurt nor need fear any danger for he will defend they from all man that seek to molest they and wheresoever they hear it cry there they set for he to eat and pot full of water to drink and dare not pass that place without give it something whereby in some corner of street and in the wood you shall see a number of pot and other meat as etc. which they set there to honour the Fetisso the petoir whereby it appear that they make great account of bird and also of some fish as of the tonny which they by no mean will take but esteem it to be their Fetisso or sea-god they take many sword-fish and cut of the sword they dry they bird and fish god which they also esteem for a great Fetisso other put their trust in some tree and when they desire to know any thing they go to those tree where the devil oftentimes appear in form tree god they kill a Dutchman for cut these tree against their will of a black dog or of such like thing and many time invisible and make answer such thing as they ask he so that if you ask they any thing touch their belief and they give you no answer which make any show of truth than they say that their Fetisso say so and will they to do it for they esteem he for their god and use many foolish toy and vain show when they pray to he and serve he think that it do they good and that they merit much thereby yet it help they not but they rather find themselves deceive and as they deal with the devil and put their trust in he so he reward they and yet they desire not to hear of he but fear he much there be some hill in those country whereon oftentimes it thunder and lighten and thereby many time some fisherman or other moor be cast away or receive some great hil-god hurt which cause they to think that their god be angry and will have some meat and drink or want some other thing and by that mean they hold many hill to be their god and set meat and drink upon they to pacify they withal and they dare not pass along by they without go up and give they something fear that if they do it not they will do they some hurt and make each other believe such thing and whatsoever they believe and once conceive in their head it will never be extirp but have as firm a opinion of their Fetissos as possible may be but when the netherlander see they use such vain toy which be so foolish and laugh and jest at they they be ashamed and dare make no more Fetissos in our presence but be ashamed of their own apishness we ask they of their belief and what opinion they have of diverse thing as first when opinion of the soul depart they die what become of their body and soul they make we answer that the body be dead but they know not what any resurrection at the latter day mean as we do but when they die they know that they go into another world but they know not whither and that therein they differ from brute beast but they can tell you to what place they go whither under the earth or up into heaven but when they die they use to give the dead body something to carry with he whereby it be to be mark that they believe that there be another life after this and that there they have need of such thing as they have here on earth for when they lose any thing or when any of their friend die than they think that those that be dead come and fetch it away and that they have need of it but they know not what the soul nor the resurrection be second ask they of their god they make answer that he be black like themselves of god. and that he be not good but do they much hurt whereunto we say that our god be white as we be that he be good that he do we much good that he descend down upon earth to save we and how he be put to death by the jew for our sake that when we die we go to dwell with he in heaven and that there we neither need meat nor drink whereat they wonder and willing hear we speak of those thing and say that we be God child and that he tell we all thing but yet they murmur say why do not your God tell and give we all thing as well as he do to you and why do he not also give we linen cloth iron basin and other kind of ware whereunto we make answer that our god send we all those thing and yet that he forget not they although they know he not and send they gold palme-wine hen ox goat Bannanas juiamas and other first-fruit to sustain they withal but that they deny or else they can not conceive that such thing come from God but to the contrary say that God give they no gold but that the earth give it they wherein they dig to find it that he give they no nor corn but that they sow it and reap it themselves and that the earth give it they that the tree which they have plant give they their first-fruit and be first bring thither by the portugal that young beast come of the old that the sea give they fish which they take themselves with many other such like thing which they will not acknowledge come from God but from the miserable and ridiculous blindness earth and the sea each accord to their nature but they acknowledge that rain come from our saviour Christ and that by mean of our god they have much gold for that by mean of the rain they find their gold and their fruit and plant grow and wax ripe by mean of the moisture and for that we bring they every thing ready make to their hand therefore they think that we find ^ll such thing and need but go into the field to fetch they as they do their fruit and when it happen that some of our hollander be in their house when it begin fear of thunder to rain blow thunder and lighten whereof they be in great fear go forth through the street not once shun the thunder and lightning neither do it once hurt they they wonder thereat for they be afraid that if they shall come out of their house at that time that it will not be good for they for that many time when it thunder and lighten there it happen that some of they that be travel abroad be carry away by the devil and throw dead upon the ground whereby they be as much afraid thereof as any man possible can be and for that they know that our god dwell above in heaven when it thunder and lighten they point upward and call he juan goemain and once we have a negro aboard our ship who we keep prisoner because he bring false gold and give it out for good which negro every morning take a tub with water in it and wash his face therein which do he take his hand full of water and cast it over his head speak diverse word unto himself and after that spit in the water and use many other apish toy which we see ask he why he do it and he make answer that he pray his Fetisso that it may rain that so his friend may find much gold to release he that he may go home again they circumcise their young child therein follow the mahometical law with circumcision diverse other opinion which they hold thereof as think it evil to spit upon the earth beside many other superstition which they use but affirm that they altogether use those toy and only trust in their Fetissos be a untruth for many of they that can speak Portugal as have deal with they and also daily traffic with we begin to leave those foolish toy and to have some understanding of God word which they do by reason that we mock and jest at their foolish ceremony and for that they say that we be god child therefore they believe much of that which we say unto they and begin to know God but it be without any ground for they ground in their own superstition because they be not otherwise instruct but the negro which dwell among the portugal know much of God and can speak of his some have some smack of Christianity commandment as I have find some among they that can tell of the birth of Christ of the lord supper of his bitter passion and death of his resurrection and diverse other such like point concern our christian faith special one who I know well and that be my good friend for he can write and read Portugal and be indifferent well learned in the scripture and which be more when we speak unto he and argue upon some point against the romish faith or against the religion which the portugal have teach he for he have dwell with a monk in the castle of mina he will dispute the contrary with we and show that it be otherwise set down in such a gospel and in such a epistle of the apostle and that it must so be understand whereby we may perceive that those among they that have any understanding of the christian faith be sharp witted and will soon comprehend any thing but it seem that it have not please God tocall they to the understanding of the christian faith and therefore we be much bind to praise and thank God that it have please he to vouchsafe we the knowledge of his holy word and to understand and know what belong unto our salvation @. v. of their house town country way war arm state of their king judgement law justice theft promise oath and other rite their house be not very curious make but altogether slight much like to a number their house of hog-sty and I be of opinion that in many country there be better hog-sty than their house be I can liken they better to any other thing then to soldier cabin in sconce and bulwark for a man may say that they have take a pattern by they to build they first they take four post or tree which they thrust deep into the ground which stand four square that do they lay other beam or tree upon they and bind they fast together then they take a number of thin small stick and enclose their house round about and those they bind very close together so that you can hardly thrust your hand in between they then they make mortar of a certain kind of yellow earth which they find in the field and that they beat very small and thin so long till it be like unto pot-earth which they take in their hand and daub it upon the small stick round about their house from the foot to the top where they desire to have it close and with their hand thrust it in between the chink of the stick that it may hold fast as if it be between lath and when they have make their house close in this manner which be almost half a foot thick in the wall then they let it stand and d (...) e so hard that it be like unto stone and be well dry than they make a other kind of mortar of red earth which be as thin as water and take a wisp of straw in their hand and therewith wash all their house round about within which serve they in stead of paint whereof they make great account and take a great pride to paint their house in such sort some with white some with red and other with black as best like they for the first thing they show you when you come into the country be their house to cover they they take two four square cover of palm tree leave they tie fast together and so close that they be able to hold out the rain which they lie upon their house for the roof thereof and bind they fast together and when it be fair clear sunshine weather than they open the roof of their house like two wing underprop it with stick and so let the sun shine into their house and when it rain they let they fall down again close together before their house they make a foursquare hole like a door and make a door of reed which they open and shut and bind it too with Withes the floor be flat and very even cover with red earth as if they be pave and in the middle thereof common they make a round hole to set their pot with palm wine in when they drink together in this sort they make two or three house close together which be place four square and in the middle of they there be a place wherein the woman dress their meat in which house they dwell together as the woman in the one the man in the other for they be asunder one from the other and make as many as they have need of and those house they enclose round about with a pale of reed or straw of maize a man height or as high as the wall of their house which be also but a man height so that if it be not for the cover of the house which stand paint-house wise a man can not go upright in their house their house stand altogether in a heap but because they separate they one from the other by those pale of straw by that mean they show like street and be somewhat separate one from the other their street be so little and narrow that but one man alone can go in they and when it rain it be very slippery to go in their town because the earth be so fatty but when the sun shine it dry up again and become as hard as a stone when you will go into one of their house you must go so long through the street till you find a door open wherein be enter you must pass through all the room till you find the place where you will be their house be not very full of household stuff but common they have wooden chest which they buy of the netherlander wherein they lock up their thing so that you see but little of their household stuff abroad king house the king or governor house be common in the market place which be pale alone by themselves and separate from all the rest have no other neighbour dwell by he but only his wife and child for he be common better furnish thereof than the mean sort of man his house be great and high than the rest and have many room which pass one into the other cover over with reed each chamber by itself wherein his man dwell and his watch stay all the day long in the middle of his house he have a four square place all open but cover over for the sun where in the day time he sit with his gentleman that come to speak with he and to pass the time away at the king door there be always two pot set deep into the ground which be full of fresh water and every day be fill with new water which I think be set there for their Fetissos to drink town their town that stand upon the seaside be not very fair but rather filthy place and stink like carrion by reason of the filth which they carry and lay without not far from they and many time when the wind blow from the land you may smell the stink of they above a mile and a half into the sea. the town that lie inward to the land be rich of good and gold than the sea-towne and full of house and man beside that they have more merchant dwell in they for those on the seaside be not so rich nor of so great power as be for the most part interpreter rower pilot servant fisherman and slave to the inhabitant of the town the king keep his court in the near town that stand within the land whereof he be king and place a captain in the sea-towne which be under his command the land-towne be very great but they have no gate wall nor fort nor any strength to resist the force of enemy I have hear some of the negro that dwell within the land say that there be many great town within the land much and far exceed the haven or sea-towne they use to reckon the gold coast to begin from cape to Rio de volta this cape lie under four degree and a half and because it have three point or head which reach into the sea therefore it be call the cape but for that the portugal have a castle there call aziem the negro be not suffer to deal with the hollander eastward five mile low there lie a place call and there the ship common cast forth their anchor for there the negro buy much iron and be very expert to make iron-worke those people traffic much with palme-wine whereof they have great store as of hen goat and diverse fruit jugnamas and Annanasos and when the time come that they draw their wine out of the tree than the canoe come thither with their negro and merchant at the least ten or twenty mile from within the land to buy wine so that it be carry almost all the coast along and great traffic make therewith this wine they esteem very good for their man to drink because it be not so sweet as the wine which be far within the country which be not mix with water as this wine be the other wine they esteem to be good to be drink by their woman because it be not mix but be exceed sweet and soon make the woman merry a mile low lie Rio st. Georgio and a place call jabbe and where the portugal also have a house and because this quarter be very Rio s. Georgio fruitful there dwell three or four portugal there which receive the custom of the fish which be take by the negro in the river and buy great store of other victual which they send continual to the castle of aziem and mina to victual they withal before this river there be a great sand which stretch far into the sea whereby you can enter into it with any ship but only with great canoe and a mile low there lie a village by the negro call agitaky by the portugal Aldea and by the netherlander comando but yet it be not comando although we call it so for comando lie upon the hill where the agitaky comando king dwell they of edom Wassa comando and other town come to this haven to buy their ware there we sell many venetian madrigetten and coral for the common people traffic much therewith by grind and sell they one unto the other small copper basin and blue cloth broad linen be well sell there in this place man sell not any ware in great quantity but all in small parcel and for that there be so many small parcel sell there therefore it be the worst place of all that coast for give of dachio and for that their gold for the most part be melt and cut in small piece therefore there be much deceit therein for they mix much yellow copper among it and many time bring copper in stead of gold and for those two point it be the worst place to deal in throughout all the coast. they have the great number of canoe in all the country beside for many time they go to sea early in the morning with seventy or eighty canoe and enter as far into the sea as you can well discern they and about noonetime they come home again with their fish for there they be very expert in fish it be likewise no less provide of fruit for there be no place in all the land where a man may have great store nor better cheap fruit than there especial a kind of fruit call Bannana and for that cause it be by we call the fruit market when you sail somewhat low and be north north-east from the high hill of comando there be a place call near to that be the castle of mina with a Portugal garrison to prohibit mina cape Crosso trade sail a long mile low you come to a place call cape Crosso this cape or point be a great place of traffic where the french man in time pass use much to lie with their ship and to traffic in the country and in the year 1590. or 1591. there be a ship of deep set upon by they of the castle of mina whereof most of the man be slay and the rest make 1592. slave and when we begin first to traffic there in the year 1592. there be some of our hollander slay in a boat at the same place but now the ship begin to traffic there again because of the great quantity of gold which be bring thither from Abrenbon and Mandinga and other town which lie above two hundred mile within the country sail a mile low you come to the chief place of traffic in all the country call mourre Infantin a mile low there lie a place call Infantin and two mile far there lie a town call Cormantin Cormantin under the king of there the hollander fetch their hoop to bind their water vessel withal for there be the best sail four mile low you come to the high hill of Mango whereon the negro offer sacrifice to the devil but there be no traffic a mile low there be a village call Biamba where they keep good store of cow for it be good Biamba pasture ground the inhabitant use great traffic along the coast by sell their cattle and because that there there be many proper woman diverse of the negro come from other place of the country thither to buy woman and to fetch slave to serve their turn withal the country people thereabouts be good husbandman and sow much Millie press good store of palm wine and bring great number of young cattle up three mile low there lie a place call Berqu the village lie upon a hill there the french man use much to anchor Berqu with their ship those people speak another language and to that place all the people forward speak one language the people be very ingenious to make all kind of thing special of gold for they can make fair chain of gold with other fair thing as ring etc. there they brew a kind of drink call pitouw which be much like small beer they have great store of hen and better cheap then in other place there also they take the green bird call parrot the inhabitant in their time use to buy great store of iron for they have many smith whereby they make fair arm but now there come no more ship thither they go with their canoe to which lie four mile low which be a low land upon the strand have a half tree make in form of a gibbet which they esteem to be their Fetisso the portugall be wont to have a castle there but for some mischief that they have do to the inhabitant the negro take their castle by force slay all the portugall and break down the castle there again they use another language they be a crafty and subtle people and the subtle of all that coast both for traffic and otherwise they have very few canoe to fish or go to sea withal but those they have be very great for I have see one that be cut out of a tree which be five and thirty foot long and five foot broad and three foot high which be as big as a shallop so that it will have hold thirty man at the least they come not often to buy ware but observe certain day in the week to that purpose and then they come with great store of money bring the gold as it be find in the hill two mile below that there lie a place call Neugo a mile low lie Temin and a mile low than that another place call Chinka where the hollander begin to place boat to traffic with the negro which from the year one thousand six hundred be first begin to be know unto we they make war for a small matter for the king be so envious and angry one against the their war and martial custom other and so proud that they can endure their equal whereupon they challenge one the other to the battle and to fight together in the field the king give warning to the town under his command to will the captain with their man to come to he to fight against the enemy their enemy likewise do the like and so make preparation to fight one against the other the king of those town have certain man that be their soldier or slave which be as much as soldier who every day watch in the king house and be as it be his guard they be very proud of their office and in the street they go stately look upon themselves some time strike with their arm over their head and sometime leap backward and forward and round about look fierce as if they will devour all the world they go to the war with the king and if not then they stay continual with he to guard his person and when the time come that they must fight every one prepare himself thereunto in the best manner that he can first they paint their face with colour some red other white and other yellow and also their breast and the whole body with cross strike and snake and many such like thing they also take their bead with they wherewith they make their Fetissos and hang they about they and think when they have they about they that their fetissoe will defend they and that they shall not be slay they make and wreathe a ring of bough of tree as thick as a man arm which they put about their neck to bear off the blow of their knife in stead of gorget on their head they wear cap make of libard or crocodile skin on their body they wear a cloth girdle which they thrust between their leg with a piece of cloth of a handful broad to cover their privity withal for than they wear as few clothes on their back as they can that they may not be cumber therewith when they fight in their girdle they stick a hew knife or a poniard in their left hand bear their shield which be almost as long and as broad as themselves in their right hand they hold their assagay wherewith they fling each at other some of they have two some three four or more as they be able and such as be not Assagay a kind of Dart. able to have shield and assagay they carry Bowos and sheaf of arrow make of skin full of small arrow with iron head at the end wherewith they will shoot most cruel the boy or servant carry the drum into the war whereon they play other have horn of elephant tooth wherewith they blow when all be prepare and every Morinni or gentleman with his man be ready they all meet at the king court and so go with their wife child and all their household together to the war where the battle shall be fight and if it be a war which concern they much and wherewith they be much move and provoke to overcome their enemy than they burn their own house and all their town that their enemy may have no such advantage against they as also because their mind shall not be move to look and harken homeward but rather to give they the better courage to set upon their enemy but if it be a war of no great importance and that will be soon end than they burn not their house nor take not their wife and child with they but they leave their town and send their wife and child to the next place with who they have no enmity which take all their householdstuff with they leave their house empty without any kind of thing in they as if they have whole abandon their town and when their war be end than their wife and child rtturne again to their own town withal their stuff the soldier on both side meet together in the field do the best they can to destroy their enemy both by cast at each other with their assagay and by blow they can cast so exceed straight right and sure with their assagay that they will not fail to hit a stiver or exact skill with dart man-eater piece of money as big as a groat the rest shoot with poison arrow the drum and horn be hear to make a great noise when they fight together and in this war whosoener be take prisoner they make he a slave all his life long and such as be slay their body be dress and eat as good meat their war be not so cruel as they seem nor accord to the noise and preparation by they make and their war continue not long but be soon overpass and end they also burn each other house and town and drive the inhabitant out of they it happen oftentimes that although they have no great controversy with each other they security make peace together promise not to war one against the other and to assure and confirm their promise they believe no word but they send each other a man for a surety who they keep by they and this man who they deliver in this sort for a surety be one of the chief of their town who be bring to the place where he must remain by the king slave he himself be brave dress and sit upon a slave shoulder and in that sort be carry to the king and to he they show much honour and yet they watch he narrow they also buy many piece and begin to learn to shoot in they and have the understanding to know that a long piece carry further than a short which both the portugal and we also teach they they be very expert in make of arm for they make poniard of a ell long without hilt and four finger broad with two edge the handle be of wood with a pummel at the end they cover the handle over with a plate of gold or with the skin of a certain kind of fish which they take which with they be esteem as much as gold be with we they make sheathe of dog or goat skin and above at the end of the sheathe in stead of a chape they put a great red shell as broad as a man hand which be in great estimation with they other that have not the ability to buy such shell make or buy hew knife in fashion like a gammon of Bacon broad at the end and narrow before which cut but on the one side and in stead of a red shell they trim they with a ape or a tiger head and those they stick in their girdle on the one side and wear they as they go along in the street and carry their assagay in their hand and if they have a servant or a slave they make he bear their assagay and shield before they and they follow they with a staff in their hand the merchant travel in the country with their arm and their servant or slave likewise carry arm with they who common have Bowes and arrow because they be weapon which be least cumbersome to be carry for they can carry they about their neck their arm their assagay be make of diverse fashion and of many sort but for the most part of iron at least two foot at both end and that part which they hold in their hand be of wood both the end be as heavy of iron one as the other because they shall weigh a even weight and for that one shall not be heavy than the other for if it shall they can not strike nor cast right with they they be very curious of their arm for they will always have six or seven of those assagay in their house which stand in the ground one by the other with their shield hang by they those shield they make of wooden hoop which they fold one within the other and so make they four square but somewhat bow like a buckler and they be common six foot long and four foot broad in the middle they make a cross of wood and bind it upon the rest of the hoop to hold they the fast together thereof also they make their handle whereon they bear their shield some of they of the better sort cover their shield over with a oxhide and put a plate of iron upon it two foot long and a foot broad they make great account of their shield think that under they they have a great safeguard for their body they make their bow of very hard wood the string be make of the bark of tree their arrow be of thin and tough wood the feather be make of the hair of a dog skin wherewith they cover almost half their arrow and on the end they put small iron head which head when they go to war one against the other they anoint with poison which be the juice of certain green herb but they must not carry such poison arrow but in time of war and that upon pain of a great forfeit or some other punishment to be inflict upon they that bear such arrow about they their sheaf they make of goat skin which they hang about their neck and put their arrow into it their drum be make of hollow tree which be cover over with buck skin with wooden pin and strike upon they with wooden stick make like spoon or ladel those drum common lie before the king captain and guard house and be sometime twenty foot long whereon they play when the king make a feast they also make small drum of hollow tree which they hang about their neck and go about the town play on they those drum be round above and under very narrow like a funnel no man may use they but gentleman they make horn of elephant tooth and race they fine with many stick in they and in the middle of the horn they make a small hole which be four square and blow at that but no man may use they but only the king or the captain they choose their king by the most voice and consent of the common people for their choice of the king. kingdom be not successive to any of their child or kinsman but when their king be dead they choose another to govern they and to possess the kingdom and he dwell in the decease king court and possess all that he find therein at his first entry into the kingdom he must buy good store of cow and palme-wine and bestow a banquet upon his subject for they make great account of a king that be liberal and fea they but if their king be covetous and seek to heap up good store of gold they hate he seek all the mean they can to find some cause to drive he out of his kingdom and to choose a better accord to their mind as it happen in my time to the king of Sabae who have be king of Infantin and be make king of Sabae who they drive out of his kingdom and take all his good from he make he go to Infantin again from whence he come and choose another in his place that please they better and for that cause the king that will be well belove of his subject every three month when his guard or customer come to pay he that which they have receive at the seaside and of the country people for custom he must make a banquet and spend more than he receive at that time and then he bid his Morrinnis which be as much to say as a gentleman or one of his counsel and buy many cow or ox and also all the palme-wine in the country that he can get which be give by he to the common the king feast people who at that time be very merry and joyful sing and play upon their drum the head of the cow be make clean and fair paint and hang full of fetissoe which do they be hang very orderly in the king the amber one under the other instead of picture and for a great honour unto the king whereby such stranger as come to the king court may perceive that he be a good king and for that cause be much esteem and belove of his people beside this they hold another feast day every year as be the day of their coronation or their fetissoe day than the king invite his neighbour king and captain with all his gentleman to a banquet and make a great feast and that day he pray to his Fetisso and he himself sacrifice unto he which he do but once a year this Fetisso be the high tree in the town which be the king upon this festival day they use many apish toy as fence drum sing and leap the woman also be very merry and dance and every king hold his feast day apart and they do it one soon after the other which they do in their summer time on their Sunday at night the king make a feast and buy up all the palme-wine which be draw out of the tree that day and bid his wife and child to supper and his chief gentleman at which time they be very merry for he eat but one day in a week with his wife and child and that be upon their Sunday these woman be very serviceable to the king their husband and every one of they fea he to win his love so that he his wive^ want no service at their hand every one of his wife have his good and riches apart by herself and keep and feed she own child and she that be in favour with the king want nothing when the king wife go abroad they lean upon the shoulder of other woman that serve they and be their slave and their child be also carry upon the shoulder of other of the king slave he himself come little abroad but stay always in his house sometime he sit at his door but not often his house be watch both day and night by his slave which watch arm in his court and in his chamber and when he go out they attend on he and his guard. go round about he in the morning betimes and late in the evening his slaune blow those horn of elephant tooth which make a pretty sound for they have the slight to draw their breath in and out as they listen and can answer one the other when they blow when the king come out of his chamber his wife stand ready to attend on he to wash his body all over and then to anoint it with palme-oile after that he eat somewhat and so set himself down upon a stool and in his hand he hold a horse or a elephant tail to keep the fly from his naked body he be brave dress after this manner his beard be knot with golden coral and other costly thing on his arm and leg he have ring of gold and other fair bead of coral and the like also about his neck and so he sit all the day talk with one or other for he want no company to pass the time away they have one attend on they who they call uiador which word they have learn of the portugal he be the his viador or treasurer king treasurer and keep his gold and other riches receive and pay all and do all other business for the king. this man be next unto the king and he common have more golden ring about his neck arm and foot than the king himself when the king child be of some year if they will have any thing they must look to get it for the king may give they nothing to live idle upon for the common people will murmurre at it if the king shall give somewhat unto they he may do wrong to his gentleman but he give they his child their patrimonial good when they marry as their custom be and beside that he give they every one a slave to serve their turn with all and they have nothing else of their father whereby it fall out that when they wax old and seek not to do any thing they be no more respect than another man be the king keep they with he to serve he and when he make peace with any other town or king than he implore his child and send his son for hostage that they may begin to be honour and thereby attain to great estate the revenue of the fruit fish wine and palme-oile which the king have be sufficient to maintain the king and his wife and child his Millie whereof he make bread be sow and reap for he at other man charge whereby he have a good life but yet miserable in respect of we when the king die he be honourable bury after their manner and then present they choose another one that be not of the last king kindred but they choose a strange man who they think good and by no mean they will choose any that in any point hold with or favour the last king. have make he king they bring he to the palace and he take the government upon he and have all the treasure and good of the dead king which he get during the time of his reign and that he hold so that the dead king child enjoy not a penny but that which he have when he be choose king that they take and part among they as their custom be they use no counsellor nor attorneye but every man must tell his own tale to the judge who send for the accuse party after who answer the plaintiff speak again and in lawyer this sort they be each of they hear to speak four or five time and when the one speak the other must hold his peace till he have do for they must not interrupt one the other when they speak upon pain of corporal punishment so that although they be wild man and without any civility or good behaviour yet therein they use a very good and laudable custom when the judge have hear they say what they can accord to his own mind he give judgement which they must stand unto without appeal if it be any thing concern the king whereby he be to have any forfeiture or otherwise the judge receive it and demand it of he that be to pay it in the king name which he must pay present without delay and if he be not able to do it he must present depart from thence to another town or some other king jurisdiction and there stay till he have content his king and pay his fine if it be a controversy which be to be determine among they and they can agree thereon than they will seek to kill each other or challenge their adverse party to fight with they appoint a day and place when they will meet with their arm to end or determine their controversy combat in themeane time they make their cause know to some of their friend and desire their help for each of they may have three or four man to help they and common they be of their near friend and kindred and when their appoint day be come each of they go with his companion to the same place and when they meet together with their shield and assagay to defend themselves withal they place themselves orderly in the field one right over against the other the plaintiff and the defendant stand in the middle and so begin to cast and shoot at each other with their assagay and shoot in that sort so long until that some of they on both side be hurt and fall to the ground then they cease their fight and so their quarrel end but his side on who the dead man be find to be slay or that have lose the victory come to the other party and desire to have the man out of their company that be the cause of that combat in stead of the dead man that be slay and if he run away and get to another town they will follow he and will never leave before they have get he into their hand and none of their king may give such a man freedom nor keep he secret in his town but if he can find he in his town he must deliver he to those that seek after he and if he do it not than they make complaint to their king and so many time one king make war upon another for that cause when they have find he he be deliver to the wife the dead man and she keep he for her slave or else she sell he to another but if he have any mean to pacify the woman or the friend of that man and to redeem himself out of bondage he may do it and go free abroad they be very great controversy that be end in this manner for they be no common man that end their quarrel in such sort the plaintiff certify the captain who cause a drum to be sound by one of his slave and he go round about the town with the drum about his neck and with he there go their law and execution of justice. two boy more each with a cow-bell in their hand without clapper and they strike upon they with stick make of wood and when they have go in this sort round about the town which be a sign unto the people that justice be to be execute then the captain with his gentleman come and sit round together in the marketplace each man with his arm wherewith all the people assemble together know not what the matter be and go to the marketplace where their common assembly be make the woman stand in one place the man in another to hear what the captain will say and he that be accuse be present take and keep prisoner in the captain house and if it be a weighty matter he be bind if otherwise he be only keep by the executioner and he must not depart from thence before his cause be try in the mean time the captain with his gentleman sit still in the marketplace to hear the complaint make against the prisoner and send he word by his slave what accusation be lay against he whereunto he must present without delay make answer otherwise if he can excuse himself he must pay the penalty which he have incur and if he can pay it he must in the king behalf be sell as a slave towards the payment of his fine and ever after while he live he must be a slave but if he have do any offence that deserve death he may redeem his life with money if he can agree with the king and content he which money be divide among the Morinni which have the one half and the king the other half without give any to the friend of the dead man and if it be one that have incur the danger of pay a fine for lie with another man wife be accuse to have win she thereunto by false promise or by force and have not keep his promise with she then the king first take all his good from he as forfeit unto he and the woman must pay two or three ounce of gold for a fine unto her husband or as he favour she and she can agree with he otherwise he may put she away and take another wife and the woman friend go and burn or pull down the man house that have do the fact and do he all the mischief they can to make he to leave the town that they may hear no more of he in my time while I lie there it happen that a man come from one town to another to gather up his debt which man a year before have lie with another man wife and the same woman be then by chance come to the same market and see he go straight and complain to the Aene which be the captain who present cause he to be take and their counsel be assemble there before they the woman complain that he have force she and have not pay she accord to his promise he make answer that he do it with her goodwill and although neither of they both be of that town yet their cause be hear and as good justice use towards they as if they have be inhabitant of that place and after long disputation by they make the Fetissero which be the priest that coniur their Fetissos or god come thither with a certain drink in a pot and set it down before the captain the woman take the pot and drink thereof to justify that he have not content she for the loss of her honour and if he will have drink thereof before the woman drink to justify that he have pay she and owe she nothing than he have be quit from pay any thing but know himself to be guilty he dare not drink but be find guilty and be judge to pay a fine of three bendaes which be six ounce of gold this drink among they be as much as a oath and be call Enchionkenou which they Enchionkenou make of the same green herb whereof they make their Fetissos and as they say it have such a force that if a man drink it false their Fetisso cause he present to die but if they drink it innocent than their Fetisso suffer they to live by reason of the great hatred and envy which they bear one unto the other they accuse each other although it be for a thing that have be do ten year before so that there be no quarrel but it be call in question and if a man have marry or buy the sister of that man that be to pay a fine unto the king and be not able to do it than his sister husband must join with he to do it and help he to pay his fine so they dwell both under one jurisdiction and for that they must agree together for before all thing the king must be pay his fine by one mean or other or else they must go out of his country and dwell in another place and so if he be not able to pay his fine than he take all his wife and child and go to another town and which be more all the friend they have dwell in that town must also go with he and dwell all in that place until they have agree with and pay the king his fine and when they come again than they go to all their acquaintance and ask they forgiveness and seek and make peace and friendship with they as they have before the man go to his friend and the woman to she the cause why their friend also depart and leave the town be because they shall not be molest nor trouble by the king for the same the fine which they pay for theft be six ounce of gold or three bendaes of their weight for in that country they be not put to death for it but if they steal any thing from the netherlander they pay no fine but only when they steal one from another if any man have falsify gold and carry it to the netherlander and that they complain thereof unto the king he must pay a fine for it as the case require if much gold be falsify many time they be sell for slave and all these fine be the king to maintain his expense if it be a case wherein any man have deserve death and that he can pay the king but with his life than he be judge to die and without any more delay the executioner or he that be appoint to do it take he and bind his hand behind he and then cover his eye lead he into a field or a wood or where he think best have no place purposely appoint to do it in and be there make he kneel down and stoop with his head and take a assagaie step back and strike he into the body wherewith he fall down than he take his cut knife and cut off his head and then he be dead for they believe not that a man be dead before his head be cut off and therefore when they put any man to death they cut off his head which do he cut his body in four quarter and cast they into the field to be devour by beast and bird but their friend come and fetch the head and keep it for a great present seethe it in a kettle and then eat the broth thereof which do they take the bare scull and hang it by their Fetisso the woman at that time make a great noise with cry and howl and take the quarter and carry they into the field when the execution be do there be no officer by but only the executioner and the party that be to be execute but when it be do than they come about he and lament the dead man as aforesaid for steal I be of opinion that of all the nation in the world they have not their master they esteem it a shame to steal one from another but when they have steal any thing lacedaemonian thief from the netherlander they esteem it to be a credit unto they and brag thereof for they esteem we to be crafty and subtle man and when they have steal any thing from we they think themselves to be the subtle and crafty and seek to be honour for do so brave a action lead that be nail without upon the ship to keep they from be eat by worm rusty nail grease weight which they hide in their hair mouth or ear any other small matter be exercise of their theft yea although they be never so great merchant and lacedaemonian bestow two or three pound of gold with you for merchandise and have no need to steal but if any thing be take from they they make so many word and such a noise as if it be a matter worthy of death they say that they may steal and we not I ask they the cause why they make answer that we be rich and have great store of ware and bring ship full unto they and take great pain and labour to sell it and be so long before we sell it that they think it fit to help we therein that we may the soon be rid thereof that we may fetch other and that we be clothe and they go naked and have nothing upon their body and that therefore it be free for they then for we to steal when they have take any thing and that you miss it you must present search they all for they steal very cunning and give it one unto the other and when they come together they part it among they when you have find it and know who steal it than you must beat he well be he never so great a merchant and the rest of the negro will laugh at he and mock he because he do his business no better but when they perceive that their theft be discover than they leap overboard and get away fear to be beat and if you let they go and beat they not at that time when you take they than they fear a great matter and expect more blow and that you will entrap they and therefore they will common ever after shun that ship and go aboard another but if you beat they for their labour when they do it they will not hate you for it nor shun the ship but will come the next day again to deal and traffic with you in their promise or oath which they make unto we they be unconstant and full of untruth promise but such promise as they make among themselves they keep and observe they well and will not break they when they make any oath or promise special when they will show it to our netherlander first they wipe their face upon the sole of your foot and oath then do the like upon their shoulder and breast and upon all their body speak thrice each to other say jau jau jau every time clap hand together and stamp with their foot upon the ground which do they kiss their Fetisso which they have upon their leg and arm some for the more assurance of their promise and oath will drink certain drink as I have say before but he that shall repose much trust therein shall soon find himself deceive because they be not to be credit further than you see they @. 5 of their summer and winter and of their manner of till and sow the land their corn rents raines beast and hunt fowl tree and fruit although it be always warm in those country yet they have a difference in the time of the year and so they account some month for their summer and some for their winter the difference which they have therein be the weather for both barren summer and fertile winter in summer and winter the tree be green and some of they have leaf twice a year in summer their field be bare and in winter they be full of corn and be very green so that they have their harvest in winter the day and night be of one length or else there be little difference for the sun rise and go down there common at six of the clock but it be rise at least half a hour above the horizon before it show itself so that you shall seldom see it clear rise
