and go down the fruit be there as plentiful and abundant in winter as in summer when the weather be warm and that the sun be above their head they esteem that time to be their winter which begin in the month of April May and june because as then it rain and be very foul weather there with thunder mist and lightning which the portugal call travado and they Agombretou which foul weather and rain follow the sun and rise up with his height at that time they be most cumber with rain but in their summer they be not so much trouble with it but then the earth dry and be hard and unfruitful and therefore they shun that time to sow their Millie and maize in but when that time be go to begin their husbandry they go into the wood or field and there seek out a good place which they think fit for their purpose to sow their corn in to serve to maintain their wife and child their husbandry no man have any land to himself which he can or may keep to his own use for the king have all the wood field and land in his hand so that they may neither sow nor plant therein but by his consent and licence which when they have obtain and have a place permit they to sow their corn in than they go with their slave and burn the wood tree root and shrub with all the rubbish down to the ground then they go with their long chopping-knive which they call Coddon and scrape and raze up the ground with Colen and all that serve they to fatten their ground about a foot deep and let it lie eight or ten day and when all of they have till their ground every man make ready his seed to sow it withal upon their Sunday and then they go to their king or governor house of that quarter for first they help to till his ground and to sow his corn and go all together to his field and take all the rubbish out of the earth and cast it into the middle of the field and then once again ^ake the earth and sow their corn in the field they begin upon a Sunday and first serve their governor or king and when they have do his work the captain send into the field a great number of pot with palme-wine and a sod goat with good store of other meat accord to the number of workman and there they sit down together and make good cheer and at that time they burn the root and sit and sing and make a great noise about they all in the honour of their Fettsso to the end that he shall let their corn grow well and prosperous up when their captain or king land be till and sow the next day they go to another man ground and do with it as they do with the king ground and there also make good cheer as they do before and be merry together and so forthwith the rest who they help the corn soon grow up and lie not long in the ground when it be as high as a man head and begin to sprout than they make a wooden house in the middle of the field cover over with reed and therein put their child to watch the corn and to drive away the bird wherewith they be much cumber they weed not their corn but let it grow up weed and all the Millie have long ear and be a seed of colour like hempseed and long like canarieseed Mille^ it have no shell but grow in a little husk and be very white within this kind of grain they always have and serve their turn therewith before the portugal come thither it grow and be ripe in three month and when it be cut down it lie a month after in the field to dry and then the ear be cut off and bind in shease and so carry home to their house they use the straw to cover their house withal this Millie be a very excellent grain have a good taste and be wholesome to eat it be sweet in your mouth but gnash in your tooth which come of the stone wherewith they grind it when they have use the land and their harvest do than they sell part of their corn to other man which be no^^able to ^ow it and by that mean get a good quantity of gold they give some to their king for the rent of his land and carry it home to his house every one as much as he think good for there be no certain sum appoint for they to pay but every one give accord to his ability and the quantity of ground that he have use and bring it unto the king so that he have at least five or six Bendas of gold of they at one time which they carry altogether to their king who welcome they and thank they for their dache or gift and for their labour give they their belly full of meat and drink and that they pay to the king for the farm of his land and no more the corn by the Indian call maize by the portugal or spaniard indian-wheat and by the their mai^ italian turkish-corne be a grain almost know throughout all the world and be bring out of west India into saint Thomas island and they of saint Thomas after they have build their castle bring it thither for to serve their necessity withal and sow it there for before the portugal come into those country the Indian know it not but they sow it first in that country and disperse it abroad among the wild Indian so that now the country be full thereof and at this present there be great abundance in Guinea they use to mix it with their Millie and sometime take half Millie and half maize the negro that dwell among the portugal grind it alone without any Millie and make excellent bread thereof where with they sustain themselves and sell it to the portugal they know how to bake it in such sort that it will endure good three or four month the child also eat it in stead of bread which they set awhile upon the fire and then crush the corn out of the husk such as eat much thereof and be not use unto it use to be scurvy and itchy or else to be trouble with great blood vein for it increase blood it be no less nourish then corn in the Netherlands and in a manner taste like our corne. the people of the west Indies can make wine of maize which they call wherewith they will make themselves drink as if it be of wine make of grape and for that they know that corn sodden or steep in water make a kind of drink wherewith a man may make himself drink therefore they lay this kind of grain to soak in the water till it be soft and then they brew thereof as some of the negro in Guinea which deal with the portugal also do and call it poitou this maize will grow in a moist fatty and hot ground and bear twice a year it be not sow like other corn but it be thrust into the ground as we use to do bean in our country it lie not long in the ground but soon spring up and grow high than a man length above the ground like to great reed that grow in the water or in drown land wherewith husbandman use to cover their shade every reed have his ear whereon the corn grow and notwithstanding that they be heavy ear as big as young cucumber and sharp above like the top of a steeple yet every reed have seven or eight ear upon it I have tell five hundred and fifty grain upon one reed which come of one grain alone they be of diverse colour as white black yellow purple etc. and sometime you shall have three or four colour thereof in one ear there be two sort thereof great and small the great grain be strong than the small they use the reed to cover their house they shun the rain and esteem it to be very ill and unwholesome to fall upon their naked rain hurtful body which they do not without great reason for we find ourselves to be much trouble therewith when we travel special when it rain much and make great Travado^ as it do once a year in those country which be in April May and june at which time there tempest be such tempest of thunder lightning wind and rain that it be incredible special the rain under the equinoctial line be so unwholesome and rot that if a man have be in the rain and be through wet and so lie down to sleep in his cabin in his wet clothes without put they off he be in danger to get some sickness for it breed fever and again if you dry not your wet clothes present in the sun but forget they chance to let they lie they will rot with the force of the water in such sort that you may pluck they in piece with your finger and they find no less unwholesomenesse therein for when it begin to rain they get they out of the way and if any drop of water fall upon their naked body they shiver and shake as if they have a fever and cast their arm over their shoulder to keep the rain from they which they do not because the water be cold for often time it be as warm as if it be sod but because of the unwholesomenesse for their body which they find thereby and when they have tread in the day time in the water with their foot at night they make a fire and lie with their sole of their foot against it which they do to draw the moisture of the water which be get into their body out again at their foot then they anoint their body with palm oil which they use also for a beautify to make their body shine and that they do to shun the rain water within those country as many palm oil man write be very unwholesome and thereof many and dangerous disease be engender they have elephant leopard tiger cat of the mountain monkey fox heart and I have omit the fish and fish their beast etc. great snake hind it be say that in this country there be white elephant but I can never understand it from the negro themselves there be the great and most venomous snake that ever be see there be one in my time take there as the negro tell i which be thirty foot long and as much as six man can carry there be also a beast like a crocodile but it never go into the water as the crocodile do which be call Languad there be spider as big as the palm of a man hand and great store of they chameleon and spider agtissen a great number but they esteem not they to be venomous for they dry many of they and eat they there be many dog and cat such as we have but their dog have sharp snout than we and their chap full of wool they can bark nor make a noise they be very fair beast for colour as black red white and yellow spaniel etc. they be also a little small foot dog than we so that they be not much unlike the dog in our country but they be unlike to we in one thing for when you strike they they run away and make no noise nor once offer to bite you but when you run away from they and be afraid of they they will leap at you and bite you by the leg those dog they use for their necessity and eat they and in many place of the country they be bring and drive to the market like sheep or hog be tie one to the other with string they be call Ekia or which be a wild sheep it be the first gift which a man of that country give when he buy his gentility they make much of our dog in these country for when they bark they think they speak and for that cause esteem great of they cat also be there much esteem because they take mouse wherewith the of the town be much trouble they be call Ambaio they have very fair skin and Ca^^^ be very good mouser they use also to eat they they be first carry hither out of Europe if they know where any elephant be they use all the mean they can to take they for they eat they also although they shall stink like a carrion and that a thousand maggot elephant creep out of they where they know that they use often time to come they make great pit which they cover over with straw and foul leaf of tree which the elephant know nothing of go that way as he be wont to do and fall into the pit and can get out again the negro hear that he be fall into the pit run thither with their weapon and smite he into the body with assagay and so kill he which do they leap into the pit and cut he in quarter and every one may go and fetch his part thereof when he will of the hide they make stool to sit on the tail be give to the king to beat the fly from his naked body and be much esteem off there with no less subtlety they take the leopard for they leopard do they more hurt than other beast and because it be a cruel beast to spoil and destroy man keep in the way where man shall pass along in every four corner way or at the end of the street they make house with wooden pale which be like to rat trap wherein they put hen sheep and other thing which he desire to eat where the leopard come to eat his prey be take with the fall of the trap and kill with a assagaie they esteem much of the skin whereof they use to cut girdle and to make cap there be no horse in that country and when there be some bring unto they for a great present they kill they and eat they because their flesh seem sweet unto they the ox and cow that be find in that country be not very great but of bigness like oxen. great calf their horn stand backward on their head they be not milk for they give none they can hardly bring up their young calf by reason of the small moisture that the cow give their calf by mean of the dry country wherein they be and by reason of the heat of the land the hen and goat which with they be sheep that they have there be bring they thither by the portugall of s. Thomas the hen prosper and increase well there and be so hen fat with the Millie that grow there as if they be capon but they be common small than we the egg which they lay be no great than pigeon egg the dove which dove they have there be also bring they thither by the portugal and be call Abranama which be as much to say as bird bring thither unto they by white man they be very like to our pigeon but their head be less like sea-mewes there be no great store off they in the country the hog also be bring they by the portugal and be call Ebbio they be very little hog but very sweet and pleasant to eat but not so good as the hog in Mosambique where the hog flesh be as dainty as hen flesh and because it be a very unwholesome place they give their sick man hog flesh to eat in stead of hen flesh they have also not long since get some goose out of a ship of Holland which they call Apatta which be there much esteem off because they be but few the country be full of monkey of diverse form for some of they have white beard and monkey black moustache with speckle skin their belly white and upon their back they have a broad tawny stroke with black paw and a black tail and by we be call board-man there be some call white nose because no part of they be white but only their nose there be a three sort call Boertkens those shun man very much and stink filthy by nature they be very crafty the four be very like to the jacken which be find in the grain coast there be also many monkey of diverse other fashion they take the ape and monkey with springe how take which hang upon the tree where into the ape and monkey leap and be take by the negro musk cat be there in great abundance the portugal call they Cato which be Agalia cat the negro call they Kankan those kind of cat be also find in east India and in java but they be not so good as those in Guinea or of the golden coast they be there call castory those cat be much esteem of by the portugal whereby they reap great profit special by their Agaly or musk which they take from they and make they clean and then musk-cat it be put into glass and carry into Lisbon it be a kind of beast much give to bite and to eat flesh because they give they flesh as hen pigeon goat and other costly meat to eat they ease themselves in a place apart and leave it and never lie in it it be almost like a fox but their tail be like other cat their skin be speckle like a leopard skin the negro take many of they in the wood when they be young and so bring they up but because they have no skill there how to use they they sell they to stranger the male cat be the best and yield the most Agalia by reason that the female piss in the cod wherein the musk grow and piss it out with their water when you perceive that they tear their bag you must take their Agalia from they for they do it to be rid of it the wild and worse they be to rule so much the costly and better their Agalia be there be hare also in this country special in a place call in form like we and hare because that country be low sandy ground therefore they be find more there then in any other part of that coast when the negro will take they they go a great number of they together to the place where the hare be every one take with he two or three cudgel of wood as long as a man arm and there they compass the field round about and stand about their hole make such a noise and cry and clap their stick one upon the other that the hare be so fear therewith that they leap out of their hole and be by they kill with those cudgel which they cast at they and by that mean get many of they heart and heart hind be sometime find there also but in some place more than other they be of the same fashion that we be in the low-countreye but they have another kind of horn than we they have no express kind of instrument to take they withal but when they see they go to the water to drink they strike they into the body with a assagaie and kill they hunt to take wild beast be lawful for any man to use in those country if they can take they without punishment for do it there be many other kind of beast of such several sort that a man can tell what to make they but for that the netherlander that use to Guinea dare not go far into the country to take wild beast lest they shall be take and entrap by the portugal or their adherent and make slave all their life long therefore there be many wild beast that be not know by we and which the inhabitant themselves know not nor can not tell by what name to call they the bird that be find there be of diverse sort and be little bird like unto we first there be blue parrot whereof there be great store which be young be take out of their parrot nest and make tame have not fly abroad they be better to teach and to learn to speak but they will not prate so much as the green Brasilian parrot do they have also a other kind of green bird as big as sparrow like the Catalinkins of west India but they can speak those bird be call asuront and by our netherlander call Parokites they be Parokites take with net as you use to take sparrow they keep much in low land where much corn or Millie grow for they eat much thereof those bird be very kind one to the other for when you put a male and a female in a cage they will always sit together without make any noise the female be of such a nature that when she be couple with the male she respect he much and let he sit on the right hand set herself on the left hand and when he go to eat she follow he and so they live together quiet be almost of the nature of the turtle-dove they be of a very fair green colour with a spot of orangetownie upon their nose there be another kind of Parokitan which be much like they be of the same nature and condition but be of colour as red as blood with a spot of black upon their nose and a black tail be somewhat great than the parokite there be other bird not much unlike to goldfinch all their body be yellow those bird make not their nest in the field for fear of snake and other venomous beast but make their nest very crafty upon the branch of high tree and there lie their egg to keep themselves from venomous beast they have other small bird not much unlike to hedge sparrow but they keep in the field among corn those bird they thrust into their mouth alive and eat they feather bone and all they have store of Muschen with many other kind of small bird the have a kind of bird like eagle which have head like turkle-cock those bird be hurtful and very fierce and do much harm to the negro whereby they be much trouble fierce bird and therefore they carry they meat up to the hill and call they Pastro de Diago which be the bird of their god and therefore they do they no hurt know well that they will revenge themselves well enough they lie always in mire and dirt and stink as ill as a prime and you may smell they afar off they have some water snite but not many and turtle-dove which have a black stroke about their neck like a crown there be many pheasant not much unlike we for fashion but have not such feather for they be speckle black and white and without long tail as we have they be not of so good a taste as other common hen be peake-cocke also I have soon there not much unlike our peake-cocke but there peacock be some difference in the feather for some of they be of other colour Pittoirs I have see there as I say before which they esteem for a great Fetisso and a soothsayer crane also there be many and kite also of the same fashion that our Holland kite be there be a kind of bird also there which be like stork but they have not so long red bill and make not such a noise speckle crow and gray sea-mewes be there in great abundance with diverse other kind specled crow of bird not much unlike we but if you mark they well there be difference between they as some in their feather other in their bill the three in their foot and the four in their head so that there be some difference although they resemble much and because bird be little take and shoot in those country for that they have no kind of instrument to do it withal there be great store in the country and by that mean both the beast and the bird wax very bold there be many owl and bat which fly by night and store of great green frog burn fly and gray grasshopper and many great land crab which keep in the earth and be of a purple colour which they esteem for a great present when I go by night to walk in the field I see thing in the grass that shine like fiery coal which I take up and tie they in my handkerchief which make it show with the light of the beast as if it have burn and when I go into the town to the negro and show it they they wonder thereat and the next day when I look on they they be small black fly like spanish fly but be as black as pitch fly moth and bee be there also to be see the bee make their hive upon tree there be great store of black ant which make hole in the earth like field mice those ant do much hurt to the bee and eat up there honey and wax Bannana in Brasilia Pacona and the tree paguover in malabar patan etc. be the fruit bannanas or indian fig whereof John write and call it indian fig this tree have no branch the fruit grow out of the tree and have leaf at least a fathom long and three span broad those leaf among the turk be use for paper and in other place the house be cover therewith there be no wood upon the tree the outside wherewith the tree be cover when it begin to wax old be like the middle part of a sieve but open it within there be nothing but the leaf which be roll up round and close together it be as high as a man on the top the leaf begin to spring out and rise up a end and as the young leaf come forth the old wither away and begin to dry until the tree come to his growth and the fruit to perfection the leaf in the middle have a very thick vein which divide it in two and in the middle of the leaf out of the heart of the tree there grow a flower as big as a ostrich egg of a russet colour which in time wax long like the stalk of a colewoort whereon the fig grow close one by the other when they be still in their husk they be not much unlike great bean and so grow more and more until they be a span long and four thumb broad like a cucumber they be cut off before they be ripe and be in that sort hang up in bunch which oftentimes be as much as a man can carry it also yield good Trennuelis like milk when the tree be cut down which come out of the body thereof have hang three or four day they be through ripe the tree bear but one bunch at a time whereon there be at least one hundred fig and more and when they cut off the bunch of fig the tree also be cut down to the ground the root stay still in the earth which present spring up again and within a month have his full growth and all the year long no time except the tree bear fruit the fruit be very delicate to eat you must pull off the husk wherein the fruit lie very delightful to behold the colour thereof be whitish and somewhat yellow when you bite it it be soft as if it be meal and butter mix together it be mellow in bite it cool the maw much thereof eat make a man very loose and raw in the throat it make woman lecherous if they eat much thereof some be of opinion because it be so delicate a fruit that it be the same tree that stand in paradise whereof God forbid Adam and Eve to eat it smell like rose and have a very good smell but the taste be better the portugal will not cut it through with a knife but break it by reason of a special observation which they have in the cut thereof which be that then it show like a cross in the middle of the fruit and therefore they think it not good to cut it the Bachovens by we so call be very like the Bannanas for the condition and form be Bachovens or Bannanas congo all one only that the fruit be small short white of colour within and sweet of taste and be esteem to be wholesome to be eat then the Bannanas but there be no such great quantity of they and for that they be first bring out of the kingdom of congo into other country they have get the name thereof the Annanas be also a delicate and pleasant fruit for smell and of the best taste that any fruit can be it have also diverse several name there be two sort the male and the female the canarians call it Ananasa the brasilian Nana those of hispaniola jaiama and the spaniard in Brasilia because one of they find that and the first in Brasilia it be as great as a melon fair of colour somewhat yellow green and carnation when it begin to be ripe the greenness thereof turn into a orange colour it be of a pleasant taste and have a fine smell like a apricocke so that it be to be smell far off when you see the fruit afar off be green it show like artichoke and be eat with wine it be light of disgesture but eat much thereof it inflame a man body in Brasilia there be three fort thereof each have a several name first jaiama the second Boniama the three jaiagma but in Guinea there be but one sort the time where they be in their flower be in Lent for than they be best it grow half a fathom about the ground the leave thereof be not much unlike when they be eat they be cut in round f^ices and sopt in spanish wine you can eat enough thereof it be very hot of nature and will grow in moist ground the sop that you take out of the wine taste like sweet musk and if you do not present wipe the knife wherewith you cut the fruit but forget it let it lie half a hour it will be eat in as if there have be strong water lay upon it be eat in abundance and without knowledge it cause great sickness there be great store of Iniamus grow in Guinea in great field which be sow and plant like turnip the root be the Iniamus and grow in the earth like earth-nut those Iniamus be as great as a yellow root but thick and full of knot they be of a mouse-colour and within as white as a turnip but not so sweet be put in a kettle and sodden with flesh and then peel and eat with oil and pepper they be a very delicate meat in many place it be use for bread and be the great meat that the negro eat the be somewhat red of colour and in form almost like Iniamus and taste like earth-nut those two kind of fruit be very abundant in Guinea they be common roast or else eat with a hodge-pot in stead of parsnip or turnip the palme-wine tree be almost like the tree or a Lantor with diverse other and be palme-wine tree of three or four sort most of they have all one kind of leaf but in manner of wood they be unlike for this tree be short of wood than the rest the wine be draw out of those tree by bore they from whence there issue a sap like milk which be very cool and fresh to drink at the first when it be draw it be pleasant and sweet have stand a while it be as sour as vinegar so that you may use it in a salad but be drink sweet and fresh it cause a man to void urine well whereby in those country there be very few find that have the disease of the stone drink much thereof a man head will soon be light the lightness which a man have in his head thereby cause it not to ache when it come first out of the tree it be sweet of taste then when it have stand awhile but yet it be esteem to be better when it have stand awhile and be somewhat settle then present to be drink for it stand seethe and bubble as if it hang over the fire and sod so that if it be put into a glass and stop up without let any air come into it the force thereof will break the glass in piece but be a meal tie old it be nothing worth because it be so sour and then it be of another colour very waterish therefore it be much mix with water and seldom come pure to the market as it be take out of the tree which be do partly to increase their wine as also that then it be the sweet to drink and have the taste of cider and the colour of must when the tree be old and will yield no more wine at the top it be cut down at the foot and a fire make at the root thereof where they set a pot whereinto the wine by mean of the heat run the tree be change and yield no more profit there grow another tree out of the root thereof but it be half a year old before it give any wine in the morning betimes a hour before day the wine be draw out and bring to the market at noonetime the tree be not much to be see in Guinea but for that a negro in that country show i some of the fruit thereof I think good to say something of it in this place it be tree a tree without branch on the top of the tree the fruit grow and it be almost like the Annanas when it be ripe it be outward of a fair gold colour and within it have grain like pomegranate they be of a very sweet taste the other be hard and unfit to eat @. 7 of their gentleman and how they be make their dance sport disease cure visitation mourning funeral and of their gold. there be many gentleman in that country but of small mean for assoon as they ambition of gentry have buy their gentility they be then poor and in miserable estate than they be before and for that they think to be man of great account when they be gentleman they seek much after it and begin to gather some wealth from their youth upward to obtain the place of a gentleman first they give three gift to be make a gentleman the first gift be a dog which they call Cabro de matto which be as much to say as a field-sheepe the second gift be a sheep or a goat the three gift be a cow with many other thing and then he be make a gentleman these gift be give among those that be gift for it gentleman and be give the one now the other at another time as the man that be make a gentleman can best do it and have the mean to perform it and then he make the captain acquaint with it which do he buy a cow which be carry and tie in the market place and then it be make know to the people that such a man shall be make a gentleman at such a time in the mean time all those that be gentleman make themselves as fine as creation they can to go with he and to fight and show many apish toy the man that be to be make a gentleman make all thing ready as meat and drink to entertain his guest and to bid they welcome in good sort he buy hen and many pot of palme-wine and send every gentleman a hen and a pot of palme-wine home to his house to make merry withal when the feast day come the inhabitant assemble together upon the market place the man as he master go and sit on the one side have many instrument as drum horn bell and other thing with they the captain arm himself and with he have many young bachelor with shield and assagay their face be colour and their body paint with red and yellow earth which make they look like a company of young devil the man that be make a gentleman be accompany with a number of other gentleman have a boy behind he which carry his stool to sit upon when he go to speak with any man and his fellow gentleman come to salute he and wish he good fortune in his new estate at which time they take a great deal of straw in the one hand and lay it under his foot which he tread upon the like also they use when their own friend come to visit they and bring they any present which they use for a great honour the wife of the gentleman go to she to do all the honour they can to the wife of the gentleman that make the feast and dress she fine fold her hair with many golden Fetissos and cross put about her neck a ring of gold and in the one hand she carry a horse-tail and on her right arm she have a ring of gold at each end thereof have a round thing like the lid of a pot all make of gold and be ready they be place in order as their manner be one after the other then the cow be lead forth and then all the gentleman in the town come and follow they as it be on procession dance and leap round about the town and when they come again into the marketplace the cow be bind to a stake and there they make a great noise with drum and pipe and the young bachelor with fence and leap with their shield and assagay now in one place then in another make as they think great joy about the gentleman every man seek to excel each other and to get most praise and commendation the woman also make no less ado with sing and dance sometime carry both the gentleman and his wife upon a stool round about the town cast white meal in their face and in that sort make great pastime three day together and every night they be lead home to their house and watch by the other gentleman the next day he be fetch by a great number of people and great honour do unto he as before at which time he hang a white flag out of his house which do signify joy or open house the three day the cow be kill by the executioner and quarter and every man have a piece of the flesh thereof that they also may be participant of the feast but the man and the woman that make the feast may not eat of the cow for they make they believe that if they eat any thereof they shall die within a year after the feast day be end the head of the cow be carry home to his house which he hang up and paint it with diverse colour hang many straw fetissoe upon it which be a sign of his gentility and a warrant to prove he to be make a gentleman then he have great privilege for he may buy slave and do other thing which before he privilege may not have do when he be make a gentleman he be very proud thereof for the first thing that they will tell unto a stranger be that they be gentleman and that they have many slave esteem themselves to be great master but it fall out oftentimes that after their feast be do and he make a gentleman that then he be poor than he be before because he disburse all his money to get it and then he must go out to fish again and do other thing if he will get his live this kind of gentility cost he about eight Bendas which be a pound of gold but deduct that which be give for present of other man which bring they to he each man accord to his mean and ability it stand he not in above half a pound of gold those gentleman have a fellowship among they and every year make a feast and then bid their friend to be merry with they and make good cheer at which time they hang their annual feast cow or sheep head with Millie straw and paint they with white colour signify thereby the remembrance of their feast beside this the gentleman have a other feast amongst they upon the six day of july at which time they paint their body with white and red stripe and hang a garland make of green bough and straw about their neck which they wear all that day that you may know the gentleman from the rest and then also they hang their cow and goat head full of fetissoe as before in the evening they meet together at a banquet in the house of the captain where they be very merry together eat and drink their head and belly full till they be drink they make themselves very fine especial the woman when they go to dance wherein their dance they take a great pride they hang many copper tin and ivory ring about their arm and on their leg they put ring with many bell that they may sound when they dance their head be frizzle and dress with a tuft of hair they wash their body fair with water and then anoint they with palme-oile to make they shine their tooth also they rub with a hard stick then they put a piece of white linen about their body which hang from underneath their breast down below their knee and common about evening they assemble together and go to the marketplace to dance there other have instrument whereon they play as some copper basin whereon they strike with wooden stick other have wooden drum cut out of a hollow tree cover over with a goat skin and play upon they other have round block cut very handsome and even whereon also they strike with wooden stick other have cow-bell some have small luit make out of a piece of wood like a harp with six string of reed whereon they play with both their hand every one have their several instrument and each keep good correspondence with their fellow instrument other sing and begin to dance two and two together leap and stamp with one of their foot upon the ground knock with their finger and bow down their head and speak each to other in their hand carry horse-taile which they cast sometime on the one shoulder then upon the other use certain order in their sport one follow the other and each do as the other do other woman take straw which they let fall to the ground and then dance upon it cast it up again into the air with their foot and catch it as it fa^^eth with their hand so that they play many apish and child sport think that they do excellent well but they desire not to be see by stranger because they laugh and jest at they and then they be ashamed this continue a hour or a hour and a half every one go home again as have end the yonker their sport there be house also among they wherein young man and maid use to dance and play the young bachelor use to drink themselves drink and by night run through the street with their arm and assagay make a great noise with cry and shout as if a company of young devil run about the street and meet with other company with who have some word they fight together wherein they be so earnest one against the other that they be almost ready to kill each other and many time can leave off they will not light begin to quarrel for they be not so hasty but will endure much special of stranger before they will quarrel but if they once begin they be not easy pacify but be very earnest and hasty to set upon their adverse party and to be revenge though it shall cost they their life and they have very quick hand to thrust and to strike their body be subject to many sickness and disease which they esteem but little and their wound and malady make no account of wound or hurt the sickness wherewith they be most trouble be pox clapdollar botch worm pain in the head and burn fever these disease they get from foul and filthy woman whereunto they be much addict and although they have any disease by such mean which be not without much danger yet they esteem not much of they but pass they away as if they ail nothing and be not fainthearted but of a hard complexion suffer their wound to swell and putrify without any mean of remedy apply thereunto for they neither have nor use any physic among they to ease they in their sickness nor surgeon or physician to heal their wound but suffer their wound and disease to have their course unless any of our surgeon give they any physic or surgery for the pox and clap-doller they use much Salsaparillia which the hollander ship bring they which salve they seethe with salt water and drink the water for drink against the pox and such like disease and also against the worm that be in their leg as I will declare worm in the leg more at large wherewith also we be much trouble whereunto they use no remedy at all but suffer their leg to continue so until they heal and wax better of themselves for the pain of the head they use certain pap which they make of green leaf and therewith anoint the place where their pain be and if they have any swell about their body which break not out than they take a knife and cut two or three long slash therein and so give the barbarous inhumanity wound a mean to work and to heal up and grow together again which be the cause that they have so much knobd flesh and so many slash in their body but be well to be discern whether they be cut and make in their flesh to beautify and set out themselves or wound and sore that be heal up again they also use no let of blood but only make a hole in their body with a knife to let their blood come out when they have any other natural sickness they will not help nor comfort one the other but if any of they be sick they will shun he as it be the plague and spurn the sick man like a dog and not once help he with a drop of oil or water although they have never so much need no not the father to the son but let they lie like beast and die with hunger and sickness so that they be not skilful to help sick person they make difference between the word morian and negro for they will not be call morion but negro or prettoe which be as much to say as black man for they say that quarrel morian be as much to say as slave or captive and also a man that know nothing or that be half a fool and therefore they will not be call morion but negro or prettoe for if you call they morion they will hardly speak unto you nor make you any answer they make one the other slave but in other sort then in congo or angola for there you can lade no ship full of slave but to the contrary they desire much to have they and buy they yet there be both slave and captive and for that in those country they take no great pain nor need any great number of slave therefore there be no great quantity of they to be have to sell they as they do in other country but only among they of the land that have need of they again no man may buy or sell they but such as be of great account and gentleman they be mark with a iron in their body that if they chance to run away they may be know again by their mark such as be blind or have any other imperfection in their body as be lame or cripple and by reason thereof can get their living the king place they with smith to blow their bellows other with those that press palme-oyle or grind colour whereunto such deform person be fit or to such occupation and labour wherewith they can help themselves and get their victual so that there you see none such as beg their victual but they be put in some place or other to earn their meat so that the inhabitant give no meat one to the other the king of the town have many slave which they buy and sell and get much by they and to be brief in those country there be no man to be hire to work or go of any errand for money but such as be slave and captive which be to spend their day in slavery hatred and envy be much use in those country and to whosoever they once bear hatred and envy they will hate they cruel and do they all the hurt and villainy that they can on the other side they bear a villainy long in their mind and will keep malice in their heart seven or eight year and when time serve they then show it open no less hatred and envy be bear by one town unto a other speak all the villainy they can and extol themselves as much as they may to have the honour of traffic and to the end that the ship shall come and anchor before their town and by that mean to bring the country merchant to traffic there wherein they be very diligent and although one town lie but three or four mile one from the other yet they be as envious one against the other as possible they can be and report as hardly of their neighbour as they can imagine that so they may get the netherlander to traffic with they and to that end they strive to show more friendship to the netherlander one than the other to draw we to affect they and bring the trade of merchandise unto they the man common live there till they be old as it seem by their face and outward appearance old age and the effect and as we conceive but they can reckon their own age nor tell how many year they have live when they begin to be old than they be not well proportion nor seemly but look evil favour with gray beard yellow wrinkle skin like spanish leather which proceed of the anoint of their body with palmeo-yle they be likewise lean of leg and arm and whole misshape special old woman with their long breast which then show and hang upon their body like old hog bladder they will not willing be old because as then they be not esteem of but much despise and not respect and as from their youth upward to the best time of their life they still wax of a fair black colour so when they be pass that time they begin to decay and to lose their perfect blackness in their winter time they be very sickly and then common there be a great mortality among they by mean of the unwholesomenesse of the air which they then endure and when they lamentable lament die their friend come to the dead man house and weep and sorrow grievous for he speak unto he and ask he why he die with many such like foolish ceremony they take the dead body and lay it on a mat upon the ground and wind it in in a woollen purposely make in that country of colour red blue black and white under his head they lay a wooden stool and cover or dress his head with a goat skin and strew all the body over with ash and dust of bark of tree they close not his eye together they lay his arm down by his side and so let he lie half a day in the air if it be a man his best belove wife go and sit down by the body and if it be a woman the man go and sit down by she cry and weep have in their hand a wisp of straw or of bark of tree wherewith cry and howl over the dead body he or she wipe his face sometime say unto it auzy and make a great noise in the mean time the friend or neighbour come to visit the dead and to moan he for his misfortune other as the near friend be woman go round about the house sing and beat upon basin sometime come to the dead body and go round about he sing and leap and kinck of hand make a great noise and then again go round about the house sing and play upon basin which they do twice or thrice one after the other in the mean time preparation be make for the burial and to make good cheer together after it be end to the which end they dress certain hen and a sheep and other meat which funeral they be accustom to eat and while the dead body be above the ground the elder Morinni of that quarter go about from house to house with a basin whereon every one must put the value of twelve penny in gold with the which money they buy a cow which cow be give to a Fetissero that use to conjure their god to will he to conjure the Fetisso to suffer the dead body to remain and rest in peace and to bring he into the other world and not to molest he in the way with this cow blood he coniur his Fetisso for a dead man must smear his Fetisso with blood than they bind the dead body upon a plank and carry he to the grave sing and leap the body be carry by man and the woman follow after one by one about their head have a crown or garland of straw and a staff in their hand the man if it be a woman go next to the dead body cry to the grave else there go no man after it unless the dead body chance to be bear to another place to be bury as sometime it happen that they carry the dead body twenty mile off from the place where he die to be bury there and then many man go arm with the body to convey it to the burial the body be carry to the earth and the grave-maker make a grave about four foot deep and therein he be lay over the grave there be many stick of wood aid close one by the other the woman creep to and fro over the grave make a great noise with howl and cry and over that they lay the earth and place it and bind it about the same as if it be a chest all his good as apparel weapon pot basin tool spade and such householdstuff wherewith he earn his live be carry to the grave and bury with he which be set round about the grave to serve his turn withal in the other world as they do when he live upon the earth other of the dead man friend bring some thing also to set in the grave for a memory which be put into the grave with the rest of his good if he be one that delight much in drink and love palm well when he live they will set a pot of palme-wine by he in his grave because he shall not die for thirst and what in his life he use that be give he and bury in his grave with he if it be a woman that die in travel of her child the child be lay in the mother right arm and bury with she above upon the grave there be a straw house make like a sepulchre wherein all the householdstuff and other thing be set the grave-maker fee be to have half the good that be set into the grave but the friend of the dead content he and he be pay for it because they shall let the good stand still untouched for it be a great credit to the friend of the dead to leave good store of good upon the grave with the dead body which they let stand there so long till it be clean consume and none of they will ever offer to take any of it away by any mean whatsoever the body be bury they go altogether to the seaside or to some other river where the woman go in and stand up to their middle in water and take up water in their hand cast it in their own face and upon their body and wash their breast and all their body other woman in the mean time play upon basin and such like instrument one of those woman take the man or woman who husband or wife be dead and lead they into the water lay they therein flat upon their back and take they up again which they do diverse time speak one unto the other and make great complaint when he or she be well and clean wash from the head to the foot she lead they out of the water again and put their clothes upon their body again and then they go together to the dead man house to make good cheer and to drink themselves drink if it be a man that die that have child the woman must not retain nor keep any of his good for the behoof of the child but must give all the man good both that which he have to his marriage and which he get by his labour while he live unto his brethren if he have any live and must not keep any thing from they if he have no brethren than the father if he be live take all his son good and enjoy it if it be a woman that die than the husband must deliver her marriage good to her brethren as aforesaid without keep any thing thereof for his child so that no child in those country inherit their father good neither be they their father heir no more may the wife inherit any of her husband good but it be all divide among his brethren but while their wife live they give she what they think good of that which they gain so young maid and man must endeavour themselves to get some thing in their youth that they may have some thing when they marry and keep house for the king death more sorrow be make by some of the gentleman who in the king life serve he when he be dead give he a slave to serve he and other man one of their wife to wait king funeral on he and to dress his meat other bring one of their son to go with the king into the other world so that there be a number of people that be appoint to go with the king to the other world which be kill and their head cut off but they know nothing thereof for such man and woman as give they to the king when he be dead tell not they that they shall be put to death to go into the other world with the king but when the time come that the burial be to be solemnize they send they on some message or to fetch water and so follow they strike they through the body with a assagaie and kill they in the way which do they carry the dead body to the king house whereby they show what faithful servant they be unto their king while he live other also do the like and those dead body be smear with blood and bury with the king in his grave that they may travel together if any of his wife love he entire they suffer themselves to be kill with the rest and be bury with he that they may reign together in the other world the head of the dead man and woman be set round about the sepulchre and grave of the king for a great bravery and honour unto he upon the grave they set all kind of meat and drink that they may eat some thing and very believe that they eat and drink it and that they live thereby and for that cause the pot of palme-wine and of water be continual fill up all his stuff as arm and clothes be bury with he and all his gentleman that serve he have every one of they their picture make of clay after the life and fair paint which be set and place orderly round about his grave one by the other so that their king sepulcher be like house and as well stu^t as if they still live which sepulcher be so much esteem off that they be watch both by night and by day by arm man to the end that if he desire to have any thing they shall straight bring it he gold at this day be as much esteem off by they as it be with we of who they say gold gold how esteem and find be our God and more too for they be greedy and earnest to have it then we be because they mark and see that the hollander take so much pain for it and give more merchandise for it in exchange than ever the portugal do for I be of a opinion that there be few negro that dwell on the sea side that know where the mine be or that ever see they also there be never any Portugal or Netherlander at they or near they but the mine be well keep and look unto by the owner thereof so I have hear by some negro that each king have his mine and cause the gold to be dig by his man and sell it to other merchant and so it pass from one to another in what manner the gold be find in Guinea I know not but as some negro have tell i they find gold in deep pit which they dig up and that with the water it be drive down like sand at which water and run spring many people sit with spoon in their hand and take up the gold sand and all and put it into a basin some piece be cover over with chalk and earth wherein they be find the small gold which be find in the sand they purge and make clean in clear run water but yet they let some sand and gravel remain among it it be find in no great quantity as they themselves say but with great pain and labour for it cost many man their life which be smother in the mine and a man that can find two or three Englishen of gold in a day have do well and have earn a good day hire the half which be find be the labourer and the other half be for the king or for he that owe the mine this I have be tell by some of the negro gold by they be call Chika and some great merchant that dwell about the main bring the gold aboard the ship to buy ware as it come out of the mine and that be esteem to be the best gold wherein there be leave deceit but the receiver must look well to it to blow the sand clean out of it and to beat the yellow earth with the stone out of it with a hammer and so he can lose by it nevertheless the gold that be bring rough out of the mine be esteem to be better and rich and more worth in every mark then the other it fall out oftentimes that some gold be more worth than other which happen by mean of the receiver negligence and many time as the mine of gold fall out for some of they be fine gold than other and also the deep that the mine be dig the gold fall out to be worse and be more mix with silver even in the earth itself than the gold that h high in the earth beside this mean merchant bring much melt gold as crakawen arm ring jewel false gold and other thing wherein there be most falsehood use for such negro as have but small mean to traffic with we be more use and addict to the falsify of gold than other be wherein they use great subtlety but we ourselves be oftentimes the cause thereof for we bring and sell they the matter and the instrument which they use therein and so deceive ourselves and make a rod for our own breech but they be wont to falsify it more than now for the portugal hang up some for it they have good knowledge in gold and can soon perceive whether it be good or falsify but of other jewel as pearl diamond ruby emerald and such like precious stone they have no knowledge but they know fine red coral well which be much esteem off by they silver also be well and too much know among they because they use it to falsify gold withal and to make it of less value than it be they learn of the portugal to melt gold they also have find the mean to put a edge of gold round about silver and red copper mix together let the false mettle remain in the middle of the piece and so when he that receive it be in haste and touch it but on the edge thereof where it be not falsify with his Touchstone it pass for good but such must be cut in sunder with a hammer and then the falsify be perceive and when they can find no mean to falsify the small fine Chika gold so that the receiver have no suspicion thereof and take the less heed there unto we ourselves bring they tool to do it withal for we bring they file and saw to sell so that they file the yellow copper and mingle it among the small gold that it can hardly be perceive because it be no small which be the subtle falsify of gold by they use but when we blow the sand and dust out of it than the copper show itself whereby it appear that the negro have many way and device to falsify gold but such as look narrow unto they will not be deceive but to try their falsify the best way be to touch their gold and to be wary of deceit and of receive bad gold an other way be to look speedy unto the negro themselves to see if they have bad gold or not for when they bring bad gold they will be in great fear with your handle thereof and when you offer to try their gold they will refuse it and alter their colour and shake and quiver withal the worm in the leg and body trouble not every one that go to those country Troublesome long-worme but some be trouble with they and some not and they be find in some man soon than in other some have a worm before the voyage be do and while they be still upon the coast some get they while they be upon the way other have they after their voyage be full end some four month after some nine month after and some a year after they have make a voyage thither other have make two or three voyage thither and never be trouble with those worm the negro themselves be much trouble with they special those that dwell about the castle of mina and it be a thing to be wonder at for the negro that dwell but 25. mile low eastward be not trouble with worm as their neighbour be and another * * Ormus at Boghar in Bactria there be the like suppose to come by drink bad water in that place as m. ant. jenkinson observe whereof John speak in his itiner be trouble therewith for the land of east India west India China Brasilia and other strange country be not trouble therewith nor know not thereof and which be more they of the island of saint Thomas which man esteem to be the unwholesome place in the world and wherein so many man be sick and lose their life know not what those worm mean but wonder much thereat when it be show they of such as have be with the hollander in Guinea the negro themselves know not whereof they be engender but the great presumption be that they proceed and breed of the water which man buy of the negro which they take out of well or pit and it be very likely as we find by the experience that they breed of the water for in Ormus or in those part the fresh water be fetch up in pot by diverse eighteen fathom deep under the salt water which those people drink because they be there also trouble with worm and as some man write the Indian themselves say that they come of the water such as have they be in great pain for some of they can neither go nor stand some neither sit nor lie other lie whole in despair as if they be senseless and sometime be fain to be bind some have they with a fever or shake as if they have a fever some get they on a sudden other have they before they know it and have little pain therewith so that the worm show themselves diverse way they appear with a little blain other with a spot like a flea-biting other with a little swell so that you may often see the worm between the skin and the flesh other show themselves with bloody vein etc. it must show itself before man use any remedy for it nevertheless it show itself many time too much and too soon for it be better that it come not so soon nor appear at all but suffer man to be at ease it will seek to help itself and thrust out his nose which a man must then take hold on lest he creep in again he show himself in diverse place as in a man leg in the sole of the foot in the arm knee buttock and common in place of a man body where there be much flesh and some man have they in their privy member and which be more in their cod with great grief and pain for those that have they there endure extreme pain but it be true that one man have less pain with they then another and shall also be soon heal of they then another which come by the handle or deal with they for it be very good when a man find himself to be trouble with they to be quiet special be in his leg and not go much and to keep the place warm where they begin to appear for thereby they shall endure less pain for they come better out of a man flesh with warmth then with cold and disease for some man have little respect themselves when they have have the worm so that they appear with a great swell whereby they endure much pain and be in hazard to loose their leg or their arm when it come forth so far that a man may lay hold on it than they must draw he out till he stay and then he must let it rest till he begin to come forward again and as much thereof as be come out of the body must be wind upon a stick or bind close to the hole with a third that he creep not in again when he come out every time he bring good store of matter with he and a man must every day look unto it and draw he so long till he be out but you must not draw he too hard lest he shall break so that by reason of the poison that be in he the wound will fester it happen oftentimes that after there be one worm draw out of a man body that there come another in the same place and have his issue out at the same hole some man be soon rid of they then another for some be ease in three week and less time and some be three month in heal of they some man have more worm than other for some have but one worm and other ten or twelve as I myself know one that have ten worm hang out at his body all at one time and I have know man that have worm that begin to open themselves and creep in again and consume away so that they have no more trouble therewith but the next voyage after they be of diverse length and greatness some be of a fathom long some short as it fall out in thickness they differ much some be as thick as great lute-string and like common pear worm other like small lute-string and some as small as silk or fine thread some say that they be not live and that they be but bad sinew and no worm I have not long since see a man that have certain worm which show themselves and the surgeon draw a worm out with one pull and the worm be draw out and hold up on high wring and writhe itself as if it have be a eel and be about five quarter long and as thick as a lutestring if it be but a sinow it will have no life in it and therefore they be natural worm the negro use no kind of surgery for they but suffer they to have their course and wash the sore with salt-water which they say be very good for it note that our return back from Moure we use to put off from that place from whence you must set sail with a wind from the land and hold your course as near by as you can lose no wind and yet you shall hardly get above s. Thomas or Rio de Gabom because of the spreame which drive you east and by north and east north-east towards the land to the bouthe of Fernando poo which you must beware off for he that fall into that bouthe will hardly get out because of the stream and be in danger to be cast away in that place or else he must have some storm or wind out of the north and so come out southward otherwise it be hardly to be do for there be some who have have the wind a little contrary be six or seven week before they can get to cape lope gonselue here you must note that the near you come to the equinoctial line the wind blow the more southerly so that as you pass under the line the wind blow south and south and by east and somewhat high you must also note when you see great fly fish that you be not far from saint Thomas or above ile @. 8 the passage from the golden coast to the kingdom of Benni or Rio de Benni and Rio Floreado the city court gentry apparel also other place adjoin describe for that the gold coast reach no further than from cape to Rio this be take out of d. r. Uolta therefore those that will go from the golden coast to the kingdom of Benni hold their course along by the land and along by the river of Rio de Ualto Rio de Ardra and Rio de Lago these river be never enter into because there be nothing to be have in they but a little quantity of elephant tooth so that the labour to fetch it be not worth the pain by mean of the danger that a man incur by enter into the river by reason of Sands before at the mouth of the river of Focrado there lie a island and the river be so indifferent great that a man may well know it the land reach most be about forty mile to Rio de Ardra this river be much use to be enter into by the portugal and be well know not because of any great commodity that be therein to be have but because of the great number of slave which be buy there to carry to other place as to saint Thomas and to Brasilia to labour there and to refine sugar for they be very strong man and can labour stout and common be better slave than those of gabom but those that be sell in angola be much better in this river there be no special thing find which be of any value but some blue green and black stone wherewith they grind colour and for their fairness be desire of other negro special in the golden coast of Guinea where they be much esteem of by they there both the man and woman be stark naked until they be sell for slave so that they be not ashamed to show themselves one to the other as they themselves affirm and by reason prove say that a man more covet and desire a thing that he see not or may not have then that he see or may borrow or have and for that cause they hide not their privy member there the portugal traffic much with bark to buy slave and the inhabitant be better friend with they then with any other nation because they come much there and for that no other nation come to buy slave there but the portugal only and there be some portugal dwell there which buy much ware and merchandize such as there to be have from Rio de Ardra to Rio de Lago be ten mile and in that river there be nothing else to buy and therefore it be not much use so that Rio de Ardra be more use than Rio de Uolta and Rio de Lago from Rio de Lago to Rio de Benni be about twenty mile so that Benni be esteem to be part of the golden coast that be about one hundred mile from mourre so that in two day with help of the stream a man may get thither where as man be wont to be six week before they can turn back again from whence they come the town seem to be very great when you enter into it you go into a great broad the city of Benni street not pave which seem to be seven or eight time broad than the warmoes street in Amsterdam which go right out and never crook and where I be lodge with Cornelison it be at least a quarter of a hour go from the gate and yet I can not see to the end of the street but I see a great high tree as far as I can discern and I be tell the street be as much long there I speak with a Netherlander who tell i that he have be as far as that tree but see no end of the street but perceive that the house thereabouts be much less and some house that be fall down so that it be to be think that the end thereof be there abouts that tree be a good half mile from the house where I be lodge so that it be think that that street be a mile long beside the suburb at the gate where I enter on horseback I see a very high bulwark very thick of earth with a very deep these be dutch mile broad ditch but it be dry and full of high tree I speak with one that have go along by the ditch a good way but see no other than that I see and know not well whither it go round about the town or not that gate be a reasonable good gate make of wood after their manner which be to be shut and there always there be watch hold without this gate there be a the gentleman go with great majesty to the court have diverse kind of music with their fashion they and be wait on by diverse other negro one have a drum whereon he play other with other instrument upon the horse there be a little wooden stool set and on the horse neck they hang a cow-bell which ring when the horse go there go two negro by he on either side one on who he lean those negro that attend on he come every morning to the gentleman door and stay there till he come out to wait on he their horse be very little not much great than calf in our country which be the cause that our war horse be so much esteem of in that coast. the king have many soldier which be sub^^ct unto he and they have a general to command over they as if he be their captain this captain have some soldier under he and go always in the middle of they and they go round about he sing and leap and make great noise and joy those captain be very proud of their office and be very stately and go exceed proud in the street their sword be broad which hang about their neck in a leather girdle which reach under their arm they also use shield and assagay as they in the golden coast do they cut their hair diverse each after the best manner that they can their apparel also apparel be the like and use strange custom not one like unto another all fine make of Cotton over the which they common wear Holland cloth. the young maid and boy go stark naked until they marry or that the king give they licence to put on some apparel then they make great joy because of the friendship the king therein show unto they and then they make their body very clean and strike it over with white earth and be very stately sit in great glory and magnificence their friend come unto they to congratulate they as if she be a bride they be circumcise both boy and girl they cut three great streak in their body on either side each streak be three finger broad which they do from their shoulder down to their waste which they think to be a great good deed tend to their salvation they be very conscionable and will do no wrong one to the other neither will take any thing from stranger for if they do they shall afterward be put to death for they light judge a man to die for do any wrong to a stranger wherein they use strange wrong to a stranger justice they bind the offender arm behind at his back and blind his eye than one of the judge come and lift he up with his arm in such manner that his head lie almost upon the ground then come the executioner and cut off his head which do his body be quarter and the quarter cast into the field to be devour by certain bird which bird they bird superstitious respect fear much and no man dare do they any hurt nor chase they for there be man purposely appoint to give they meat and drink which they carry with great magnificence but no man may see it carry nor be present but those that be appoint to do it for every man run out of the way when they see those man come to carry the bird meat and they have a place where the bird come purposely for it they respect stranger very much for when any man meet they they will shun the way for he and step aside and dare not be so bold to go by unless they be express bid by the party and pray to go forward and although they be never so sore lade yet they dare not do it for if they do they shall be punish for it they be also very covetous of honour and willing desire to be praise and reward for any friendship they do upon the island of corisco or about Rio de Angra in the mouth whereof the island of corisco Rio de Angra corisco lie the island of corisco be a bad place to dwell in for no man dwell in it for there be nothing to be have in it but fresh water and wood so that the ship that come from the golden coast and fall upon it provide themselves there of water and wood within the river there lie three other small land which also be worth nothing because they yield no profit and there be nothing abound in they but wood those land at this day be call for before they have no name the isle Moucheron because one Balthasar de Moucheron have by his Moucheron factor find they wherein he cause a fort to be make in the year 1600. think to dwell there and to bring great traffic from other place thither but they of Rio de Gabom understand that there be stranger inhabit in they they by force murder all the man that be in it and call it the island of corisco which name it have of the portugal because upon that island there be many tempest of thunder and lightning and great store of rain and therefore it be not good to inhabit in and there will nothing grow therein but cucumber it be well provide of fresh water excellent fair red bean and brasil wood so exceed fair and glister when it be shave as any glass can be which be so hard that without great pain and labour it can be cut down the island be almost a great mile in compass but it be a bad anchor place when the travadoe come from Rio de Angra to Rio de Gabom be fifteen mile the inhabitant of Rio de Gabom be not friend with they of Rio de Angra for they oftentimes make war one against the other and great suburb when you be in the great street aforesaid you see many great street on the side thereof which also go right forth but you can see to the end of they by reason of their great length a man may write more of the situation of this town if he may see it as you may the town in Holland which be not permit there by one that always go with you some man say that he go with you because you shall have no harm do unto you but yet you must go no far than he will let you the house in this town stand in good order one close and even with the other as the house in Holland stand such house as man of quality which be gentleman or other dwell in their house have two or three step to go up and before there be as it be a gallery where a man may sit dry which gallery every morning be make clean by their slave and in it there be a Mat spread for man to sit on their room within be foure-square over they have a roof that be not close in the middle at the which place the rain wind and light come in and therein they lie and eat their meat but they have other place beside as kitchen and other room the common house be not such for they have but one wall before wherein there be a wooden door they know not how to make window but such light and air as they have come in at the roof of the house the king court be very great within it have many great foure-square plain which round about they have gallery wherein there be always watch keep I be so far within the court. that court that I pass over four such great plain and wheresoever I look still I see gate upon gate to go into other place and in that sort I go as far as ever any Netherlander be which be to the stable where his best horse stand always pass a great long way it seem that the king have many soldier he also have many gentleman who when they come to the court ride upon horse and sit upon their horse as the woman in our country do on each side have one man on who they hold fast and the great their estate be the more man they have go after they some of their man have great shield wherewith they keep the gentleman from the sun they go next to he except those on who he lean the rest come after he play some on drum other upon horn and flute some have a hollow iron whereon they strike the horse also be lead by a man and so they ride play to the court. such as be very great gentleman have another kind of music when they ride to the court which be like the small net wherewith man in our country go to the fishmarket which net be fill full of a certain kind of thing which they strike upon with their hand and make it rattle in like sort as if their net be fill full of great nut and so a man shall strike upon it those great gentleman have many servant that go after they strike upon such net the king have very many slave both man and woman whereof there be many woman slave see carry of water Iniamus and palme-wine which they say be for the king wife there be also many man slave see in the town that carry water Iniamus and palme-wine which they say be for the king and many carry grass which be for their horse and all this be carry to the court. the king oftentimes send out present of spice which be carry orderly through the street and as the other thing aforesaid be carry so they that carry they go one after the other and by they there go one or two with white rod so that every man must step aside and give they place although he be a gentleman the king have many wife and every year go twice out of his court and visit the town at which time he show all his power and magnificence and all the bravery he can than he be convoy and accompany by all his wife which be above six hundred in number six hundred wife but they be not all his wed wife the gentleman also have many wife as some have eighty some ninety and more and there be not the mean man among they but have ten or twelve wife at the least whereby in that place you find more woman then men. they also have several place in the town where they keep their market in one place they have their great market day call dia and in another place they hold their gentleman their make little market call to those place they bring all thing to sell as quick dog whereof they eat many roast ape and monkey rat parrot hen Iniamus Manigette in bonche dry Agedissen palme-oyle great bean diverse sort of kankren with many other kind of fruit and beast all to eat they also bring much wood to burn cup to eat and drink in and other sort of wooden dish and cup for the same purpose great store of Cotton whereof they make clothes to wear upon their body their apparel be of the same fashion as they of the golden coast be but it be fair and fine make but to show you the manner thereof it will be overlong they also bring great store of iron-worke to sell there and instrument to fish withal other to plough and to till the land withal and many weapon as assagay and knife also for the war this market and traffic be there very orderly hold and every one that come with such ware or merchandise to the market know his place where to stand to sell his ware in the same they also sell their wife as they do in the golden coast. then again make peace so that the friendship between they be very small they have a king among they but they be not so mighty as those of Rio de Gabom but better people to deal withal then those of gabom for since the time that they of gabom take the sconce and the good of Moncherom and kill the man they of Rio de Angra will have nothing to do with they but be grieve that it be do but because they fear they of Rio de
