not stay long with your shallop or boat there for if you deal not with they for their tooth in two or three day you shall not deal with they at all for by reason that few Pinnasses or shallop come thither to traffic therefore the negro bring all their tooth thither at the first to barter for other ware their speech be not like they of gabom but for opinion and religion they be almost one and agree therein the river of gabom lie about fifteen mile southward from Rio de Angra and eight mile northward from cape Lopo Gonsalues and be right under the equinoctial line about r. gabom fifteen mile from saint Thomas and be a great land well and easy to be know at the mouth of the river there lie a sand three or four fathom deep whereon it beat mighty with the stream which run out of the river into the sea. this river in the mouth thereof be at least four mile broad but when you be about the island call Pongo it be not above two mile broad on both side the river there stand many tree the island lie near to the north than the south and a little further there be a island wherein there be good provision to be have as of Bannanas Iniamus and orange about two mile within the river you monstrous high hill he of Pongo be strong of man and oftentimes make war upon he of gabom he of Caiombo be a great friend to he of Pongo and the inhabitant of the south point of the river be great friend with those of cape Lopo Gonsalues the twelve of December we get to cape Lopo Gonsalues where we find three ship lie at anchor two of Zealand and one of Schiedam touch their religion they neither know cape Gonsalues God nor his commandment some of they pray to the sun other to the moon other to certain tree or to the earth because they receive food from thence so that they esteem it a great fault to spit upon the earth they go little abroad in the street but when they go abroad they carry a great broad knife in their hand both the man and the woman have their body pink in diverse sort strange to behold wherein they put certain grease mix with colour they will not drink before they first put some of it out of the pot or can and when they eat they use not to drink but when they have dine than they drink a great draught of water or of palme-wine or else of Malaffo which be mix or make of honey water in the morning as soon as it be day they go to salute their commander or Chaveponso and to bid he good morrow and when they come to he they fall down upon their knee and clap both their hand together say Fino Fino Fino whereby they wish peace quietness and all good unto he they be much addict to thievery and to steal something special from stranger whereof they make no conscience but think they do well but they will not steal one from another the woman also be much addict to lechery and uncleanness special with strange nation whereby they think they get great credit and which be more the man offer their wife unto stranger that come thither and the king himself present and honour stranger with some of his wife whereof he have a great number they have a filthy custom among they which be that the king when any of his daughter wax great he take and keep they for his wife and the use of their body the like be do by the queen his wife when their son begin to be great for they lie with they as well as the king do incestuous custom with his daughter their apparel be fair than they on the golden coast for they trim their body more about their middle to hide their privity they wear a Mat make of bark of tree which be colour red with a kind of red wood wherewith they die it upon those mat they hang some ape and monkey skin or of other wild beast with a bell in the middle such as cow and sheep have about their neck they paint their body red with a colour make of red wood which be very good but much light than brasil-wood oftentimes they make one of their eye white the other red or yellow with a streak or two in their face some wear round bead about their neck make of bark some small some great not much unlike the box which man in hamborough hang up to put money in for the poor but they will not suffer you to look what be in they the man and woman also for the most part apparel and ornament go bareheaded with their hair shoar and pleat diverse some of they wear cap make of the bark of or indian nut-tree other wear bunch of feather make fast to their hair with little iron some of they have hole in their upper lip and through their nose wherein they put piece of elxen bone as thick as a Doller with a stalk which shut the hole which be thrust in come out at the nose and over their mouth which serve their turn well and to good purpose when they be sick and fall into a swoon and that man can open their hand by force than they take that bone and crush the sap of some green herb through it wherewith they come to themselves again so that they serve they for two purpose some wear ring in their lip and in the middle part of their nose some thrust small horn or tooth through they and wear they so which they think to be a great ornament unto they other boar a hole in their neither lip and play with their tongue in the hole many of their man and woman wear ring in their ear whereof some weigh at least a pound weight some have stick thrust through they of five or six finger long most of they special the man wear a girdle about their middle make of buffols skin with the hair still on it which meet not together before by almost a hand breadth with a piece thereof stick out at each end which be tie together with a small cord of thread upon their belly they carry a broad iron knife the sheath thereof also be of iron some of those girdle be a hand broad and some two or three-handful broad beside those they use another sort of knife with two or three point which be very fearful to behold wherewith they cast at a man and wheresoever they hit they take hold they be better arm for weapon than they of Myna or the golden coast their arm arm be pike or assagay bow and arrow long target make of bark of tree their drum be narrow below and broad above their pike be very cunning make for they be very curious workman in iron the woman carry their husband arm for he and when they will use they their wife give they they be cruel and fierce against their enemy and fight one against the other by land and by water in canoe and when they take any of their enemy they be wont in time past to eat they but now they do it not they put they to great torture the woman also set themselves out very fair as they think and wear many red copper and tin ring upon their arm and leg some one other two which many time weigh three or four pound weight which be so fast and close about their arm that man can hardly imagine how they get they on those ring also be wear by some man but more by woman the woman wear apron make of rush which I have see they make touch their diet clothes and set forth of their body it be beastly and unseemly they have no less unseemliness in their eat and housekeeping for they live like beast and sleep upon mat lay upon the ground which they make very cunning the chief meat they eat be Iniamus and Bannanas the Bannanas they use in stead of bread when it be well dry they also eat fish and flesh with root and sugarcane they lay all their meat in one dish and sit round about it and eat great than any in all the town he be call Golipatta he be brave set out with many bead make of bean and shell which be die red and hang about his neck and upon his arm and leg they strike their face with a kind of white colour they be very much subject to their king and do he great honour when they be in his presence before his house there lie a iron piece with certain base which he buy in former time of the frenchman they be very subtle to learn how to use all kind of arm special our small gun their winter be from April to August at which time it be exceed hot and few clear day and then it rain mighty with great drop which fall so hot upon the stone that they present dry up by which mean also the water be thick and slimy in the river and also upon the shore there be good fish oyster grow on the branch of the tree which hang down into the oyster on tree water they draw their speech long so that it be better to learn then they in the golden coast. the cape be low land and be well to be know for there be no land thereabouts that reach so far westerly into the sea as that do it lie about a degree southward from the equinoctial line when you be at the cape there be a river which river there be many sea-horse and crocodile so that it be think that he river of Nilus join thereunto and have a issue there into the sea in this country there be many cruel and strange beast as the strange adventure of ANDREW battle of Leigh in Essex send by the portugal prisoner to angola who live there and in the adjoin region near eighteen year @ i andrew battle his voyage to the river of plate who be take on the coast of brasil be send to angola in the year 1589 Abraham Cock of limehouse begin his voyage towards the river of plate with two Pinnasses of fifty tun a piece the one be call the Abraham cook voyage may-morning the other the dolphin we sail from the river of Thames the twenty of April and the six and twenty of the same month we put into Plymouth where we take in some provision for the voyage the seven of may we put to sea and with foul weather be beat back again into Plymouth where we remain certain day and then proceed on our voyage and run along the coast of Spain and Barbary we put into the road of cruz and there set Cruz. our light-horse-man together which we carry in two piece Abraham Cock make great account hereof think that this boat shall have make his voyage this do we put to sea calm on the coast of Guinea and run along the coast of Guinea we be becalm because we be so near the coast. here our man fall ficke of the scurvy in such sort that egyptians and moriscoe that be banish as myself to one of these egyptian I break my mind and tell he that it be better for we to venture our life for our liberty then to live in that miserable place whither we travail we tell they that we be go to congo these negro say that we be in the wrong way and that they be and will carry we to bambe where the duke of bambe lay so we go some three mile east up into the land till we perceive that we be the wrong way for we travail by the sun and will go no far that way and turn back again to the westward they stand before we with their bow arrow and dart ready to shoot at we but we determine to go through they discharge six musket together and kill four which do amaze they and make they to retire but they follow we four or five mile and hurt two of our company with their arrow the next day we come into the border of Bamba and travail all that day at night we hear the surge of the sea. the seven day in the morning we see the captain of the city come after we with horseman Bamba and great store of negro hereupon our company be dismay seven of our fainthearted portugal hide themselves in the thicke I and the four egyptian think to have escape I bethink myself that if the negro do take i in the wood they will kill i wherefore think to make a better end among the portugal and mullatos a. b. leave alone I come present out of the wood with my this gold. store of gold and that they gather up great store of grain of gold upon the sand which the fresh water drive down in the time of rain we find some of this gold in the handle of their hatchet which they use to engrave with copper and they call it copper also and do not esteem it these Gagas delight in no country but where there be great store of palmare or grove of palm for they delight great in the wine and in the fruit of the palm which serve to eat and to make oil and they draw their wine contrary to the these palmtree be six or seven fathom high and have no leaf but in the top and they have a device palme-wine how draw to go up to the top of the tree and lay no hand on it and they draw the wine in the top of the tree in a bottle but these Gagas cut the palmtree down by the root which lie ten day before they such difference between wasp and bee will give wine and then they make a square hole in the top and heart of the tree and take out of the hole every morning a quart and at night a quart so that every tree give two quart of wine a day for the space of six and twenty day and then it dry up when they settle themselves in any country they cut down as many palm as will serve what they do be resist they wine for a month and then as many more so that in a little time they spoil the country they stay no long in a place than it will afford they maintenance and then in harvest time they arise and settle themselves in the fruitfull place that they can find and do reap their enemy corn and take their cattle for they will not sow nor plant nor bring up any cattle more than they take by war when they come into any country that be strong which they can the first day conquer than their general build his fort and remain sometime a month or two quiet for he say it be as great war to the inhabitant to see stratagem he settle in their country as though he fight with they every day so that many time the inhabitant come and assault he at his fort and these Gagas defend themselves and flesh they on for the space of two or three day and when their general mind to give the onset he will in the night put out some one thousand man which do emboske themselves about a mile from their fort. then in the morning the great Gaga go with all his strength out of the fort as though he will take their town the inhabitant come near the fort to defend their country be between they the Gagas give the watchword with their drum and then the embosk man arise so that very few escape and that day their general overrun his attire Bamba shell maso shell of great account among the Gagas the country the great Gaga have his hair very long embroider with many knot full of Banba shell which be very rich among they and about his neck a collar of Maloes which be also shell that be find upon that coast and be sell among they for the worth of twenty shilling a shell and about his middle he wear land which be bead make of the ostriche egg he wear a palm cloth about his middle as fine as silk his body be carve cruel bravery and cut with sundry work and every day anoint with the fat of man he wear a piece of copper across his nose two inch long and in his ear also his body be always paint red and white he have twenty or thirty wife which follow he when he go abroad and one of they carry his bow and arrow and four of they carry his cup of they use this ceremony in Florida drink after he and when he drink they all kneel down and clap their hand and sing their woman wear their hair with high trump full of Bamba shell and be anoint with civet. they pull out four of their tooth two above and two below for a bravery and foolish gallantry those that have not their tooth out be loathsome to they and shall neither eat nor drink with they they wear great store of bead about their neck arm and leg about their middle silk clothes the woman be very fruitful but they enjoy none of their child for as soon as the woman generation of viper a generation without generation of Gaga panizary boy train up in the war be deliver of her child it be present bury quick so that there be not one child bring up in all this generation but when they take any town they keep the boy and girl of thirteen or fourteen year of age as their own child but the man and woman they kill and eat these little boy they train up in the war and hang a collar about their neck for a disgrace which be never take off till he prove himself a man and bring his enemy head to the general and then it be take off and he be a freeman and be call Gonso or soldier this make they all desperate and forward to be free and count man and so they do increase in all this camp there be but twelve natural Gagas that be these Gagas come from serra leona their captain and fourteen or fifteen woman for it be more than fifty year since they come from lion which be their native country but their camp be sixteen thousand strong and sometime more when the great Gaga Calandola undertake any great enterprise against the inhabitant of his solemn sacrifice to the devil any country he make a sacrifice to the devil in the morning before the sun rise he sit upon a stool have on each side of he a man witch then he have forty or fifty woman which stand round about he hold in each hand a zevera or wild horse tail where with they do flourish and sing behind they be great store of Petes ponge and drum which always play in the midst of they be a great fire upon the fire a earthen pot with white powder wherewith the man witch do paint he on the forehead temple thwart the breast and belly with long ceremony and enchant term thus he continue till sun be down then the witch bring his Casengala which be a weapon like a hatchet and put it into his hand and bid he be strong against his enemy for his Mokiso be with he and present there be a man-child bring which forthwith he kill then be four butcherly rite man bring before he two whereof as it happen he present strike and kill the other two he command to be kill without the Fort. here I be by the man witch command to go away because I be a christian. for then the devil do appear to they as they say and present he command five cow to be kill in the fort and five without the fort and likewise as many goat and as many dog and the blood of they be sprinkle in the fire and their body be eat with great feast and triumph and this be use many time by all the other captain of their army when they bury the dead they make a valut in the ground and a seat for he to sit the burial of their dead cruel funeral dead have his hair new embroider his body wash and anoint with sweet powder he have all his best robe put on and be bring between two man to his grave and set in his seat as though he be alive he have two of his wife set with he with their arm break and then they cover the vault on the top the inhabitant when they die be bury after the same fashion and have the most part of their good bury with they and every month there be a meeting of the kindred of the dead man which mourn and sing doleful song at his grave for the space of three day and kill many goat and pour their blood upon his grave and palme-wine also and use this ceremony as long as any of their kindred be alive but those that have no kindred think themselves unhappy man because they have none to mourn unkind kindness for they when they die these people be very kind one to another in their health but in their sickness they do abhor one another and will shun their company @. 4 his return to the portugal invasion of diverse country abuse flight from they and live in the wood diverse month his strange boat and come to Loango be depart from the Gagas I come to Masangano where the portugal have a Masangano a town of Portugal town of garrison there be at that time a new governor which be call Sienor juan Continbo who bring authority to conquer the mine or mountain of cambamba and to perform that service the king of Spain have give he seven year custom of all the slave and good that be carry thence to the west-indies brasil or whither soever with condition that he shall build three castle one in Demba which be the salt mine the other in cambamba which be the silver mine and the other salt mines silver mine in or the bay of Cowes this gentleman be so bountiful at his come that his fame be spread through all congo and many Mulatos and Negro come voluntary to serve he and be some six month in the city he march to the Outaba of tomb and there ship his soldier in Pinnasses and go up the river consa or Coanza and land at the river Coanza the Outaba of sixty mile from the sea. this lord Songo be next to Demba where the salt mine be in this place there be such store of salt that most part of the country be perfect clear salt without any earth or filth in it and it be some three foot under the earth as it be ice and they cut it out in stone of a yard long and it be carry up into the country and be the best commodity that a man can carry to buy any thing whatsoever stone-salt a special commodity the like be in Poland here the governor stay ten day and send a pinnace to Masangano for all the best soldier that be there so the captain of the castle send i down among a hundred soldier and I be very well use by the governor and he make i a sergeant of a Portugal company and then he march to Machimba from thence to cavo and then to malombe a great lord here we be four day and many lord come and obey we from thence we march Andrew battle make sergeant of a Portugal company to a mighty lord call Augoykayongo who stand in the defence of his country with more than sixty thousand man so we meet with he and have the victory and make a great slaughter among they we take captive all his woman and child and settle ourselves in his town because it be a very pleasant place and full of cattle and victual and be signior juan de Continbo die eight day in this town the governor sicken and die and leave a captain in his room to perform the service after we have be two month in the country of Angoykayongo we march towards cambambe which be but three day journey and come right against the serra da Prata and Prata pass the river Coanza and present overranne the country and build a fort hard by the river side here I serve two year they open the silver mine but the portugal do not like of they as yet because they yield small store of silver this new upstart governor be very cruel to his soldier so that all his voluntary man leave he and by this mean he can go no far at this time there come news by the Jesuit that the queen of England be dead and that king james have make peace with Spain then I make a petition news of the death of the queen of England 1603. to the governor who grant i licence to go into my country and so I depart with the governor and his train to the city of saint Paul but he leave five hundred soldier in the fort of cambambe which they hold still then I go with a Portugal merchant to the province of Bamba and from thence to the Onteiro or Bamba the Onteiro of congo city stand upon a mountain of congo from thence to Gongon and Batta and there we sell our commodity and return in six month to the city again then I purpose to have ship myself for Spain and thence homeward but the governor deny his word and command i to provide myself within two day to go up to the conquest again this governor have serve his three year and the citizen look every day for another out of Portugal so I determine to absent myself for ten or twenty day till the other governor come and then to come to the city again for every governor that come make proclamation for all man that be absent to come with free pardon the same day at night I depart from the city with two negro boy that I have which carry my musket and six pound of powder and a hundred bullet and that little provision of victual which I can make in the morning I be some twenty mile from the city up along the river Bengo and there I stay certain day and then pass Bengo and come to the river which be to the northward purpose to know what news be in the city for I be near the highway of congo and one of my negro inquire of those that pass and bring i word that it be certain that the new governor come not that year now I be put to my shift whether I will go to the the river Bengo the river Dande city again and be hang or to stay and live in the wood for I have run away twice before so I be force to live in the wood a month betwixt the river of dande and Bengo then I go to Bengo again to mani and pass over the river and go to the lake of Casansa the lake of Casansa here be the great store of wild beast that be in any place of angola about this lake I stay six month and live only upon dry flesh as buff dear mokoke Impolancas and robuck and other sort which I kill with my musket and dry the flesh as the savage do upon a the manner of the savage dry of their flesh hurdle three foot from the ground make underneath it a great fire and lay upon the flesh green bough which keep the smoke and heat of the fire down and dry it I make my fire with two little stick as the savage use to do I have sometime guiney wheat which my negro boy will get of the inhabitant for piece of dry flesh this lake of Casanze do abound with fish of sundry sort I have take up a fish that have skip out of the water on shore four foot long which the heathen call sombo. thus after I have live six month with dry flesh and fish and see (@) end of my misery I wrought mean to get away in this lake be many little land that be full of tree call Memba which be as light as he make a boat with a knife cock and as soft of these tree I build a jergado with a knife of the savage that I have in the fashion of a boat nail with wooden peg and rail round about because the sea shall not wash i out and with a blanket that I have I make a sail and prepare three oar to row withal this lake of Casanza be eight mile over and issue into the river Bengo so I enter the lake of Casanza fall into Bengo into my gi^gado and my two negro boy and row into the river Bengo and so come down with the current twelve league to the bar here I be in great danger because the sea be great and be over the bar I row into the sea and then sail afore the wind along the coast which I know very well mind to go to the kingdom of which be towards the north and be that night at sea the next day I see a pinnace come before the wind which come from the city and be bind to San Thomo and she come near to i the master be my great friend for we have be mate together and for pity sake he take he be three year in i in and set i on shore in the port of where I remain three year and be well belove of the king because I kill he dear and then he keep always one house the house be very long and at twelve of the clock it be full of nobleman they sit upon carpet upon the ground the house be always full of people till midnight the last king Gembe never use to speak in the day but always in the night but this king speak in the day howbeit he spend most of the day with his wife and when the king come in he go to the upper end of the house where he have his seat as it be a throne and when the king be set they clap their hand and salute he say in their language Ampola Moneya Quesinge on the southside of the king house he have a gymbe have four hundred child by his woman when the king drink he have a cup of wine bring and he that bring it have a bell strange custom of drink in his hand and assoon as he have deliver the cup to the king he turn his face from the king and ring the bell and then all that be there fall down upon their face and rise not till the king have drink and this be very dangerous for any stranger that know not the fashion for if any see the king drink he be present kill whatsoever he be there be a boy of twelve year which be the king son this boy chance to come unadvised when his father be in drink present the king command he shall be well apparel and victual tyrannical custom prepare so the youth do eat and drink afterward the king command that he shall be cut in quarter and carry about the city with proclamation that he see the king drink likewise for his diet when it be dinner time there be a house of purpose where he always eat and there his diet be set upon a like a table then he go in and have the door shut so when he have eat than he knock and come out so that none see the king eat nor drink for it be their belief that if he be see eat or drink he shall present die and this be a order with all the king that now be or shall succeed unless they abolish this cruel custom this king be so honour as though he be a god among they and be call sambe and Pongo that be god. and they believe that he can give they rain when he list so once a arrogate to give rain (@) rain here in December year when it be time to rain which be in December the people come to beg rain and bring their gift to the king for none come empty then he appoint the day and all the lord far and near come to that feast with all their troop as they go in the war and when all the troop of man be before the king the great lord come forth with his bow and arrow and show his skill with his weapon and then he have a merry conceit or jest that he speak before the king and kneel that his foot and then the king thank he for his love and in like manner they do all the king sit abroad in a great place and have a carpet spread upon the ground which be some fifteen fathom about of fine ensack which be wrought like velvet and upon the carpet his seat which be a fathom from the ground then he command he dembe to strike up which be drum so great that they can carry they and other that be very great he have also eight which be his waiter make of the great elephant tooth and be hollow and scrape light which play also and with the drum and wait they make a hellish noise after they have sport and show the king pleasure he arise and stand upon his throne and take a bow and arrow in his hand and shoot to the sky and that day there be great rejoice because sometime they have rain I be once there when the king give rain and it chance that day to rain mighty policy of the devil which make the people to have a great belief in their folly here be sometime bear in this country white child which be very rare among they some white child bear among they for their parent be negro and when any of they be bear they be present unto the king and be call Dondos these be as white as any white man these be the king witch and be bring up in witchcraft and always wait on the king. there be no man that dare meddle with these if they go to the market they may take what they listen for all man stand in awe of they the king of have four of they this king be also a witch and believe in two idol which be in the one be call the other be call checocke this last be a little black image and stand in their Mekisso and Checocke a village call Kinga a little house at a village that be call Kinga which stand in the land place of this house of checocke stand in the highway and they that go by clap their hand which be the courtesy of the country those that be craftsman as fisherman hunter and witch do offer to this idol that they may have good luck this checocke do sometime in the night and haunt some of his best belove sometime a man sometime a boy or a woman and then they be frantic for the space of three hour and whatsoever the frantic person speak that be the will of checock and they make a great feast and dance at his house there be another Mokisso which be also in Kinga and it be call Gomberi it be the name of a woman and be in a house where a old witch dwell and she be call Ganga Gomberi be a strong Mokisso that be come to abide with checocke colour of their child when they be bear the child in this country be bear white and change their colour in two day to a perfect black as for the town of mani Mayombe the author be twelve month in this country all angola circumcise Engeco this Pongo be in all proportion like a man but that he be more like a giant in stature then a man for he be very tall and have a man face hollow eye with long hair upon his brow his face and ear be without hair and his hand also his body be full of hair but not very thick and it be of a dunnish colour he differ not from a man but in his leg for they have no calf he go always upon his leg and carry his hand clasp on the nape of his neck when he go upon the ground they sleep in the tree and build shelter for the rain they feed upon fruit that they find in the wood and upon nut for they eat no kind of flesh they can speak and have no understanding more than a beast the people of the country when they travail in the wood make fire where they sleep in the night and in the morning when they be go the pongoe will come and sit about the fire till it go out for they have no understanding to lay the wood together they go many together and kill many negro that travail in the wood many time they fall upon the elephant which come to feed where they be and so beat they with their club fist and piece of wood that they will run roar away from they those pongoe be never take alive because they be so strong that ten man can hold one of they but yet they take many of their young one with poison arrow the young Pongo hang on his mother belly with his hand fast clasp about she so that when the country people kill any of the female they take the young one which hang fast upon his mother when they die among themselves they cover the dead with great heap of bough and wood which be common find in the forest the morombe use to hunt with their country dog and kill many kind of little beast and great store of pheasant but their dog be dumb and can bark at all they hang wooden clapper about their neck and follow they by the rattle of the clapper the huntsman have Petes which they whistle their dog withal these dog in all this country be very little with prick ear and be for the most part red and dun the Portugal masty dog or any other great dog be great esteem because they do bark I have see a dog sell up in the country for thirty pound in the town of mani Mayombe be a Fetisso call Maramba and it stand in a high basket make like a hive and over it a great house this be their house of religion for they believe only in he and keep his law and carry his relic always with they they be for the most part witch and use their witchcraft for hunt and kill of elephant and fish and help of sick and lame man and to forecast journey whether they shall speed well or evil by this maramba be all theft and murder try for in this country they use sometime to bewitch one another to death and when any die their neighbour be bring before Maramba and if it be a great man that die the whole town come to swear the order be when they come before Maramba to kneel and clasp maramba in their arm and to say Emeno eyge bembet Maramba that be I come to be try oh Maramba and if any of they be guilty they fall down stark dead for ever and if any of they that swear have kill any man or child before although it be twenty year past he present die and so it be for any other matter from this place as far as it be to cape Gonsalues they be all of this superstition I be twelve month in this place and see many die after this sort these people be circumcise as they be through all angola except the kingdom of congo for they be christian and those that will be swear to Maramba alone and kill the with their poison arrow I have ask the marombos whether the elephant shed his tooth or no and they say no. but sometime they find their tooth in the wood but they find their bone also when any man be suspect for any offence he be carry before the king or before mani bomma which be as it be a judge under the king. and if it be upon matter that he deny and can be prove but by their oath then the suspect person be thus swear they have a kind of root which they call Imbondo this root be very strong and be scrape into the virtue of the root Imbondo he tell i that this root make the water as bitter as gall he taste it and one root will serve to try one hundred they which have drink and make water after be clear before which if dizzine take they they cry vndoke Undoke and or priest. water the virtue of this root be that if they put too much of it into the water the person that drink it can void urine and so it strike up into the brain as though he be drink and he fall down as though he be dead and those that fall be count as guilty and be punish in this country none of any account die but they kill another for he for they believe they die not of their own natural first he come to the Tandala and bring his present as slave cow and goat then the Tandala carry he before the Portugal governor and bring two slave for the governors page before he go in then he must have a great gift for the governor which be sometime thirty or forty slave beside cattle and when he come before the governor he kneel down and clap his hand and fall down with his face upon the ground and then he rise and say I have be a enemy and now I protest to be true and never more to lift my hand against you then the governor call a soldier which have deserve a reward and give the lord to he this soldier see that he have no wrong and the lord acknowledge he to be his master and he do maintain the soldier and make he rich also in the war he command his master house to be build before his own and whatsoever he have take that day in the war he part with his master so that there be no Portugal soldier of any account but he have his negro Sona or lord they use upon this coast to fish with harp iron and wait upon a great fish that come once a day to feed along the shore which be like a Grampas he run very near the their fish on the coast. shore and drive great skull of fish before he and the negro run along the shore as fast as they be able to follow he and strike their harp iron round about he and kill great store of fish and leave they upon the sand till the fish have do feed and then they come and gather their fish up this fish will many time run himself on ground but they will present shove he off again which be as much as four or five man can do they call he Emboa which be in their speech a dog and will by no mean hurt or kill any of they also they use in the bay and river where shall water be to fish with mat which a strange kind of fish with mat be make of long Anthony isle of s. James furnish himself with fresh victual and wine which in great abundance grow in that island yea and in my opinion the best in the world whereof they carry abroad great store into diverse country and especial into England he provide there also sundry other confection and conserve of sugar which in that island be make and wrought both in great quantity and also singular excellency from this island they depart leave all the canary belong to Castille and take haven at one of the island of cape uerde call s. Anthony without have any sight thereof before they be come upon it and from thence to another call s. jacopo which command all the rest and bishop and a chaplain in it that rule and govern they and here they provide themselves again of victual these island of cape Verde be establish by Ptolomee in the table of his geography to be the beginning of the west together with the cape or promontory which he term or the island macarie or blessed which we common call fortunate in these island of cape Verde the portugal do often arrive and in those country do traffic with sundry merchandise as little ball of diverse colour glass and other such thing wherein those people do great delight and Holland cloth and cap and knife and colour clothes in exchange whereof they bring back again slave wax honey with other kind of food and cotten-cloth of sundry colour now the ship call s. Anthony hold on his course meet with the general wind * * these general wind be the etesij which blow from some northerly point unto twenty nine degree south latitude for about six month together for this cause they use to set off towards brasil to gain the wind and return to congo isle of s. elena all of eben wood the port of Loanda palmas the second course of sail to Loanda the isle of s. Thomas and then turn their prow and their sail by north and by northwest on the right hand towards the kingdom of congo and sail on-ward close with the half ship they come in twelve date and twelve night to the island of s. elena not look for the same nor think of it this island be so call because on the feast day of s. to take arm and do fight on foot their weapon be different from the weapon of all other people round about they for their bow be small and short make of wood and wrap their bow about with serpent skin of diverse colour and so smooth wrought that you will think they to be all one with the wood and this they do both to make the bow strong and also to hold it the fast their string be of little wooden twig like reed not hollow within but sound and pliable and very dainty such as the cavaliero of Portugal do carry in their hand to beat their palfreyes withal they be of a ash-colour and of a lion-tawney somewhat tend to black they grow in the country of the anzigue and also in the kingdom of Bengala through which the river Ganges run their arrow be short and their arrow slender and of a very hard wood and they carry they on their bow-hand they be so quick in shoot that hold eight and twenty shaft or more in their bow-hand they will shoot and discharge they all before the first arrow light on the ground yea and sometime there have be see diverse stout archer that have kill bird as they fly in the air other weapon also they make as axe and hatchet which they use and frame after a their weapon strange manner for the handle be short by the half than the iron be and at the low end of it there be a pommel for the fast hold of it in the hand and all cover over with the foresay skin of a serpent in the uppermost end of it be the iron very bright and shine fasten to the wood with plate of copper in the manner of two nail as long as the handle it have two edge the one cut like a hatchet and make a wound after the fashion of a half roundel the other be a hammer when they fight with their enemy or defend themselves from their arrow they be so exercise with a wonderful speed and nimbleness to manage their weapon that whirl they round about as it be in a circle they keep all that compass of the air which be before they so that when the enemy shoot and the arrow begin to fall it light upon the hatchet be so swift and vehement whirl about that it break the force of the arrow and so it be repulse then do they hang the hatchet upon their shoulder and begin to shoot themselves the pleasure of their general be put in execution that be to say either that they shall join battle or else retire or put on forward or turn to the right hand and to the left hand or to perform any other warlike action for by these several sound distinct deliver from one to another they do all understand the commandment of their captain as we here among we do understand the pleasure of our general by the sundry stroke of the drum and the captain sound of the trumpet three principal sound they have which they use in war one which be utter aloud by great rattle fasten in certain wooden case hollow out of a tree and cover with leather which they three kind of instrument use in their war strike with certain little handle of ivory another be make by a certain kind of instrument fashion like a pyramid turn upward for the low end of it be sharp and end as it be in a point and the upper end wax broad and broad like the bottom of a triangle in such sort that beneath they be narrow and like a angle and above they be large and wide this instrument be make of certain thin plate of iron which be hollow and empty within and very like to a bell turn up-side-downe they make they ring by strike they with wooden wand and oftentimes they do also crack they to the end that the sound shall be more harsh horrible and warlike the three instrument be frame of elephant tooth some great and some small hollow within and blow at a certain hole which they make on the side of it in manner of the fife and not aloft like the pipe. these be temper by they in such sort that they yield as warlike and harmonious music as the cornet do and so pleasant and jocund a noise that it move and stir up their courage and make they not to care for any danger whatsoever now of these three several sort of warlike instrument there be some big and some less for the captain general carry always with he the use of these instrument the great sort to the end that by they he may give signification to the whole camp what they shall do the particular band and troop of the army have in like manner their small sort and every captain in his several regiment have also one of the small which they strike with their hand whereupon it fall out that when they hear the sound of the general rattle or cornet or the other three kind of instrument every part of the army do present answer in the same note signify thereby that they have well understand the good pleasure of the captain and so consequent the under captain do the like neither do they only use these instrument and sound universal but also when they be in fight and in skirmish the valiant and courageous soldier go before the rest and with this kind of bell which they strike with their wooden wand they dance and encourage their fellow and by the but the king of congo be by a certain Portugal call Francisco Barbuto that be his confessor and great familiar persuade to the contrary that he shall not in any case suffer those mine to be discover signify unto he that thereby peradventure the free enjoy and possession of his kingdom may by little and little be take quite from he and therefore advise he that he will cause these skilful master to be lead and guide by some other way where he know there be no metal mine to be find which he do accord but assure it grow afterward to a great mischief for thereupon begin the great trade and traffic in that country to cease and the Portugal merchant do not great care for venture thither or dwell there any more and so consequent very few priest resort among they so that as well upon these occasion as also for other such cause afore rehearse the christian religion wax so cold in congo that it want very little of be utter extinguish but the king don Alvaro cease not still to send new ambassador into Portugal with earnest request that he may have more priest and such as be skilful in the holy scripture to maintain the catholic faith which be now almost utter forget in that realm only for want of religion by the reason of the former war and scarcity of priest and thereupon request his majesty to provide he a competent number of confessor and preacher that may be sufficient to maintain the gospel in those remote country be but late convert to Christianity moreover that he shall show unto he the sundry trial of metal which he have make and many other matter which be worthy to be know and withal that he shall proffer unto he in his name free and liberal traffic of they which heretofore be ever deny to his predecessor touch the pope that he shall likewise on his behalf kiss his foot deliver unto he his letter and recount the miserable trouble and detriment that his people have suffer for the christian faith. that he shall recommend those poor soul to his holiness and beseech he as the universal father of all christian to have compassion upon so many faithful person who because they have no priest to deliver the holy faith unto they and to administer the wholesome sacrament be now descend into a better life he be kind welcome and receive by his holiness to who he discourse the miserable estate wherein the christian people of the realm of congo do stand for want of the worship and service of God and also the small number of priest that be there to instruct they in the doctrine of the gospel and to deliver unto they the sacrament of the church especial the multitude in that country be as it be innumerable that every day resort together to be baptize instruct confess and communicate moreover he make a vow and resolve in his mind that with such store of wealth as God have bless he withal in congo which be not very small he will build a house wherein for the service of God there shall dwell certain learned man and sundry priest to instruct the youth of those country in all good language and in the art liberal and in the doctrine of the gospel and in the mystery of our salvation out of which house as it be out of a holy school there may come forth from time to time many learned man and well study in the law of God that shall be able in their own natural country tongue to awaken and raise again the faith of christ. which be now asleep and dry up in those region and thereby in process of time there will spring up many first-fruit of blessing and vigilant soul in the christian faith. hereunto he mean also to add a hospital that may be a recourse and harbour for God poor which come and sail out of strange country shall have relief and entertainment in that hostelry and the be cure and restore of their infirmity and necessity with this purpose therefore he go to Rome to obtain of his holiness a licence to erect this seminary and hospital and to beseech he also that he will grant he jubily indulgence and other dispensation that for such christian and wholesome work be requisite especial to the use and benefit of those country which be so remote from Christendom he present himself to the pope and deliver unto he his letter of credence and then declare unto he at large the tenor of his commission wherein he have a gracious audience but when the pope do understand that the kingdom of congo belong to the king of Spain he remit that matter the pope remit the whole matter to the king of Spain whole unto he @. 7 of the court of the king of congo of the apparel of that people before they become christian and after of the king table and manner of his court. in ancient time this king and his courtier be apparel with certain cloth the ancient apparel of the king of congo and his courtier make of the palmtree as we have tell you before wherewith they cover themselves from the girdlestead downward and gird the same strait unto they with certain girdle make of the same stuff very fair and well wrought they use also to hang before they like a apron certain delicate and dainty skin of little tiger of civet-cat of sabels of materne and of such like creature for a ornament and for a more glorious pomp and show they do wear upon their shoulder a certain cape like a hood upon their bare skin they have a certain round garment like a rotchet which they call Incutto reach down to their knee make after the manner of a net but the stuff of it be very fine cloth of the say palmtree and at the skirt there hang a number of threedtassel that make a very gallant show these rotchet be turn up again and tuck upon their right shoulder that they may be the more at liberty on that hand upon that shoulder also they have the tail of a zebra fasten with a handle which they use for a kind of bravery accord to the most ancient custom of those part on their head they wear cap of yellow and red colour square above and very little so that they scarce cover the top of the ancient apparel of the mean sort their head and wear rather for a pomp and a vanity then to keep they either from the air or from the sun the most part of they go unshod but the king and some of the great lord do wear certain shoe of the old fashion such as be to be see in the ancient image of the roman and these be make also of the wood of the pasme-tree the poor sort and common people be apparel from their middle downward after the same manner but the cloth be courser and the rest of their body all naked the woman use three kind of traverse or as it be apron beneath their girdlestead one be very long and reach to their heel the second short than that and the three short than both the other with fringe about they and every one of these three fasten about their middle and open before from their breast downward they have another garment like a kind of doublet or jacket that reach but to their girdle and over their shoulder a certain cloak all these several garment be make of the same cloth of the palmtree they be accustom to go with their face uncover and a little cap on the head like a man cap. the mean sort of woman be apparel after the same manner but their cloth be courser their maidservant and the base kind of woman be likewise attire from the girdle downward and all the rest of the body naked but after that this kingdom have receive the christian faith the great lord of the court their new kind of apparel begin to apparel themselves after the manner of the portugal in wear cloak spanish cap and tabbard or wide jacket of scarlet and cloth of silk every man accord to his wealth and ability upon their head they have hat or cap and upon their foot moil or pantofle of velvet and of leather and buskin after the Portugal fashion and long rapier by their side the common people that be not able to make their apparel after that manner do keep their old custom the woman also go after the Portugal fashion save that they wear no cloak but upon their head they have certain veil and upon their veil black velvet cap garnish with jewel and chain of gold about their neck but the poor sort keep the old fashion for only the lady of the court do bedeck themselves in such manner as we have tell you after the king himself be convert to the christian religion he conform his court in the court of congo now imitate the court of Portugal a certain sort after the manner of the king of Portugal and first for his service at the table when he dine or sup open in public there be a throne of estate erect with three step cover all over with indian tapestry and thereupon be place a table with a chair of crimson velvet adorn with boss and nail of gold. he always feed alone by himself neither do any man ever sit at his table but the prince stand about he with their head cover he have a cupboard of plate of gold and silver and one that take assay of his meat and drink he maintain a guard of the Anzichi and of other nation that keep about his palace furnish with such weapon as be above mention and when it please he to go abroad they sound their great instrument which may be hear about five or six mile and so signify that the king be go forth all his lord do accompany he and likewise the portugal in who he repose a singular trust but very seldom it be that he go out of his palace twice in a week he give audience public yet no man speak unto he but his lord the custom and law of congo and because there be none that have any good or land of their own but all belong to the crown there be but few suit or quarrel among they save peradventure about some word they use no write at all in the congo tongue in case criminal they proceed but slender no write for they do very hardly and seldom condemn any man to death if there be any riot or enormity commit against the portugal by the mociconghi for so be the inhabitant of the realm of congo call in their own language they be judge by the law of Portugal and if any mischief be find in any of they the king confine the malefactor into some desert island for he think it to be a great punishment to banish he in this sort to the end he may do penance for his sin then at one blow to execute he and if it so happen that those which be thus chastise do live ten or twelve year the king use to pardon they if they be of any consideration at all and do employ they in the service of the state as person that have be tame and well scool and accustom to suffer any hardness in civil disagreement there be a order that if a Portugal have any suit against a Moci-Congo he go to the judge of congo but if a Moci-Congo do implead a Portugal he cite he before the consul or judge of the portugal for the king have grant unto they one of their own nation to be judge in that country in their bargain between they and the portugal they use no write nor other instrument of bill or bond but dispatch their business only by word and witness they keep no history of their ancient king nor any memorial of the age past because they can write they measure their time general by the moon they know not the time measure by the moon hour of the day nor of (...) ight but they use to say in the time of such a man such a thing happen they reckon the (...) ance of country not by mile or by any such measure but by the journey and travel of man that go from one place to another either load or unloden touch their assemble together at feast or other meeting of joy as for example when they be marry they sing verse and ballad of love and play upon certain lute that be their manner of assembly their instrument of music make after a strange fashion for in the hollow part and in the neck they be somewhat like unto our lute but for the flat side where we use to carve a rose or a rundle to let the sound go inward that be make not of wood but of a skin as thin as a bladder and the string be make of hair which they draw out of the elephant tail and be very strong and bright and of certain thread make of the wood of palmtree which from the bottom of the instrument do reach and ascend to the top of the handle and be tie every one of they to his several ring for towards the neck or handle of this lute there be certain ring place some high and some low whereat there hang diverse plate of iron and silver which be very thin and in bigness different one from another accord to the proportion of the instrument these ring do make a sound of sundry tune accord to the strike of the string for the string when they be strike do cause the ring to shake and then do the plate that hang at they help they to utter a certain mingle and confuse noise those that play upon this instrument do tune the string in good proportion and strike they with their finger like a harp but without any quill very cunning so that they make thereby I can tell whether I shall call it a melody or no but such a sound as please and delight their sense well enough beside all this which be a thing very admirable by this instrument they do utter the conceit of their mind and do understand one another so plain that every thing almost which speech by instrument may be explain with the tongue they can declare with their hand in touch and strike this instrument to the sound thereof they do dance in good measure with their foot and follow the just time of that music with clap the palm of their hand one against the other they have also in the court flute and pipe which they sound very artificial and accord to the sound they dance and move their foot as it be in a moresco with great gravity and sobriety the common people do use little rattle and pipe and other instrument that make a more harsh and rude sound than the court-instrument do in this kingdom when any be sick they take nothing but natural physic as herb their physic and tree and the bark of tree and oil and water and stone such as mother nature have teach they the ague be the most common disease that reign among they and plagu they in winter by reason of the continual rain that bring heat and moisture with it more than in summer and beside that the sickness which here we call the french disease and Chitangas in the congo tongue be not there so dangerous and so hard to be cure as it be in our country they heal the ague with the powder of a wood call Sandale or sander whereof there be both red and grey which be the wood of aguila this powder be mingle with the oil their medicine for a ague their medicine for the headache and other grief of the body be let of blood their medicine for the french pox their purgation cure of wound of the palmtree and have anoint the body of the sick person two or three time with all from the head to the foot the party recover when their head ache they let blood in the temple with certain little box horn first by cut the skin a little and then apply the cornet thereunto which with a suck of the mouth will be fill with blood and this manner of let blood be use also in Egypt and so in any other part of a man body where there be any grief they draw blood in this fashion and heal it likewise they cure the infirmity call Chitangas with the same unction of sanders whereof there be two sort one red as we tell you and that be call Tavila the other grey and be call Chicongo and this be best esteem for they will not stick to give or sell a slave for a piece of it they purge themselves with certain bark of tree make into powder and take in some drink and they will work mighty and strong when they take these purgation they make no great account for go abroad into the air their wound also they common cure with the juice of certain herb they from those place which they have already surprise howbeit the matter fall the king of Quiloa overthrow by the portugal and drive out of the island out quite contrary for when it come to weapon he be utter overthrow and discomfit by the portugal and so flee away but they take and possess the island and enrich themselves with the great spoil and booty that they find therein they erect there also kingdom of Quiloa between this island and the firm land there be as it be a channel which at the entry westward be three hundred and forty mile broad in the midst where it be narrow over against the island of Mozambiche one hundred and seventy mile and for the rest it enlarge itself very much towards India and contain many isle within it the ship that go from Spain into India or return from India to Spain do always for the most part pass and sail in and through this channel if by time or weather they be not force to the contrary and sure this island deserve to be inhabit with a better people because it be furnish with singular commodity for it have many safe and sure haven it be water with sundry river that cause the earth to bring forth first-fruit of diverse kind as pulse and rice and other grain orange lemon citron and such like fruit flesh of all sort as hen etc. and venison as wild boar and dear and such like and all this of a very good taste and relish because the soil be very fat their fish also be exceed good the inhabitant the inhabitant of the i will of saint Laurence their weapon be pagan with some of the sect of Mahomet among they they be of the colour which the spaniard call Mulato between black and white very warlike they be and give to their weapon which be bow and arrow and dart of very light wood strengthen with iron whereof they make the head of their dart which be crooked like hook and these they will cast and throw most slight and cunning they use also target and jack that be make of certain beast skin wherewith they save themselves in fight from the blow of their enemy this island be divide among several prince that be at enmity one with another for they be in continual war and persecute one another with arm there be diverse mine of gold of silver of copper of iron and of other metal the savage people do not use to tail out of the island but only from one side to the other they go coast along the shore with certain bark that be make but of one stock of a tree which they hollow for that purpose the most part of they do not willing entertain stranger neither will they consent that they shall traffic or converse with they notwithstanding in certain port the portugal do use to trade with the islander for amber wax silver copper Rice and such other thing but they never come upon the land. in the channel before mention there be sundry land in the channel diverse land some great and some less inhabit with mahometans the chief of they be the i will of saint Christopher and then of santo Spirito and another call magliaglie and so the rest as the isle of Comora Anzoame Maiotto and some other but let we return to the sea side and prosecute the coast of the kingdom of Quiloa where the kingdom of Mombaza rich in also call Mombaza where there be a fair city with house that have many sollar furnish picture both grave and paint the king thereof be a mahometan who take upon he to resist the portugal receive the same success that happen to the king of quiloa so that the city of Mombaza spoil as Quiloa be the city be ransack and spoil by his enemy who find therein good store of gold and silver and pearl and cloth of Cotton and of silk and of gold and such other commodity this kingdom lie between the border of Quiloa and melinde and be inhabit with pagan and mahometans and yield obedience to the empire of Mohenemugi a little beyond be the kingdom of melinde which be likewise but a little one extend the kingdom of melinde itself upon the sea coast as far as the river Chimanchi and lie in the height of two degree and a half and up the stream of that river it reach to the lake Calais the space of one hundred mile within land near unto the sea along the bank of this river there be a great deal of country inhabit by pagan and mahometans of colour almost white their house be build after our fashion but there be one particularity to be admire that their mutton or sheep be twice as great as the sheep of our country for they divide they into five quarter the tail of a sheep in melinde weigh common 25. or 30. pound see Leo aser of egyptian sheep if a man may so call they and reckon the tail for one which common weigh some five and twenty or thirty pound the woman be white and sumptuous dress after the arabian fashion with cloth of silk about their neck and hand and arm and foot they use to wear lewel of gold and silver when they go abroad out of their house they cover themselves with taffeta so that they be not know but when they listen themselves in this country there be a very good haven which be a land place for the vessel that sail through those sea general the people be very kind true and trusty and converse with stranger they have always entertain and welcome the portugal and have repose great confidence in they neither have they ever offer they any wrong in any respect in the sea between these two cape of Mombaza and melinde there be three isle the first be call towards the sea this emperor stand in good term of peace with the foresay king of Quiola melinde and Mombaza by reason of their traffic together and the better to secure the intercourse and trade by sea by mean whereof they have bring unto they much cloth of Cotton and cloth of silk from diverse country and other merchandise that be well esteem in these part and particular certain little ball that be make in the kingdom of Cambaia of a kind of bitumen or clammy clay like unto glass but that it be as it be of a red colour which they use to wear about their neck like a pair of bead in stead of necklace it serve they also in stead of money for of gold they make none account likewise with the silk that be bring unto they they do apparel themselves from the girdle downward in exchange and barter of all these commodity they give gold silver copper and ivory but on the other side towards Monomotapa there be continual war yea and sometime so bloody that it be hardly discern who have get the victory for in that border there meet together two of the great and most warlike power and force that be in all those region that be to say on the party of Monomotapa there come forth into the field the amazon of who we tell you before and on the other party of Mohenemugi be the Giacchi as the moci-congi do call they but in their own tongue they be call Agagi who do the Giachas or Agagi and. bat. say that the jag come from Sierra Liona but they disperse themselves as a general pestilence and common scourge through most part of Ethiopia sometime so great afflict the kingdom of congo as you may remember neither be these people less courageous or strong than the amazon but be of a black complexion and presumptuous countenance they do use to mark themselves above the lip upon their cheek with certain line which they make with iron instrument and with fire moreover they have a custom to turn their eyelid backward so that their skin be all black and in that blackness show the white of their eye and those mark in their face it be a strange thing to behold they for it be indeed a very dreadful and devilish sight they be of body great but deform and live like beast in the field and feed upon man flesh in fight they show themselves exceed courageous and do utter most horrible shout and cry of of purpose to daunt and affright their enemy their weapon be dart and pavise of leather that cover all their whole body and so defend themselves therewith sometime they will encamp together and stick their pavise in the ground which be unto they instead a trench sometime they will go forward in the battle and shroud themselves under they and yet annoy their adversary with the shot of their dart and thus by warlike policy they do ordinary plague their enemy by endeavour with all subtlety to make they spend their shot in vain upon their target and when they see that they have make a end of shoot then do they renew the battle a fresh and drive they to flight make a cruel slaughter of they without all mercy and this be the manner which they use against their enemy and the amazon the amazon but the amazon on the other side which be very well acquaint herewithal do fight against they with other military stratagem as we have above declare and do overcome the force of their adversary with their swiftness and great skill in matter of war for they do assure themselves that if they be take they shall be devour and therefore with double courage they fight for life that they may overcome and in any case save their life from that fierce and cruel nation and in this sort do they maintain continual war always with great mortality on both side these agag dwell at the begin of the river Nilus where it run northwards out of the lake upon both the bank of the river till it come to a certain limit wherein they be bound and then westward all over the bank of the say Nilus even to the second lake and to the border of the empire of prete-gianni touch these agag I think it convenient in this place to add this which before I have omit between the confine of this Mohenemugi and prete-gianni there be sundry other petty lord and people that be of a white colour and yield obedience sometime to one of these two prince and sometime to the other they be man of a far great stature than all the rest of the people in those country towards the cape of guarda-fuy there be many place inhabit with mahometans all along the seaside of colour be white upon this shore there be diverse good haven where many good haven the ship of sundry country do traffic which follow of abassia Nilus etc be omit metal and in victual of all sort then follow the mouth or entrance into the red gulf chap. v. the voyage of sir FRANCIS Alvarez a Portugal priest make unto the court of PRETE JANNI the great christian emperor of Ethiopia in the name of jesus amen I Francis Aluarez priest of the mass which by especial I know not who translate this book I find it in master hackluyt paper and have abbreviate it where I can although it still continue very long if not tedious I also examine it with Ramusio his italian edition and in many place amend the translation in many supply it and add other thing illustrate it with marginal note etc. he that compare these relation with those of the great mogoll in sir t. roe shall find great correspondence in the uncivil custom whereinto wild majesty and barbarous greatness both here and there have degenerate both vast body rather than strong the one flourish the other fall and now retain but the struggle extreme of that giantly unwieldiness here by this eyewitness in those time observe he call he Prete or priest John follow the vulgar error grow from the relation of a priest John in Asia and by ignorance apply to this negus of Ethiopia as in my pilgrimage you may see at large I esteem his relation true in those thing which he say he see in some other which he have by relation of enlarge traveller or boast abassine he may perhaps sometime rather then even yet the lawgiver be not depart from juda i^ melech posterity have ever since reign wily wit have their fraud to make religion a stirrup of state. commandment of the king our lord don Emanuel who God have receive into his glory go with Edward Galuano a gentleman of his house and one of his counsellor which be secretary unto the king don Alfonso and unto king John his son till his die day and by king don Emanuel be send ambassador unto king Prete janni have determine to write all thing which happen unto we in this voyage and to describe the country wherein we be with the quality custom andusage thereof and how they agree with christian religion neither do I here take upon i to reprehend or approve their custom and usage but leave they whole unto the reader which be able to instruct i to praise amend and correct whatsoever they shall think good and because I may seem sometime speak of one country and eftsoon of another to confound the same together I say that we be resident in these country for the space of six year together wherein I seek to know a great part of the country kingdom and signiory of the say Prete janni and their custom and usage some by sight and some other by the report of credible person and ever as I come to the knowledge of they so I put they down in writing that be to say deliver such thing as I see as have see they and thing report as receive by hear and therefore I swear and protest upon my conscience that I will not witting report any untruth and even as I hope and trust in our lord God that my confession shall be true unto my life end so likewise shall this my present writing be true for he that lie to his neighbour lie to god. @. i MATTHEW the ambassador of PRETE JANNI be conduct by the portugal unto the haven of Maczua in the red sea and what happen to his death whereas I say that I go with Edward Galuano who God pardon true it be that the chapter as they be divide in Ramusio be express by the figure in the beginning of the line which method I have reduce to our wont form of paragraph lose so many division shall make the book to swell overmuch Maczua or Mazua Ercoco. 1520. the king of Portugal to the haven of Maczua near unto Ercoco be a port-town of Prete janni this Diego Lopez prepare a goodly and great fleet wherewith we sail into the red sea and arrive at the say island of Maczua on Monday in the octave of easter the sixteenth of the month of April in the year 1520. which island we find abandon and forsake by the inhabitant because that five or six day before they have knowledge of our come this i will be distant from the continent about two crosbow-shot whither the moor of the say island be flee with their good our fleet therefore ride between the continent and the island the Tuesday follow there come unto we one Christian and a Moor from the town of Ercoco the christian say that the town of Ercoco belong to the christian and be under the jurisdiction of a great lord call Barnagasso be subject unto Prete janni and that the inhabitant of this i will of Maczua and of Ercoco when the turk come thither flee all into the mountain but at this present they will not flee away have understand that we be christian our general have hear thus much give thanks to God that he be come to the happy knowledge of christian and this procure great favour unto Matthew which before that time be little account of 2. the day follow be Wednesday the captain of the say town of Ercoco come to speak with our general and present four ox unto he and the general give he very courteous and honourable entertainment twenty or four and twenty mile from this place stand a very high mountain with the monastery of Bisan a famous monastery thereupon which Matthew oftentimes make mention of be call the monastery of Bisan that be of the vision the friar of this monastery have knowledge of we come seven of they the Thursday after the octave to visit we who our general and all his people go on shore to meet with great joy and gladness and they seem to rejoice no less and say that they have long time look for christian because they have certain prophecy in their write book which foretell that christian shall arrive at this haven prophecy and that a pit shall there be dig after the open whereof no more moor shall dwell in that place with many other speech tend to the like purpose at all these thing the ambassador Matthew be present who the foresay friar do great honour kiss his hand and his shoulder accord to their manner and he on the other side take great delight in they also these friar say that they observe then the feast of easter and eight day next ensue and that during those eight day they use neither to travel nor to do any other work but so soon as they hear say that christian be arrive at that haven a thing which they Easter rite by monk so earnest desire they crave licence of their superior to undertake this journey for the service of God and that Barnagasso be likewise inform of our arrival but that he will not set forward out of his house till eight day after easter 3. these friar use to carry cross in their hand and other people wear they about their neck make of black wood and all our company buy of the same cross which they wear about their neck because it be a new thing and not usual amongst we while these friar abode with we the general command one Fernando diaz which understand the Arabic tongue to go and view their monastery 4. on Tuesday the four and twenty of April Barnagasso come to the town of Ercoco come of Barnagasso and give we advertisement of his arrival order be take that they shall meet one another in the midway Barnagasso come thither first but he will not come to the place which state observe be prepare for he the general be light see that he will not come thither cause the preparative to be carry before near unto the place where he stand which again to maintain his grandeur and reputation will not once stir with his people to come unto the place prepare so that the say Anthony and matthew the ambassador be constrain to return again which in the end resolve that both of they at one instant shall set forward that be to say the general and Barnagasso and so they do meet together and league confirm by oath confer in a large champain field as they sit on the ground upon certain carpet and among many discourse that they have together give thanks to God for this their interview Barnagasso take a cross of silver in his hand which be there ready for the same purpose say that he swear upon the sign of the cross upon which our lord suffer his passion in the name of Prete janni his master that he will always favour and aid the people and affair of the king of portugal and also assist his captain which shall arrive at that haven or in any other haven or land where it lay in he to aid and assist they and likewise that he will take into his protection the ambassador Matthew and other ambassador which it please the general to send into the kingdom and dominion of Prete janni with all such people and good as they shall carry with they the general swear on the other part to do the like for the subject and affair of Prete mutual gift janni and of Barnagasso there and in every place where he shall find they and that the rest of the captain and lord of the king of Portugal shall do the like the general give unto Barnagasso a fair armour and certain piece of cloth of silk and Barnagasso give unto the general a fair horse and a mule and so they depart glad and content on either part this Barnagasso have in his train two hundred person mount upon horse and mule and two thousand footman our gentleman and captain see these so good news which God have send we and that a door be open to exalt the catholic faith whereof afore we have small hope of any success all man hold this Matthew for no true ambassador but for a false man and a counterfeit whereupon they be only of opinion to put he on land and let he go his way when they have see these thing as we have say before they all rouse up themselves request the general of his favour that he will suffer they to go with the say Matthew to Prete janni in that ambassage consider that by that which they have see it be perfect know that the say Matthew be a true ambassador and albeit many request this
