bread and wine of the country we stay there because in that place they be to provide we of horse and camel to carry our good this be upon a Friday and because in this country they observe the old and the new law we rest the Saturday and the sunday to keep both those day holy Saturday and Sunday sabbath in this mean space the ambassador Matthew deal very effectual with don Rodorigo and with we all not to stay with Barnagasso although he be a great lord but that it be far better to go unto the monastery of the vision where we shall have far better dispatch whereupon give he to understand that we be not to stay with he he depart and go his way nevertheless he give we fourteen horse and ten camel to carry our good 6. we depart out of this plain near unto the town of Ercoco on Monday the thirty of April we travel not above two mile from that place but that we rest about noon drought heat barrenness near unto a river which be dry up which have no water save in certain small pit and because the country through which we be to travel be dry and barren and the heat extreme each of we carry with he his vessel and bottle of leather full of water upon the bank of this river grow many tree of diverse sort among which be sallowe and tree of bear the fruit call juiuba with other fruitless tree while we rest by this river about giuggiole noon there come a gentleman unto we name Framasgual which in our language signify the servant of the cross who in his blackness be so fair that he seem to be a gentleman a gentleman indeed and they say that he be ally to Barnagasso that be to say his wife brother before he come at we he light from his horse because this be their custom and they use it also for a courtesy the ambassador Matthew hear of his come say he be a thief and come to rob we and that we shall all betake we to our weapon and Matthew himself catch up matthew suspicious his sword and put on his head-piece framasqual hear this noise send to crave leave to come unto we and though he can not obtain it of Matthew yet nevertheless he come unto we as a man well bring up and very courteous and as one that have be conversant at the court. this gentleman have a very good horse before he and a fair mule whereon he ride and four man which go by he on foot 7. from this lodging we depart all together and the say gentleman ride upon his mule with his horse before he accost our ambassador don Roderigo with his interpreter and they ride a great while confer and devise together he be in his conference and in his answer very gentle and courteous and the ambassador take singular delight in he we a Caravan find a caravan of camel and people which come from Ercoco because they travel not but in caravans for fear of thief we lodge all in a wood where there be water be a ordinary place for caravans to lodge in and the foresay framasqual remain with we where we and those of the Caravan keep watch all night for fear of wild beast the next morning dry Rivers mountain and wood we depart from this place always travel over dry river and brook most huge mountain stand on both side of the way with great wood and tree of diverse sort most beautiful and tall the great part whereof be without fruit and among they be some which I myself know be call Tamarindi which bear cluster of fruit like unto grape tamarind which be press be somewhat black because they make wine of they some quantity whereof they carry unto all their fair as they use to make of raisins the river and way whereby we pass seem to be high and ragged which come to pass through the fury of furious storm and thunder the water of storm and tempest mingle with thunder which water hinder not the way accord as they tell we and as we see ourselves in other place like unto these the remedy be at the time of these storm to stay upon the side of some hill the space of two hour until the force of these storm be run down and how great and terrible soever these river become through the foresay shower the water be no soon fall from the say mountain strange suddenness of shower and come into the plain but it be disperse and soak up and never come unto the sea neither can we learn that any river of Aethiopia enter into the red sea but that all of they have their end as soon as they come to the low and plain field upon these mountain and rock be many beast of diverse kind as we ourselves see to many beast a kind of beast no bear coney wit elephant lion tiger buff badger Ant dear without number and other beast of all sort save two which I neither see nor hear to be in those part that be to say bear and coney there be likewise all kind of sing bird which may be imagine and also partridge quail wild hen dove and turtle in such incredible number that they cover the sun of all those sort which be in our part save that I see no pie nor cuckoo all along these river and rock I see great plenty of sweet herb which I know not save store of basil and sweet herb only basil whereof there be exceed store which yield a fragrant and sweet smell and have leaf of diverse sort 8. the time of rest ourselves be come Matthew determine to cause we anew to leave the high way and to travel with he towards the monastery of the vision through mountain and wood exceed full of high tree we depart from this lodging and travel through a more rough and craggy country matthews perverseness to lead they way-less^ way contrary to framasqual like wild beast and through far great and thick wood be ourselves on foot and our mule before we which be not able to travel the camel yell out as though they have be possess with devil it seem to we all that Matthew have bring we into this way either to make we lose our life or our good for in that place we can do no other but call upon God to help we and the wood be so dark and fearful that spirit will have be afraid to pass they we see many savage and cruel beast at noone-daye pass this way and that way without be any whit afraid of we for all this we go forward and begin to find people of the country which keep their field that be sow with millet and come far off to sow millet it upon these high and craggy mountain we see likewise many herd of goodly ox naked people and goat feed the say people which we find there be all naked and use in a manner no part of their body they be very black and be say to be christian they have their wife with they which cover their privity with a rag of cloth half tear these woman wear upon their head a kind of attire make after the fashion of a crown as black as pitch and their hair bind up in round wreath like kandle of tallow the blackness of these attire with these lock of hair fasten unto they seem a very strange thing to behold the man wear a piece of skin before their privity thus travel forward through many other wood which can hardly be pass and we ourselves light on foot and unlade our camel there meet we ten or twelve friar of the monastery of the vision among who there be four or five very age and one old than the rest who all the rest do reverence and kiss his hand and ourselves do the like because Matthew tell we that he be their bishop but afterward we know that he be no bishop matthew false David and abba but that he have the title of David which signify a warden and that in the monastery there be another above he who they call abba which signify a father be like unto a pronvinciall and in regard of their age and dryness for they be as dry as a stock they seem to be man of a holy life at the first blast the foresay friar travel through the wood to gather their millet which they have sow as also to gather up their root which be pay unto they by such as sow corn in those mountain and wood their apparel be make of dress goatskinne other wear apparel make of old yellow cotton and go barefoot from hence we depart not till our camel have rest a little afterward within the space of half a mile we come to the foot of a very rough and cragged mountain upon the which our camel inaccessible mountain can not ascend and hardly the mule without their burden and here we rest ourselves at the foot of a tree 9 the next day the ambassador Matthew command his good to be lade upon the back of negro to carry they into a small monastery half a league distant from we call saint Michael Is^o here framasqual depart from we and we come unto the monastery half dead as well for the roughness and steepness of the way as also because of the great heat s. Michael Is^o while we abode there the say Matthew come unto we with a countermand and say unto we that he have write unto the court of Prete janni and to queen Helena and to mark the patriarch and that the answer can not be return in less than forty day and that without the same we can not depart because from that place they be to furnish we and to have mule for we and for our good neither be he well assure of the performance of this but say that winter begin to approach which last about the space of three month wherein we can not travel and that therefore it be needful that we shall provide victual for ourselves for three month in the winter they travel not in these country to wit from the midst of june to the midst of September which be their ordinary winter within a their winter from june to September they fall sick short space after our arrival here our people as well Portugal as slave fall so sick that few or none escape untouched and many be sick to the point of death insomuch that they stand in need often to be let blood and to be purge among the first master John our physician fall sick which be all our human help yet it please God that he recover and from that time forward he labour for we with all his power among these matthew the ambassador fall sick also which have many medicine minister unto he and when he seem to be very well recover and strong he rise up and command his good to be carry to a town belong to the monastery of the vision where he yield up his spirit unto our lord which be the four and twenty of May dom. 10. we determine to send to request Barnagasso that he will give we some mean to return into our country to the end we may not perish in that place the friar understand this take it in very ill part and call don Roderigo aside persuade he not to send thither pray he to attend the come of the provincial which will be within abassine untrusty and therefore mistrustful ten day and if he come not they will furnish we with necessary for our journey and because they be people of small trust themselves they give no credit unto we although the ambassador have promise they to do so but seek to minister a oath unto each of we upon a crucifix that we will stay during those ten day and they likewise take a oath to perform that which they have promise @. 2 of the manner and situation of the monastery and of their holy rite time place and thing and first of this of saint MICHAEL 11. first this monastery be situate upon the crag of a mountain which be very wild seat at the foot of another huge mountain upon the which no man can ascend the stone of these rock be of the colour and grain of the stone wherewith the wall of the city of Portugal be build and the stone be very great all the ground except these stone be cover with many great wood and the great part be wild olive tree and great store of herb grow among they and the most part be basil the tree which be not olive be not know of we and all of they be without fruit in certain narrow valley which belong to this monastery be grove of orange-tree lemon cedar vine and fig of all sort as well of those which be find in Portugal as those of India and peach there be also cabbage coriander Cressis wormwood orchard the abassine not industrious the build of the monastery myrtle and many other kind of herb fragrant and medicinal and all be ill husband because they be people of no industry and the earth bring forth the thing aforesaid as it bring forth wild thing and will bring forth much better all they shall plant or sow the house of the monastery seem indeed to be a church-building be make like unto we it have about it a circuit like to a cloister and the cover above be fasten to the cover of the church it have three gate as we have to wit one chief gate in the forefront and one on each side in the midst the cover of the church and of the circuit be make of wild reed which last the life of a man the body of the church be make with isle very well wrought and the arch be very well store it seem all to be make like a vault it have a little choir behind the great altar with a cross afore it whereupon hang curtain which go from one side to another and likewise little bels. there be other curtain before the gate pass from one wall to another and they be of silk and the entry by these curtain be at three place and be fasten against the wall and at these three entrance or gate be little bell fasten to the curtain about the bigness of saint Anthony bell and a man can enter in at the gate but these bell will ring there be but one altar belong to the whole church which stand in the great chapel above the altar be a cloth of gold bear up with four pillar and the altar touch all these four pillar and the say cloth of gold be hollow like a vault it have his superaltare or consecrate stone which they call Tabuto and upon this stone stand a very great basin of copper and it be flat in the bottom and be low brim which reach unto all the four pillar of the altar because the pillar be set in a square and in the say basin be set another lesser basin and on every side of this cloth of gold that be to say behind and on both side a curtain hang down which cover the whole altar down to the ground save that it be open before bell of stone their bell be of stone that be to say long and thin stone hang up with cord and they beat they on the inside with a piece of wood and they make a very strange sound like to the sound of break bell when they be hear afar off and likewise on festival day they take basin use for bels. iron bels. basin and strike they with certain small stick which make they sound very loud they have likewise bell of iron which be not full round but have two side like unto the jacket of a Muletier whereof the one part cover he before and the other behind they have a clapper which beat the same first on the one side and then on the other and it make a sound like unto a man that dig vine they have also other bell ill-favoured make which they carry in their hand when they go on procession and ring they altogether upon festival day dark matin butter use for oil on other day they use their bell of stone and of iron they ring to matin two hour before day and they say they by heart without light only there hang a lamp before the altar wherein they burn butter for they have no oil they sing and say with a loud and harsh voice as of one that cry without any art of sing they say no verse but their speech be as it be in prose and yet they be psalm and they stand always in the church on their holiday beside their psalm they say prose and accord to the feast so be their prose and always they stand on their foot in the church they say not above one lesson at their matin with a harsh disorder and untuneable voice and like unto that wherein we pronounce the word of the jew in represent the passion of our saviour christ. and although their voice be so harsh yet they speak it run as fast as the tongue of a man can vndevour devotion procession censer and cross wag and a clerk or a friar say the same and this lesson be read before the principal gate which be end on Saturday and sunday they go on procession with four or five cross be carry upon certain staff not very high and they carry the same in their left hand because in their right hand they carry a censer and always there be so many censer as there be cross they wear certain cope of silk but rude make for they be no broad cope and other holy vestment than the breadth of a piece of damask or of any other piece of silk from the upper part to the neither part and on the breast before they have a traverse and on both side they sue a piece of other cloth of what colour soever although it agree not with the principal and of the principal cloth they let a train hang down upon the ground they make this procession in their circuit which be like unto a cloister which be end on saturdaye and sunday and festival day he which be to say mass with two other enter into the chapel and take image of our-lady out a image of our lady which they have in a old cell for in all church they have of their * * Ancone cell and they put it on a crozier turn the face towards the principal gate and this image hold her hand before her breast and they which stand on both side of it hold light candle in their hand and then they which be before it begin to sing in manner of prose and candle they go all cry and dance as if they be in a towne-dance and go before this image with this their song or prose they ring their little bell and cymbal with the like sound and as often as any chance to pass before this image they do great reverence to it which seem to the beholder to be do with great desire of devotion and so they carry in this feast cross and censer as they do in their procession when this be end which continue for a long space they salute the image and then they go unto a certain closet which stand towards the north and that part where the gospel be say accord to our mass be without the circuit wherein they make the host which they call Corbon and they carry cross censer and bell with they and from hence they the manner of minister the communion among the ethiopian great unleavened cake bring a cake of wheat-flowre unleavened new make very white and very fair of the bigness and roundness of a great paten because there be but a few people in this monastery but in other monastery and church whereof there be many they make this cake great or small accord to the number of the people for all do communicate and accord to the breadth so they make the thickness either half a finger or a whole finger or a thumb thick and they carry this cake in the little basin which be one of they that belong to the altar cover with a cloth with a cross and censer and a bell ring afore they behind the church where that choir be which they hold as a cloister no man may stand which be not in holy order * * a order sometime so strict observe that saint amb. send Theodosius to remove etc. procession with the host chalice of gold silver brass wine of raisins communion in both kind rather speak then sin but all of they must stand before the principal gate where there be another great circuit which all church have but it be not cover and there may stand any man that listen when they go in procession with this cake all they which stand in the church and in the circuit when they hear the little bell bow down their head until the bell cease which be when they set it upon the altar in the lesser basin which be set as I say before in the great basin and they cover it with a black cloth like unto a corporal this monastery have a chalice of silver and likewise in all principal church and monastery they have chalice of silver and in some they have chalice of gold. in the church of the poor people which they call the church of the balgue that be to say of the husbandman they have brazen chalice these vessel be more wide than we be but evil make but they have no cover they power into the chalice wine make of raisin in great quantity for as many as receive the body receive also the blood he that be to say this mass begin say Halleluia with a loud voice rather squeak then sing and all the company answer he and then he hold his peace and begin to bless they with a little cross which he carry in his hand and as well they that be about as those which be within begin to sing until a certain time when as one of they two that stand at the altar take a book and receive blessing of he that say mass and the other take a cross and a bell and go ring the same towards the principal gate where all the people stand in that circuit and there he read the epistle run very fast the epistle with his tongue and afterward sing return back to the altar sudden he which sing the mass take a book from the altar kiss the same and give it to he which be to say the gospel which bow down his head and ask he blessing which when he the gospel kiss the book have receive as many as stand at the altar do kiss the same a candle be bear with this book and he which read the gospel read it as the epistle be read very hasty and with as high a sound as his tongue can utter and his voice can bear and return to the altar on the way he begin likewise another song and those which go with he follow he and when they be come to the altar they give the book to kiss to he that say mass and so they put it in his place and sudden he which say mass take a censer and cense the upper part of the altar cense and they go often about it and cense the same when they have do these censing he turn to the altar and bless it very often with the cross and then he uncover the cake which he have cover in stead of the sacrament and take it up in both his hand and bless with cross lift up his right hand the cake remain in his left hand and with his thumb he make five sign like prick that be to say one in the top another in the midst another in the bottom consecration in the vulgar tongue no elevation and the other two on both side and therewithal he consecrate it in his own language with the very word that we use and he use no elevation the very same he do over the cup and lift it not up he say over the same the very word that we use in his own tongue and he cover it and take the sacrament of the bread in his hand and break it in twain and of the part that be in his left hand he break a little morsel of the top of the same and the other two piece he lay the one upon the other the priest take this little morsel for himself and likewise take part of the sacrament of the blood and afterward he take the basin with the cover sacrament and give it to he which have say the gospel and likewise he take the chalice with the sacrament and give it to he which read the epistle and sudden they give the communion to the priest which stand at the altar receive a small piece of sacrament out of the basin which a deacon hold in his right deacon and sub-deacon the wine administer with a spoon holy water hand and while the deacon give the same a sub-deacon take of the blood in a spoon of gold of silver or of copper accord to the abiltie of the church and give it unto he which receive the sacrament of the body in very small quantity and on the other side stand another priest with a little vessel of holy water and pour into the palm of his hand which receive the communion a little of that water wherewith he wash his mouth and afterward swallow it up this be do they all go to the altar with this sacrament before the first curtain and in this sort they give the communion to they which stand there and afterward to all those of the other curtain and last to the secular people which stand at the principal gate as well man as woman if the church be such that woman may be suffer to come thither at the give of the communion and at all other divine service all stand upon their foot and when stand they go to receive the communion all of they come with their hand lift up before their shoulder with the palm of their hand spread abroad before they and when any man receive the sacrament of the blood he receive of that holy water as I say before and also wash general all such as be to receive the communion before the mass use to wash their hand with water which be place in all church and monastery for this purpose the priest which say the mass and they which stand with he at the altar the communion be end return unto the altar and wash the basin wherein the sacrament be put with the water remain in the vessel which they say be holy water this water be put into the chalice and he which say mass drink it up all this do one of the minister of the altar take a cross and a sacring bell and begin a little song go to the principal gate where the epistle and gospel be read and where they cease to give the communion and all they which be in the church and without the church incline their head and take their leaf say that this be the blessing and that without this no man may depart on Saturdays and sunday no man may depart without the blessing short mass and festival day in all church and monastery they use to give holy bread. the form of ceremony which this little monastery use which have not above twenty or five and twenty friar be observe in all other monastery and church the service of the mass except the procession be very short because the mass in the week day be end almost as soon as it be begin 12. the manner how they make the cake aforesaid be this the house where they make manner of make the cake it in all church and monastery be place as be say before towards that part where the gospel be say without the church and the cover circuit which be as a cloister in all church and monastery and they use the other circuit which be without and not cover as a churchyard this house be as big as the choir behind the great altar and somewhat big and in all church and monastery they have nothing else in that house but that which serve for house of purpose for it this business to wit a staff to beat the corn out of the ear and a instrument to grind the meal because they make it very white as be convenient for such a purpose because they make not the say sacrament with meal or wheat wherein woman have put their hand they have earthen platter wherein they knead the meal and they make the Dow hard no woman may touch the meal the oven than we make it they make a little oven like a still to still water and upon the same a plate of iron and some church have it of brass and some other of brick which be round with a large compass and they put the fire underneath it and when it be hot they make it clean with a course cloth and then lie a good piece of this Dow upon it and spread it abroad with a wooden knife as broad as they will have it and make it very round and when the cake be bake they take it away lay it aside and make another after the same fashion and this second cake after it be likewise ready they take the former and lay it thereupon to wit that side which be uppermost they turn downward and so both these two cake be lay together as they be one cake and they do nothing all the while but turn and toss they upon this plate until they be bake beneath and above and on every side and so they make as many as they will in the same house be also the raisin wherewith they make their the raisin holy bread. wine and the instrument wherewith they press the same in these house also be the holy bread make which be distribute on the Saturdays and sunday and other festival day and when their great feast be hold as Christmas Easter and our lady of August they fetch out this sacrament of bread with a vestment * * palio bell and cross very devout and before they enter into the church therewith they go once about the circuit which be like unto a cloister but when it be not holy day they go straight into the church the Saturday before ascension day when we use to say our litany these friar make a procession and because we be stranger in the rogation or gang procession country it seem a goodly sight unto we and it be on this wise they take cross and a consecrate stone of the altar with great reverence cover with cloth of silk and a friar which carry it on his head be likewise whole cover with the like cloth of silk they carry also book bell censer and holy water and go into certain field sow with millet and there they make their devotion with cry after the manner of litany and with this procession they return unto the monastery and when we ask they wherefore they do this they say because the worm do eat their corn therefore they go to sprinkle they with holy water and pray to God to take they away he which say mass have no other difference sprinkle worm with holy water to kill they in his apparel from a deacon and sub-deacon save a long steal slit in the midst so that he may thrust his head through it and behind and before it reach down to the ground the friar which say mass wear their hair long and the priest wear it not but be shear and so they say mass and be always barefooted and no man may come shod into the church and barefooted in imitation of Moses for this purpose they allege that which God say unto Moses put off thy shoe for the place where thou stand be holy ground 13. in this monastery of saint Michael where we be we say mass every day not in the monastery but in the circuit which be like a cloister because in this country they say but one mass a day in every church or monastery the friar come unto our mass with great devotiou but one mass a day as they seem and supply our want with censer and incense because we have bring none with we and they think it a ill thing to say mass without incense and they say that all thing seem well unto they save that they think it not commendable for one priest alone to say mass because among they they use not to say mass except they be three or five or six and all these stand at the altar also they mislike that we go with many priest necessary to our mass shoe and spit in church mislike the great fast which these religious man use in fast no eat till sun be down our shoe into the church and much more when we do spit in the church but we excuse ourselves say that this be the fashion in our country and so we say mass every day until Trinity Sunday and when the Monday after the say trinity Sunday come than they will suffer we to say no more mass in the morning and we marueil thereat and not well please and have at that instant no interpreter to learn wherefore they will not suffer we to say mass at length we understand that which by experience afterward we see to wit that they observe the old testament in their fast for they fast very strait in the lent which they begin the Monday after the Sunday of which be ten day before our Shrovetide and so they make their lent of fifty day and say that they take those day before for the saturdaye on which they do not fast and their fast be to eat at eventide and every day they receive the communion and therefore they say not mass but in the evening and when mass be do they receive the communion and then go to supper and like as they have these fifty day of fast so they take as many day after easter and Whitsuntide wherein they fast not at all and when it be not fast day they say mass in the morning and all those day they eat flesh without observe any one of they and say mass in the morning and strait way go to dinner because they fast not when this time be end and Trinity Sunday past all the clerk and friar be bind to fast every day save saturdaye sunday and this fast continue until Christmas day and because they fast all they say mass at night allege for proof hereof the supper of Christ how that it be fast time and almost night when he consecrate his body but common the lay-people as well man as woman be bind to fast weekly on wednesday and friday from trinity Sunday until Advent and from Christmas day till the purification of a fast from Trinity Sunday till Christmas lay fast till Advent fast of Nin^ue the virgin Marie which they call the feast of saint Simeon they fast not at all the three day after the purification be not Saturday nor Sunday be a exceed straight fast for the clerk friar and lay-people for they say that they eat but once in all these three day and they call it the fast of ninive these three day be end until the beginning of Lent they fast again as they do before until the feast of the holy trinity in the Advent and all the lend the clerk the friar the laity the man and woman small and great sound and sick do all fast and likewise from easter unto Trinity Sunday and from Christmas unto the purification the mass be say in the morning because there be no fast all the rest of the year it be say in the evening because they fast the monastery where we bury Matthew be distant from this wherein we abode three mile space of very bad way and it be call the monastery of the vision of jesus it be seat upon the point the situation and form of the monastery entitle the uision of jesus dreadful valley form of the church of a rock exceed high and from every part as a man look downward there be a valley which seem to be as deep as hell. the church of the monastery be very great of body and great in revenue and be very well dispose and govern it be build with three great ally or walk which be very fine make with their arch and their vault which seem to be make of wood because they be all paint over so that a man can perceive whether the church be build of stone or of wood it have two walk place in form of a cloister about the body of the church which be both cover and paint with the picture of the apostle and patriarch and with the story of all the old testament and with sa (...) George on horseback which be to be see in all their church and likewise there be in the same a great piece saint George on horseback in all their church saint in arras image in a vestry of arras wherein be weave a crucifix our (@) the apostle the patriarch and prophet and every one have his title or name in latin which show that the same work be nor make in those country there be also many ancient image which stand not upon the altar because it be not their fashion but they keep they in a vestry lap up with many book and they bring they not forth but on holiday in this monastery there be a great kitchen with all thing thereto appertain with a great room to dine in where they fate altogether and they eat three and three in a treen dish which be not very deep but plain like unto a wooden platter their diet be very homely their hard diet bread be make of millet and of barley and of another seed which they call Tafo which be small and black this bread they make round about the bigness of a apple of Adam and they give three of these to each one and unto the no (...) es they give three of they between novice two and I wonder great to think how they can live with so little a quantity likewise they give each of they a little fresh fish without oil or salt. of the selfsame diet they send so many age and honourable friar towards who they use great reverence which they abode six year in Aethiopia come not unto the dine hall and if any man ask i how I know this I answer that beside that which I see when we bury Matthew the great part of the six year which we abode in Aethiopia our lodging be not far from the say monastery so that I depart oftentimes from our house upon my mule and come in the evening to the monastery and for the most part I go to pass the time with the friar and principal at their festival time and I learn many thing of they concern their affair revenue usage and custom a hundred friar be common in this monastery and the most part of they be very age and as dry as a stock few of they be young there be also many little child of eight year old and upward which they bring up and many of they be jame and blind this monastery be wall round about and have no entry but by two gate which be always shut 14. this monastery be the head of six monastery which stand about the same among these six other cell subject to this monastery of the nine and twenty or thirty mile off and all of they be subject and yield obedience unto this monastery in every one of they there be a David that be to say a warden place by the abbot or provincial and that monastery which have a David that be to say a warden be subject to the abbot which be as (...) (@) I always hear report that there be about three thousand friar in this monastery and because I doubt much thereof I come once to their feast of our lady in August to see how many be assemble there together and sure I take pleasure when I behold the riches of this place in a certain procession which they make and in my judgement the friar be not above three hundred and the great part of they be old man I see a great circuit which this monastery have about two place which be like to cloister which circuit be open but at that time it be all cover over with great and small clothes of gold velvet of Mecca all long piece sew one unto another to hang round about that circuit through which they make a goodly procession all clad in cope of the say cloth of gold but make ill-favoured as I have say before they carry fifty cross of silver small and bad make and as many brazen censer when they say mass I see a great chalice of gold and a spoon of gold young friar earn their live wherewith they give the communion and of the three hundred which be assemble in this monastery there be very few of my acquaintance I inquire of certain of my friend wherefore see so many friar belong to this monastery as they say so few be present at so great a solemnity they answer i that the number be great than they look for because they be divide in other monastery church and fair to earn their live as long as they be young for they can be maintain in the monastery but by their own industry and when they be so old that they can travel they come to end their day at this monastery this day I see seventeen young man take into order in this monastery be the burial of a abbot or provincial call Philip and his work of Philip a erroneous saint holiness be very great for they say that there be once a king or Prete janni which ordain that they shall not keep the Saturday holy throughout all his kingdom and dominion and this Philip repair immediate unto he with his brethren and with many book and show he how God have command that the sabbath day shall be observe and that whosoever observe it not shall be stone this man dispute this question before all the religious man of Aethiopia and be commend before the king and therefore they take he to be a saint and they observe a holiday unto he every year in the month of july which they call the Fascar of Philip which sinifi the testament or memory of saint philip. holy day to he and therefore the inhabitant of this country and monastery be more infect with this jewish heresy than any other part of the dominion of Prete janni although all of they be in part infect but these be more than any other I have see they with my eye seethe fish on the sabbath and bake bread also and on the sabbath in this monastery they make no fire at difference of rite all on the Sunday follow they make ready all thing needful for their diet and I come twiceto this Fascar of Philip at which time they receive i with great honour and at this feast yearly they kill many ox and at one of they I see they kill thirty and at another ox offer to Philip feast eight and twenty which be offer by the inhabitant their neighbour for devotion unto this Philip and they give this flesh raw to all the people that come to the Fascar without any bread at all the friar eat no kind of flesh they send i yearly two great and fat quarter of beef with much bread and wine of honey which likewise the friar drink not in the monastery but when they be abroad with we friar eat no flesh wine of honey or Mead. no woman nor beast of the female sex may come near this monastery portugal they drink wine and eat flesh if they be but one alone but if they be two they do it not for fear the one of the other this monastery and all the rest which be subject to it observe a order that no woman may enter into it nor she mule nor cow nor hen nor any other beast of the female kind this I both learn and see myself for when I come thither a crossbow shoot distant from the monastery they come to take my mule not suffer i to come with she to the monastery and they send she to a house of they call Giangargara where Matthew die they kill their cow and hen a certain distance from the monastery I see but one cock in the monastery with two bell at his leg without hen and they say that they keep he to crow at the time of their matin if any woman come into the house they know it for oftentimes I ask certain child which be bring up there who son they be and they name unto i the friar for their father and so I know the young friar to be call the son of all the old friar @. 3 of the husbandry of this country and how they preserve themselves from wild beast and of the revenue of the monastery their departure strange river mountain ape barnagassoe entertainment Barua polygamy marriage divorce baptism and circumcision their brand and bury 15. these friar or those of other monastery their subject may very well play the good husbandman and may cherish up tree vine and orchard with neglect of husbandry their diligence yet nevertheless they do nothing at all and the soil be good and fit to bring forth every thing as may be gather by that which be wild and savage but they till nought else but field of mill and keep swarm of bee and as soon as night be come they go not once out of their house because of the wild beast which be in that fear of wild beast country and they which keep their millet have their house very high from the ground upon tree where they lodge in the night there be about this monastery and in the valley of these mountain great herd of cattle keep by arabian moor which go forty or fifty together with their wife and child and the captain among they be a Christian because the cattle which they keep be christian gentleman of the country of Barnagasso the moor receive none other wage for their pain but the Millie and butter which they get of the cow and therewithal they sustain themselves their wife and their child certain moorish herdsman time it chance we to lodge near these arabian and they come to know of we whether we will buy any cattle and offer they unto we at a reasonable price it be report that they be all thief favour by the lord which be owner of the cattle and that man travel not among they but in great caravans the revenue of this monastery of the vision be very great as I see and understand first the revenue of this monastery very great this mountain whereon this monastery be seat contain thirty mile in compass whereon they sow much millet barley Rye and Tafi and of all this they pay a portion unto the monastery and also for the pasture of their cattle in the valley of these mountain be great town and the most part of they belong unto the monastery and within one or two day journey there be very many and sundry place which belong unto the monastery and they be call the of the monastery which signify privilege place don Roderigo the ambassador and I on a certain time travel towards the court depart from this monastery five day journey at the least and come to a certain people place call Zama where we rest all Saturday and Sunday in a small village where there be to the number of Zama twenty house there they tell we that this place belong unto the monastery of the vision and that there be one hundred place all belong to the monastery and therewithal show we many of they and tell we that these one hundred place pay unto the monastery every three year one horse apiece which amount to thirty four horse every year rend horse and to understand the same the better I inquire of the alicasin of the monastery which signify the anditour or steward of the house because he receive and disburse the alicasin this agree to antiquity all thing and he tell i that it be true that they pay the say horse and I inquire of he why the monastery require so many horse consider that they use not to ride he say that they pay not the horse but cow in their stead that be to say fifty cow for one horse and this tribute of horse continue all the time that fifty cow pay in exchange these place be in the king hand which endow the monastery with these jurisdiction and afterward the inhabitant of those country compound with the monastery and change the payment of horse into so many cow beside which they pay many other tribute of corn this monastery have above fifteen day journey distant within the kingdom of tigrimation a great territory which be sufficient to make a dukedom which be call Adetyeste which pay yearly sixty horse and infinite tribute and rent there go Adetyeste always unto this territory above one thousand friar of this monastery because therein be many church of these friar some be very good reverend and devout and other some as bad and evil condition beside the tribute of the foresay horse which be pay unto the say monastery be many other place which appertain only to the king which pay tribute of horse accord to their ancient custom and these be place which frontier upon the a excellent breed of horse in Egypt country of Egypt from whence come good and stately horse and other place of the arabian which likewise have good horse but not so good as those of Egypt from this monastery of saint Michael we depart the fifteen of the month of june some go on foot there be also but few people to carry our good and the ox be not able to travel through the wood and thicket because all the way be rocky and craggy the gunner with their skourer be leave behind and the barrel of gunpowder and they have not travail past two mile great while look when they will send for we to have audience at length we be send for and enter into the first gate we find three man like unto porter have each of they a staff in their hand and when we will have enter they will not suffer we say that we shall give they some pepper where they keep we out for a long while at length be enter in at the first gate we come to the second where we find three other porter which seem to be man of more account who make we to stand wait there above half a hour upon a little straw and the sun so scorch we that we be almost smother with heat and we shall have stay there much long have not the ambassador send he word in choler either to admit he into his presence or that he will return again unto his lodging than one more honourable than the rest come and tell we that we may come in the say Barnagasso be in a great house in a low room the ambassador have audience of Barnagasso no house with story because in those country they build no house with story and he lie upon a couch as his manner be compass with certain curtain which be very homely he have sore eye and his wife sit at his head here after due salutation the ambassador offer he his physician to cure he to who he answer that he need no physician and that he reckon of he then the ambassador beseech he of his courtesy to furnish he with mean for the performance of our voyage Barnagasso reply that he can not give he mule and that we must buy they ourselves but that he will furnish we with all other thing and will send a son of he with we which shall accompany we to the court of Prete janni and so he dismiss we 19 be come forth out of the house where Barnagasso remain they cause we to sit down upon certain mat spread upon the ground whither they bring we a treene between these two town be a very goodly country that be to say very well manure and field of wheat of millet of barley of chich-peason of lentils and of many other kind of grain which be in that no pain although they receive great damage by they in their corn but they know not how to kill they 20. in this town of Barua where we be and where afterward we abode a long time be Barua three hundred house and the great part of the inhabitant be woman for in this town be keep as it be a court for many respect one be because it be never without people belong to the court of Prete janni and those which come thither have no woman with they use the woman of the town as their concubine another be because here the court of Barnagasso common woman be keep where for the great part of the year he make his residence and continual have in his stable above three hundred horse and as many more which daily come thither to dispatch their business with Barnagasso in regard of their affair and suit and few or none of they will be without their concubine and hence it be that here many light young woman settle their abode which after they be grow old betake themselves to another kind of life for in this town there be a great market every Tuesday where Tuesday market there be three or four hundred person meet together and all the old woman and young lass carry measure in their hand wherewith they measure in the market all the corn and salt that be sell and in this sort they earn their live and moreover they lodge those that remain in the town and keep the good which be leave unsold until the next market day and all thing else in like sort and because there be many woman in this town those which be rich polygamy use and how punish and have the mean take two or three wife neither be it forbid they by the king nor the justice but only by the church because all such as have above one wife may not come within the church much less communicate or receive any sacrament of the church and be hold for excommunicate person during the time we abide in this place a cousin of i and myself lodge in the house of a man who name be ababitay which have three wife which be all of our acquaintance ababitay our author host have three wife and by they seven and thirty child and our good friend and he tell i that he have seven and thirty child by they and that no man have forbid he their company save that the church admit he not to the communion before our departure he have dismiss two of they and hold himself to one only namely to she which he have last marry and for all this he be restore to all the sacrament and license to come to church as though he have never have but one wife and therefore there be many woman in this town because rich man and courtier take two or three marriage unstable or more of they accord to their pleasure their marriage be very unstable for they will be divorce for a small trifle I have see many of their woman marry and myself be present at a certain marriage rite of marriage make without the church which be celebrate on this manner in a court before a house be place a litter or couch and they cause the bridegroom and the bride to sit down thereon and there come three priest which begin to sing with a loud voice haleluia and thus sing as it be certain verse they go thrice about the say couch or litter afterward they cut off a lock of hair from the bridegroom crown and as much from the same place of the bride head bathe the say hair in wine make of honey and the bridegroom hair they lay upon the head of the bride and the bride hair they lay upon the head of the bridegroom in the same place where they be cut off and upon the same they cast holy water and afterward they begin to make a feast after the manner of marriage and at night the say marry person be accompany home unto their house and for the space of one month no man enter into that house save only one man which be the bridegroom godfather who remain all the month with they and the month end he depart home and if the bride be a woman of account it be five or six month before she come out of her house and she wear continual a black veil before her face and if she be with child before six month she lay off her veil and if she prove not with child within six month space she lay it aside 21 moreover I have see Abuna Marco who they call their patriarch use certain Marco the patriarch his marriageblessing blessing in the church that be to say before the principal gate where they cause the bridegroom and the bride to sit down on a litter about which he go with incense marriage be make they be conclude by contract or covenant in this sort if thou leave i or I thou he which shall be the cause of this division shall pay such or such a penalty which penalty be appoint accord to the quality of the person either in so much gold or silver or so many mule or so many kine or goat or so many clothes or so many measure of corne. and if any man will divorce himself immediate he seek a occasion wherefore he may do so and by divorce these mean few do fall into those penalty and thus they divorce themselves as well the husband as the wife and if any observe the order of matrimony they be the priest which can be divorce priest can and husbandman will not be divorce and also the husbandman which love their wife because they be a great help unto they in keep of their cattle and bring up their child and in-digging their field and weed of their corn and because they find all thing needful make ready when they come home at night and therefore by reason of these commodity they continue marry as long as a Pardai amount to a ducat double iniquity adulterous and incestuous they live and whereas I have say that in their contract they put down penalty the first Barnagasso who he know who name be Dari be divorce from his wife and pay for a penalty one hundred ounce of gold which be one thousand Pardai that be to say one thousand ducat and be marry to another and his wife marry unto a gentleman call aron brother to the say Barnagasso and both these brethren have child by this woman who we ourselves know these be great lord and be brethren to the mother of Prete janni who all of we do very well know and we Portugal know also romana orgue a noble lady the sister of Prete janni which be marry unto a great and noble young gentleman and in our time she be take to wife the wife of his brother Dori marvel not awhit thereat because it be the manner of this country and seem not any strange thing that a brother shall lie with his brother wife for they say that the brother raise up seed unto his brother as be accustom scripture abuse 22. any man may circumcise that list without any ceremony only they say that-they find it write in their book that God command they to be circumcise and let no man circumcision marvel which hear this for they circumcise woman as well as man which thing be not use in the old law. they baptize in manner follow man child they baptize within baptism forty day and the female sex after sixty and if they die before they go without baptism and I often tell they and in sundry place that herein they commit a great error and that they do against the gospel of our lord which say that which be bear of the flesh be flesh and that which be bear of the spirit be spirit Wherewto they answer i very often that the faith of the mother and the communion which she receive while she be with child of they be sufficient for they and this baptism they minister in the church as we do but not in not in the fount the christen fount use the sacrament of the chrisom nor the oil of extreme unction their form of baptism be not so long as that which be use in the archbishopric of Braganca but seem to be about the length of that which be use in the church of Rome at the time when they will baptize the infant with this water one which be there as a godfather rite of baptism take the infant out of the hand of the midwife which bear the same and he take it under both the arm and so hold it hang down and the priest which baptize it have the pot in his one hand and sprinkle the water upon the child with the other hand he wash it say the same word that we use to wit I baptize thou in the name of the father and of the son and of the holy ghost they always minister this sacrament on the Saturday or on the Sunday and it be do in the morning at the mass and all that they baptize as well male as female they cause to receive the sacrament of the lord supper in small quantity the baptise do then also communicate and by force of water they constrain they to swa low it touch this point I say that this communion be very dangerous and nothing necessary and whereas I have say that they pour oil upon the crown of the child head this be because all the infant be bring to be baptize with their head shave and those mark which we see certain negro slave to have on their nose and between their eye or on their eyebrow be not make with fire nor for any token of christian religion the cause why they mark themselves with a iron in the face and how they do it but only for a bravery with a cold iron and they say that these mark be very beautiful to behold and there be woman which be very skilful in make these mark and they make they in this sort they take a head of garlic which be great clean wash and somewhat stale and they lay it to the eye or to the other part where they will make the mark and then they cut round about it with a sharp knife to wit about the say head of garlic and then they widen the say cut and power upon it a little wax and upon the wax they clap a little dough and bind it with a cloth and so bind they let it alone for one night and this mark remain as long as the party live which seem to be make with fire because the colour of that mark be black than any part of their body when any one die I have see they carry as well person of honour as they of the middle and poor degree all after one sort first at the time of their death they be not accustom their manner of burial to light candle but after they be dead they bestow upon they much cense and wash they and then wind their whole body in linen cloth and if it be a person of honour they lay a oxhide over the street spread it over the litter and the priest come to carry he to the burial say a short service and they take he and carry he to the church with a cross a censer and holy water run as fast as ever they can so that a man can overtake they and when they be come to church they bring not the dead corpse into the same but no service for the dead but the gospel of saint John no or mass for the dead Ali comer receive straight way set he down at the grave neither say they any of our service for he that be to say no service for the dead nor any psalm of David nor of job. and when I inquire what it be which they say they answer i that it be all the whole gospel of saint John which be end they put the corpse into the grave but first they cense it and sprinkle it with holy water neither say they any or mass at all for the dead and much less for devotion of any man live only they say one mass a day in every church and and no man shall escape he yet bless be God it be not perceive that he do any more harm and we at the same time go often on hunt near the same place and never find any lion we find indeed panther about they have a custom how they keep their cattle from the wild beast in the night to enclose themselves ten twelve or fifteen of they in a court all wall and strong enclose which court have not past one gate and herein they shut up their cow of which they have their milk and butter they shut up likewise their small cattle as seepe mule and ass and beside the lock up of their gate in the and of this town of Barua and the other town adjoin be the man which go to sow millet unto the mountain of the vision and they go thither three month before the geverall winter and the cause why they go thither be two the first be because they be near to the sea whereby all victual be transport to Mecca to ziden to Toro and to all Arabia and India and have many sort of corn they seek a fit place for the vent thereof the second cause be for two winter that in this country there be two winter divide into rainy storm neither do the corn grow but with abundance of water therefore they depart from Barua and go to sow their corn in the mountain of the vision where at that time it be winter which last all the time of February March and April and the self same winter be in another country which be under the government of Barnagasso call lama distant from the mountain of the vision at least eight day journey at this very time also it be winter in another country which be winter and summer strange dispense call doba be thirty day journey from this place and because these seed of millet require much rain therefore these winter be out of the ordinary season of the place above mention they go to sow they where it rain and so they make their profit of the two foresay winter in this town of Barua be two very great and goodly church wherein be many priest two great church one for man and one for woman the one fast by the other one be for the man call saint Michael and the other for the woman call the church of the apostle that be of saint Peter and saint Paul they say that the church churchyard and be compass about with high wall and they make the sacrament that be to say the bread for both of they in one house and both of they say their mass at one and the self same time and the be twenty priest and ten or twelve friar continual resident and I never see church of priest where there be abundance of friar not friar nor monastery of friar where there be any priest for the friar be so many that they cover the world both in the monastery the church on the ware and in all market and last in all place be friar 26. the priest marry with one wife and observe matrimony better than the laiety they priest best observer of matrimony continue always in house with their wife and child and if perhaps their wife die they marry no more and likewise if the priest die his wife marry not a second husband but she may become a nun if she will and if a marry priest lie with another woman he enter no more into the church neither be he partaker of the revenue thereof but become as it loss of order or degradation be a layman and this I know to be true for I see a priest accuse before the patriarch that he have lie with another woman and I hear he confess the fault and straight way the patriarch command that he shall never carry cross more in his hand nor come any more into the church but shall become a layman and if any priest be a widower do marry again he become a layman as it give order and order be give to these no bishop priest twice in the year as I will hereafter declare have myself oftentimes be present at their take of order in all these country the churchyard be people refuse to sell we any say that they be afraid of Barnagasso because he himself will have the sell of their mule the custom of all the realm of Prete janni be that there be no other coin money currant but only gold and it the usual coin through all the kingdom of Prete janni pass from man to man by weight and the principal weight be a ounce which make ten pardaos or ten cruzado the next be half a ounce and the least money be a dram and ten dam make a ounce and the value of a dram be accord to a dram in the kingdom of Portugal or in India their gold differ in fineness three quarter of a ducat so that one ounce of gold be sometime worth but seven ducat and a half moreover the say Barnagasso have command that none but himself and his officer shall keep any weight to weigh wicked policy gold withal and whosoever will buy and sell must come to entreat they for their weight and by this mean he and his factor understand to who hand the gold come which gold afterward he will take from and because all the monastery be of one order therefore they be obedient unto the monastery that be next they from whence they receive their habit. these nun enter not into the church but do as other woman do the number of they be very great and in a manner as great as the number of the friar they say that some of they be woman of a very holy life again some of they have child the habit which the priest wear be little differ from the habit of the people for it be make all of one cloth and they be gird like the common people their difference be in that they carry a cross always in their hand and their head be always shave and contrariwise the cross and shave lay-people wear their lock long and the priest shave not their beard but the layman be shave under the chin and cut off their moustache there be also certain other priest call debetera which be as much to say as canon these be priest of great church as a man will say of cathedral or collegiate church and these man go very well apparel so that they well declare what manner of man they be and these go not up and down the market as the rest do 30. the state of this Barnagasso although he be a great lord and have the title a innumerable company of locust which eat and consume all the corn and tree and the number of these creature be so great as it be locust like those of Egypt incredible and with their multitude they do be general the mischief by they through all the province and realm of Prete janni they will perish with famine and it be impossible to inhabit the same but one year they destroy one province great guard. as soon as the people of these captain understand damute that they be banish into those country they rise up in arm and make as many more new captain begin to make war and break the peace that the thing belong unto God after what manner soever they be do seem always to be well do this ceremony be end they begin to go about the church with five and twenty cross and five and twenty censer carry their cross in their left hand as it be standard and the censer in their right hand cast incense upon they without any spare and upon the step where we stand be two great latton basin gild and wrought about full of a kind of incense sweet than that which be bring into these part and as often as they pass by they cast great quantity thereof into the censer and they which go about in procession be clad in very rich cope and hood make after their fashion and so be they which dance and sing 102. the nine and twenty of january the ambassador and all the frank whereof some be come to this court before we with all his company go to visit the Abuna mark because he have not as yet speak with he we find he as before sit upon a couch the ambassador will have kiss his hand but he will not suffer he but give he the cross to kiss which he always carry in his hand and so he do to all the rest as soon as we be set the ambassador say that he be come to visit he in the name of the grand captain and pray he to pardon he that he come no soon to he because they will not suffer he to visit any body the Abuna answer he that he ought not to marvel thereat for it be the custom of that court not to suffer any stranger to go unto any man house and that this be not by the consent of the Prete which be a good and godly man but of the courtier which be malicious the ambassador tell he that the king of Portugal be inform of his bounty and holiness by his brother Matthew and also by other and that therefore he beseech he to keep the Prete janni constant and immutable in this enterprise of chase and destroy of the moor the Abuna answer that he be no saint but a poor sinner and that Matthew be none of his brother but be a merchant and his friend and although he come with lie yet be it manifest that his come be ordain by God see it turn to Matthew be a merchant so good service and profit etc. @. 15 a discourse of PETER COVILLAN of the pretes gift and present and the portugal quarrel and their licence to depart out of the country 103. whereas I have speak often in this book of Peter de Covillan be the story of Peter Covillan a honourable person and of great credit with Prete janni and all the court it be convenient that I shall declare how he come into this country and the cause thereof as he have oftentimes tell i himself but first I will say that he be my spiritual son and that I have oftentimes confess he because in three and thirty year while he live in this country he tell i that he never be confess because confession not use here the custom here be not to keep that secret which be utter in confession and that therefore he go into the church when he confess his sin unto god. his beginning be thus he be bear in the town of Covillan in the kingdom of Portugal and be a boy he go into his life in his youth Castille and get into the service of don Alfonso duke of sivile and when the war begin between Portugal and Castille he return home with don John de gusman brother to the say duke which place he in the house of Alfonso king of Portugal who for his valour present make he a man at arm and he be continual in that war and serve also abroad in France after the death of king Alfonso he be one of the guard of the king don John his son until the time of the treason when he send he into Castille because he speak the castilian tongue very well to spy out who be those gentleman of his subject which practise there against he and return out of Castille he be send into Barbary where he stay a time and learn the arabian tongue and be afterward send to conclude a peace with the king of tremizen and be return he be send again to the king which restore the bone of the infant don Fernando at his return he find that the king don John desire by all mean that his ship shall find out the spicery have determine to send by land certain man to discover as much as they may and Alfonso be choose for Alfonso this enterprise a citizen of castle blanco a very skilful man and very expert in the arabian tongue when Peter de Covillan be return king John call he unto he and tell he secret that have always know he loyal and his faithful servant and ready to do his majesty good service see he understand the arabian tongue he purpose to send he with another p. cou. send to discover the spice and Prete janni his country companion to discover and learn where Prete janni dwell and whether his territory reach unto the sea and where the pepper and cinnamon grow and other sort of spicery which be bring unto the city of Venice from the country of the moor see he have send for this purpose one of the house of Monterio and one friar Anthony of Lisbon prior of porta which can not pass the city of jerusalem say that it be impossible to travel this way without understand the arabian tongue and therefore see he understand the same well he pray he to under-take this enterprise to do he this so principal service promise to reward he in such sort that he shall be great in his kingdom and all his posterity shall always live content Peter answer he that he kiss his majesty hand for the great favour which he have do he but that he be sorry that his wisdom and sufficiency be not answerable to the great desire he have to serve his highness and yet nevertheless as his faithful servant he accept this message with all his heart and so in the year 1487. the seven of May they be both dispatch in saint arren the his journey king don Emanuel always there present which at that time be but duke and they give they a sea-card take out of a general map of the which we be to carry with we to the king and to the the use of writing be not in Ethiopia in these day grand captain and they bestow much time and labour in make they for their manner be not to write the epistle of saint Paul of saint Peter and of saint james and those which study in they be take for the most learned and wise among they they write the letter to the king in three language the truth and may know whether that be it or no and the other which he have not find in fault he have also send we and that we may do with he what we think good either kill he or free he or make he a slave 107. two great man be send to we from the court which see the enmity and rancour that be betwixt the ambassador and burn which come from word to blow they wist not what course to take concern our matter see it be a custom in that country that no great personage may go from the court without licence nor come to the court unless he be call a court custom for therefore the say lord stand in doubt what they shall do concern we because on the one side they dare not leave we and on the other side to bring we to the court in such great the particular of the ambassador wilfulness against burn a ethiopian be omit rancour be not send for they fear they may incur some great punishment yet at length they choose rather to return to the court although they shall suffer some great punishment 108. these nobleman have consider that the monson be pass wherein the grand captain be to come for we and that they can not pacify we determine to carry we back to the court and we set forward altogether with the franks and as we come to the town of Bacinete before mention whither the fame of our fall out be come all the countrypeople put themselves in arm and will not suffer we to pass and such number of friar a skirmish come down a hill with bow arrow and staff that they seem to be flock of sheep and here we have a great skirmish and many of both side be wound howbeit we beat they back and
