commit we to certain captain to conduct we several one from the other in such sort as we come to that place and so we return with he towards his territory by this time the winter be begin which be exceed terrible and cruel with huge rain here the author cease to speak any more of his voyage @. 16 of the time and day when their Lent begin in the country of PRETE JANNI and strange abstinence and other bodily exercise with other their holy of the troglodyte and goraise 109. in the country of Prete janni they begin their lent in the Monday after which be ten day before our Shrovetide and after the day of ethiopian Lent long and strict the purification be past the priest friar and secular man general observe a great fast for three day and they say they do fast the penance of the city of ninive and many friar eat not above once in these three day and then they eat but herb without bread and they say that there be many woman which then will not give suck to their child pass once a day the general fast of the Lent be bread and water for although some will eat fish yet they can not have it because they have not the sea near they in the river there be great abundance of fish which be very good but they know not how to take they they eat no milk nor butter neither drink wine of grape nor of honey but their common drink be of Zauna which be make of barley or of millet or of Aguza for of each of these grain they make a several wine which in taste be like unto ale. Zauna there be also many friar which for devotions sake eat no bread all the lent and other all the year and all their life time as I go on a time with the ambassador towards the court in a place call jannamora a jannamora friar fall into our company and because I will pleasure he I cause he to ride upon a mule and lodge he in my tent. the first day I invite he to eat with i because it be eventide the fast and abstinence which some use in the lent. and supper time and he excuse himself that he have no lust to eat in the mean space the novice six or seven of which go with he to receive order come with which be herb of that country and give he a handful without salt or oil or any other mixture and those he eat alone without bread or any thing else whereof when I have ask the say novice they tell i that they never use to eat any bread when I doubt of this I cause he diligent to be watch night and day for on the day he go on foot by my mule side like unto a lackey and on the night he sleep by my side and lay on the ground in his apparel and I always see he eat herb call and Rabasas and when they who have require these thing at your hand can find none sometime he take mallow and nettle and when they pass by any Mona sterie he send the novice to gather some garden-herb and if they find none the novice bring he lentile so long steep in a gourd of water that they begin to grow and he feed of they which I will needs taste of and find they to be the worst meat in the world this man travel thirty day with we unto the court and afterward stay three week with we in our tent and never eat any thing else but the thing aforesaid afterwards I see he in the town of Caxumo where the Prete cause we to stay eight month and when he understand that I be there he come to visit i and bring i certain lemon he wear a habit of leather without sleeve and his arm be naked whereas I embrace he by chance I thrust one of my hand under his arm and find that he have about he a girdle of iron of four finger broad and I lead he by the hand into our chamber and show he to Peter Lopez my cousin and we see the say girdle which be join the one end with the other with certain point as if they have be to peg in a piece of wood * * Comesaria and this girdle be fasten upon his flesh and the say friar take it in very ill part and seem as though he have receive great wrong and sudden depart so that we never can see he after after this we see many other friar which wear the like girdle of iron in the lent and we hear say that there be other also which during all the time of Lent do never sit but very strange kind of penance always stand upright when we hear that there be one of these in a cave six mile off we ride thither and find he in a frame make of wood of that bigness that he only may stand within it and it look like a old chest without a cover and his hip be besmear with chalk and oxe-dung and where his buttock stand he have a open place three finger broad a frame to stand in without sit he have likewise another open place where his knee touch and before he he have a little desk of wood whereon lie a book his habit be a haircloth make of the hair of a ox tail and underneath the same upon his flesh he wear a iron girdle like to that abovesaid and he show we the same willing in another cave adjoin dwell two young little novice which provide he victual which be nothing but herb and for this our visitation he become our great friend these cave seem to have be make in old time to do the like penance for there be grave in they in the town of Barua in another lent I see two friar in the church of the say town supererogation if not supererogation obedience better than sacrifice that be to say without the church gate which be in the like tabernacle one on the one side of the church and another on the other side which do eat the say herb and steep lentile and I go to see they often time wherewith they seem high to be please and if I go not to they they send to visit i and they wear upon their flesh a sackcloth and a girdle of iron and it be tell i that one of they be a kinsman of the Prete and they continue in this penance until easter day and when mass be sing they go out of the same have hear report that in the aforesaid town of Caxumo every Wednesday and Friday stand in water like josephus his pharisee in the lent many friar priest and nun stand all night in the water up to the neck when we can not be persuade to believe the same John Scolaro my cousin Peter Lopez and I go thither on a Wednesday at night and be astonish behold so great a multitude of they which be in the water up to the neck and it be tell we that they be canon and the wife also of canon with friar and nun and there be seat of stone make by the water side and where the water be shallow there be one stone whereupon they sit until the water reach up to their neck and if the water be more deep they lay another stone there and so all the say lake be full of people which come from all the country round about and in this time of Lent there be great frost and cold in the night and have frost and cold talk with Peter de Covillan concern this matter he assure i that they use to observe this custom in all the dominion of the Prete and also that there be many which do not only eat no bread all that time but also go into mighty forest and into certain monstrous deep valley lie between exceed high mountain where they may find water whereas no other people come and there they do their penance all the time of Lent and for proof hereof go into forest and valley for penance I be on a time with the Prete in a town call dara which be near those great and deep trench whereof I have speak before into the which a great river fall down headlong from a high mountain into a bottom and the water of this river break in the air become as white as snow as we stand aloft peter de Covillan show i a cave in this bottom which we can hardly discern and say that in the same there be a monk which they hold for a saint and under this cave there seem to be a garden on the side of this bottom and not far off he show i such another cave wherein a white man be dead which be know to have be twenty year in that desert and that the time of his death be not know only when they see he no more in this mountain they go to see his lodging or cave and they find it close up on the inside with a good wall so that none may go in or out thereat and the Prete be advertise hereof command that by no mean it shall be open or touch 110. the general fast in Lent which the most part of the friar and nun and the priest also do observe be to eat once from two day to two day and that always in the the general fast in lend of friar and nun queen Helena eat but thrice in the week night time they fast not on sunday the like do many old woman when they be go out of the world and so they report that queen Helena do as often as she fast at any time in the year that she do not eat above thrice in the week to wit on Tuesday Thursday and Saturday in the kingdom of Tigrai which be a kingdom subject to Barnagasso and in the kingdom of Tigremahon every body eat flesh in the lent on Saturday and Sunday and they kill more ox on these two day then in all the year beside and if they will marry their first or second wife they marry they the Thursday before our Shrovetide for upon custom of Tigrai their marriage they have licence to eat flesh milk and butter for two month space at what time soever they will and therefore that they may eat the same they marry wife and drink wine in all the other territory kingdom and signiory they fast all the lent as polygamy well great as small man as woman male-children as female without break the same in any point and so they do almost all the Advent on Palme-Sunday they say their service after this manner they begin to say matin about midnight and they continue their sing and dance carry paint image uncover Palmesunday in their hand until broad day and at the hour of prime they all get bough and hold they in their hand at the gate for the woman and layman may not come into the church and the priest stand sing in the church with bough in their hand and sing very loud make oftentimes the sign of the cross with the say bough and go about without the church they come unto the principal gate into which six or seven of they enter as we be wont to do which they shut and he stand without which be to say mass and they sing both within and without the church as we do and then he which stand without come in and say mass and give the communion unto all on the holy week or week before easter no mass be say save on Thursday and Saturday and their ordinary custom week before easter which all nobleman and gentleman use at all time in the year of salute one another be when they meet together once a day they kiss their shoulder and embrace one another and one kiss the right shoulder and the other the left these salutation be not use this week but when they do meet they speak not one to another but pass by without lift up their custom of salute eye and man of any quality be apparel all in black or in blue and they do no kind of work but all the whole day be spend in great devotion and sing in the church and always silence there be no candle light on Holy-thursday at Euentide a they make the Maunday that be to say the ceremony of wash of foot and all the people assemble together unto the church and the chief priest Mandy-thursday of the church sit on a chair like unto a gird with a towel and a great basin full of water before he and begin to wash the foot of the priest which be do they begin to sing and sing all night and the priest friar and clerk go not out of the church neither eat nor drink until Saturday after they have say mass on Good-friday about noon they trim up the church accord to their ability and riches for there be some church which be hang all with cloth of gold and crimson and Good-friday chief they deck up the principal gate because there be the stand place of all the people and they hang up a crucifix upon the cloth make of print paper and over the same be a little curtain which cover it and they sing all night and all day and read the passion which be do they uncover the crucifix and straightway all the people fall prostrate of their great lamentation and beat one another upon Good-friday at night on the ground beat one another with Wandes and cuff and fist with great fury jowl their head one against another and also against the wall and make so bitter mourn that any heart of flint will be move to tear with pure denotion this lamentation and sorrow continue two hour at the least after this two priest go to every gate of the circuit which be three which go into the churchyard and stand at all these gate one on the one side and another on the other side with a little whip in their hand which have five great thong of leather upon it and all they that be before the principal gate come out through one of these three gate strip from the waste upward whip and as they pass they bow down their body and these priest with the whip do nothing else but lie on they as hard as they can as long as they stand still some pass by and have but few stripe other stay and receive many but the old man and old woman stand there half a hour until the blood trickle down their time be the motion of the sea and we see no body come for we we remain very sad as we have be before the month of july be come when the Prete understand that the portugal be not arrive he give order the midst of januarie 140. on easter Tuesday at midnight there come letter from don Hector captain of India that he be come for we and be at Maczua which letter be read we conceive all of we the ithiofagis or be wild or savage they have no king. they worship Mahomet and be very bad moor above all other people they be give to stealth and rapine they eat raw flesh and drink milk their habit be vile and filthy they be great endue with swiftness and nimbleness they fight on foot and horseback their weapon be dart they never have peace with their neighbour but continual have war and fight with every one those that dwell along the red sea from as far as Zeila unto suaquen do fight with the and those from suaquen to Alcocer have war with the and those which inhabit from Alcocer to Soez and end of this sea do molest continual the egyptian but return by the arabian side by all the coast of the sea that lie from Soez to the straight of ormuz do contend with the arabian among the Badois there be no king or great lord but live in troop or faction they permit no town in their field neither have they any certain habitation for their custom be to be vagabond from one place to another with their cattle not only do they abhor law and ordinance but also the suit and difference that arise amongst they they will not have they judge by any custom and they be content that their Xeque do determine they as he listen their dwell be in cave and hole and other such like habitation but the great part do help themselves with tent and booth their colour be very black their language the be all one it will whether this sea of the straight be red or no and the cause wherefore they call it the red sea. opinion of the red sea. be just to speak something of my opinion and of that which I have see touch the reason that move the ancient man to call all this sea the red sea and likewise whether her colour do differ from the other of the great ocean or not Pliny in the 6 book of the natural history cap. 23. rehearse many opinion whereby the people call this straight the red sea. the first be that it take this name of a king that reign in it call Erithra because Erithros in the greek be to say red. another opinion be that of the reflection of the sunbeam there grow in this sea reddish colour some hold that of the sand and ground that run alongst it other also believe that this water be red of his own nature whereby all this sea get this name of these opinion the writer choose they that they like best and seem most certain now the portugal that have navigate this way in time past affirm this sea to be all spot with certain red streak the cause they attribute unto it be this they say the coast of the arabian be natural very red and that as in this country there arise many storm and do raise great dust towards the sky after they be very high drive with the force of the wind they fall in the sea and this dust be red it do die the water of it whereby it be call the red sea. when I come to Socatora till I pass all the coast of this sea and set myself before Soez I never leave by day nor night to consider of these water and view the colour and manner of the country that go along the shore and certain I be not so trouble for any thing as for the bestow my labour in obtain the truth of the thing and to search out the occasion of they and that I get of my own industry and most clear have I see many time be as follow first it be false to say that the colour of this sea be red for it have no difference from the colour that all the other water of the sea do show we and to say that the dust which the wind do snatch from the land and drive into the sea do stain the water where they fall till now we see no such thing see many storm raise great dust and drive they into the sea but not to change th^ colour of the wave thereof and to say that the land over the sea coast be red they observe not well the coast and strand for general on the one side and on the other the land by the sea be brown and very dark and seem scorch and in some place it show black and in other white and the sand have their own colour but only in three place there be certain piece of mountain which have certain vein of red where portugal never come except these which now be here-away which place be all far beyond suaquen that be towards Soez and the end of this sea but the three hill that show this red colour be of a very hard rock and then all the land round about that we can see be of the common and accustom colour but the truth of these thing be that the water of this sea take substantial have no difference of his colour but in many place of it the wave thereof come by accident to seem very red which be cause in this manner from the city of suaquen unto Alcocer which be one hundred thirty six league journey the sea be all thick with shoalds and shelf who ground be of a stone call corall-stone which grow in certain tree and cluster spread one way and another way certain branch proper as the coral do and this stone be so like unto it that it deceive any person that be not very skilful in the growth and nature the colour of this stone be of two sort the one wonderful white and the other very red in some place this stone lie cover with very green ozy and in other free from this herb which slime or ozy in some place be very green and in other it make a colour very like orange-tawny now we must presuppose that the water of this sea be clear especial from suaquen upward then ever be any in sort that in twenty fathom water you may see the ground in many place this presuppose we be to note that wheresoever that these shoalds and shelf do appear the water over they be of three colour that be red Greene or white the which proceed of the ground that be under as many time I see by experience for if the ground of these shoalds be sand it cause that the sea over it appear white and the ground where the corall-stone lie cover with green ozy the water that cover it do give a colour green than the weed but wheresoever the shoalds be of red coral or of corall-stone cover with red weed it make all the sea that be over it seem very red and because this red colour comprehend great space in this sea red coral stone than the green or the white because the stone of the shoalds be the great part of red coral I believe it be the reason whereby it receive the name of red sea and not of Greene nor white sea notwithstanding this sea do represent these colour most perfect the mean that I have to obtain this secret be to fasten many time upon the shoalds where I see the sea look red and command diverse to bring i of the stone that lay in the bottom and the most time it be so shallow that the foist do touch and otherwhiles that the mariner go on the shoalds half a league with the water to the breast where it happen that all or the great part of the stone they pull up be of red coral and other cover with weed like orange-tawny and the practice I have whereseover the sea seem green and find beneath white coral cover with green weed and in the white sea I find a very white sand without any thing else whereof it may proceed for some sailor give relation of the red colour that they see in this sea as of the great and most compendious of all be ignorant of the cause or not be willing to offer it for to increase admiration to their navigation and travel and see that man do not only know this sea by the name of red sea but do believe that the water be natural red I have talk many time with moorish pilot and curious person of antiquity which dwell in some place of this straight about the name of this sea every one do say to i they know no other name then the sea of Mecca and they wonder very much at we to call it the red sea. I ask of the pilot if they find sometime the sea stain red with the dust that the wind bring of the land they tell i they see no such thing with all this I reprove not the opinion of the portugal but I affirm that go through this sea more time than they do and see all the length thereof and they only one piece I never see in the whole that which they say to have see in the part the nine of August we enter in the port of and remain there till the one and twenty of August that we embark in foist and go direct to Goa we enter over the bar thereof under sail and our voyage be end and this book JOHN BERMUDEZ elect patriarch of the presbyter and send to Rome his return into Ethiopia arrival at Maczua the death of the negus entertainment of he and CHRISTOPHER of gama with the Portugal force by the queen regent a faithful and good christian call onadinguell be emperor in the kingdom of Ethiopia vulgar call presbyter John and the patriarch of that country by name Abuna marcos be at the point of death in the year of our redemption 1535. the say emperor say to the patriarch that he request he that accord to their custom he before his death will institute i for his successor and patriarch of that country and the say patriarch do so order i first with all the sacred order the which I accept with such condition that it shall be confirm by the chief bishop of Rome successor of saint Peter to who we all be to give obedience the say emperor answer i that he be well content and moreover he desire i that for myself and for he and for all his kingdom I shall go to Rome to give the obedience to the holy father and from thence shall come to Portugal to conclude a embassage that he have send hither by a man of that country call Tegazavo in who company come the father Francis Zaga Zabo the friar mention in Aluarez Aluarez after many trouble pass in the journey I come to Rome the pope Paul the three govern then in the apostolic sea the which receive i with great clemency and favour and confirm all thing as I bring they and at my request he ratify it all again and command i to sit in the chair of Alexandria and that I shall entitle myself patriarch and bishop of the sea. from Rome I depart towards Portugal where I come the king your grandfather of glorious memory be in the city of Euora who rejoice particular at my come to conclude as he desire the embassage which the tagazavo have bring for he have be here twelve year without conclude any thing through mere negligence for the which the emperor onadinguel command i that I shall take away his charge of ambassador and Zaga zabo his negligence shall apprehend he and carry he a prisoner with i and therefore I bring he a letter from the emperor the which I give he in Lisbon where he be and he take it and kiss it and reknowledge it to be true and by it he acknowledge i for his patriarch and superior and kiss my hand and give i his place without speak any more word I command to imprison he with two chain of iron on each arm one after the manner of his country the which I take from he again within a few day because his highness entreat i the his imprisonment Bermudez his embassage from the negus to the king of P^rtugall embassage which the say emperor demand be his perpetual friendship and brotherhood and therefore he desire he they will marry their child interchangeable the one with the other and that from Portugal a son of he shall go to marry with a daughter of he and reign in his kingdom after his death that this alliance between the pertugal and they and also the obedience of the pope may be great and endure and likewise he send to request he he will send he some man for to defend himself from the king of Zeila which usurp his kingdom and he will send he great store of riches for he can very well do it and likewise to send he some pioner for to cut a hill whereby already eylale belale his predecessor do bring the river Nilus to bring it now also that way to annoy Egypt the king your grandfather have take counsel think good to grant i that which I demand and command to give i four hundred and fifty caliver-man and pioner and that they shall dispatch i that I may return that year in company with don garcia of Noranya which then go for viceroy of India I fall sudden sick and the physician say of poison as it be suspect the Tegazava cause it to be give i the chief physician which then be name james Lopez cure i and ^e which now be Leonard nunyes and other which his highness command for the which sickness I remain that year in this realm present the next year be recover by the goodness of God I go in his highness army I carry also Anthony Fernandes and Gaspar Suriano both armenians bear which by Anthony Fernandes see dam. a go of this siege 1538. commandment of presbyter John come to seek i to the which his highness do many favour we arrive in India safe at such time as the viceroy don garcia be come from Dio with the victory which he have of the turk Anthony Selueyra be captain of that fortress the which viceroy receive we with great joy and show i great (...) the bishop of Goa come to receive i with his train in procession with cross on high and captain of Goa and reknowledging i for patriarch give i the honour due unto my dignity in the meanwhile the viceroy sicken of a flux whereof he die and don Stephen Stephen gama viceroy of gama succeed in his stead the which I present request to dispatch i and send i to the presbyter John with the succour as his highness have command and he answer i that he can not do it because one hundred thousand crown be not sufficient to dispatch i or more in hazard of never be recover and I answer he that all that be nothing for the presbyter John which without miss it may spend a million of gold or more for he have Maczua or Macua the death of king David innumerable riches it be determine that he in person shall transport i and present he command a good navy of galley and galleon and other ship well furnish as for such a voyage be necessary and many choose man of the best that be in India with the which army we come to the port of Macua in the red sea where we find news that the emperor onadinguel be dead of his natural death of the which we all be very sorry and I above all as he who it touch most I encourage myself till there come from presbyter John two friar good religious man one of they prior provincial of many monastery and a great man among they call Aba joseph which go to jerusalem and tell we how the queen and a son and heir of she do joseph maintain their estate and resist their enemy this be know the governor don Stephen say unto i that I shall send to visit they as in effect I present send by one Arias Arias a mulato Portugal tawny man bear in Coymbra in the meantime the governor like a good gentleman and willing to lose no time and be a captain of a valiant spirit go with the galley that come in the fleet to the port of suez for to take or burn the turk galley which be in that haven which he can not do because they be on dry land. be there tarry the governors come there flee from the fleet sixty man in a skiff and a boat to the firm land the which come to a port of land very dry and excessive sixty fugitive hot and be willing to travel into the land they find it so dry that they die for thirst and be thus pinch with necessity one captain of the king of Zeila that be in that country send to tell they that he will send they meat and water and will assure they their life so that they will give he their weapon and they see they have no other remedy and be pinch with need they give they with which present they ^^ue they all at that instant the chief captain send a galley to Arquico to seek water in the which he send also a thousand Cotton web for to change for cow or beef to eat and they which carry they go from Arquico by land where the army be a Bernagais call Nero captain of the king of Zeila take they from they and send word present to the chief captain that the king of Zeila his lord be lord of all Aethiopia and have win all the country of the presbyter John therefore that he will make peace with he and traffic with commodity of Zeila his merchandise in his country in the which there be much gold ivory Civet frankincense myrrh and many other drug and slave wherein they may make great profit and he also will give he store of provision and will restore the cow that he have take and will make amends for the sixty man that be slay Sicars I tell the captain that he shall not trust the word of moor for they be false and that they say be feign to do we some harm therefore that we shall also use some slight with they and it shall be this that he will send he a present and with it word of thankfulness for the good will that he show we whereby he may think that he have deceive we and may be assure of we for by this slight we shall hinder his deceit the chief captain do so and command the factor of the army to carry to the Bernagaiz a barrel of wine and another thousand of Cotton web the wine for a present and the web for to change for beef and that he shall tell he from he that the other web that see they be take in good and lawful war he shall not speak of they and as touch the man that be slay that they deserve not to be revenge for as much as they be rebel and traitor and deserve the death they have and as touch traffic and peace that for the present they be in the holy week and can do no work but as soon as the feast be past we will do that which he desire and will bring our ware ashore for to traffic with they the portugal stratagem have take counsel again the chief captain command that the boat shall not go ashore because no Moor or Blacke-moore may have any mean to go thither and give he warning and command the soldier to be in a readiness the secret that they can and that in the boat and the other light vessel that be in the army in the which he command the king of Maczua fly and the Barnagasso be slay they shall make no fire because they may not be perceive and command Martin correa that at ten of the clock at night he shall land with six hundred man and possess the passage whereby they may escape he go and kill some turk and Fartaquis and take all the carriage they have which be but little for he have no time to take any store the Bernagaiz of Zeila when he see the king set himself to flight he likewise flee and light upon Martin correa where be know a caleever-man kill he and man come to rescue he be many of they slay foot and horse and the rest save themselves by flight our man think good to cut off his head and send it for a present to the queen wherewith she rejoice very much she send a great man of her country call Esmacherobel tigremacan to the chief understand already that the enterprise be of honour and profit many do covet it more than before among the which one be don Christopher gama brother to the governor who desire i very earnest that I the best I can don Christopher and his man and the murmur cease and they conclude how to carry the ordnance wa^t of iron when they journey they make present certain carriage like unto we the which because in the country there be no iron they shod they with certain old caleever which break because they will serve for no other use I send to the queen who come with all speed possible who we go to whereof she be amaze be a thing unaccustomed the first thing she do as one that have a respect unto the thing of God she receive my blessing and present receive don Christopher with great prevail in the three be overthrow a new captain appoint don Christopher resolution and death mountain of the jew depart from Debarua we go eight day by rough country at the end of which we come to plain ground and very well inhabit and better than they pass but in they there dwell christian which for fear do follow the Moor which as soon as they know our come go present to don christophor and give he obedience at the end of three day we come to a very pleasant field and in it a fountain of fair water in the which we pitch our camp round about the fountain the next day there come a messenger to we from goronya king of Zeila with some of his man in company and ask for the captain of those man say unto don Christopher that his Goranya king of Zeila some call he Gradame^ Godignus call he Gragna which variety happen by the different pronunciation of so different a language provoke present king send to ask he who he be and from whence he come or who give he leave to enter in his kingdom with man of war for those realm be he and he have win they by his lance and of his gentleman with the help of his prophet Mahomet therefore if we will become moores and serve he he will entertain they well and give they his wage and moreover wife and good to live upon and if not that we shall present avoid his country and go out of it don Christopher answer he that he be a captain of the king of Portugal by who commandment he come with those man for to restore the kingdom of the presbyter John which he tyrannous have usurp and to take they out of his hand and give they to who they be and with this message he send he for a present a looking-glass and a pair of mullet to pull the hair with and a egg of silver of Pegu signify that those thing pertain to he and to the messenger he give two bracelet of gold and a very rich suit of cloth of gold which thing the queen have give to he and he give he also a cypress of Bengala and a turkish cassock with his upper garment this by my counsel in disgrace of the goranya raise present his camp and begin to march towards the place where we be with one thousand horseman and five thousand foot and fifty turk caleever-man and as many archer don Christopher command to place the queen who be very fearful and the woman with all the carriage in the midst of the squadron the Moor when he see we go up a hill whereon stand the church of the lady of pity wheel upon we to take the height from we and he come already so near unto we that the shot begin to fight on both side when I see the battle be begin I call six portugal and with the queen and her sister in-law I be go aside and in this I know the moorish king which come near to his ancient on a bay horse and I show he to Peter Deca a gentleman and a good shot which shoot at he and slay his horse and hurt he in the leg his man come about he and set he on another horse and take he from that place our captain don Christopher be also hurt in his leg and I command the steward to set up the queen tent in sign of victory the Moor have environ we on every side when they see we set up tent and their king hurt they begin to retire and go after their king which withdraw himself with the pain of the wound towards a mountain that be near to that place to be cure at this instant there come to we a Moor that have be a Christian cousin German to the Bernagaiz and tell we how the king be hurt in his leg and how great a favour God have do to we therein for if it have not be so he have take we all without doubt but that God miraculous have deliver we from his hand and that therefore he with all his man do return to we and will serve we and pay the tribute that unto that time they pay to that king and that he go present to his country for to send we beef and provision for our camp for he be captain and governor of all that country where we be the which belong and in to the presbyter and he also and when the king of Zeila conquer it he yield unto he and now that he see he overcome he return to we again whereby he seem to be a man of live he that overcommeth in the mean while it please God that don Christopher heal of his wound but we suffer great hunger for there be very little provision in the camp and the people die with scarcity hunger don Christopher go to the queen and tell she that the people suffer great hunger and that they have need to eat all they find notwithstanding it be lend that it will be good to kill the beast that they have in the camp for to eat and with this request they come both to my tent pray i that I will give the people leave to eat flesh in Lent because flesh in lent. of the necessity there be and beside the queen request i that I shall give she my ox that I have for my carriage to give they to the people and as soon as her captain aforesaid come she will satisfy i which will stay three day and so it be for he present come with great store of provision viz. beef sheep and goat butter and other provision for Lent and for easter which be already at hand as soon as easter be past the goranya send word to don Christopher that he will come to see he that he shall prepare himself which he do as he have say he come to seek we with more and better man then before he bring for he have above two thousand horse and infinite number of foot and a hundred turk for the which the queen be in such a fear with her sister in law that they know not what to do in such sort that be at dinner as soon as they know the come of the Moor they will have leave dinner don Christopher be the next day order his man before day for to set upon the moor the queen send the queen fear for i and say to i that she see the great power that the king Goranya bring and that it be impossible to escape his hand if we stay therefore that she desire i that we shall be go for she have so determine and that in any sort she will do it therefore that she request i very earnest that I will not let she go alone see I be her father but I shall accompany she and go with she and I to show she the love that I bear she and that she shall not think that I esteem not her life grant her request and we both interprise the flight but don Christopher which be already warn for that purpose send after we ten horseman and some footman cry aloud and say that it be neither service of God nor the work of a father to go away and leave they hear these word shee by my mean return to the camp weep and bewail herself there don Christopher say unto i that as a father and prelate accord to the good custom of the portugal he request i that I shall give he my blessing and shall make he a general absolution before he enter into the battle I do so and grant he a plenary indulgence of all his sin which indulgence I may do because the pope have grant it i and be the stile of the patriarch of Alexandria from thence we remove with our camp by the break of day down the hill and march till we come to a plain and present with great fury they assault our stand on every side our man defend themselves with the ordnance and firework wherewith they the second battle annoy they very much and before they come they have cast a great quantity of powder in the way whereby they be to come up the which when they be in the heat of the battle be set on fire and it burn they proceed under their foot they not know from whence it come they understand not the stratagem our man do cast among they certain fiery stratagem ball of wild fire and pot full of powder wherewith they burn the great part of they and the other retire with fear and dare come no more near we the ordnance kill many of the horseman and of other people that the field be all full of they and the horse run masterless about the field the turk with their piece and their bow kill we twenty man and the master gunner our man kill fifteen turk the queen be next to i embrace a cross and weep and say unto i oh father what have you gain in bring i hither wherefore do you not let i go my way I say unto she lady do not afflict yourself commit yourself to God and open your eye and you shall see the great destruction that be do in your enemy at this time the footman begin already to flee and the horseman dare not come near but skirmish a far off and the king say to his man that the portugal be no man but devil for they fight like devil and with this he retire himself towards the hill and the victory leave his campe. we gather our camp and go forward as fast as we can but they flee as fast as they can and we can not overtake they but we find many abexin on foot and horseback which return to we which afterward be baptize and loyal to their king. of who return the queen and we all be as glad as of the principal victory we come to the camp of the moor which we find forsake without any people but we find in it all the spoil for the fear which saint james put they in give they no leisure to take any thing away we great spoil find it with tent up and in they apparel household stuff money and other riches and store of provision which be very needful for we for it be already very scant here we stay and let the people rest two day this country and all the border be call the province of Nazareth and it be of the patriarch their own proper with all jurisdiction without the king entermeddle in it by any Nazaretha country appertain to the patriarch mean neither have he any rent thereof it yield for the patriarch three thousand ounce of gold every year the which King appropriate unto they for a certain offence that he commit against a patriarch from the camp we draw towards the mountain where the king Goranya withdraw himself and pitch our camp in a field at the foot of the mountain environ with the carriage of the ordnance the Moor send to zebide to a bassa of the great Turk which be there to ask he succour the Turk solicit say that he shall succour he and not suffer those kingdom to be lose which be all of the great Turk and he hold they for he and that in token thereof he send he one hundred thousand oquy of gold and twenty thousand for his person a Oqui be a weight of gold which in that country be worth as much as ten crown or cruzado in this and weigh as much we withdraw ourselves while we know what pass to a strong mountain the which be compass on every side with rock and crag in such sort that in it there be scarce a way for footman for to carry the ordnance and other carriage be needful to make a new way the which the captain of the country make with their man and it be so straight and so rough that the ordnance can not be carry upon the carriage but they carry it on their back with lever above be a plain where we pitch our campe. from thence the queen send through her province and I also through i that they shall bring we store of victual and other provision necessary of which we be present well provide and the wound be well cure be there well lodge don Christopher say unto i that we shall remove to a high hill which be near from thence because the army may be more safe and that in the mean while he will go to a mountain which be near from thence inhabit with jew in the which be a captain of the Moor with a hundred and fifty horse as we be advertise mountain of jew and be go with the portugal and some few of the country for to show he the way he leave with we two Portugal captain with his man as soon as he come to the mountain he set upon the Moor and kill sixty horseman and take thirty horse the rest flee the jew inhabiter of the mountain pursue after the moor and take the passage of the mountain which they know very well they kill they almost all and among the jew pursue the moor they the captain and take all the spoil they carry and the woman which they bring all to don Christopher and give it he for a we with six hundred turk which the bassa send unto he an^ two hundred moor on horseback six hundred turk send to aid the Moor and a great number on foot and come to the foot of the hill where we be he the praise of God and the profit of his faithful we send in all haste to call don Christopher which be not come from the mountain mean while the turk in despite of our man enter the mountain and do we much hurt present that night after they be enter come don Christopher and send present for the other captain to take counsel with they what be best to do which tell he that it be best to set upon the moor by night for when the force be not equal in strength the weak have need to use some policy and this be one of the best we can use with they for the manner of the turk be not to fight by night in so much that come out of their tent they dare not and beside we shall take they on a sudden and unprepared and we shall overthrow they before they can come to themselves and for the more amaze they we will assault they on two side this counsel seem not good to don Christopher because mutable fortune be willing to change her course and God to make a end of sensuality which at such time man that be christian shall not remember don Christopher say that he will give battle to the enemy by day because they shall not think that he be afraid of they wherein he prevail though none like his counsel as soon as it be day they go all down and before they set any thing in order because the unfortunate battle the misfortune be to have some beginning by a mischance a horse of we break loose and run towards the moor camp they come out to catch he and our man go out to defend he and in this sort the fight begin without any order or government this skirmish last a great while in the which many moor and turk die and likewise of we there die some among who don garcia of Noronia be one the ancient-bearer of don Christopher fight with the ancient royal like a valiant gentleman and in his defence slay some of the enemy and wound they so fierce that they dare not come near he until that for weariness he can fight no long than they slay he don Christopher be wound with a shot don Christopher hurt in the arm of the which although he suffer great pain he leave not therefore the battle till very late that he sound himself almost alone than he retire to the top of the mountain with some few that he find about he before he retire I see the spoil of our man say to the queen that she shall mount and go to the mountain and because she will not leave some woman that have not whereon to ride I make she mount perforce and one sister-in-law of she and so I send they before and I take her daughter behind i a nurse of the queen a virtuous woman with two daughter and other woman take a lamentable and desperate act barrel of powder say God forbid we shall be deliver to the power of infidel they bring it into the tent set it on fire and burn themselves the like do fif^eene or sixteen himself so much for with his life and health he will recover again God will that which then he have lose for so we see it fall out every day in matter of war etc. and as touch the ancient in that country they take no such regard of it and that present they will make such another have man to fight under it and a captain to govern they for the man be the true ancient and not the sign which they carry we make he mount and go from thence and with all speed we pass two river so great that the footman wade to the breast we travel till we come to the river of the draw-bridge which they have tell we which be so deep that it can not be pass but by that bridge there don Christopher say to i that he will not pass the bridge but will don Christopher disconsolateness remain on this side the river and call present his servant which take he down and set he up a bed whereon he cast himself he call i and request that I will shrive he have end his confession he say unto i that his will be to remain there I say unto he that I will not suffer it and command those that be there to take the bed and to carry he in it as he be and he say that he will kill himself if they carry he from thence when I see his determination I say unto he that I will remain with he he answer i that I shall not do it for I be necessary for to govern those man that they may not altogether be lose and therewith all that country but that I shall leave he a little balm for to dress he with and that his chamberlain his secretary and other three portugal with which he will go hide himself in a grove that be there I can never understand to what end he remain from thence I go to the queen and desire she to mount and that we shall pass on the other side the bridge for it draw towards day and our enemy will come she answer that in no wise she will do it nor pass any far see don Christopher remain there desolate but I desire she to mount say to she that not only she but her son with all his kingdom will be lose if we tarry there and wi^h this the queen mount weep and speak so many dolorous word as she can have utter for she own son if he have remain there we command all the man to go with the carriage and all the people with the great haste possible and before we have pass we hear a rumour of man and noise of horse for the which we make great haste to go over and draw the bridge after we by this time it be already day and we beginning to go up the side of a hill on the other side we see many moor about the place where don Christopher remain the queen when she see they be great afraid and say that we can not escape her man tell she that she shall not fear for she be already in her own country notwithstanding we go on with all haste possible for to lose they out of sight and we travel all that day pass many mountain and river with great trouble and heat of the day there be by those river great store of cassia and indian date whereof our man do eat for they have no other food or final we come to a river somewhat big where the people catch some fish which they do eat while the captain of that country come with victual which present bring great store and there we begin to rest for we be already in a sure country we want forty Portugal to the rest that remain which be few more than three hundred I make my speech thus and say unto they that they see very well that it be necessary to give they a captain that may govern they and fight before they see we know not what may become of don Christopher remain as he be willing to be leave they answer i that I shall do what I think best for they September 1566. from Ethiopia to the Jesuit in Goa which so much as concern this purpose I have here transcribe on the fifteen of May we come to the king of Ethiopia he be then in his camp encompass Claudius at his return for he open say as I learn of a Portugal near about he that he neither need our doctrine nor intend to obey the roman church it be also common report that some of the chief man do open affirm that they will more easy subject their neck to the yoke of saracen then exchange their custom with we which do the more confirm i to deliver my mind rather in write then by word so to learn his answer and unmask his opinion so long close conceal so soon therefore as he return to these part we go to his camp and be entertain of the Portugal soldier for the emperor have quite forget we nor care to know how or where we live now because I have make my book in portuguse and it be necessary to turn it in Chaldee I petition of he by letter to assign i two of the best learned monk to turn some doctrine of christian faith into the Chaldee tongue for I will in writing show how undeserved the abassine reckon the follower of the roman faith amongst heretic and affirm that they be worse than Mahumetans for so they open say and report abassine blind zeal a book call the adultery of the frank that be of the western church and because I know that they have a book which they call the adultery of the frank make by the Alexandrine schismatic wherein the chalcedon council be reprove and many lie be forge on we I desire of the emperor that I may have the use thereof the book he deny the monk he grant which yet when they have begin to translate the book whether because they have be so command or else be afraid of any thing or for some other unknown cause refuse to proceed in the enterprise until that by the Portugal captain intercession they be command to finish it assist therein by a Portugal a honest man and well skill in the Chaldee when again I need another to soil rock arise rocky hill which in time of war serve they for fortress the whole country abound with vein of metal and metall-medicine but the inhabitant partly by ignorance and partly for fear of the turk invasion if such thing shall be know suffer they to lie hide in the earth only they make use of so much iron as they find upon the face of the earth without dig of plant and tree be great variety but first-fruit not so pleasant as in Europe one yet there be very useful for the worm which breed in they by eat raw flesh which will gnaw through their entrails if they do not prevent that evil with worm in the belly by use of raw flesh monthly purgation by this fruit which both kill the worm and empti the belly peach pomegranate indian fig orange and vine be there see but rare and few hare goat heart boar elephant camel buffal lion panther tiger rhinocerote and other creature be there see and one so huge that a man sit on horseback may pass this seem to be the upright under his belly his shape be like a camel but his nature diverse feed on leaf which he reach from the top of tree with his neck stretch forth there be many river and lake in all which be river-horse innumerable very hurtful to their corn of great body and a mouth so wide that they can gape a cubit and half by night they go out of the water river-horse and their nature into the field to feed for they live on herb and if the husbandman watch not well in one night they will destroy their corne. in the water they be very bold and assail man like fierce dog and cruel tear those which they get they be so afraid of fire that a little boy hold a light torch may scare away many thousand of they there be some which hunt the torpedo a strange kind of fish and kill they for their flesh which differ little from beef in these river and lakes be also find the torpedo which if any man hold in his hand if it stir not it do produce no effect but if it move itself never so little it so torment the body of he which hold it that his artery joint sinew and all his member feel exceed pain with a certain numbness and as soon as it be let go out of the hand all that pain and numbness be also go the superstitious abassine believe that it be good to expel devil out of human body as if it do torment spirit no less than man they say if one of these alive be lay amongst dead fish if it there stir itself it make those which it touch to stir as if they be alive there be great store of this kind in Nilus in the further part of Goyama where there be a mere or fen a a palus a bottomless pool succession of emperor without bottom well and admirable boil forth water continual whence Nilus spring it arise small and first for a day journey and half trend eastward then it enter into a lake as great as any imagine to be in the world run through the midst thereof with a swift course fly all mixture of water and throw itself from very high rock whence have get free scope it expatiate itself a to the west and sometime great sometime less accord to the season pass towards Egypt the abassine report that it be no hard thing to turn the river course some other way and to starve Egypt which I scarce believe the abassine air be most part warm and temperate but in low land be exceed hot and somewhat unwholesome their winter be from the end of May to the begin of September and than it begin in the red sea. I have find by experience that this sea from the change of the moon to the full fourteen day together flow in and as many through the whole wane eb or run out in winter it rain almost every day in these part always afternoon and not without thunder from this kingdom of Dambea where we live both pole be see but antarctike the high near it be many star in form of a cross whence it have that name in this Tract of heaven appear a certain spot like a cloud we suppose it a part more thin than other not star let philosopher examine about this spot many star shine less than those which adorn the other pole. the year begin here with the spring on the first of September their year h^th twelve month each of they thirty day and those which remain from August to September be reckon by themselves the abassine no way more express their joy and jollity then by eat and drink and easy on holy day they come to the church which usual be compass with tree for shade where be many vessel set full of their wine which after service end they suck in so unmeasurable that first drunkenness and then brabble and last fray usual follow they make wine of honey temper with opium both pleasant and profitable take moderate wine of vine be rare and for their mass in vintage time they use must at other time wine of raisin Peter paez a jesuite write that 1604. he be with the emperor who desire he to say mass which he can not for want of wine which nowhere can be get at what time Roderick lima enter Abassia David * * before he be Nahu who predecessor be Alexander to he Ciriacus etc. abassine apparel reign and after he have hold the empire thirty six year his son Claudius succeed who in the year 1559. be slay have rule almost twenty year his brother Adamas succeed call also mena and reign four year die in the year 1563. son call (@) paez call he antonius fernandez thus write of their apparel the rich sort buy garment of the saracen and clothe themselves in their fashion the rest both man and woman cover their body either with a skin or pelt or with a course hempen cloth without other art then the weaver when they do reverence to any they put off this cloth from the shoulder to the naviil remain half naked they let their hair grow and that serve they for a hat and head-ttyre for fine bravery they curl and anoint their hair with butter which show in the sun like grass in the morning dew lest their lock and curl shall be disorder when they go to bed each one pitch a fork or Cratch a foot high foolish bravery in the ground betwixt the horn whereof he repose his neck and sleep with his head hang they use to brand mark in their body especial in the face and on their little finger they suffer the dull ignorance and idleness nail to grow as long as they will like cock spur which also they sometime cut from cock and sit to their finger they colour their hand and foot which be bare with the juice of a reddish bark they usual be artless and lazy neglect hunt and fish and whereas whole hemp and cotton may easy be have yet the vulgar be clothe with undress pelt each wear a ram skin tie to his hand and foot they lie on oxe-hides without quilt or mattress their Arts. for table they use great bowl of wood rude hollow without any naperie vessel they have of black chalk few but saracens use merchandise and in few place most exercise husbandry the gentry follow arm and the court. they have no great city but village unwall and unfortify their great town have scarce one thousand six hundred house their house be small without town and house little or no writing elegance without story almost without art round and cover with earth and straw they write no letter nor use record in judgement or other write but in their holy thing and officer of account for the king. they use no dirge or devotion for the dead they use picture but not carve nor grave image they paint Christ the bless virgin and other saint in black form as devil and wicked man in white so they paint Christ and his apostle at the Maundie black and judas white Christ in his passion black Annas Caiphas Pilate Herod and the jew white Michael black and the devil white their fast be rigorous not free the sick some religious man abstain whole from flesh which be no easy thing far from the sea where they have few fish they fast wednesday and friday not taste ought till night then eat herb see of these fast Aluarez church without oil which they have not or butter and bread with apple their temple be round and encompass with a double porch they neither walk nor talk nor spit nor sit nor laugh in the church nor admit dog the church to the other wherein none not in order may enter without many layman stand which have crutch to support they if they be sick or old some church be only for man other only for woman in small forsake they follow the emperor I take view of great part of the ethiopian continent touch their rebaptisation and tradition of soul from human seed and equality of Christ human nature with the divine with other abassine error I have have often conflict with their learned man which yield to other thing easy but in the two last opinion be obstinate they call dioscorus blessed condemn Leo with the chalcedon council with many reproach and father on he many lie touch the nature and operation of christ. they hold also that God do effect nothing beside the consecration of thing and miracle when they be do and thence gather that the soul be produce of seed they circumcise not only male but with a peculiar rite female also yearly on twelve day they renew baptism return from mahumetanisme be also rebaptise and likewise they which have commit some erroneous crime or have marry or have enter into any religious family on the otherside they be so rigorous to infant that before their appoint day they die without baptism they come to the eucharist without contrition or confession even the most wicked amongst they they dissolve marriage when they listen before the day of judgement they say that neither the soul of the bless be in heaven nor of the wicked in hell purgatory they deny and the spirit proceed from the son these error be common to all some be peculiar to some of they new heresy daily spring up without danger as every man list in his letter 1609. in this ethiopian empire every man live in manner in arm nor be the emperor life more quiet than of other man for every year winter be scarce pass himself in person and his captain renew the war sometime against rebel sometime against neighbour enemy it can be utter what confusion have happen these two last year as soon as the present emperor begin his reign three or four chief man usurp Ethiopia civil combustion the royal name rebel against he but be vanquish in battle this very year the second of his reign as many as have attempt the same and come into the field neither of long time have thing be quiet we be also constrain to wave up and down with these storm sometime fly to the mountain sometime hide ourselves in secret cave sometime we pierce thick wood and unpassable place and suffer innumerable evil which we can more patient endure if we can gather any harvest to offer to god. this very year when the emperor be go against a rebel sudden news come to the camp that the Galae a savage nation of cafres beget of devil as the vulgar report be at hand it be a the Galae hundred year since these pass from I thank he and say that I will go to acertaine town to see whether my kinsman be dead I may succeed in the inheritance the banean saranga or captain of the ship have receive charge of the owner touch i and send two saracen with i with who and five christian of abassia I depart on the five of may. I go in a vile ragged habit for fear of thief which there use to rob and kill which so free our company that as we go by night none speak but whisper near morning we think to have sleep but a lion terryfy we within eight pace of i but with our shout he depart the next day we pass high and cragged hill for fear of thief and come at night to a village of saracens on Holy-Thursday we come to certain christian herdsman which suppose i a Turk flee but learn that I be a priest kiss my hand with joy and refresh we with store of milk in vessel of straw which they set on burn stone to heat bread they have none and be they say a rare thing to they and far bring their wife which have hide themselves come the next day to entreat my blessing some kiss my hand other fall at my foot we go thence over rough mountain trouble also with rain the way not above three foot broad on both side so steep that I dare not look down for fear of giddiness blind almost strange path and weary we come at last to the top and find a plain path for I have not be able to have descend the like and a town of christian which bring we their book and cross here we be invite to a poor cottage which yet be in good season for we a violent rain follow which else have oppress we on the ten of may we come to Barua where all my company leave i but one saracen and a christian. another saracen which dwell here send i a hen but the Christian which be with i get he away because the abassine forsooth eat not any thing kill by a Turk and vain superstition I for fear of offence send it back with thanks to the sender eat dry biscuit bring from Diu without any other thing though faint neither will the gold I have do i any service here to buy provision their currant money be stone of salt. the bread of my companion be half bake dough of round form which they bake with put a hot stone into the dough and roll it cast it into the fire so that the outside be scorch the inside unbaked this they carry in their budget but my stomach can not bear it hither on the eleve of May come John Gabriel the captain of the portugal have receive my letter from Mazua with other portugal to give i better entertainment they kill a sheep which I taste not they eat it a little scorch and half raw after the country custom here I have a mule and we travel twenty together yet not without fear of raw flesh wet heat cold and ill way thief the rain also towards evening daily molest we and we be force to lie in the open field heat also exceed in the ascent of a exceed mountain and as exceed cold on the top FULCHERIUS CARNOTENSIS which go thither with ROBERT earl of Normandy in the year 1095. when manifold evil in all part of Europe be increase the faith languish urban the second be pope of Rome a man excellent in life and manner * * this the sanctity of those time to advance the church not to freedom from sin but to fullness of power in exemption from king and sovereignty over they wherein Vrbanus be call Turbanus this the state of the church that be the clergy and more special the papacy this the great article of popish faith. which always to the utmost of his wit and strength endeavour above all thing to exalt high the state of holy church and see that the faith of Christendom be decay in all both clergy and laity and the secular prince in continual war with each other spoil the good captive the person who miserable prison enforce to unreasonable redemption violate holy place burn of town and monastery make a mockery of thing divine and human spare no man and hear that the province of Romania * be possess by the turk he call a council at claremont herein he decree the church freedom from all secular power that tithe of all which come by husbandry shall be proper to God and neither sell nor detain that he which shall take a bishop shall be a outlaw and the taker or spoiler of clerk monk and nun pilgrim or merchant shall be anathema as likewise robber and incendiary these and other like be ratify by the council he exhort they not I but the lord to exterminate the turk out of the christian confine I speak to the present I send to the absent and Christ command it and all that go thither if they shall die in the go by land passage over water or in fight against the pagan shall have present remission of their sin which I grant to those which undertake the voyage have so great a gift from god. those that have former abuse war against christian let they go against infidel and let they now be soldier which before be robber and let they fight just against the barbarian which they do before against their brethren and for a eternal reward which be before mercenary for a few shilling and for a double honour which weary themselves for double detriment of body and soul here they be poor there they shall be wealthy here the lord enemy there his friend let they not delay but make money of that which they have and the next spring set forward many present promise to go of which be Ademarus bishop of afterward the pope legate which rule the whole army these thing order in the council and the blessing of absolution be give they depart home and divulge what have pass truce be every where confirm by oath and many of every profession vow to go the remission of sin be purchase oh what a goodly sight and worthy it be to we all to see the cross of silk or wrought in gold or of cloth which they wear on their jacket coat and garment on their shoulder such a work do pope Vrban meditate by which the world after flourish and restore the church right but the devil raise up Guibertus bishop of Ravenna a adversary to he who the perverseness of the emperor while Gregory this author speak like one of urban faction against Guibertus and the emperor ignorant of papal sleight this Stephen father of king Stephen be call come Carnotensis and be say to have as many castle as be day in the year hildebrand hold the seat support in his usurpation of the apostleship but the better sort acknowledge Gregory and after he urban who by the emperor aid Guibertus force from Rome till that year when the frank go to jerusalem by Rome Guibertus be in Almain urban by help of Matildis obtain the whole apostolic power she be then very potent in the roman country 1096. some in march other in April May june july August September and October set forth as they Robert earl of Normandy and Stephen of Bloise return to the sea and see such sacrilege and smell perhaps the pope plot on the five of April than easter-day set sail at the haven Brundisium there we begin dom. 1610. write by master GEORGE SANDYS and beer contract @. i his journey from Venice to Constantinople and observation by the way from Venice we depart on the twenty of August 1610. in the little defence of London the venetian be lord of this sea but not without contention with the papacy on ascention day the duke accompany with the cla^^ssimoes marriage of the sea. of that signiory be row thither in the a triumphal galley rich and exquisite gild above a room beneath which they row comprehend the whole length and breadth of the galley near the poop a throne the rest accommodate with seat where he solemn espouse the sea confirm by a ring throw therein the nuptial pledge and symbol of subjection this ceremony receive a beginning from that sea-battell fight and win by the uenetians under the conduct of Sebastiano zany against the force of Frederick Barbarossa in the quarrel of pope Alexander the three who fly his fury in the habit of a cook repair to Venice and there long live disguise in the monastery of charity zany return in triumph with the emperor son be meet by the pope and salute in this manner here take oh zany this ring of gold and by give it to the sea oblige it unto thou a ceremony that shall on this day be yearly observe both by thou and thy successor that posterity may know how you have purchase the dominion thereof by your valour and make it subject unto you as a wife to her husband we sail all along in the sight of Dalmatia at this day Sclavonia of the a people of Sclavonia Sarmatia they dissent not from the greek church in their religion throughout the north part of the world their language be understand and speak even from thence almost to the confine of Tartary the man wear halfe-sleeved gown of violet cloth with bonnet of the same they nourish only a lock of hair on the crown of their head the rest all shave the woman wear they not long and die they black for the most part their chief city be Ragusa heretofore Epidaurus a commonwealth of itself famous for merchandise and plenty of ship many small land belong thereunto but little of the continent they pay tribute to the Turk fourteen thousand zecchin yearly and spend as much more upon they in gift and entertainment send the grand signior every year a ship load with pitch for the use of his galley whereby they purchase their peace and a discharge of duty throughout the ottoman empire corfu the first island of note that we pass by lie in the ionian sea stretch east and west in form of a bow four and fifty mile long four and twenty broad distant about twelve from the main of Epirus call former Corcyra adorn with grove of orange lemon pomegranate figtree olive and the like enrich with excellent wine and abundance of honey upon the north-side stand a city that take the name of the island with a castle strong seat on a high rock which join by a Isthmos to the land and impregnable fortify the turk have testify as much in their many repulse it be the chair of a archbishop inhabit for the most by grecian as be the whole island and subject to the venetian saint maura lie next unto this once adjoin to the continent and separate by the labour of the inhabitant yet no further remove then by a bridge to be pass into call it be former leucadia of a white rock which lie before it towards Cephalonia on which stand the temple of Apollo in this island they have a city inhabit for the most part by jew receive by Bajazet the second at such time as they be expulse Spain by king Ferdinand Val compare a little beyond present her rocky mountain contain in circuit about fifty mile now inhabit by exile and pirate once call Ithaca so celebrate for the birth of Ulysses between this and the mouth of the gulf of Lepanto once name the gulf of Corinth lie certain little land or rather great rock now call Curzolari heretofore echinades make famous by that memorable sea-battell there obtain against the Turk by don John of Austria in the year 1571. and sing by a crown muse. we sail close by Cephalenia triangular in form one hundred and sixty mile in circumference the mountain intermix with profitable valley and the wood with champion vnwatered with river and poor in fountain but abound with wheat honey corent manna cheese wool turkeye excellent oil incomparable though not long last muscadines and powder for the die of scarlet this grow like a blister on the leaf of the holy oak a little shrub yet produce acorn be gather they rub out of it a certain red dust that convert after a while into worm which they kill with wine when they begin to quicken among her many harbour Argostoli be the principal capacious enough for a navy the inhabitant of this island be grecian the uenetians their sovereigns have pass through the straits that divide this island from the next vulgar call Canale Zant on the second of September we enter the haven of zacynthus and salute the castle with our ordnance this island nine hundred mile distant from Venice so call of zacynthus the son of Dardanus and at this day Zant contain in circuit not past threescore mile on the south and zacynthus or zant. southeast side rocky and mountainous but plain in the midst and unspeakable fruitful produce the best oil of the world and excellent strong wine both white and red which they call Ribolla but the chief riches thereof consist in corent which draw hither much traffic especial from England and Holland for here they know not what to do with they insomuch that whereas before they be scarce able to free themselves from importunate famine they now beside their private get amount to one hundred and fifty thousand zecchin store of corant do yearly pay unto saint mark forty eight thousand dollar for custom and other duty it be impossible that so little a portion of earth so employ shall be more beneficial the mountainous part be barren and the rest comprise within two or three not very ample valley but those all over husband like a entire garden they sow little corn as employ their ground to better advantage for which they sometime suffer be ready to starve when the weather continue for any season tempestuous and they can fetch their provision which they have as well of flesh as of corn from Morea be ten league distant they have salt-pit of their own and store of fresh water but little or no wood though celebrate for the abundance thereof by Homer and virgil. it be here a custom strict observe as also elsewhere within the straits belong to the christian not to suffer any to traffic or come ashore before they have a pratticke from the pratticke of health signior of health which will not be grant until forty day after their arrival especial if the ship come from Turkey and bring not a certificate that the place from whence they come be free from the infection if so perchance their restraint may be shorten during which time they have a guardian set over they they will not suffer a letter to be deliver if seal with thread before it be open and air if such as come to speak with they do but touch one of the ship or sometime but a rope they shall be force to ascend and remain there for the time limit it be death to he that shall come ashore without licence notwithstanding they upon request will carry you to the Lazaretto which be the nature of a pest-house there to abide until the date be expire but if any fall sick amongst they in the meane-season their pratticke be accord prolong a great inconvenience to the merchant but at Venice intolerable where when they have pratticke they be enforce to unlade at the Lazaretto so under pretence of air their good be open their quantity quality and condition know redound much to their detriment but for that we come from Venice we be free from this mischief and present suffer to land the town take or give a name to the island stretch along between the west side of the haven and the foot of the mountain perhaps a mile in length in breadth but narrow the street unpaved the building low by reason of the often earthquake whereunto this island be miserable subject two happen during my short abode here though of small importance although the seat of the town be excessive hot yet be it happy qualify by a north-east gale that blow from sea most constant about the midst of the day the great Turk have yearly a present of falcon from the governor accompany as some say with twelve hundred zecchin which he call a tribute it be in his power to distress they at his pleasure by restrain the relief of victual which they have from Morea and his adjoin dominion while we be here the captain Bassa pass by with sixty galley who yearly about this time sail in circuit to receive tribute suppress pirate and to do some exploit upon the Malteses spaniard and florentine with who they be only in hostility diverse of their galley put into the haven be courteous entertain for the venetian endeavour as much as in they lie to keep good quarter with the Turk not only for the reason aforesaid which perhaps may extend as far as their city their territory though large and fruitful too narrow to sustain so populous a state if unrelieve from Turkey and that their passage into the midland sea be interrupt not for the loss they shall sustain by the cessation of traffic with the mahometan but know he by dear experience too powerful a adversary for they by land and though they be perhaps strong enough by sea yet shall they lose a navy their loss be unrecoverable whereas the Turk within the space of a year be able to set forth another the inhabitant of this island be in general
