their bow and arrow ready draw but messenger also send to raise up all the whole rabblement thereabout upon we he tell we we be best give they content or else we be all but dead man wherefore to avoid further danger we give they their own desire upon condition they will pursue we no further nor suffer any of their company to molest we the chief of they answer stopherlo stopherlo that be God forbid God forbid we shall do you any harm if you pay we what we demand which we do with all speed and ride away from they be glad we be rid of they about ten mile from they we ride through a wood a very fit place to harbour thief dangerous wood who have kill certain man travel that way the day before and take away both a man and horse from the caravan which follow after and a woman also ride on a ass with their carriage and as our guide tell we he never travel that way but he see some man kill and therefore bid we all charge our piece and shoot off when he bid we though we see no body lest the wild arabs shall set upon we on the sudden lie in ambush which we also do in a place most dangerous to daunt the enemy before we see each other but before we come unto the most dangerous place there overtake we many turk well arm who dwell in jerusalem and be glad of our company thither and short after we have discharge every man his piece we see a great company of arab on a high mountain near unto our way yet out of the reach of our shot who perceive we to be too strong for they dare not set upon we and so by the providence of God we come that night to a ancient and famous city situate in a fruitful valley betwixt two mountain call Sychar a city in Sychar Samaria mention John 4. near whereunto we see Jacob well where our saviour Christ Jacob well pleasant water ask water of the woman of Samaria we come thither in good time for we be exceed thirsty and drink thereof liberal and free the water thereof go down very pleasant like unto milk from Jacob well we go into the city and lodge in a very ancient and stately cane but very bad keep it have be better for we to have sleep by Jacob well as other do for here we sleep on the hard stone near unto a chapel in the middle of the cane under two or three great figtree and mulberrie-tree where we be scarce safe from thief for we have some thing steal from we in the night while we sleep under the tree on fair broad stone whereunto we ascend by a fair stone pair of stair six or seven step from the ground Sychar be distant from en-gannim seven and twenty mile the nine and twenty of march we depart from Samaria to jerusalem and meet many soldier in several company by the way who know our janissary and other turk in our company let we pass by they quiet and give we the aliek that be peace be unto you the first part of this day journey be somewhat pleasant but the near we come to jerusalem the more barren and tedious our way be about ten of the clock we come to a great forest or wilderness full of tree and mountain when we be on the top of this mountain we see the main sea on our right hand and small ship sail towards joppa about three or four of the clock we come to a ruinous village call beer but of old as it be report beer Beersheba which in former time be a great city and it be say to be the place where joseph and Mary come from jerusalem the feast be end miss the child jesus and seek jerusalem he sorrow and return to jerusalem find he in the temple amidst the doctor hear they and pose they our purpose be to lodge here all night be all of we weary and hungry and all our provision spend but find nothing here to be have for money either for man or horse and understand that jerusalem be but ten mile off we go on in our way somewhat faint five or six mile and then behold the prospect of the city we be somewhat cheer and revive and solace ourselves with sing of psalm until we come near unto the city many Greek dwell in jerusalem see we afar off come to meet we suppose their patriarch have be in our company who come two or three day after we we dismount from our horse at the west gate of the city call joppa gate or the castle gate which be a very strong gate of iron with thirteen piece of brasse-ordnance plant on joppa gate the wall about the gate we stay in the porch of the gate and may not be admit into the city until we be search by a officer as the manner be in the mean time there come to we two italian friar viz. padre Angelo and padre Aurelio and kiss our hand and bid we welcome and tell we that two other englishman be at their house viz. master timberley master timberley^ath ^ath publish a book of his voyage and master borel when we be search without the gate by a turkish officer and deliver up our weapon to the porter to keep for we in the gatehouse until our return because no christian may enter into jerusalem with weapon these two Padres lead we to their monastery at the gate whereof we be search again by another turkish officer before we may enter into the house for the office of the former searcher at the gate of the city be only to receive the weapon of all christian and deliver they safe to they again at their departure but this searcher go further and search all our carriage which he cause to be open to see whether we have any gunpowder or any other engine there for they be very suspicious of all christian fear lest for devotion to the place they shall work treason therefore they suffer not christian to enter into the city weapon lest they make insurrection against they when they be many together and conquer the city as heretofore they have do to this end also be the city wall about with strong wall and fortify with four strong gate and a castle but by sultan Solyman and every gate well plant with ordnance for fear of christian and partly for hope have they environ this city with such strong wall that christian for devotion to the place may come and build within the wall and be subject to the Turk for though their wall be large and strong yet there be great room within the wall to build more house than be there for there be field of corn within the wall of the city and the house stand very thin scatter and disperse here one and there two or three together there be not one fair street in all jerusalem as it now be after they have thus narrow search all our carriage even to our case of bottle we be entertainment with the friar admit into the monastery at the entrance wherinto meet we master timberley and master boreel and then signior Franciscus Mann^rbu the padre guardian of the monastery and all the rest in order and bid we welcome and lead we into a fair parlour and set good cheer before we and serve we themselves after supper we deliver they our letter which we have bring from the Venice consul of Aleppo and other italian merchant there in our behalf which when they have read the guardian say our custom be when stranger come to we to call they the first night to mass and to confession and to give every man a candle to hold in his hand at mass time and at night to wash their foot and to bring they to bed and to many other ceremony during the whole time of their continuance there but as for we they understand by letter what we be and tell we that we be so high commend by their patron and benefactor the Venice consul and merchant of Aleppo that if they shall show we half the favour which be require at their hand they shall themselves lie without door and suffer we to rule and domineer at our pleasure and that therefore they will not urge we to any thing against our conscience but give free liberty both of person and conscience as if we be in England or in our own house elsewhere and so much the rather because they understand our merchant be rich and hope to gain by we in regard whereof although it be lend wherein they eat no flesh yet offer we hen egg milk any thing that be there to be have for money they request we to command it and during the time of our continuance there he command one padre Aurelio to attend upon we and see that we want nothing and another of his brethren one padre Angelo to be our guide abroad and to show we all ancient monument and place worth see either in the city or out of the city these kind speech be use they bring we to our chamber where we shall lodge all night and provide for every man several a good neat bed with fair sheet and all thing very wholesome and handsome where we sleep sweet and refresh our weary body all that night very comfortable but although they deal thus kind with we at the instance of their benefactor in give we liberty of conscience yet they deal not so with other for some I do know who have be there and make no conscience to do as they have do wherefore I admonish those a admonition to such as travel to jerusalem who have a desire to travel to jerusalem hereafter to take heed to themselves that they make not shipwreck of conscience for if they come not well commend or well moneyed or both there be no be for they except they partake with they in their idolatrous service true it be that the turk give liberty of conscience unto all that come thither but they give not entertainment unto any christian in their house and the greek patriarch be poor and not able to protect such as come unto they for refuge these Padres though they be papist yet have they rich benefactor and want nothing and for the most part very kind and courteous to stranger in all thing liberty of conscience only except wherein they seek to make other like unto themselves and to seduce they from their faith and to win they to the church of Rome and offer unto they who have money in their purse to make they knight of the sepulchre but no good english subject will accept of that order of knighthood for at the receive thereof they swear to be true to the pope and to the king of Spain and to other thing which no man can do with a good conscience and this kindness and liberty of conscience which we find amongst they we impute not so much to the man as to our own money for it cost we viz. one hundred ducat for our entertainment after we have rest one night in jerusalem the first day we walk about the city ourselves without our guide only to view the city we find it exceed hot and hot than it be usual at midsummer in England it seem strange unto i how it shall once be so cold that Peter shall creep to the fire and now at the same season so hot that we can not endure the heat of the sun but after I have be there a few day the very place resolve that doubt for there fall great dew and before the sun have dry it up it be cold and in the night season about that time of the year somewhat cold as I feel by experience when I sleep in the field all night and Peter have watch with Christ in the night may well be cold in the morning before the heat of the sun have expel cold but here we will break off have with master sandys his eye curious view jerusalems holy in the former chapter chap. x. the journey of plain appear to the town the governor present apprehend and answer again with three other fire in like manner each thus know the other be and intent smith though distant seven mile signify to he these word on Thursday at night I will charge on the east at the alarm sally you eberspaught answer speech by torch he will and thus it be do first he write his message as brief you see as can be then divide the alphabet in two part thus a b c d e f g h i EDWARD l with one light the other letter follow with two m n o p q r s t five w 10 z. the first part from a to l be a good stratagem signify by show and hide one link so oft as there be letter from a to that letter you mean the other part from m to z be mention by two light in like manner the end of a word be signify by show of three light ever stay your light at that letter you mean till the other may write it in a paper and answer by his signal which be one light. it be do begiun to account the letter by the light every time from a or m by this mean also the other return his answer thereby each understanding other the guide all this time have well view the camp return to Kizell who doubt of his power be but twenty thousand be 1601. chap. 3 two voyage of master JOHN NEWEERIE one into the holy land the other to Balsara Ormus Persia and back through Turkey i John Newberie citizen and merchant of London desirous to see the world the eight of march 1578. accord to the computation of the church of England begin a voyage from the city of London to Tripoli in Syria and thence to jop and Jerusalem and the country round about adjoin which I perform in pass through France to Marceils where I embark myself and pass through the Levant or Mediterrane sea arrive in Tripoli the thirteen day of May and within few day after at joppe and thence at Jerusalem and the chief place thereabout and spend a month in visit the monument of those country I return to jop the ten of june 1579. and the fifteen of the say month arrive again in Tripoli from whence short after I visit mount Libanus and return speedy to the say port of Tripoli I embark myself in a ship of marceil the first of julie and the three and twenty of the say month I put in at Candia and the seven day of September arrive safe in marceil and pass through France by lion Paris Rouen and deep the ten of November of the aforesaid year 1579. by god help arrive safe in London i the say John Newberry * * this voyage as the former for time be before that of sir Anthony Shirley but that in honour of the person and employment have and deserve precedence be encourage by the prosperous success of my former voyage to Tripoli Jerusalem and mount Lybanus undertake a far more long and dangerous voyage by the straits of Gibraltar the mediterranean sea the aforesaid Tripoli and down the river of Euphrates as far as the city of Ormus in the gulf of Persia and from thence through the country of Lar and the most eastern part of Persia to Media Armenia more than thirty foot high from the water and can stow in hold but two butt of height one upon another except it be in the middle in this town of Tomourra be sell twenty egg for a Asper and a good hen for two asper and beef Bacon bread wine beer and Mede plenty and very good fresh fish more than of any thing else here be sell for one Asper two pike either of they better than three span long and three carp either of they a span and a half long also here be great store of sturgeon and herring in this river the order of their make of caviar of their sturgeon be this the caviar or roe must be take whole out of the fish and then slash it a little with a knife and so salt it well for three the order of make caviar day and three night and put it in a barrel or fat and make a hole underneath that the water or salt that come from the caviar may void forth and after these three day be past take it and wash it very well with fresh water until the salt be clean go from it and after this put it in barrel for the space of other three day and one must tread it down with his clean foot also you must make a hole under the barrel for the water to void away and then lie some great stone upon it to press it and to make it hard and after these three day be past they make caviar of three sort of fish take out the bottom and set in a new and so it may be carry through out the world. and the name of the three fish of the roe whereof they make it be these sturgeon and Mourrounna and Merssenne and the best time of the year to make it in be june and july in this town of Tomourra be certain merchant of Sio that be lord of the same and in time past it have be a fair town but the tartar have two or three time spoil it and once they carry away fifty person out of it and the country near come down from the lake chieldor-giol in Armenia in manifold arm and branch and therefore be call by the country people by a name which signify a thousand head here it be that merchant use to pass down by bark unto Babylon thereby to avoid and shun the great charge and wearisomeness of travel through the desert of Arabia which passage they make sometime in fifteen day sometime in twenty day and sometime in thirty day answerable to the rise and fall time and manner of go down the river of the river and the best time to pass thither be either in April or October when the river do swell with abundance of rain the boat be flat-bottomed because the river be shallow in many place so that when they travel in the month of july August and September they find the river at so low a ebb that they be fain to carry with they a spare boat or two to lighten their own if they shall chance to fall on the shoal every night after sunset they fasten these boat to a stake the merchant lie aboard and the mariner upon the shore as near as they can unto the same in this passage down the river you shall meet with diverse troop of arabian who will barter their provision of diet for they care not for money as hen kid lamb butter and sour milk for glass comb coral amber knife bread and pomegranate pill wherewith they use to tan their goat skin in which they churn with all all of they as well woman child and man be very good swimmer who oftentimes will swim to the bark side with vessel full of milk upon their head these people be very thievish and therefore in your passage down good watch must be keep but to return where we leave we be constrain by the deepness of the river to ferry over our whole Caravan which consist of a thousand person beside camel horse mule and ass by reason of which multitude we spend a whole day in transport over the say Caravan the gain of which transportation yield the ferryman a Shaughee which be five penny english upon a beast be over the aforesaid river we we be encounter with a certain troop of people call the Curdies which some think to be a remnant of the ancient parthian this rude the description of the Curdies a most thievish people the curdies worshipper of the devil people be of a goodly stature and well proportion and do never go abroad without their arm as bow and arrow scimatarre and buckler yea and at such time when a man for age be ready to go down to his grave they do adore and worship the devil to the end he may not hurt they or their cattle and very cruel be they to all sort of christian in which regard the country which they inhabit be at this day term the land of the devil they participate much of the nature of the arabian and be as infamous in their latrociny and robbery as the arabian themselves they live under the commandment of the great Turk but with much freedom and liberty this thievish company do sundry time arrest our Caravan affirm that their prince have send for a dollar on a sum of good without the payment whereof be five several time demand we shall not pass through their country one village of note be there in this country whole inhabit by the Curdies be five day journey from Caraemit and the persian king and government of sir ANTHONY Shirley after two day travel from Com we arrive at cassan a principal city in Parthia very famous and rich howsoever Ortelius and other make no mention of it this the description of cassan. city be seat in a goodly plain and because it have no mountain near it but within a day journey the heat be very fastidious as great almost as it be in ormuz the spring and harvest be soon in this climate then in any other part of the persian dominion it want neither fountain spring nor garden but abound with all necessary whatsoever consist altogether in merchandise and the best trade of all the land be there be great frequent with all sort of merchant especial out of India the people be very industrious and curious in all science but especial in weave girdle and sash in make velvet satin damask very good Ormuzenes and persian carpet of a wonderful fineness in a word it be the very Magazeen and Warehouse of all the persian city for these stuff here may you buy all manner of drug and spice and turkass with store of pearl diamond and ruby as also all sort of silk as well wrought as raw I be persuade that in one year there be more silk bring into cassan then be of broad-cloath bring into the city of London this city be much to be commend for the civil and good government which civil and good government be there use a idle person be not permit to live among they the child that be but six year old be set to labour no ill rule disorder or riot be there suffer for they have a law among they resemble the egyptian law which Diodorus mention whereby every person be compel to give his name to the magistrate therewith declare what kind of life he like how he live and what be he exercise and if any do tell untrue be either well beat on the foot or employ in public slavery the great annoyance that this city be the persian law against idleness scorpion of m. Mild^all you have sup. l. 3. c. 1. the description of Hispaan infest withal be the abundance and multitude of black scorpion of a exceed greatness which many time do much harm if a special care be not have of they at this city master John Mildenall and myself part company he travel to lahor in the east Indies and my self set forward to the great city of Hispaan three day travel distant from cassan. this city in time past be call Ecatompolis the city of a hundred gate and well it may keep that name still since the huge wall of the same contain in circuit a easy day journey on horseback and be become the great city in all the persian dominion which be so much the more magnify and make populous by reason of the king resiance therein very strong be this city by situation compass about with a very great wall and water with deep channel of run spring convey into it from a part of the coronian mountain which the sort of Hispaan be as a wall inaccessible about it on the north side be erect a strong fort or castle be compass about with a wall of a thousand and seven hundred yard and in the midst thereof be build a tower or rather a strong keep sundry chamber and lodging therein but store with little ordnance on the west side of this city stand two seraglio the one for the king the the king seraglio other for his woman palace of great state and magnificence far exceed all other proud building of this city the wall glister with red marble and parget of diverse colour yea all the palace be pave with chequer and tesseled work and on the same be spread carpet wrought with silk and gold the window of alabaster white marble and much other spot marble the post and wicket of massy ivory chequered with glister black ebony so curious wrought in wind knot as may easy stay then satisfy the eye of the wonder beholder near unto this palace be a garden very spacious and large all flourish and beautiful the king garden replenish with a thousand sundry kind of graft tree and sweet smell plant among which the lily the hyacinth the gillyflower the rose the violet the flower-gentle and a thousand other odoriferous flower do yield a most pleasant and delightful sight to all beholder there be a thousand fountain and a thousand brook among they all as the father of they all a pretty river which with his mild course and delightsome noise do divide the garden from the king palace neither be this garden so strait look unto but that both the king soldier and citizen may and do at their pleasure oftentimes on horseback repair thither to recreate themselves in the shadow and walk of those green and as a guard for the gate of this sumptuous palace the king keep certine order of the guard of the king palace soldier whereof the most noble and the great in number be call church which be as it be the king pensioner be eight thousand in number all of they divide under several captain which captain do yield obedience to the general captain call churchi-bassa a man always of great authority next unto this order be another call Esahul to the number of a thousand distinguish also under particular captain and the chief captain be call esahul-bassa all these be maintain by certain town and village which be feudatary to the crown of Persia and they receive at certain time of the king armor horse apparel and tent every one as he be in place and degree with this strong garrison be the king daily attend upon and maintain the majesty of his court especial when he ride in progress and for the government of this city there be beside the king and the prince twelve Sultanes the order of the persian dignity in Hispaan the sultane the treasurer the great chancellor the Caddi or judge but three especial be appoint by the king for the general government of the whole empire have their several distinct charge one have the care of all martial affair throughout the kingdom and the other two receive all the revenue keep a just account thereof which then we may call treasurer next unto these be the Mordari two great chancellor who offie be to write all order commandment and letter concern the government of the kingdom one of they keep the seal and the other the pen. beside these there be two Caddi that be two judge who make answer and give sentence only in matter of controversy and civil quarrel but as touch criminal cause they have no further authority then to frame examination of witness and to make declaration thereof which they call the sygill and this sygill they deliver up into the hand of the sultan that be either governor of the city or else of the empire and he cause execution to be do accord to custom and look as Hispaan be govern so other city have the selfsame magistrate all be at the king disposition and appointment concern the church government there be in this city first the chief of the law who the mustaed-dini they call the a wicked and profane priest and in the other subject city be certain peculiar head obedient to this chief priest who be not choose and displace at his pleasure as the popish bishop be by the pope but by the king himself who be not only a king but a priest as Mahomet and aly be but to avoid trouble the king grant that favour and put over that burden from himself unto other to who judgement he also refer himself whensoever any consultation be touch their law or profane superstition under this the calif great priest be calif and these do daily execute service in the mosque or temple the chief of these calif be he that put the horn upon the king head when he be first enthronize a ceremony once perform in Cafe near Babylon but since Solyman the turkish emperor win Assyria from the persian it have be sometime perform in Casbin and sometime in Hispaan final the inhabitant of this city do much resemble the ancient parthian in diverse the nature of the Persian thing but special in their continual ride they ride on horseback for the most part on horseback they fight with the e^^mie they execute all affair as well public as private on horseback they go from place to place on horseback they buy and sell and on horseback they confer and talk with one another and the difference between the gentleman and the slave be that the slave never ride nor the gentleman never go on foot beside the nature of people be arrogant seditious deceitful and very unquiet but that the fierceness of their nature be much restrain by the king severe government to sensuality they be much the Persian give to sensuality incline have three sort of woman as they term they viz. honest woman half honest woman and courtesan and yet they chastise no offence with like extremity as adultery and that as well in the half honest woman as in the honest last of all they be full of crafty stratagem the Persian very inconstant and be breaker of their promise a vice that be very inbred in all barbarian not content with any man government long and lover of novelty abas howsoever by the shed of much blood * * of Africa and the christianity there @. i thing remarkable observe in his voyage to the Indies sea-fight with the portugal apology very often call truth into question have therefore nothing for to countenance these my rude relation but the certainty of they I omit all unnecessary introduction use no further preface than this that the reader will undoubted believe what the relator do most faithful deliver so to make a entry upon the first beginning of our voyage the three of February 1615. our fleet consist of six goodly ship the Charles unicorn james globe swan and rose all under the command of captain Benjamin joseph fall down from Gravesend into Tilburie hope the nine of march after a long and tire expectation it please God to send we what we desire a north-east wind which day we leave that weary road and set sail for east India the wind be favourable to we till the sixteenth day at night at which time a most fearful storm overtake we we be then in the bay of Portugal in this storm we lose sight both of the globe and Rose the globe come again into our company the two and twentieh follow but the rose be no more hear of till her arrive at Bantam about six month after this storm continue violent till the one and twenty the eight and twenty we have sight of the grand canary and that mountain which Pico de Teneriffa threaten the sky in the island of Teneriffa common call the Peake which by reason of its immense height in a clear day may be see more than forty league at sea as the mariner report these land lie in eight and twenty degree of north latitude the one and thirty be easter day we pass under the tropic of cancer and the seven of April the sun be our zenith from that day until the fourteen we be becalm endure extreme heat the sixteenth we meet with wind which the mariner call the turnadoe so variable and uncertain that sometime within the space of one hour all the turnadoe two and thirty several wind will blow these wind be accompany with much thunder and lightning and with extreme rain so noisome that it make man clothes present to stink upon their back the water likewise of these slimy unwholesome shower wheresoever it stand will in short time bring forth many offensive creature these turnadoe meet with we when we be about twelve degree of north latitude and keep we company ere they quit we till we be two degree southward of the equinoctial under which we pass the eight and twenty of April the nineteenth of May be whitsunday we pass the tropic of Capricorn so that we be seven week complete under the torrid zone between the tropic we see almost every day different kind of fish in great abundance than elsewhere as the great Leviethan who God have make to take his pastime in the sea dolphin boneetooe albicore fly fish and many other some whale we see of a exceed greatness who in calm weather often arise and show themselves above the whale water where they appear like to great rock in their rise spout up into the air with noise a great quantity of water which fall down again about they like a shower the dolphin dolphines be a fish call for his swiftness the arrow of the sea differ from many other in that he have tooth upon the top of his tongue he be please to the eye smell and taste of a changeable colour fine like a roach cover with very small scale have a fresh delightsome send above other fish and in taste as good as any these dolphines be wont often to follow our ship not so much I think for the love they bear unto man as some write as to feed themselves with what they find cast overboard whence it come to pass that many time they feed we for when they swim close to our ship we strike they with a broad instrument full of barbe call a harp iron fasten to a rope by which we hale they in this beautiful dolphin may be a fit emblem of a race of man who under sweet countenance carry sharp tongue boneetooe and albicore be in colour shape and taste much like to mackeril but boneetooe and albicore fly fish grow to be very large the fly fish of all other live the most miserable life for be in the water the dolphines boneetooe and albicore persecute they and when they will escape by their flight be oftentimes take by ravenous fowl somewhat like our kite which hover over the water these fly fish be like man profess two trade and thrive of neither but to proceed in our passage the twelve of june early in the morning we espy our long wish for harbour the bay of Soldania about twelve league short of the cape of good hope wherein we come happy to a anchor that forenoon here we find one of the company ship call the lion come from surat and bind for England who have a fair gale put to sea the fourteen day at night we make our abode in this harbour till the eight and twenty follow on which day we Soldania be well water and refresh depart when the swan our five ship take her way for Bantam the nine and twenty we double the cape of good hope who latitude be in thirty five degree south off this cape there set continual a most violent current westward whence it come to pass that when a strong contrary wind meet it their impetuous opposition make the sea so to rage that some ship have be swallow but many endanger in those mountain of water few ship pass that way without a storm the two and twenty isle of Comora of july we discover the great island of Madagascar the use of man as that it be able to subsist and flourish of itself without the least help from any neighbour to speak first of that which nature require most food this land abound in singular good plenty of victual wheat Rice barley and diverse other kind of grain to make bread the staff of life their wheat grow like we but the grain of it be somewhat big and more white of which the inhabitant breath their building be general base except it be in their city wherein I have observe many fair pile many of their house be build high and flat on the top from whence in the house and street cool season of the day they take in fresh air they have no chimney to their house for they never use fire but to dress their meat in their upper room they have many light and door to let in the air but use black as a raven but not curl they love not a man or woman that be very white or fair because that as they say be the colour of leper common amongst white in bad estimation they most of the mahometan but the moolaes which be their priest or those that be very old and retire keep their chin bare but suffer the hair on their upper lip to grow as long as nature will feed it they usual shave off all the hair from their head reserve only a lock on the crown for Mahomet to pull they into heaven both among the mahometan and gentile be excellent barber the people often wash their body and anoint themselves with sweet oil the habit both of the man and woman be little different make for the most part of white cotton-cloth for the fashion they be close straight to the middle hang loose downward attire below the knee they wear long breeches underneath make close to their body that reach to their ankle ruffle like boot on the small of their leg their foot be bare in their shoe which most common they wear like slipper that they may the more ready put they off when they come into their house who floor be cover with excellent carpet make in that kingdom good as any in Turkey or Persia or somewhat else accord to the quality of the man more base upon which they sit when as they confer or eat like tailor on their shop-board the man head be cover with a long thin wreath of cloth white or colour which go many time about they they call it a Shash they uncover not their head when as they do reverence salutation to their superior but in stead of that bow their body put their right hand to the top of their head after that they have touch the earth with they as much as to say the party they salute shall if he please tread upon they those that be equal take one the other by the chin or beard as joab do Amasa 2. sam. 20 but salute in love not treachery they have good word to express their wel-wish as this greeb-a Nemoas that be I wish the prayer of the poor and many other like these most significant the mahometan woman except they be dishonest or poor come not abroad they be their woman very well favour though not fair their head cover with veil their hair hang down behind they painter for the language of this empire I mean the vulgar it be call Indostan a smooth tongue language and writing and easy to be pronounce which they write as we to the right hand the learned tongue be persian and arabian which they write backward as the hebrew to the left there be little learning among they a reason whereof may be their penury of book which be but few and they manuscript but doubtless they be man of strong capacity and be there literature among they will be the author of many excellent work they have hear of Aristotle who they call Aplis and have some of his book translate Aristotle and Avicen into arabian Auicenna that noble physician be bear in Samarcandia the country of tamerlaine in who science they have good skill the common disease of the country be bloody flux hot fever and calenture in all which they prescribe fast as a principal remedy that filthy disease the consequence of incontinency be common amongst they the disease age. music poem and annal people in general live about our age but they have more old man they delight much in music and have many string and wind instrument which never seem in my ear to be any thing but discord they write many witty poem and compose story or annal of their own country and profess themselves to have good skill in astrology and in man of that Profession^ the king put so much confidence that he will not undertake a journey nor yet do any thing of the least consequence unless his wizard tell he it be a good and prosperous hour the gentile begin their year the first of march. the mahometan they at the very instant their year as the astrologer guess that the sun enter into Aries from which time the king keep a feast call the signify nine day which time it continue like that Abasuerus make in the three year of his reign ester the first where all his noble assemble in their great pomp present he with gift he repay they again with princely reward of this see before in sir t. roe at which time be in his presence I behold most immense and incredible riches to my amazement in gold pearl precious stone jewel and many other glitter vanity this feast I take notice of at Mandoa where the mogul have a most spacious house large than any I have see in which many excellent arch and vault speak for the exquisite skill of his subject in architecture at agra he have a palace wherein two large tower the least ten foot square be cover with plate of the pure gold. there be no hang on the wall of his house by reason of the heat the wall be either hang paint or else beautify with a pure white lime then that we call spanish the floor pave with stone or else make with lime and sand like our plaster of Paris be spread with rich carpet there lodge none in the king house but his woman and eunuch and some little boy king house which he keep about he for a wicked use he always eat in private among his woman upon great variety of excellent dish which dress and prove by the taster be serve in private among his woman upon great variety of excellent dish which dress and prove by the taster be serve in vessel of gold as they say cover and seal up and so by eunuch bring to the king. he have meat ready at all hour and call for it at pleasure they feed not free on full dish of beef and mutton as we but much on Rice boil with piece their diet of flesh or dress many other way they have not many roast or bake meat but stew most of their flesh among many dish of this kind i will take notice but of one they call make of venison cut in slice to which they put onion and herb some root with a little spice and butter the most savoury meat I ever taste and do almost think it that very dish which jacob make ready for his father when he get the blessing in this kingdom there be no inn to entertain stranger only in great town and inn city be fair house build for their receipt which they call sarray not inhabit where any passenger may have room free but must bring with he his bedding his cook and other necessary wherein to dress his meat which be usual carry on camel or else in cart draw with ox wherein they have tent to pitch when they meet with no sarr (...) the inferior sort of people ride on ox horse mule camel or dromedary the woman ride like the man or else in slight coach with two wheel cover on the top and back but the forepart and side open unless they carry woman they will convenient hold two person beside the driver they be draw by ox one yoke in a coach suit for colour but many of they be white not very large they be guide with cord which go through the part of their nostril and so betwixt their horn into the coachmens hand they dress and keep they clothe as their horse they be natural nimble to which use make they so fit to perform that labour as that they will go twenty mile a day or more with good speed the better sort ride on elephant or else be carry upon man shoulder alone in a slight thing they call a Palankee which be like a couch or stand palate but cover with a canopy this shall seem a ancient effeminacy sometime use in Rome Inuenal thus describe a fat lawyer that fill one of they for pastime they delight in hawk hunt of hare dear or wild beast their dog pastime for chase be make somewhat like our gray-hound but much less they open not in the pursuit of the game they hunt likewise with leopard which by leap seize on that they pursue they have a cunning device to take wildfowl where a fellow go into the water with a fowl of that kind he dsire to catch who skin be stuff so artificial as that it appear Sly fowl alive he keep all his body but the face under water on which he lay this counterfeit thus come among they pluck they by the leg under water they shoot for pastime much in shoot bow which be make curious in the country of buffeloes horn glue together to which they have arrow make of little cane excellent head and feather in these they be so skilful that they will kill bird fly other take delight in manage their horse on which they ride or else be otherwise carry though they have not one quarter of a mile to go the man of quality hold it dishonourable to go on foot in their house they play much at that most ingenious game we call chess or else at table chess table God mountebank they have card but quite different from we sometime they make themselves merry with cunning juggler or mountebank who will suffer snake they keep in basket to bite they and present cure the swell with powder or else they see the trick of ape and monkey in the southern part of Indostan be great store of large white ape some I dare bold say as tall as our big gray-hound they be fearful as it shall seem to bird that make large ape cunning bird their nest in tree wherefore nature have teach they this subtlety to secure themselves by build their little house on the twig of the utmost bough there hang like pursenet to which the ape can possible come every great town or city of India have market twice a day in the cool season present market twice a day after the sun be rise and a little before his set they sell almost every thing by weight in the heat of the day they keep their house where the man of better fashion lie on couch or sit on their carpet have servant stand about they who beat the air with broad fan of stiff leather or the like make wind to cool they and take thus their ease they often call their barber who tender gripe and smite their arm and other part of their body in stead of exercise to stir the blood it be a please wantonness and much use in those hot clime I must needs commend the mahometans and gentile for their good and faithful service amongst fidelity who a stranger may travel alone with a great charge of money or good quite through the country and take they for his guard yet never be neglect or injure by they they follow their master on foot carry sword and buckler or bow and arrow for their defence and by reason of great plenty of provison in that kingdom a man may hire they upon easy condition for they will not desire above five shilling the moon pay the next day after the change to provide themselves all necessary and for it do most diligent service such be their piety to their parent that those which have no great mean will impart half of it at the least to relieve their necessity choose rather for to famish themselves then to see they want there be both among the mahometans and gentile man of undaunted courage those of courage of some note among the mahometans be call baloche inhabit haiacan adjoin to the kingdom of Persia or else patans take their denomination from a province in the kingdom of Bengala these will look a enemy bold in the face and maintain with their life their reputation of valour among the many sect of gentile there be but one race of figliter call rashboote a number of which live by spoil who in troop surprise poor passenger cruel butcher those they get under their power those except all the rest in the country be in general pusilaminous and have rather quarrel they fight have such poor spirit in respect of we christian that the mogul be please often to use this proverb that one Portugal will beat three of they and one Englishman three portugal touch their munition for the war they have good ordnance make for aught I can gather munition vertoman tell of Portugal fugitive which at the portugal first come run to the Indian and teach they this art. very ancient in those part iron piece carry upon elephant before describe and lesser gun make for footman who be somewhat long in take their aim but come as near the mark as any I ever see they fire all their piece with match as for gunpowder they make very good they use lance and sword and target bow and arrow their sword be make crooked like a falchion very sharp but for want of skill in those that temper they will break rather than bend and therefore we often sell our sword-blade at high price that will bow and become straight again I have see horseman there who have carry whole armoury about they thus appoint at their side good sword under they sheve of arrow on their shoulder buckler and upon their back gun fasten with belt at the left side bow hang in case and lance about two yard and a half long have excellent steel head which they carry in their hand yet for all this harness the most of they dare not resist a man of courage though he have for his defence but the worst of those weapon the army in those eastern war oftentimes consist of incredible multitude they talk of some which have exceed that mighty host which zerah king of Ethiopia bring against asa 2. Chron. 14. the music they have when they go to battle be from kittle-drum and long wind instrument the army on both side usual begin with most furious onset but in short time for want of good discipline one side be rout and the controversy not without much slaughter decide the mahometan have fair church which they call mesquit build of stone the broad mesquit side towards the west be make up close like a wall that towards the east be erect on pillar so that the length of they be north and south which way they bury their dead at the corner of their great church which stand in city be high pinnacle to who top the Moolaas ascend certain time of the day and proclaim their prophet Mahomet thus in arabian Mahomet resul-alla that be no god but one God and Mahomet the ambassador of god. this in stead of bell which they endure not in their temple put the most religious in mind of their devotion which word master Coryat often hear in agra upon a coryats crudity certain time get up into a turret over against the priest and contradict he thus in a loud voice la Alla hazaret-eesa ebn-alla no god but one God and Christ the son of God and further add that Mahomet be a impostor which bold attempt in many other place of Asia where Mahomet be more zealous profess have forfeit his life with as much torture as tyranny can invent but here every man have liberty to profess his own religion free and for any restriction I ever observe to dispute against they with impunity now concern their burial every mahometan of quality in his life time provide a fair burial near thank sepulchre for himself and kindred encompass with a firm wall a good circuit of ground near some Tanke about which they delight for to bury their dead or else in a place nigh spring of water that may make pleasant fountain near which he erect a tomb round or square vault upon pillar or else make close to be enter with door under which be the body of the dead inter the rest of the ground they plant with tree and flower as if they will make elysian field such as the poet dream of wherein their soul may take their repose they bury not within their church there be many goodly monument of this saint calendar kind rich adorn build to the memory of such as they have esteem saint of which they have a large calendar in these be lamp continual burn whither man transport with blind devotion daily resort there to contemplate the happiness these peer for so they call of this see before in other journal Finch etc. they enjoy but among many fair pile there dedicate to this use the most excellent be at Secandra a village three mile from agra it be begin by achabar-sha this king father who there lie bury and finish by this present king who mean to lie beside he their Moolaas employ much of their time like scrivener to do business for other they have liberty to marry as well as the people from who they be not distinguish in habit some Moolaas or priest live retire that spend their day in meditation or else in give good moral precept unto other there be of high esteem and so be another sort call seayd who derive themselves religious from Mahomet the priest do neither read nor preach in their church but there be a set form of prayer in the arabian tongue not understand by most of the common people yet repeat prayer in unknown tongue by they as well as by the Moolaas they likewise rehearse the name of God and Mahomet certain time every day upon bead like the mislead Papist who seem to regard the bead number rather than the weight of prayer before they go into their church they wash their gesture of prayer foot and enter in put off their shoe as they begin their devotion they stop their ear and fix their eye that nothing may divert their thought then in a soft and still voice they utter their prayer wherein be many word most significant express the omnipotency greatness eternity and other attribute of god. many word full of humiliation confess with diverse submissive gesture their own unworthiness when they pray cast themselves low upon their face sundry time and then acknowledge that they be burden to the earth and poison to the air and the like and therefore dare not so much as look up to heaven but at last comfort themselves in the mercy of God through the mediation of Mahomet and many amongst they to the shame of we christian what impediment soever they have either by pleasure or profit pray five time every day at six nine twelve three and six of the clock but by the way they distinguish their time in a different manner from we divide the day into four and the night into as many part which they call pore these be again subdivide each into eight part which they call grease measure accord to the ancient custom by water drop out of one little vessel into another by which there always stand servant appoint for that clepsydra clock purpose smite with a hammer a concave piece of pure metal like the inner part of a ordinary platter hang by the brim on a wire the number of grease and pore as they pass for temperance the temperance of many both among the mahometan and gentile it be such as that they will rather die like the mother and her seven son 2. mac. 7. then eat or drink any thing their law forbid such meat and drink as their law allow they use only to satisfy nature not appetite hate gluttony and esteem drunkenness as indeed it be a second madness and therefore have but one word in their language most for a drunkard and a madman mest. fast and feast they keep a solemn Lent which they call the Ram-Ian about the month of August which continue one whole moon during which time those that be strict in their religion forbear their woman and will take neither meat nor drink so long as the sun be above their horizon but after he be set eat at pleasure towards the end of this lend they consecrate a day of mourn to the memory of their dead friend when I have behold diverse of the mean sort make bitter lamentation beside this common sadness there be many foolish woman who often in the year so long as they survive moisten the grave of their husband or child with affectionate tear but when the night begin to cover the day of general mourn they fire a innumerable company of lamp and light which they set on the side and top of their house and all other most conspicuous place and when these be extinguish take food the Ram-Ian full end the most devout mahometans assemble to some famous misquit where by a moola some part of the Alcoran which they will not touch without reverence be public read they keep a feast in November call buccaree signify the ramfeast when they solemn kill a ram and roast he in memory of that ram which redeem ishmael as they say when Abraham be ready to make he a sacrifice many other feast they have in memory of Mahomet and their peer they have the book of Moses who they call moosa carym-alla Moses the righteous book of god. Ibrahim calim-alla Abraham the faithful of god. so ishmael the true sacrifice of god. dahoode David the prophet of god. Selimon Solomon the wisdom of God all express as the former in short arabian word to who particular remembrance they daily sing ditty and moreover there be not a man amongst they but those of the rude Mendee who like the priest of Baal often cut their flesh with knife and lancer other I 1. king. 18. have see who out of devotion put such massy fetter of iron upon their leg as that they can scarce notwithstanding this polygamy the hot jealousy of the lustful mahometan be such that they will scarce endure the brother or father of their belove wife or woman to have speech with they except in their presence and time by this restraint have make it odious for such woman as have the reputation of honesty to be see at any time by stranger but if they dishonour their husband bed or be unmarried be find incontinent profess chastity adultery punish rather than they shall want punishment their own brother will be their executioner who for such unnatural act shall be commend rather than question who eunuch in their minority be deprive of all that may provoke jealousy their marriage be solemnize in great pomp for after the moola have join their hand marriage with some other ceremony and word that there be seven orb above which be the seat of God that God know not petty thing or if he do regard they not they circumscribe God unto place say that he may be see but as in a mist afar off not near they believe that there be devil but so bind in chain that they can hurt they they call a man Adam from our first father Adam who wife tempt with the forbid fruit take it as they say and eat it down but as her husband swallow tradition of Adam it the hand of God stop it in his throat whence man have a bunch there which woman have not call by they Adam apple as ancient among the jew their priesthood be hereditary for every brahmins son be a priest and marry a brahmins daughter and so among all the gentile the man take the daughter of those to be their wife which be of their father marry in the same tribe and trade tribe sect and occupation for instance a merchant son marry a merchant daughter and every man son that live by his labour marry the daughter of he that be of his own profession by which mean they never advance themselves these gentile take but one wife of which they be not so fearful as the mahometan of their multitude for they suffer they to go abroad they be marry young at six or seven year old their parent make the contract and about twelve come together their nuptial as those of the mahometan be perform with much pomp and jollity for their habit it differ little from the mahometan but many of the woman wear ring their habit upon their toe and therefore go barefoot they have likewise broad ring of brass or better metal accord to the quality of the woman about the small of the leg to take off and on haply such as the prophet mean by the tinkle ornament about the foot or the ornament of the leg which the jewish woman be wont to put on Esay 3 and such as these they have about their arm the flappe or neither part of their ear be bore when they be young which ear and earring hole daily stretch and make wide by thing keep in it for that purpose at last become so large that it will hold a ring I dare bold say as large as a little saucer make hollow on the side for the flesh to rest in both man and woman wash their body every day before they eat wash which do they keep off their clothes but the cover of modesty till they have feed this outward wash appertain as they think to their cleanse from sin not unlike the pharisy who will not eat with unwashen hand mar. 7. hence they ascribe a certain divinity to river but above all to Ganges daily flock thither in troop and there throw in piece of gold or silver accord to their devotion and ability after which they wash their body both man and woman paint on their forehead or other part of their face red or yellow spot spot now far for their gross opinion they believe not the resurrection of flesh and therefore burn the body of their dead near some river if they may with conveniency wherein burn they sow the ash their widow marry not but after the loss of their husband cut their widow hair and spend all their life follow as neglect creature whence to be free from shame many young woman be ambitious to die with honour as they esteem it when their fiery love manner of wife burn with their husband bring they to the flame as they think of martyrdom most willing follow their dead husband unto the fire and there embrace be burn with they but this they do voluntary not compel the parent and friend of those woman will most joyful accompany they and when the wood be fit for this hellish sacrifice and begin to burn all the people assemble shout and make a noise that the screeche of this torture creature may not be hear not much unlike the custom of the ammonite who when they make their child pass through the fire to moloch cause certain Tabret or drum to sound that their cry may not be hear whence the place be call tophet a Tabret 2. king 23. 10. there be one parcel sect among the gentile which neither burn nor inter their dead they be call parcees who encircle piece of ground with high stone wall remote from house or roade-waye and therein lay their carcase wrap in sheet thus have no other tomb but the gorge of ravenous fowl the gentile for the most part be very industrious they till the ground or else spend their gentile industry and idleness of m^^res time otherways diligent in their vocation there be amongst they most curious artificer who be the best ape for imitation in the world for they will make any new thing by pattern the mahometan be general idle who be all for to morrow a word common in their mouth they live upon the labour of the gentile some of which poor seduce infidel will eat of nothing that have life and these live upon herb and milk and butter and cheese and sweetmeat of which they make diverse kind whereof the most wholesome be green ginger as well preserve there as in any part of the world other will eat fish and no live thing else the rashboote eat swines-flesh most hateful to the mahometan some will eat of one kind of flesh some of another but all the gentile abstain from beef out of the beef not eat excellent esteem they have of cow and therefore give the king yearly beside his other exaction great sum of money as a ransom for those creature whence among other good provision we meet there but with little beef those most tender heart idolater be call Banians who hold Pythagoras his (@) (@) (@) (@) (@) Banians as a prime article of their fath. they think that the soul of the best man and woman when their body let they out of prison take their repose in cow which in their opinion be the best of all creature so the soul of the wicked go into vile beast as the soul of glutton foolish pity charitable work and drunkard into swine the soul of the voluptuous and incontinent into monkey and ape the soul of the furious cruel and revengeful into lion tiger and wolf the soul of the envious into serpent and so into other creature accord to their quality and disposition successive from one to another of the same kind by consequence believe the immortality of the world so that there be not a silly fly but if they may be credit carry about some soul haply they think of light woman and will not be persuade out of these gross opinion so incorrigible be their sottish error and therefore will not deprive the most offensive creature of their life not snake that will kill they say it be their nature to do harm how that they have reason to shun not liberty to destroy they for their work of charity many rich man build Sarraas or make well or thank near to highway that be much travel where Damascus it be in manner incredible and pass all belief to think how fair the city of Damascus be and how fertile be the soil and therefore allure by the marvelous beauty of the city I remain there the governor of Damascus and of jerusalem the prince of jerusalem a prince a these in the time of harvest and gather of first-fruit he be give whole to prey and rob and with great subtlety deceive the arabian for when they think he to be a mile or two off he be with they sudden betimes in the morning and invade their land carry away their first-fruit wheat and barley even as he find it in the sack and so live continual day and night with such incursion when his mare be weary with continual run he mare rest a while and to refresh they give they camel milk to drink to cool they after their great labour those mare be of such marvelous swiftness that when I present see they they seem rather to fly then to run note also that these arabian ride on the arabian live by robbery horse without saddle and wear none other vesture then only a inward coat or petticoat except some chief man for weapon they use a certain long dart of reed of the length of ten or twelve cubit point with iron after the manner of javelin and fringe with silk when they attempt any incursion they march in such order that they seem to go in troop they be of despicable and little stature and of colour between yellow and black they have the voice of woman and the hair of their head long and black and lay out at large they be of great multitude than a man will believe and be among themselves at continual strife and war they inhabit the mountain and have certain time appoint to robbery for this purpose they observe especial the time when they be of the passage of the pilgrim and other that journey that way to Mecha then like thief they lie in the way and rob they when they make these thievish invasion they bring with they their house bear on camel back wife child family and all the good they have their house some of the arabian dwell in city some in the desert those better civilise and fit for art these which inhabit the desert be call be (...) or Beduois that be the people of the desert exceed in number and wander without house use tent make of Cotton wool or of goat Beduois or beduines activity and camel hair always move and remove as water and pasture move they carry their wife child and utensil on their camel their horse be lean little swift laborious bold and the horseman active beyond belief dart and catch with their hand the same dart in the horse swift race before it come at the ground and avoid a dart throw at they by slighty wind under the horse side or belly also take up weapon lie on the ground while the horse be run and in like swift race hit the small mark with arrow or sling their arm be arrow javelin with iron head sword which they use not to thrust but stroke dagger sling and use the same in adverse fight or in averse flight they lie in wait for caravans pray upon traveller live on rapine and spoil and often make themselves the great Turk receiver and treasurer and raise new impost on all such as they can enforce whether traveller or city obey neither the Ottoman nor any other sovereign but be divide in innumerable family obey the head of their own family or tribe these tribe their tribe or family be distinguish by the name of their first parent as abi-helal abi-risce abizaid and six hundred other all esteem and salute gentle and equal in right their food be brown their food bread new and sour milk cheese goat and camel flesh pulse honey oil and butter Rice be esteem a great delicacy by reason of their tradition that it come of Mahomet sweat for say they when Mahomet compass the throne of God in paradise God turn and look foolish and blasphemous tradition on he which make the modest prophet sweat and wipe it off with his finger six drop fall out of paradise one whereof produce the rose the second rice the other four his four associate they use a certain hodgepodge or frumenty of boil wheat lay after a dry in the sun then beat and boil with fat flesh till the flesh be consume this they call herise and say that Gabriel the angel teach it Mahomet for strengthen his reins whereby one night he fight against forty man and in another have forty time carnal deal with woman these may seem calumny devise by some mahometan adversary if the former author both learned in and zealous of the law of Mohamed have not relate the same in a chapter of the choice of meat Mohamed or Mahomet commend also the eat of gourd and of the affirm that he have see this plant in paradise and measure the quantity of man wit by their eat store hereof when he be once in prison say bensidi Aali the angel Gabriel come down from heaven and carry he into jennet Elenaam or the garden of pleasure where amongst other he see this shrub and he ask why it grow there the angel answer because it have confess the unity of God and that thou be a payment of duty and also we find that they ought to use these use right and custom in manner and form follow it be find that every town of the say land have certain governor some more some less accord to their custom and as the land and the town be in bigness and that the say name Gancares be as much to say as governor ruler or benefactor and it be thus ordain in old time there go four man to make profit of a island and of another unprofitable waste place the which they manure and fortify in such manner and so well that in process of time it come to such increase that it become very populous and these beginner for their good government rule and traffic be call gancare and afterward there come lord and conqueror upon they which do make they for to pay tribute and custom for to let they do not lose their office by that which be speak and at all time that they shall ask or demand the town pay the whole rent or custom it shall be deliver unto they and the say town shall be no more of the farmer have end their time or lease the governor by authority of their office and because they be beginner and also because the say office or charge do come to they by descent they do not lose they to wit the governor every one in the town in person for any error he do commit nor the clerk of common council which also come to he by inheritance or descent and this order be make by the governor themselves only the one and the other shall have for the error and hurt that they do commit the penalty that they do deserve in their good and body notwithstanding such a error they may do that they may die for it or it shall be convenient that they shall not serve in their office and in such case it shall remain to their son or heir and if the case be not great the chief master of the the captain of our city of Goa or to the overseer of our good if the matter be thereunto attain for to provide in it what shall be convenient and right and also the governor of the say town have the say office by inheritance or descent and if they do commit any error they shall be punish as these other and so their office shall remain to their son or to their heir the governor may give such field as within every town be waste or unprofitable to such as shall ask or demand they for to make they profitable in garden or palmtree grove or to other good use with condition that they shall pay a certain rent or custom as shall seem good unto they and this so give shall be for the space of five and twenty year for from that time forward they shall pay accord to the order and custom which be every field or plaine of twelve pace in length which be the space between palmtree and palmtree reckon one hundred palmtree to the field some of they to pay five worth four Barganis every Tanga and after this rate the great or lesser field so give shall pay and the say governor may give the waste field and plain for to be profit in palmtree grove be two penny half penny farthing and a sixteenth part of a penny and garden for less than five and they shall pass their warrant for this accord to their custom notwithstanding they may not exceed above when they shall give field or plain to make rice ground they shall be give in this manner to wit five cubit in length and five in breadth which be the space between one rue and another reckon in this manner one hundred rue to every field and any field or plain which be eleven penc^ farthing english. of they be water with well water they shall give it for four Barganis every year rend and if they be water with run water their rent shall be six Barganis every year and after the say garden be so give unto they by the governor they can be take away from they for they remain to their son grandchild and heir and this be the general custom notwithstanding if any other custom be use beside this in any town or village it shall be fulfil the clerk of the council must be present at all the bargain and agreement which amongst which be a kind and when they make the say assembly which among they be call Gangaria or a assembly of governor if any governor be want of they which be ordain in the say town there can nothing be do except they be all together and if there be any heir of that governor that be want it be sufficient for the say assembly or meeting to be make with he and if other people do not come they shall incur the penalty that among themselves they have ordain if any governor or any other person be willing to sell any land in any of the say town they may not do it without licence of all the governor of the say town and also no person may buy without the say licence and if any person shall make any sale or buy any land without the licence it shall be in itself of no effect and at any time when the governor will it shall be void for the benefit of the duty which they be bind to pay unto we and because they also that do buy may be content and acquaint with the say right and may have their letter with a declaration of these duty which they be to pay when any bill of sale shall be make of any land or inheritance it shall not be sufficient to be sign by the letter but also it must be sign by all the heir and although some of the heir be under age declaration shall be make that some other person that do appertain unto he do sign for he and if any one of the heir remain that have not sign the say sale shall at any time be of no effect take the quantity that it be sell for and if the buyer shall be at any cost or charge upon the say land he shall lose it if any governor shall go or run away because he will not or be not able to pay we the rent that he be bind to pay the other governor of the say town shall meet and call a court about this matter and shall prefix a time wherein he may come and if within the say time he do not come they shall require the heir of the say governor so flee to take the say land and government so as they be bind to pay unto we our right and the debt that he do owe and if he will not accept it it shall remain to the say governor for the obligation that they have to pay the say right or custom and they may give they to who they shall think best pay beside our right all the debt that he do owe. if a governor or any other person shall run away for debt or any other matter no man shall take away his land and his heir shall be demand if they will remain in the say land and be bind to pay his debt and our right and if there be no heir or be any if they will not accept it than the say land shall remain to the say governor for want of a owner and they shall pay for it the right and debt that they do owe unto we and they shall take the overplus of that which be remain and if any thing be want they shall pay that which it amount unto and as touch the movable good they shall remain unto we whensoever the heir shall not accept of the inheritance or land if any person governor or other do chance to die or go out of the country and have no Alfonso mexia don Philip by the grace of God king of Portugal and of the algarue on this side and that side the sea in Africa lord of Guinea and of the conquest navigation and traffic of Aethiopia Persia and India etc. be it know to you that I see how much the good government and preserve of my estate in those part of India do import and justice to be true administer in they to my subject and vassal and desire that in my time it may be do with that integrity liberty and brevity that thereunto belong I think meet to send or provide after I have succeed in the crown of those kingdom person of conscience and learning to the most of the fortress of those part that shall administer it to the which we give power and authority accord to their government or charge and be now inform that in the city of Goa principal and head of the say estate the king my predecessor of glorious memory do ordain there shall be a house of justice or place of hear wherein some officer by they choose as in a supreme tribunal shall determine the as Westminster hall. cause give they for that purpose at sundry time diverse charge the which for the variety of matter ought to be reform and I be willing in duty to continue with the same intent and command to provide in those cause which at this present be most necessary for the good of the say house command for that effect learned man of my counsel and of experience that they shall determine what may be do in that case as well in the order and govern of the say house as in the multiply of the minister belong to it that matter of justice may with more ease and facility be prosecute and have hear their opinion and necessary diligence be use and have give i relation of all thing and account I think good to provide for they in manner and form follow execution shall not be make without give account to the viceroy thereof although he be absent or out of the city the viceroy and judge may in the house of justice supply the defect and annihilate of the act when he shall think that the cause do require it for the perform of justice. and the say judge while they be in the say house execute their office with the viceroy shall be set in plain chair charge for any matter whatsoever criminal or civil except it be by the commandment of the viceroy or the court of relation and because it import much to the keep of good justice and the administration thereof that the say judge have the authority that belong to the charge whereof we have give they commission and because that they be subject to the captain do arise many inconvenience and they be oppress in such manner that they can not perform their duty with that integrity and liberty that belong to the service of God and i and I be willing to provide in this case do think it meet and do command that the say captain may have no jurisdiction nor any superiority over the say judge and that they do not intermeddle with any thing pertain to their office or charge any thing to the contrary notwithstanding and if the say judge do commit any crime or excess so that it seem to the captain that they ought to advertise the viceroy thereof they shall do it by their letter the which the viceroy shall command to be peruse in the court of relation that they may proceed against they accord to justice. and the say judge shall take such fee for their assignment as the justice of the border may take by the authority of their office and accord to my ordinance and when the say judge shall be absent or hinder so that by themselves they can serve they may nominate a person to serve in their place and if he chance to die after he have nominate the person so nominate shall serve until the viceroy do provide another and if he die without nominate any person to serve in his place the factor of the king revenue shall serve the place the which person shall serve the same place all the time that the viceroy do not nominate or provide as it be already declare and the viceroy shall provide a man of learning and quality in who the say charge may well be employ the which person in all thing shall use the order of this decree and it be my will and pleasure that touch the suspicion that shall be lay to the say judge in such case as by reason of their office they may take notice of they shall keep this order follow to wit when any suspicion shall be intend against they by any party of what degree or quality soever he be the judge not yield himself guilty of the suspicion the act thereof shall be commit to the ancient ordinary judge that serve the year before the which judge shall determine of the same accord to justice and the say judge shall proceed always in the cause wherein the say suspicion be lay against he until it be final determine take to himself for a adjunct one of the justice of that present year which do serve in the say fortress or garrison where he be judge not be suspect but if he be he shall take another justice and be both suspect he shall take the ancient alderman and the same be so he shall take the second and if he be suspect he shall take the three to the which no suspicion can be lay and the act that they two shall make it be my will and pleasure that they be in force and power as if the suspicion have not be lay unto the say judge and be judge that he be not suspective he alone shall proceed in the case as he shall have do it if the suspicion have not be intend against he and be judge to be suspective in such a case he shall proceed no further and there shall be a judge set in his place that may take notice of the say case accord to the form of my ordinance and it be also my will and pleasure that when a suspicion be thus lay to the say judge in whatsoever case as well criminal as civil and the party that do lay the say suspicion be not content with his own deposition but be willing to give other proof he shall deposit four cruzado before any hear be give to the proof the which he shall forfeit to the poor
