hundred @. 5 the choice Agiamoglans severe discipline and education in four subordinate school and their after-aduancement it now remain that I say somewhat of those youth which be keep in better fashion in the seraglio for the king and country service bring up in learning in the knowledge of the law and in military exercise that they may be able to perform those thing which belong to the government of the whole empire and albeit for the most part these be Christian captive and renegado yet there be some natural bear Turk amongst they youth of very comely aspect who outside must promise a great deal of goodness bring in by the agha mean who be the great chamberlain with the king consent but this happen but very seldom and that with great difficulty for the ancient institution be that they shall always be of christian renegado of the Turk hardly admit most civil and noble that can be find and when in the war either by sea or land it shall so happen that any youth be take who be of noble parent he be present appoint and mark for the grand signior and be instruct in matter of government be as it be ordain for great employment now noble captive such be of great esteem for the turk themselves affirm that nobleness of birth can but produce the most virtuous and generous spirit especial when they be well nurture and tutor as it be profess in the seraglio where there be great severity use in all the order of discipline the government of they be in the hand of the master who be all for the most part white eunuch which be very rough and cruel in all their action insomuch that their proverb eunuch cruel mortification turkish say that when one come out of that seraglio and have run through all the order of it he be without all question the most mortify and patient man in the world. for the blow which they suffer and the fast which be command they for every small fault be a thing of great admiration nay some of they be so severe handle that although their time of be in the seraglio be almost expire and that they shall in few year come forth to be make great man yet not be able to suffer such cruelty any long they procure to be turn out content themselves with the title and small pay of a Spahee or a rather than be so often punish and make weary of their life the number of these youth be not prefix but there be of they sometime more and sometime less for the king entertain very willing all such as be give he of the aforesaid their number quality if so be that they be young and as I have hear they be common about a hundred the course that be take with they so soon as they come into the seraglio be admirable and nothing resemble the barbarism of turk but beseem subject of singular virtue and discipline for they be exceed well enter and daily teach aswell good fashion and comely discipline in religion and civility behaviour as they be instruct in the rite and ceremony of the mahometan law or in military discipline and for this purpose they have room which the turk call oda but we may more proper in regard of the use they be put unto call they school of which four Oda'h school silence first lesson 2. reverence there be four the one take degree from the other now into the first they all come when they be but childden where the primary precept they learn be silence then their personal positure betoken singular reverence to the king which be that they hold down their head and look downward hold their hand before they join a cross they be see of the king and register in a book by their turkish name and the name of their native country set down with they they receive pension from the grand signior book or check-roll which be ordinary from three to five aspars the copy of the book be send to the great Defterdar that every one of they may in due time have the aforesaid pension send unto they then by a white eunuch who be chief over all the other master and usher they be 3. grammar and religion to write read and speak turkish and arabian prayer set to learn to write and read and to practice the turkish tongue and be teach their prayer with all reverence to the religion in the arabian tongue and in this Oda'h they be both morning and eevening so diligent follow and careful look unto that by report it be a thing of admiration now for the most part they all stay at the least six year in this school and such as be dull and hard of apprehension stay long from this Oda'h they be remove to the second where by more learned tutor then the second shoole former they be teach the persian arabian and tartarian tongue and take great pain in read diverse author that they may be the better able to speak the turkish elegant which 4. rhetoric and language Persian arabian tartartan can be do without some knowledge in those three tongue upon which the turkish chief do depend so that there be find a great difference between their speech and that of the vulgar sort here also they begin to learn to wrestle to shoot in a bow to throw the mace to toss the 5. bodily exercise pike to handle their weapon to run etc. and in these exercise in their several order and several place they spend whole hour be severe punish if they shall in any wise seem to grow negligent they spend other five or six year likewise in this from the which be become man strong and fit for any thing they be remove to the three Odah where forget nothing of three school what they have learn before but rather better themselves they also learn to sit a horse and to be quick and nimble in the war moreover every one of they accord to his inclination 6. horsemanship and activity 7. trade and disposition shall learn a trade necessary for the service of the king person viz. to make up a telbent to shave to pair nail to fold up apparel handsome to keep land-spaniel to keep hawk to be sewer to be quiry of the stable to be targetbearer and to wait at the grand signior table and the like service as it be also use in the court of other king and emperor so that have be in these office four or five year they become man able to teach other and while they be in these three school they be but indifferent apparel have their two vest of cloth some what fine but their linen be such as the other wear and so they must be content to be under the correction of their mast who be so severe that for every fault or for suspicion only of dishonesty cause they to be punish with a hundred punishments blow on the sole of the foot and on the buttock insomuch that they leave they oftentimes for dead neither be they permit while they remain in these three oda to be familiar with any but themselves and that with great modesty too so that it be a matter of great difficulty for any stranger to speak with they or see they which if it be obtain it must be by closeness express leave from the Agha who cause a eunuch to be there present so long as any stranger shall be in the company of any of the say youth nay when they have occasion to go to the or the like necessary business they be very narrow look unto by the eunuch to keep they by all mean from any filthy action and if they shall be find guilty or accuse of any fault they be most severe punish for it and in their bedchamber which bedchamber be long room and hold about forty or fifty in each of they for they sleep near one another upon the sofa there be every night lamp light and eunuch lie by they to keep they in awe and from lewd and wanton behaviour some of they also do learn mechanic art as sew in leather which be in great esteem sew in leather etc. amongst the turk to mend gun to make bow and arrow and quiver and the like from which trade they often have both their surname and their reputation too for they be exceed belove who be diligent and fly idleness and the eunuch make great trial of their constancy in religion search as far as in they lie their heart to see how they stand affect to turkism for the time grow near trial of religion four school wherein they be to pass to the four Odah which be the chief and last and from which they be call to business of great import they will not then have they at all remember that they be former christian or to have any desire imaginable to turn to their first belief lest they shall by some stratagem and politic carriage prove disaduantageous to the turkish empire so then all possible proof and trial be make and they find to be most strong persuade in themselves of the truth of that religion they then be prefer to the four Odah where they be once more register for all they which be of the three Odah be not translate to the four at one and the same time but only such as have go through all the degree in the three former and be become fit for service and there be a account keep apart of they which come into this four Odah for they be immediate ordain for the grand signior own service and have their pay increase some more and some less unto eight asper preferman (...) and their habit change from cloth to silk and cloth of gold of great price but continue still with their head and beard shave only they suffer some lock to grow on each side from their temple which hang down below their ear for a sign that they be they which be near to the preferment of come into the king chamber they must be very clean and neat in their apparel before they come about the grand signior person many of they accompany he ever when he go abroad upon pleasure and neatness they may free converse with all the great man of the seraglio and with the pasha also and be often present with great gift by man of great quality to keep in their favour hope that they may become man of great command and be able to stand they in stead upon diverse occasion now out of these young man after they have finish the appoint term of year and have be well instruct in all thing as aforesaid the grand signior choose his agha which be his gentleman and serve he only who name and place be as follow all which be of the elder sort of they and be always in his majesty presence hold down their head for they may not be so bold as to look he in the face and stand with their hand across before they in token of the great humility and reverence that may be gesture imagine neither be they permit to speak at all to the grand signior nor in his presence to one another but if the king shall command or call for any thing they be wonderful speedy and ready to obey these all do execute their office distinct as aforesaid and attend in place wait appoint for they that they may be the better able to perform their service and the more ready to obey at every beck and at the hour of dinner and supper they wait in the room take the meat from the hand of the vnder-sewer at the door and so his majesty table be make minister in the charge assign unto they they also accept of the service of other which come in by gift which likewise redound to the benefit and advantage of the great one now they which succeed in preferment those that be go out of the seraglio upon the order in succession aforesaid employment be as the custom command such as be next in year unto they and of the long stand neither can this course be alter unless by some sinister accident or evil behaviour they fail thereof so that it be always know amongst themselves who be next capable of public employment nay the business be so orderly carry and their course so regular that even they of the three Odah do know what their future fortune will be if they live to enjoy they and indeed all of they live in hope and desire that the grand signior will often be please to send they abroad that they may the soon be out of their hard service in the seraglio and enter into the state of ample government they be most common of five and thirty or forty year of age before they be send abroad and because they come out of the seraglio with their beard shave they be fain to stay within door for some few day to let they grow that they may be fit to come amongst other great man with which stay at home they be very well content for that in that time they receive the present which be send they from all the sultanaes of vest shirt linen-breeches present from great person while they stay and hand-kerchief of all sort rich wrought and of great worth and from the pasha and other great man horse carpet vest slave and other thing fit for the erect of a house and family the which present be make the great and rich by so much the more as the party to who they be give be know to be favour and belove of the king. now so soon as their beard be grow they go abroad and begin their visit first to the chief and then in order to the other great one till they have be with they come abroad and visit Capee Agha all and last of all offer their service to the Capee Agha in all humble manner acknowledge that all their best fortune and honour have be confer upon they by his mean and promise for ever all dutiful respect unto he for the same but this compliment with the Capee Agha be perform without that gate on the king side which be keep by the eunuch for they may not come no more within that gate unless they be call for by the king for to treat of thing belong to their employment before their departure they all strive to gain the love of the Capee Agha that he may be a protector and patron unto they to possess the grand signior with a good opinion of they in their absence he be the chief in the seraglio and always near to the king. @. 7 of inferior person as buffoon mute musician of white eunuch and of the grand spoon well relish he neither use knife nor fork but only a wooden spoon of which there be two lay before he the one serve he to eat his pottage and the other to sup up certain delicate syrup withal delicate dress that as I say before he need no knife but pull the flesh from the bone very easy with his finger he use no salt at his table neither have he any but immediate fall aboard the flesh and dish for his highness table be all of gold and so likewise be their cover they be in the custody of the Keelergee who attend at the kitchen and so be all the yellow purcelaine dish and cover of gold. yellow purcelaine for Ramazan or Lent dish which be very costly and scarce to be have for money in which the king eat in the Ramazan time which be their lent and last a whole moon and the month itself be so call in which time they never eat in the day but only in the night not make any difference in meat except swine flesh and thing strangle of which they be forbid by their law to eat at any time the king seldom eat fish unless it be when he be abroad at some garden house by the seaside with his woman the meat which remain of that which be at the grand signior table be immediate remainder under ground in house make of purpose for that use they do not ordinary use comfit nor cheese for the turk do hardly know how to make they especial cheese which although they do make of it it never prove good so comfit and cheese not use that the Sultanas and all great personage eat none but parmezan of which the Bailo of Venice do always furnish they and that very plentiful for they love it well and eat hearty of it when they go abroad upon pleasure or a hunt for the provision of the say seraglio all thing be prepare in great abundance and every particular provision be assign to particular person to take care therefore so that there be never any want of thing necessary order the first and best sort of bread which indeed be very white and savoury be for the king the bread of consume so much corn for beside the servant as aforesaid all the Sultanas and great personage with diverse other have their daily allowance of bread from the keeler that be the pantry or from his highness bakehouse pantry allowance every sultana twenty loaf every bashaw ten to the mufti eight and so to diverse other a several proportion even to one loaf a man all which be by the commandment and discretion of the chief the several allowance be set down in the chief butler book or else in he who be the overseer of the bake-house every loaf be as big as three penny loaf of we here in London but very light and spongy and easy of digestion the rice and lentils and all other sort of pulse of which there be a great quantity spend be Rice lentils pulse from Alexandria spice and sweet meat expense of sugar bring yearly from Alexandria in the galeon which make two voyages and bring out of Egypt not only the say pulse but also all sort of spice and sugar and a great quantity of preserve and pickle meat which the turk much delight in and as for sugar there be spend a unspeakable deal in make of sherbet and tart which not only the seraglio use but be also ordinary present from one bashaw to another and from one friend to another insomuch that it be a thing to be admire to see so great a quantity so sudden consume true it be that there be but little spice spend in the seraglio nor indeed any great store among little spice the turk pepper only except for inasmuch as wine be not a ordinary drink amongst they they therefore avoid such thing as provoke a desire thereunto howsoever in the storehouse of the port there be provision of all sort of spice and drug for whatsoever occasion shall happen that may require the use of they there likewise come from Egypt great store of date prune and other dry plum of egyptian first-fruit diverse sort which the cook use in their dress of meat aswell for roast as boil and indeed they make delicate dish of they the honey of that which be present to the king as that which come for particular man account yet that which be use in the king kitchen come from Candie and be far better and pure than the other the oil of which be spend in the king kitchen be bring from Candie it of Candie be sweet clear and in every respect better than that of the Morea the butter of which there be also spend a very great quantity in that it be use almost in all butter from Bogdania etc. their meat especial in Pillawe come out of the black sea from Bogdania and from Caffa be put into great oxe-hides and buffalo-hides and so lay up in magazine for the yearly provision of the king court but common they have so much that they sell part of it into the city as they do likewise the oil honey etc. which be beggleek that be for the grand signior account when they have more of they then they think they shall spend and make a no fresh butter little milk eat great benefit of it the turk know not what belong to fresh butter there be little or none at all make about Constantinople neither do they eat much milk except it be make sour which they call Yoghurd for that it be so turn sour it do quench the thirst and of that both they and the christian do eat a great quantity they eat also some store of Kaymack that be clout or cloded cream but that be only for the better sort for it be a meat of too high a price for the vulgar now as for flesh every year in the autumn winter draw nigh the bashaw cause the provision of flesh kow beef provision of Basturma to be make for the king kitchen and they make it of cow great with calf for then say they the flesh be most tender and savoury they use it in the same manner as christian use swine flesh for they make pudding and sauceage of it and the rest they boil and dress after other fashion this sort of dry flesh after that it be sufficient dry with hang a month or better in dry and hang a room and little or no salt use about it will last the whole year and eat very savourly and it be in such use amongst the turk that there be scarce a house of any fashion or account but do yearly make provision of it and it be hold a very thrifty and spare course but they do not all make their Basturma of cow great with calf for there be some which love the other better which be make of ox and bullock and they can buy it far cheap the bashaw have the oversight of that which be prepare for the king kitchen and there be ordinary spend four hundred cow for the say provision of Basturma the other flesh which be daily spend in the kitchen of the seraglio as I be tell by one of the aschee be as follow sheep 200. lamb or kid when they be in season 100 calf 10. goose 50. hen 200. chicken 100 pigeon 200. there be but very little store of fish spend in the seraglio yet sometime the aghae for dainty will eat some the sea thereabouts fish. do exceed abound with diverse kind and they may easy take as many as they please but the christian be well serve with fish in the market and at reasonable price and the common sort of turk do bear they company the grand signior nor any of the seraglio can want for fruit there be in time of year so many present thereof bring thither continual beside what come from the king fruit own garden which be many and near the city every morning in great abundance and excellent good the gardener sell the remainder at a place in Constantinople where only the king fruit be sell and bring the money weekly to the bustangee Bashee who afterward give it to his majesty and it be call the king pocket-money for he give it away by handful as he see occasion to his mute and buffoon the furniture of the kitchen in the seraglio as ketle cauldron and skillet etc. be almost all of brass and they be so neat keep and of such a largeness that there can be a scullery brave sight of that nature and as for the dish they be of copper tin over but so often new furbish and trim that they be daily use it be wonderful to behold their continual brightness and of these they have a great number but the king sustain great loss by they for there be such a company of people serve daily from the kitchen with meat loss by pilfer both within and without especial upon the four Divan day there be so many of they steal that the defterdar weigh the loss and charge of those dish have often be almost resolve to make they all of silver and so to consign they to the custody of the sewer and butler who shall from time to time give account of they and look the better to they but find it a thing so costly not any Defterdar as yet have perform it nor adventure to begin the wood which be spend in the aforesaid kitchen and in all the seraglio be almost a infinite wood and fewell number of weight for at Constantinople the wood be all buy and sell by weight there be for the account of the seraglio which they call begleek above thirty great caramusal which do nothing else at one time of the year but sail into the black sea there to lade at the king wood it be a business which cost but little in respect of the worth of it for they have it for the cut down and the bring and unlade of it require little or no charge at all for they be to make so many return for the king but receive no freight and the master be to see it unlade at their own cost and charge receive only a discharge but no recompense at all @. x. apparel bedding sickness hospital inheritance king expense recreation receive petition stable Ramazan solemnity the grand signior apparel be nothing different in fashion from other man save in fashion of king apparel the length of his vest and the richness thereof nor be his shoe shod with iron at the heel as other turk wear they but be raze and paint like child shoe with knot and flower and as for his lodging he sleep upon matteress of velvet and cloth of gold in the summer in sheet of Shash embroider with silk sow to the quilt and in the winter his bedding betwixt coverlet of lucerne or of sable wear all night a little on his head and when he lie alone in his own lodging he be always watch by his page of his chamber page watch by two and two at a time change every three hour one of they stand at the chamber door and the other by the bed side to cover he in case the clothes shall slide off and to be near hand if his majesty shall want any thing and in the same chamber where he lie there be always two woman that attend with burn torch in their hand nor two Torchwomen may they put they out till such time as the king be rise out of his bed. the habit of the woman be much like to that of the man for they wear chacksir and buskin and have their shoe shod with iron at the heel they sleep as the man do in linen woman habit breeches and in quilt waistcoat have thin and light one for the summer and more thick and warm one for the winter the turk never have any closestool or such like inplement in their chamber but have a will to that business they rise and go to their privy make in place apart where there no closestool do always stand water-pot ready that they may wash when they have do nor may they use paper in that service as we do the several stipend which the grand signior allow to those of the seraglio of what no paper etc. stipend degree or condition soever they be be pay out of the outmost Hazineh and the chief Defterdar who have a book as well of the name of the stipendary as of their stipend be bind to send once every three month to all the odahs in several bag so much money as their pay import and there they share it amongst they the like he do also by the woman and the agiamoglan pay they in good money and against the Biram which be their Carneval he send they their vest their linen and such like necessary of which he never fail they for they want they if he shall disappoint they they will so complain against the say Defterdar that it will be his utter overthrow for he shall be sure at the least to lose his place when any one die in the seraglio his chamber-fellow be make his heir and that seraglio heir which he leave be divide amongst they and if any great eunuch die all come to the king for they be always very rich by reason of the manifold gift which come to their hand but if any eunuch of the serraglio abroad or in place of other government shall die than two three of his estate fall to the king by canon the other three part be to be dispose of accord to the testator will and that be only when the king give way unto it and will not testament out of his supreme authority take all to himself as he use to do by all great rich one the king person be hold the principal and most lawful heir of all they be account as slave which have receive their livelihood good estate and all that they have enjoy mere from his greatness and bounty and to this end there be a officer call the Beytilmawlgee Beytilmawlgee who so soon as any one die make inquisition for their estate and so certify the Defterdar thereof leave the execution to he if it be in matter of import but the Beytilmalgee for his own private gain do oftentimes conceal a great part of the estate of the decease part the same betwixt the kindred and himself when any ordinary person fall sick in the seraglio he be carry from his chamber in a cart which be cover and draw with hand and be put into the aforesaid hospital or Lazaretta hospital where he be look unto after the turkish fashion and keep so close that none may come to the speech of he but with great difficulty and grow well again he be carry back in the same manner to his own chamber where he be at the first shout and prayer of gratulation and gratification prosperity and happiness and for recompense he oftentimes put his hand into his pocket and throw whole handful of money amongst they now they of the seraglio which go by his stirrup have charge to receive such petition petition as be prefer to his majesty as he ride along and many poor folk who dare not to approach nigh he stand a far off with fire upon their head hold up their petition in their hand the which the king see send immediate to take the say petition and be return home into his seraglio read they all and then give order for redress as he think fit by reason of which complaint the king oftentimes take occasion to execute justice even against the most eminent in place before they be aware without take any course in law against they but cause a sudden execution of what punishment he please upon they which make the pasha that they care not how seldom the grand signior stir abroad in public for fear least in that manner their unjust proceed and bad justice shall come to his ear and indeed they always live in great fear through the multiplicity of business that pass through their hand and in danger of lose their life at a short warning which make they use the proverb that he that be great in office be but a statue of glass the grand signior for the use of his household have in Constantinople near unto the seraglio his great stable a exceed large stable of a thousand horse and upward and the Imrohor Bashee which be master of the horse have the charge of they together with a under Imrohor for his assistant beside many ordinary groom which be to look to they and see that they be keep in good case now the say Imrohor Bashee and his deputy be to see the king servant provide of horse at such time as they accompany his majesty abroad either a hunt or for other sport beside this stable he have diverse other in other place for his own service and for the other stable use of his gentleman at such piece in they for to those house he carry but few follower with he he have also stable for his stallion for race in Bursia and in diverse other place from which be bring very stately horse beside such little byram month after the other @. 11 the old seraglio and woman life therein of their marriage and child slave-selling witness have oftentimes mention the old seraglio which be as it be a dependent of the the old seraglio king seraglio it will not be amiss brief to make some kind of relation of it this be a very large seraglio immure with a very high wall the building be fair it have many inhabitant and be about a italian mile in compass be seat in the noble part of the city it be the first seraglio which Mahomet the second build for to dwell in with all his court when he take own to help sometime they will pass but coarse so that they be fain to betake themselves to their needle by which they reap a reasonable benefit and have diverse ha^d state Jew woman who frequent their company and sell their labour for they a Turk if he please may take seven wife at Kebin beside he may have as many slave seven wife slave unlimited as he will and the child of the slave be hold as true beget and legitimate as those of the wife and have as much right to the inheritance of what the father leave behind he nay a bashaw have marry a sister or a daughter to the king and have son by they pasha son keep under if of royal blood those son may not rise above the degree of a saniack Begh or a Capoogee Bashee to the end they may be keep under be ally to the crown that so be but in mean place they may not be apt for revolution but their brother which their father beget of slave may come to be pasha for they be free from suspicion in regard they be not of the blood royal and hence it be that those child which have a sultana to their mother be so often see to be in low degree than the other for he which be bear of the slave be above he which be bear of the sultana yet with the child of the other subject it be otherwise for they be equal the party marry may upon diverse occasion specify in their law leave one another especial divorce when they can agree together and if the man put away the woman he be bind to allow she the jointure or dowry which he promise she when they be contract but if the woman forsake the man she can recover nothing but depart only with a small portion such as she bring with she into her husband house now in case a Turk take slave for his use he may not sell they again but they become member of the family in which they be to remain till they die but if they prove barren slave sell if barren they may be sell from hand to hand as often as their fortune so betide they the turk may buy of all sort of slave of every religion and use they as they please kill only except which the christian and jew there may not do for they have liberty only to buy christian and jew there be for this purpose in Constantinople a bezisten that be a common public market where every Wednesday there be buy and sell slave of all sort and every one come free to bezisten buy for their several use some for nurse some for servant and some for their lustful appetite for they which make use of slave for their sensuality can be punish by the justice as they shall be if they be take with free woman and with turkish woman especial these slave be buy and sell as beast and cattle be they be view and review and feel all about their limb and body as if they be so many horse than they be examine manner of sell slave of what country they be and what they be good for either for sew spin weave and the like buy sometime the mother with the child and sometime the child without the mother sometime two or three brother together and again sometime take the one and leave the rest use no term of love regard or honesty but even as the buyer or the seller shall think will best turn they to profit now when there be a virgin that be beautiful and fair she be hold at a high rate and be sell for far more than any other and for security of her virginity the seller be not only bind to the restitution of the money if she prove otherwise to he that buy she but be for his fraud fine at a sum of money in the restitution if not a virgin. bezisten there sit a Emeen that be a customer who receive custom of the buyer and seller which amount to a reasonable no benefit by affinity to the king. or freedom with his majesty then if there be no such matter of kindred betwixt they but only what may well befit their office and dignity they remain still slave as the other do nay their servitude be thereby increase and they loose a great part of their former liberty for they must be very obsequious to the sultanaes who they have marry and turn loss by it away the great part of their other woman and slave if they have any and must with patience support all their imperfection so that for this reason few pasha of worth and judgement seek after such marriage for they be both chargeable and bring discontent but when the king command they as his slave must submit and obey though their vexation and charge increase never so much thereby the ceremony of turkish marry be nothing else but in the presence of the Cadee who be the justice to make Hoget that be a write express the vow and good like of the party rite of marriage to be marry with a specification of the dowry which the husband be to make to the wife all which be do in presence also of witness which be true and honest and not to be deny for in Turkey it be not permit that every one that will shall bear witness but who may be witness only such man as be free of a good age that can say the namaz and have some knowledge in the law know to be man of civil life and which drink no wine for the witness of a Turk which drink wine be nothing worth and thus their law command but for all this corruption be so creep in amongst they that now in Turkey especial in Constantinople there be to the outward appearance grave and honest man more false witness then in any other emir false witness part of the world beside and who be they at least the chief of they but a certain sort of emeers that be such as pretend to come of the race and stock of Mahomet which wear green telbent and certain poor cadee out of office and these be they which for money do use that detestable trade which our knight of the post do practice here with we and hence it be that Auanias be so common frame for they can stout and that with ease outface the poor christian and jew nay for a bribe they will not spare their own generation in bear false witness or raise calumny against they for the turk be natural give Turk covetous and dangerous to covetousness not fear God but altogether incline to rapine although without question there be many very honest man amongst they when they meet with a fit opportunity they will play the rogue with any man be he of what condition soever wherefore it prove dangerous to have any deal with they for that they with that trick will easy free themselves from any obligation or agreement before make for judgement there consist force of evidence only of the force of proof by witness so that a man have need to be wondrous circumspect in his proceed with Turk especial in matter of covenant @. 12 of their religion opinion person time place and rite sacred the turk believe in almighty God that he be the creator of the whole universe and the gracious redeemer of all good man in the day of judgement that he be in the high heaven serve with especial angel have from the beginning cast out the disobedient one for who as also for wicked man he make hell. and as they affirm everlasting life to be in these two place viz. heaven and hell so they confess and wait for the resurrection of the body to be reunite with the soul at such time as the resurrection fearful trumpet shall be found by Mahomet at the commandment of the great GOD of the judgement they believe also that life everlasting in paradise be such a happiness that it consist only in the delight and please of the sense and that they shall have there the use of natural sensual paradise thing in all perfection without make any difference enjoy perfect health and free from all manner of trouble and on the contrary that in hell the use of the aforesaid thing shall be in unquenchable fire and shall have a most bitter and loathsome taste and this be all that they attribute unto they either for the reward of the bless or the punishment of the reprobate they say moreover that the power of God be such that have at man creation prefix and appoint a set time for his end it be impossible that the wit or device of mortal man shall fate be able to divert or prevent it wherefore in the war or in other occasion they be so much the more bold resolute and courageous say that their end be write in their forehead and it be not for they to go about to avoid it so that if they die they die they also affirm God power to be such that after man body be rise again he will give they such a agility that they shall be able in a moment to pass from one heaven to another agility in the next life transparent heaven even to the far part of they to visit and embrace their wife mother brother and other of their kindred the heaven be all transparent be of diamond ruby turkess and crystal as concern God throne or seat of majesty they affirm that every one can behold God throne it by reason of the brightness of the beam which come from his eye and by reason of the unspeakable splendour proceed from his glorious face and that the angel and prophet only have the grace to enjoy that sight these be the principal foundation of their religion upon which they build the course of this their present temporal life and by which they hope to obtain a life everlasting and happy affirm by their prophet to be full of the delight and pleasure of this world but enjoy in all perfection and excellency in a supernatural and incorruptible manner they say that almighty God send four prophet into the world to instruct govern and four prophet and book save mankind each of they be holy pure and undefiled to wit Moses David Christ and Mahomet and that God send to every one of they by his angel Gabriel a book that they themselves be first perfect may the better know how to instruct the people to Moses he send the teurat that be the old law to David the Zebur that be the psalm to Christ the Ingil that be the gospel and to Mahomet the kurawn that be the Alcoran as we call it and that the three first prophet with their people do fail somewhat in the law give they by God but Mahomet come last bring a law more true plain clear and sincere in which all such as believe shall obtain the love of God but they say that other nation continue still in their error and have suck of their mother milk do not embrace the truth for which fault be by right deprive of heaven they have no other mean to recover and to come thither at the day of judgement but by Mahomet protection who be the only intercessor and mediator unto the almighty God and stand in the dreadful day of judgement at the gate of paradise he shall be seek unto and entreat by the other prophet to save their people also and his clemency shall be such as to make intercession for they so that the good christian and the good jew shall by his mean obtain everlasting life with perpetuity of sensual delight as aforesaid but in a place apart and inferior to the turk they be belove of God and more dear unto he than other the woman also shall come into heaven but shall be in a place far inferior to man and be less glorify woman heaven all the prophet be hold in great honour amongst they they call Moses Musahib Alloh that be a talker with God and Christ Meseeh rooh-^lloh and Hazrettee isaw that be Messiah the spirit of God and venerable jesus and Mahomet resul Alloh that be the messenger of god. when they talk of Christ jesus they speak very reverent of he and confess that the jew through envy apprehend he and malicious condemn he and lead he along to put he to death but the angel be send from God take he away from they in a cloud and carry he into heaven at which the jew be astonish and vex take one that be there present and c^^cified he in his stead not be willing to have it know that jesus be the Messiah he be in heaven in company of his brethren the prophet belove of God and ser^ing he as the other prophet do the ministry of their religion or rather their confuse sect be as follow they have first a mufti that be to say a expounder or of case in law who amongst they be the mufti as a archbishop be with we for he be also the primate over the church and must be a man very expert in the law and one accustom to justice choose by the grand signior himself the which muftee charge be to oversee and hear such thing as be belong to the law or to the church and although he have not a absolute command over the muftee of the other province yet with his subtlety he prevail with the king and effect what he listen especial when he have the chief to friend who in degree dignity and authority be his superior under the say mufti there be two cadeelesher that be to say judge of the army one of Grecia cadeelescher cadee and their order and the other of Anatolia who also be man of the law and they which always succeed the mufti have the oversight of all the other cadee who be justice of which there be one in every city and town to do justice and end controversy betwixt man and man and to punish offender but they be change every three year and other put into their place by the cadilescher with order from the grand signior among the say cadee they have also their order those of the first rank and they be call meulaw which signify lord and they be employ in the principal city the other be but cadee and they get employment as they can by their virtue and good carriage in former place now the cadeelescher have book lie by they wherein be exact set book down the revenue of every Cadeelick so that by that mean they know the better how to furnish they none of they surmount above five hundred asper this order of turk amongst the rest have only this privilege which be that they can be put to death so that if any of they by commit some notorious crime against the law privilege shall deserve death it must be do by absolute command from the grand signior and that very wary and secret but this happen very seldom or never the mufti and cadeelescher be change at the king pleasure for there be no office in Turkey during life howbeit their ordinary residence be three year their chief fortune depend their continuance whole in their continuance in the grace and favour of the chief all the aforesaid man of the law that be the mufti the cadeelescher mulaes and cadee turban wear their turban far big than any other turk and make up after another fashion in token that they ought to be reverence above other and although their habit be in fashion like other man yet in this there be a difference for they wear much white chamblet and the fine cloth but no silk at all the principal charge of the mufti be to answer to all such proposition as be make unto he of matter in general upon case concern conscience and the rite of turkish justice Muftees office and law the which answer be of few word very brief and they be call fetfa that be declaration or judgement of the mufti with which he may compel not only the cadee and pasha to the performance of the content thereof but the king own person be also bind to see they execute for in conclusion they seek altogether to amplify their sect in honour of their prophet the Muftees Fetfa be in high estimation in asmuch as it be uphold very stout by the whole order of the cadee then next they have a governor of the Moscheas call the Mootevelee and eemawm priest and clerk which be parish priest and next to they Muyezins which be as our church clerk all which be employ in the service of the Moscheas call the people to prayer bury the dead read upon the grave of the dead and to conclude perform all such office as be any way belong to the church for the good of the people they pray five time a day aswell in the Moscheas as in their house or wheresoever they prayer five time a day be that be at four of the clock in the morning at noon between three and four in the afternoon between seven and eight at night and at midnight and upon the Friday which be their sabbath at nine of the clock in the forenoon also which make six time and upon that day there be more muyezin which cry in the steeple then upon other day for at all those hour in stead of bell the people be call to prayer by the voice of one or two man in the steeple or turret adjoin to the Moscheas of a reasonable height by which voice they be stir up to the praise of God and Mahomet and may prepare themselves for their prayer and because the muyezin which cry can hear no clock for they have none in their church hour glass they use hourglass by which they be direct aswell in this service as in other ordinary matter in every great Moschea there be mudereese which be reader that teach diverse scholar the common prayer and instruct they in the service belong to the Moscheas be pay for reader their pain out of the revenue of the say church the condition of they which be to pray be only to be corporal clean it be unlawful cleanness and purifying for any one to enter into the Moscheas or to pray if he find that he have any natural pollution or carnal uncleanness about he be it of what condition soever or of never so small moment wherefore for their cleanse every one be bind either to wash himself in the if it be for carnal commerce or else for other sort of uncleanness with cold water every city and place abound with bagnoe both public and private and every churchyard with very fair fountain for the use of the common sort now immediate after every one be cleanse and come into the Moschea the eemawm which be the parish priest begin to pray and all manner of their prayer their gesture they which be present imitate he in gesture for of themselves a great part of they will not else know how to perform that business for their prayer consist chief in rise up fall down kiss the ground and sometime sit still one while touch their eye sometime their face than their beard than their head say some few word in the praise of God and Mahomet the church be all mat underfoot and in some place there be woollen carpet spread for the better sort of people the say prayer accord to the hour be diverse some long and some short none of their length they be above a hour long only that prayer of the evening in the time of the Ramazan which be their lent which be long than the other prayer they pray after their eemawm for he be their guide and esteem of if he have a good voice as we esteem of our sing man they also use preach upon every Friday in the Ramazan and when they will pray for any preach good success in the war or curse any rebel they have a custom then to go a procession along the street by two and two but without any light or any such thing in their hand and procession and curse as they go along they praise the name of God and read very long prayer which they have for those purpose the people still cry amen make one whole day work of it and then they hold that rebel or enemy whosoever he be to be without all doubt accurse in the time of trouble or affliction they publish in the most eminent place a convocation other convocation and prayer of all the chief man in the city and of the common people also such as will come may to pray in the field which be for that use therein imitate the jew and be all come together diverse of their santons of esteem for their holiness make sermon of exhortation to fortitude patience and to the love and fear of God but if those trouble continue espy a Turk that be drink with wine so forthwith example of severity he cause he to be bring unto he and without give he any respite to recover his wit cause a ladle full of boil lead to be pour down they think to appease God wrath and regain his love and favour those turk which be professor of humility and devotion have their bead long than other man and carry they in their hand into the Moscheas God be great they go also many of they to Meccha on pilgrimage and to Jerusalem also which pilgrimage Mecca temple they call gudd ill shereef to Meccha to visit the temple which they say be build by Abraham in the which temple Mahomet in the time of idolatry do hide himself and they affirm that when he be almost forty year of age he receive the Alcoran from God and that from that time the Mussulmanlick begin that be the true belief and short after he die and his sepulchre be visit by all such as go the say pilgrimage and when they go to jerusalem they go not to visit Christ sepulchre for they say he do not die but they go only to see the place which he most frequent as be a miraculous prophet who raise the dead to life heal the sick and wrought such like wonder they go likewise to the valley of jehoshaphat for they say that in that place shall be the resurrection at the day of judgement now such as have go the say pilgrimage and return home again to their house be ever after call hagee that be pilgrim and be much reverence and esteem of there be also diverse turk who forsake the world leave all that they have and go to live near to the aforesaid valley for devotion and for that they will be the near to the place of resurrection suppose thereby to get a great advantage to themselves above the rest at that day the great ceremony for pomp and solemnity which be use amongst the turk be circumcision that o^ the circumcise their child wherein they differ from the jew in this one particular for the turk never circumcise they till they be pass ten year of age follow the example of Ishmael who they imitate allege that Abraham love and esteem he and not Isaac and will have sacrifice he this circumcision be do without the church because of the shed of blood all the kindred and friend be invite unto it in token of joy and gladness they use the like to those which turn from any other religion and become turk who in token that they embrace the religion of Mahomet hold up their forefinger say these word Alloh Muhamet resull Alloh that be there be but only one God and Mahomet be his messenger there be in the city and by the highway also in most place of the of their servant to keep when any one be extreme sick and as they think past hope of recovery then the imawm sickness fatal and death come to use comfortable word unto he and pray by he and be dead discover I have hereunto add a letter send by sultan Osman the late murder emperor to his majesty by Husein Chiaus and translate into english by master Robert withers although in this transitory world the king or the beggar shall enjoy the long term of life that may be and obtain all that his heart can wish yet it be most certain that in the end he must depart and be transport to the world eternal and it be well know unto the wise that it be unpossible for man to abide for ever in this world. the occasion of this prologue be that the immortal omnipotent and only God have through his divine will and pleasure call unto himself our glorious father of bless memory sultan achmet can who in life be happy and in death laudable and depart out of this momentany world to be near the merciful creator be change into perfect glory and eternal bliss have his habitation on high and his rest in paradise this paternal empire and monarchical kingdom have almost until this present bless time be always hereditary from grandfather to father from father to son and so cursive in that manner but have regard unto the age and year of our great and noble uncle sultan Mustafa he be prefer and honour to sit on the ottoman throne and be settle for some time take care for the affair of the empire and for all that may concern the people both in general and particular but he have be many year retire in solitariness and give to devotion and divine obedience be also as it be weary with the care of the empire of his own accord withdraw himself from the government for that the diadem and sceptre of the empire of the seven climate be the true right and inheritance of our most excellent majesty of the which with the meeting and consent of all the vizier and other deputy of state of the primate of the Mussulman law and of the other honourable doctor of the soldier and of all subject both public and private the almighty God have make a high present and worthy gift unto we and in the happy day in the begin of the moon Rebea (...) levelly of this present year 1027. in a expect time and in a acceptable hour be our bless and happy sit establish upon the most fortunate ottoman throne the seat and wisdom of Solomon in the pulpit of all the mosque the congregation of the faithful and devotion of the mussulman throughout all our dominion be read to our imperial name the Hutbeh and in the mint where innumerable sum of money be coin as well upon the silver as the gold our happy name and mark be stamp and our most powerful commandment be obey in all the part and dominion of the world and the brightness of the light of the sun of our justice and equity have cause the darkness of injury and molestation to vanish away now see it have be a ancient custom of our most famous predecessor to give notice of the same to such prince as be in sincere friendship and that do continue it with the house of great majesty and our imperial court we also have write these our princely letter and appoint for their bearer the choice amongst his equal Husein Chiaus who power be great one of the honour and respect servant of our magnificent port the refuge of the world to the end that such news may cause great joy of our most honourable assumption and we do hope that when they shall come to your hand in conformity of the well ground friendship upon the sure league article and write which have be establish of old with our most royal race and permanent empire you will manifest infinite joy and gladness and certify as much to the ruler and governor of the dominion and country under you that they may know that the article of peace and league and the point of the oath which be firm and to be desire on both part from the time of our grandfather and predecessor of royal stock now in paradise who soul God enlighten undoubted during the time of our reign shall be observe with all respect and let there not be the least imagination of any want of due observance of the sign of friendship on our part or by any manner of mean on your part for the violate the foundation of the peace and league the ensue letter be write by Halil bashaw chief and general in the persian expedition at his return in April 1618. to sir Paul Pinder ambassador for his majesty english by master Robert withers to the courteous lord of the nation of the Messiah both great and honourable among the people of JESUS and the true determiner of christian affair our good friend the english ambassador who latter day be with all felicity to who noble presence after our many kind salutation tend to all good affection and manifestation of joy worthy and be seem our friendship our love advice be this that if you desire to hear of our state and be you shall understand that after we depart from the happy port with the army for the war of Asia we arrive and winter in Mesopotamia and remove then^e in the spring with all the Mussulman host always victorious we go to van from which place until we come to Tauris the Mussulman army go on always sack and destroy all those place and town of the Persian which we meet withal by the way in those part where be burn pillage and ruin some thousand of village and torment all those people that come to hand and when we be come near to Tauris the general of the persian force of perverse religion call Carcighai Han the accurse retire himself into the say Tauris where beat up his drum in every quarter make a show that he have a will to fight so we send a little before we some tartar and other of our army to hearken out and take notice of the enemy who meet with seven or eight hundred Persian of note put they to the sword very few escape and that with great difficulty and hazard by which the say general find himself unable to resist the power and fury of the Muslulman host or to stay any long in the say place the very same day that we arrive there the say general have spoil all the city flee away so we take the place ransack it and burn all the building tower garden and whatsoever else we find within it and thus the great city Tauris by divine favour and grace become we then forthwith we send after the enemy the bohemian-tartar with some beglerbegh who overtake they give they battle and albeit some of we do fall yet they which fall of the enemy side be innumerable and so go forward towards erdevil their obscure residence about ten day journey of country we go burn and spoil it and kill all the Persian that we meet that indeed there be so much honour and glory win as that all the ancient man of the country do affirm there never be see the like insomuch that from the confine unto Erdevile twenty day journey of country be on that manner by we destroy thus afterward the king cause to empty the say place of Erdevile of these ware see before in sir Thomas r^e and flee into a place call hulchal and cause his army to go to the top of a high mountain from whence have send three or four time man of quality unto we seek and entreat for peace with promise to give yearly to our emperor a hundred sum of silk and all such place as be upon the confine make in the time of sultan Solyman except and der think and we be content with the peace and his ambassador be upon the way come towards we and so we return the same way again always spoil we come to and this our present letter be write unto you for the respect and preservation of our friendship and even as our amity have ever be hitherto sincere and firm so likewise by the grace of God at our arrival in the happy port it shall be in like manner maintain and continue that more can possible be this last reasonless likelihood so I they leave to become wise and better if goodness will who in all be ever glorify and we christian by our lord and saviour jesus Christ sanctify and save our sin be which thus much I have here present in memory of he and master burrell chap. 17 a report of the voyage of master Henry timberley * * or timberlake from cairo in Egypt to jerusalem in fifty day 1601. I depart from grand cairo the nine of march 1600. which day I come to the place where the virgin Mary stay with our saviour when she flee into Egypt from thence with my fellow traveller master burrell in our pilgrim weed come that night to a town name Canko where we lodge that night m. burrell in a yard upon the bare ground want no flea nor louse the next day we come into the land of goshen and here we find a company of turk Jew and christian about seven hundred and fifty which be all bind over the desert of Arabia for Damascus among which be some two and twenty Greek and armenians bind for Jerusalem of which company I be right glad here at this town we stay two day and one night call in their language philbit at which town I go into the house where I see the secret of hatch chicken m m if thunder or trouble air happen all die they all have a claw too much or too little the hatcher have the ten for his furnace and pain by heat artificial in great abundance than I have before see at cairo the thirteen of march we depart from philbit and travel all night in company of the caravan of Damascus and the fourteen at nine of the clock we pitch our tent at bohaire in the land of goshen from thence that night and pitch at on the east of goshen on the edge of the desert here we stay two day for fear of the wild arabian depart the seventeen and that night pass over a great bridge under the which the salt water stand this water come out of the sea from the part of Damiata and be cut out of that place by man hand some one hundred and fifty mile into the land by Ptolomeus king of Egypt intend to bring the mediterranean and red sea together but foresee hereby the drown of all the country he leave and build this bridge which be the part of Egypt and Arabia we be no soon pass this place but we be set upon by the arabian notwithstanding we be about 1000 we have a camel lade with calico take away and four man before hurt and one of the four mortal thus they run away with their prey and we can not remedy it because it be in the night so the eighteen in the morning we pitch at a well of brackish water in this uproar in the night past my fellow master burrell escape very hardly here we repose ourselves till three of the clock in the afternoon call Lazera for the arabian and egyptian divide the day but into four part and then we depart and the next morning pitch at a castle in the desert call cattay this be one of the three castle which the turk keep in the desert to defend the traveller from the arabian and therefore here we pay a certain tax that be to say sixty piece of silver and two penny the piece for the head of man or boy and seventy six for a lade camel and fourteen for a mule. hence we depart and pitch at another brackish well thence at another the twenty of march at the second castle call Arris here our tax be twenty piece of silver by the head a camel thirty from hence with many soldier to conduct we to the three castle and so make a long journey of four and twenty hour we arrive at a castle call Raphael here we pay ten piece of silver and a beast twenty in the one and twenty we pitch our tent at Gaza in Palestina a goodly fruitful country be now clear of the desert here do I see the place as they say where Samson pull down the two pillar here we pay two and twenty for the beast and ten for the head the two and twenty we pitch at a place call of the arabian canuy of the christian Bersheba here we pay two for the head and four for the beast the three and twenty we pitch upon a green under the wall of ramoth gilead hence the next morning I with the other christian depart towards Jerusalem the caravan to Damascus yet we pitch short that night at a place in Arabia call cude chelaneb be fifteen mile from Hebron from Jerusalem five little mile hence we depart in the morning be our lady day and at nine of the clock I see Jerusalem kneel say the lord prayer sing we go to the west gate and then stay for it be not lawful for any Christian to enter not admit then master burrell request i to say that I be a greek only to avoid go to mass but I not have the greek tongue refuse absolute so to do affirm to he even at the gate that I will neither deny my country nor religion so that when they ask what we be master burrell answer in the greek tongue that he be a greek and I a Englishman so he be admit to the greek patriarch and I be take and cast into prison after that I have stay a hour at the gate for the turk do all deny that they have hear either of my queen or country or that she pay they any tribute then the guardian who be their defender of all the christian pilgrim and the principal actor of my imprisonment because I will not offer myself under his protection but say I will rather be protect under the Turk then under he make the Turk so much my foe that they suppose I be a spy and so will not let i out of the dungeon now for my deliverance you shall understand that be at ramoth gilead I go to a fountain to wash my foul linen in which time one come and call i by my name and take my linen from i to help i whereat I marvel what captain quoth he in the Frank tongue I hope you have not forget i it be not yet forty day since you land i at Alexandria among the passenger which you bring from Argier in your ship call the trojan here be also another that you bring I ask if he dwell there he answer no but that he and his fellow be go in the caravan to Damasko which they call shame and from thence to Bagdet which we call Babylon and so to Mecha to make a hadge for so they be call when heap of stone in such abundance as may be wonder at how the inhabitant can live for proof we be within five mile of the city lodge in the field I send my Moor to a place not far hence to buy some bread who return with this answer that he and he do never eat bread in all their life a man may go twenty mile before he find a place to feed a horse or a cow but the country about Palestina Galilee and Syria be all goodly plentiful country and jerusalem itself be the most barren that I see in all my travel the desert except I can compare any place in England to it except the barren place in Cornewal where be nothing but rock and stone and daily by the report of the inhabitant the stone grow more and more that jerusalem and fifteen mile round about be but a heap of stone and I be of opinion that it be quite forsake of God for the more sort of turk there inhabit use all filthiness that the christian be force to marry their child very young yea even at ten year of age boy they keep open and show they at their door which have the fair thus have my patent seal with the great seal of the guardian and a letter patent that do show I have wash in the water of jordan the thirty one of march I depart from jerusalem in my moor company the same night I come to ram. April 1. to Askalon so to Gaza where I hire two wild arabian with two dromedary to carry i to Cayro we ride two upon a beast by the break away of one of our dromedary at our light be leave alone we be dromedary seize by four other arabian who will have make prey of we have not the other their fellow thief return I have nothing to lose but my clothes but promise to pay they twenty four piece of gold the four at night we come to these thief tent where we have camel milk the next night to Salhia where be overshaken I hire horse the dromedary be like a camel but that his head be less his leg long and a very small neck the difference be as between a greyhound and a mastiff in this four day travel I never see they eat nor drink from which they say they will abstain ten day but not so long from meat yet I think a good horse will run fast but not continue with this beast their pace hard than a trot I pay they give my Moor six piece of gold and send he to Mecha with the caravan so I come to bolack to Roshetta thence with a janissary to the wall of Alexandria in the eleven of April 1601. those that have great store of good the bashaw will take the good and say that the good do belong unto he that be dead and by this mean they shall be in great trouble and lose half their good if they can escape so and if any of our company shall die here as God defend the rest shall be in great trouble about it as also that it may be in your commandment that it shall not be lawful for the bashaw or any other for to take away from we any of our good except he will pay for the same to our content for many time there be fine thing bring out of the Indies and the pasha man fit always in the customhouse especial at the come of the frank and if there be any thing that like he he take it and pay for that which be worth a hundred pound ten pound and so the bashaw have deal with many but if you send this commandment that it may be register both here and at Bagdett it will for ever hereafter prevent those trouble that now we be in danger of and this be a thing very needful to be send with those that shall next come hither there be as yet no spaniard come into the Indies and by report of one that be here who come from Ormus there be a Spaniard send out of Spain to at this time Portugal they see paindoue that our companion have money this money be about five hundred crown which we take while we be in the ship and the first night we come on land we bury in the ground which they after dig up want necessary but we that be in the i will of paindoue have none of it they try by extremity of famine to make we to give they some also for they believe miserable famine we have some by reason of this evil resolution of the islander to give we nothing without money we be bring into great misery all that we can do be to gather petiwinckle on the sea shore to eat and sometime to meet with a dead fish. this extremity endure a long time till that the inhabitant see we have no money begin to have a little more commiseration on we we offer our service to they to do what they will employ we about I go often with they to the neighbour land to get and sometime on fish he learn (@) language and in recompense of my labour they give i part of the fish or while we live thus I to that which they ask i be curious to understand the habit manner marriage and fashion of our french dame I be about four or five month in good health and want nothing but the exercise of my religion and my liberty have all thing else to my content after this I fall sick of a hot burn fever there pass not a day but the king and queen send to know how I do and every hour send i delicious viand to eat and thus I continue a great while but afterward the king send i to the i will of bandos a little i will in sight of male which have a better air Bandos then male where a experience man by the king present so that I become some what wealthy after the manner of the country while I thus continue here despair ever to return into France I be diligent to inquire of the people their manner and custom which here I have write and particularise @. 2 description of the maldive their thirteen canton twelve thousand isle sea-change strange current monsons maine-inlets black boil sea heat season civility and hair ceremonionsnesse the land of the maldive begin in eight degree of the equinoctial line on the north-side and end in four degree on the southside they be of a extraordinary length about two hundred league but not above thirty or five and thirty league in latitude situation they be distant from the firm land that be to say from cape comorin from Covan and their distance cochin one hundred and fifty league the portugal reckon that there be four thousand and five hundred league by sea to go thither from Spain they be divide into thirteen province which they call atollon which be a natural partition accord to the situation of the place forasmuch as every Atollon be separate from other division into 13 atollon and contain in itself a great multitude of small isle it be admirable to behold how that each of these atollon be environ round with a huge ledge of rock the atollon be all after a sort circular or oval have each of they thirty league some a little more some a little less and lie all one at the end of the other from the north to Susan they almost touch one another there be between two channel of the sea the one large the other exceed narrow be in the midst of a Atollon you shall see about you a great ledge of rock which impale and defend the isle against the impetuousness of the sea. but it be a very fearful thing even to the most courageous to approach to this ledge and see the wave come afar off and force of the sea. break furious on every side for I assure you as a thing which I have see a thousand time that the surge or billow be great than a house and as white as Cotton so that you shall view round about you as it be a very white wall especial when the sea be lofty now within each of these canton be almost a infinite number of land both small and great the inhabitant tell i that there be about twelve thousand but I conjecture that there appear 12000. land not so many and that they say twelve thousand to note a incredible number and which they can count it be true that there be a innumerable multitude of small one which be as it be hillock of sand all unpeople and moreover the king of the maldive put this number in his title for he be call sultan Ibrahim Atholon that be to say Ibrahim sultan king of thirteen province and twelve thousand iles. king title which notwithstanding the current and daily flow of the sea diminish that number as the inhabitant inform i who say also that a proportion of the number of the people be consume and that there be not so many as be accustom to be ancient also they report that within one of the atollon all the little isle and sea which part they be one sea make daily alteration continue ground and that it be in former time but one only i will cut and divide after into many and sure they which navigate near the maldive discern all within white by reason of the sand which be of this colour upon all the flat and rock the sea thereabouts be very quiet and of a mean depth insomuch that the deep entrance be not twenty fathom and yet here be very few entrance for a man may almost see the bottom every where all the shallows be stone rock and sand so that when the tide be out it reach not to one waste and for the most part to the midleg so that it be very easy to go without a boat throughout all the isle of the same Atollon if it be not for two cause the one great fish call paimone which devour man and break their leg and arm when they danger by shark and sharp stone encounter they the other be that the depth of the sea be general very keen and sharp rock which hurt they wonderful that go into it and moreover they meet with many branch of a certain thing which I know not whither to term tree or rock it be not much unlike white coral which be also branch and pierce but altogether polish on the contrary a kind of coral this be rugged all hollow and pierce with little hole and passage yet abide hard and ponderous as a stone they call it in their language aquiry they keep it to make their honey and sugar of have bruise they with little stone and put they to boil with the water of this be that which fashion their honey and their sugar it great hinder those which wash themselves in the sea it be very difficult to i to go so from i will to i will without a boat but they which be accustom go often among these land there be very many and as I believe the great number which be many of the land ^r^ n^^ inhabit whole unhabited and which have neither tree nor herb other which have no green thing and be but a movable sand yet there be some which be for the most part overflow at spring tide and be discover when the sea be out the residue be all cover with great crab which they call and cray-fish there be great store of fowl call pinguy which here lie and hatch and here be such a prodigious number of he pinguy fowl prodigious multitude of they that a man know not I have often make trial where to set his foot without touch their egg or young one or the old bird which fly not far when they see man the islander eat they not and yet they be very good meat and as big as pigeon their feather white and black these isle which I have say to be habit appear afar off white as if they be cover with snow by reason of the great whiteness of the sand which be fine and subtle as that of a hourglass and so hot and burn that the heat of sand egg of those bird be hatch with great facility they have great scarcity of fresh water some land be well wood and inhabit which have not any except some few whither the inhabitant be constrain to go and seek it from want of water the confine isle also they have invention to receive rain water and although they have water in the isle they be not like one another be better in one respect then another all their pit-water be neither very sweet nor wholesome they make their pit in this manner dig pit how make three or four foot in the earth a little more or less they find freshwater in abundance and that which be very strange not above four foot from the seashore in place also which be often hot at night and cold at noon overflow I have observe that their water be very cold in the day principal at noon and in the night very hot but to return to the thirteen atollon here be their name begin at the north point which be in the head which the portugal call for that cause cabexadel alas ilhas and in the maldives circuit of one Atollon be surround shoalds with a shall and there be but one or two open place which be very straight and difficult to heed wherefore it be necessary that they understand well the good saint (...) m^^^ part of the sea preserve they daily and to speak true they be as it be half fish they be so use to the sea whither they go daily either swim or road or sail I have see they many time within the ledge of rock where the sea be calm run swim after the fish which they have sudden perceive bathe themselves and have take they in their course and this be usual and yet they fail not often to lose their bark notwithstanding all their dexterity the great discommodity be the current which run aswell to the east as the west in the channel of the isle and in diverse in-draught of the sea six month on one coast and six strange seacurr^n^s month on another yet not certain but sometime more someimes less this be that which deceive they and ordinary cast they away the wind be aswell fix as the current from the the monsons east quarter or the west but they vary sometime and be not so rule fetch their compass towards the north or the south and the current go perpetual his accustom course till the season alter it be a very remarkable thing that whereas the atollon be continue one at the end of the other and separate by channel of the sea which go through they they have open inlet opposite place and entrance opposite one to the other two on one side and two on the other by which mean man may go and come from Atollon to Atollon and always communicate together wherein may be observe a effect of the providence of God which have leave nothing unperfect for if there be but two open place in every Atollon that be one on one side and another on the other it be not possible to pass from Atollon to Atollon nor from entrance to entrance because of the boisterousness of the current which run six month to the east and six to the west and permit not to cross over but force they down and when the two entrance be not adverse but one on the east coast the other on the west man may easy enter but not return except the six month be end and the current change now as these entry be dispose man may notwithstanding the current go from one Atollon to another in every season and traffic and merchandise free together as they do for as much as every Atollon be open with four entrance which be in opposition to their two neighbour the entrance of these atollon be unlike some competent broad other very narrow the large be not more than two hundred pace or thereabouts some be be very intemperate and the heat excessive notwithstanding the heat day and night be always equal the night be very cool and bring abundance of dew this coolness be a cause that the country may be
