also they take their soldier the people be very religion great addict to manufacture of all kind of work religion wherein they excel also in letter and science after their manner principal in astrology whereof they make great esteem they be a wise and circumspect nation very fraudulent in their merchandize and their live in the world. they be valiant and hardy and well see in arm and live in great order and policy the woman be fair but that they be of a olive woman colour and some be find as white as they be in Europe yet they have all black hair but they esteem that beauty and many make it to come so wherefore they keep their daughter haire-cere^ money head shave till the age of eight or nine year not leave they till then any hair but a little on their forehead to distinguish they from boy who have none at all yet this come not low than their eyebrow and after that the child be bear they shave they from eight day to eight day which make their hair very black that will not be so else for I have see little child with half flaxen hair the beauty and ornament of the woman be to have their hair very long thick and black which they accommodate and wash often and purify with water and lie make of purpose have well wash and cleanse their head and hair they abide in the wind all dishevel but bathe and oil within the compass of their house until it be thorough dry after they rub and oil their hair with odoriferous oil which cause that their head be always moist and oily for they never wet their body man nor woman but after they oil they two or three time in the week for their hair but for their body often than there be day as for their hair they be not oblige to wash it but when they have accompany together and they be bind particular every Friday which be their sabbath and in all their great feast the man on their friday the woman on their several feast only but sleep after it when they shall think good and accord to their necessity the woman also perfume their head for a little reason which they have and so wash oil and perfume they attire themselves which be to bring all their hair from before backward and draw it out as much as may be that one hair may not mo^e nor waver this way nor that way after they tie they behind or they make a great tuft bind on for which greatness they have a counterfeit lock of man hair but as long as the woman in will feast which they hold a great honour be in feed their own house they love not the other shall see they eat and go therefore to the further side of their house let down all the clothes and tapestry which be before they that so they may be unseen before they eat they say their prayer they have no other table than the floor of their lodging which be cover with a little fine Mat whereon they sit crosslegged they use no naperie but for fear of waste their mat they use great leaf of the neatness bannane whereon they set their dish and other before they instead of trencher they be so neat in their feed that they shed nothing in the place where they eat no not one drop of water although they wash their mouth before and after their repast their dish be of earth figure after the manner of the country and come from Cambaya as good as China porcelain and dish so common that all use they but they have no platter of earth or porcelain which be not after the fashion of a box round varnish and neal and a cover of the same matter the poor sort have cover platter in stead of these box which cost little the reason be because of the ant pismire troublesome which in great number fill every place so that it be very difficult to keep any thing without a cover they be also so nice in their diet that they will not taste of any meat wherein have fall nicety a fly or a emit or any little creature or the least filthiness so that they will give it to the bird when they come for they have no mind to give it to the poor to who they never give any thing which they will not have or which be not aswell dress as for themselves wherefore when the poor come to their door they make they come in and make they as good gharitie cheer as for themselves say that they be the servant of God aswell as themselves the grand signior and rich man have no other vessel than other man although they may have they of gold and silver yet their law forbid it if a dish happen to be a little rive or crack they eat no more in it say that it be pollute they use no spoon neither to eat rice no plate finger-spoon nor honey nor any liquid thing but take they with their finger which they do neat and nimble without lose any thing for they account it the great incivility in the world to let any thing fall in eat in the mean while also none dare spit nor cough but must rise and go forth in eat they never use the left hand because therewith they wash their privity they dexterity willing eat at the begin of their feed a half ripe and drink the water of it say that it be healthful and lose their belly they eat all greedy and in haste hold quick at meat it mannerliness not to be long in eat and in the mean while though they be in company they speak not a word to drink while they be eat be reckon clownishness but after they have eat their fill drink rite they drink once their drink be common of water or of wine of draw forth the same day they have also other sort of drink for the king and noble or at their great solemnity they drink in copper cup well wrought with cover on they after their repast and when they have wash they present a platter of bettell instead of sweet meat for bettell the most part they have no ordinary hour of eat but eat at all hour when they be hungry no man cousin their wife and daughter prepare and dress their meat and not man it be the great injury that a man can do to one to call he Cisday that be to say cook and if any be find to addict themselves to this they be mock and despise every where in such sort that they esteem they not for man but woman and they dare not accompany with any but woman nor do any other exercise also they make it no difficulty to leave they with they when they kill any creature for their food they have many mystery they cut the throat but her-^ites turn themselves towards Mahomet sepulchre and say their prayer and all speedy let it go or go forth not touch it till it be thorough dead if any touch it before they cast away the flesh and eat it not also they cut it not everywhere but in a certain place of the throat otherwise they eat it not and every one understand not this but principal their priest or know it they which enterprise it must be ancient and not young and such as have superstition have child in all their action they be very scrupulous and superstitious after they have sleep whether in the night or day they fail not present after they be awake to wash their eye and face and rub they with oil and put also a certain blackness upon their eyelid and eyebrow they dare not speak nor bid any good morrow till they have do thus they be careful to rub their tooth and to wash and cleanse they say furthermore that the red colour of bettell and Arecka which they chew continual take the better so that they have all red tooth by reason of champ of bettell and they account this bravery they carry it also always bettell and Arecka about in the pleat of their girdle and it shall be a dishonour to be find without it it be the custom when they encounter one another by the way interchangeable each to give the other some of he they bathe often in the day not only for pleasure and commodity but for religion or bathe entrance into the Mosche they wash their extreem after they have make urine or do their necessity they wash their privity with the left hand or they wash all their body which they call junan accord to their feast with diversity of form and ceremony so that when they wash in public as they do a man may know wherefore they bathe as if they have accompany with their wife whether by night or by day they plunge their head three time under the water when they be to go any voyage they desire not to meet or touch any body and if any disastrous thing chance to they they attribute it to he who touch they above all when they go on fish they must not salute any nor bid they good morrow from the go superstion down of the sun on Thursday in the evening till the day follow about three or four of the clock they will not permit any thing to be carry out of their house although their dear love or their father will borrow any thing they will not give it they neither will they render that which shall be send for although it be not they yet they will receive any thing and let it enter into their house in the meanwhile without any scruple they wrangle not nor quarrel together although there be enmity between they above all take heed of reproach in sail if they be surprise with contrary wind of calm or storm they make vow their Aeolus rite to he which command the wind who they call not God but king. there be no isle where be not find a siare as they call it which be a place dedicate to the wind in a desolate corner of the i will where they which have escape danger make offering daily of little boat and ship make purposely full of perfume gum flower and odoriferous wood they burn the perfume and cast the little boat into the sea which go float till they be burn for they put fire in they to the end they say that the king of the wind may accept they also they set not willing their ship and galley afloat but they kill hen and cock and cast they in the sea before the ship or boat which they will use they believe also that there be a king of the sea to who in like sort they make prayer and ceremony in their navigation and when they go on fish fear upon every error and offence the king of the wind and of the sea. so that be on the sea they dare not spit on the windy side nor cast any thing overboard for fear that they shall be angry with they also they never look behind they all the boat bark and ship be devote to the power of the wind and of the sea and sure they respect they as if they be their temple keep they neat and never commit superstitious neatness any filthy and dishonest thing in they they have also the king of the other element as they call they and especial that of war but all with great ceremony they great esteem certain character which they call ta^ide which they wear under their garment enclose in little box which the rich make of gold or silver they wear they often on their arm on their neck or at their girdle or else at their foot accord to character see the like in jobsons note of Gambra the subject of the disease for they wear they for all thing as well offensive as defensive that they shall love or be love or hate or to heal or cure any malady the magician and sorcerer sell they these for money and tell they that it bring they good luck and heal their disease they have few remedy for their malady but have recourse to the magician and sorcerer who be their only physician they believe also that all their evil be cause by the devil to vex they who be the only cause of their death and disease therefore they call magician devil invoke upon he and offer flower to he and prepare banquet of all sort of viand and beverage which they set in a certain secret place where they let they consume if no poor people happen to take they away for the same purpose they kill cock or hen turn they towards the sepulchre of Mahomet after leave they there pray the devil to accept of they the fever be common among they but most dangerous to stranger from ten year to ten year here come a disease call for which they abandon one another as if it be fever the plague it be like the small pock and kill many the disease of the eye be very common decenniall disease blindness I have see a great number blind and the most part have little eye it happen also often that have be long in the sun in the height of the day after the sun be down they see not at all whatsoever fire or light be put near they although it be a hundred torch yet without feel any other evil to heal it they boil the liver of a cock and write word and charm and set it towards the point of the set of the sun my companion and I be sometime vex with this malady but have learn the receipt we take the liver of a cock reject their charm to see if that will serve and we find that it heal we as well as they without observe their sorcery they be much subject to the itch which they heal with oil of remediless tetter terrify they much some tetter have almost their whole body overrun with they these evil come by reason of the quantity of saltfish which they eat and also because they seldom salt their meat but power sea-water to it in the winter although the rain be continual yet they go barefoot they have under barefoot foot worm their foot and between their toe a kind of hand-worme which breed in the filth it make weal and push full of water which after they increase engender ulcer which great hinder their go they be also trouble all over the body with these worm they have all common great spleen and be subject to obstruction and endure much evil they have some receipt and composition of herb and drug for diverse malady and principal splenetike for wound which they heal very cunning they use no binding nor linen to their soar but only ointment cathaire and flux rheum sometime trouble they and ache in the bone the neapolitan disease be not very frequent they heal it with China wood without sweat or any other thing they call it Farangui Baesrour this malady come from Europe who inhabitant they call it Farangui or europeans call frank no toothache hardiness they be never trouble with the toothache it seem their ordinary chaw of bettell be the cause hereof as soon as their infants-are bear they wash they in cold water six time a day and after they chafe they with oil and continue this wash a great while and moreover when they make urine or do nature office they wash their privity with water the mother nourish their own child and dare not put they forth to nurse to other no nursery of infant not the queen say ordinary that the beast bring up their young but they have servant to tend carry and govern they beside the breast they make a kind of pap of rice or honey bray and macerate after boil with milk and sugar of the most part especial the poor give they Bananes they never swaddle their child but let they go free and yet I never see any deform now their couch hang in the air within little bed of cord or little chair where they shogge and rock they at the age of nine month they begin to go at nine year old they bring they up in the study and exercise of the country these education study be to learn to write and to read and to understand their Alcoran and know what they be bind to do their letter be of diverse sort the arabic with some letter and point which they have add to express their language another whereof the character be peculiar to the language of the maldive and moreover a three which be the vulgar of Ceylan and of letter peculiar learn to write the great part of the Indies they write their lesson on little table of wood which be white and when they can say their lesson by heart they blot it out and white it again if the writing be to abide and remain perpetual they write upon parchment which be make of the leaf of the tree call Macore Queau which be a fathom and a half in length leaf parchment and a foot broad to teach their child to write they have board make of wood purposely very smooth and plain whereon they spread very fine and thin sand after with a bodkin they make the letter and make they imitate they blot out the rule which they have write and never use herein any paper they carry as great respect and reverence to their tutor as to their father so that they may new kindred of teachers not contract marriage together as be ally in affinity there be some find among they who follow their study who be very skilful in the Alcoran and ceremony of their law they be principal the Modins catibe or naybe these two office be compatible for a catibe may be a naybe and a naybe a catibe the mathematics be there teach and be great esteem especial astrology astrology which many study for they consult with the astrologer about every thing they will enterprise nothing without their advice they will not only know their nativity and time of their birth but also if they build whether with wood or stone they must inquire of the ginger what hour will be best to begin that it may be under a good constellation or if they employ a boat although they do it diverse take a different day or hour for a ship of war or of merchanchize or a fish bark if they undertake any voyage or any thing else they inquire of the ginger what shall be the issue and whether the day be good or evil if the planet be favourable or unfortunate whatsoever sinister accident happen to they they attribute the cause to the day and take it patient say it be the will of God that have bring it to pass the islander be much exercise in arm either to serve with a sword and buckler or ready Arme^ to bend the bow or use the harquebuse or manage the pike they have school the master whereof be great honour and respect and ordinary he grand signior use this exercise they have no play but the ball and tennis which they receive and cast forth with great agility although it be not but with their foot their great exercise be fish which all in all place of the maldive use indifferent Fishing^ without have any as in other place certain person of this vocation or certain place proper to it which be not public this exercise they account honest and honourable wherein also the gentleman exercise themselves as they do here in hunt the king have twelve person appoint to guide and conduct his boat when he go on fish and to prepare all thing necessary for it they have a admirable quantity of great fish as bonito albachore guilt-head and other which (...) be very like one another and of the same taste and have no more scale than the mackerel they take they in the deep sea on this fashion with a line of a fathom and a half of great find Cotton thread make fault to a great cane their hook be not so much bow as we but strange form of take fish more stretch out and be point in the end like a pin without have any other beard or tongue they fasten not on their b^it but the day before provide a quantity of small fish as great as our little bleak or roche which they find in great number on the bank and sand and keep they alive enclose in little pursnet make of the thread of with little mash and let they hang in the sea at the stern of their bark when they come into the deep sea they sow about their little fish and let their line hang down the great fish see the little fish which be not frequent in the deep sea run together in great shoal and by the same mean they fasten they to their hook which they white and trim over so that be a ravenous and foolish fish it take the white hook think it be a white little fish. they do nothing but lift their line into their boat and the fish fall off present be not strong fasten and then they put it into the sea again thus they take a strange quantity so that in three or four hour their boat be in a manner full and that which be remarkable they go always with full sail the fish which they take thus they general call in their language cobolly mass that be to say the black fish for they be all black they have another sort of fish on their bank when the moon be in the change and when it be at the full three day each time this they do on raft make of the wood call Camdou they have great line of fifty or sixty fathom pitch over in the end they hang hook whereon they fasten the bait as we do and thus take great quantity of fish one kind very delicious which they call the king of the sea. they have all sort of net and toil make king of the sea. of Cotton twine weel and outstretch instrument of fish near the sea shore and where it be shallow they pass their time and take delight in fish for small fish like pilchard with cast net twice in the year at the equinoctials they make a general fish a great number general fish of person assemble together in certain indraught of the sea. the sea at that time arise high than all the time of the year and pass the limit of other tide the ebb after the same proportion recoil and retire discover the rock and shoalds which at other time appear not in those place while the sea be go out they observe some fit corner and set about it great stone one upon another to a great height so that it resemble a round wall or ravelin this enclosure have forty pace in circuit or compass but the entrance be but two or three pace large they gather together thirty or forty man and every one carry fifty or sixty fathom of great cord of where from fathom to fathom they tie a piece of the bark of dry to make it float on the water as we use cork after they tie they together and stretch they out in a round upon the flat it be strange that all the fish which be within the cord find themselves take although there be no other net nor instrument but the cord which swim on the water but the fish fear the line and shadow of the line so that they dare not pass under to escape but fly from the line think that it have a net underneath the man go all drive they to the enclosure of stone draw up the cord by little and little some in boat and some in the water for upon these flat the sea be shallow and not above ne^ke high for the most part less so moderate draw up the line the fish fly from it and be lock up in the enclosure so that in the end the line be all draw up all the fish enter in and they speedy stop the entire with faggot of bough and leaf of bind end to end twenty or thirty fathom and compact together about the greatness of a man and so when the sea be out the fish remain take on the dry land. they often take thus of all sort ten and twelve thousand or more this fish they make but once in six month upon every flat and every time continue five day and they change daily their division and return not often into the same place to fish in this manner except at another equinoctial the people be above measure superstitious and addict to their religion but yet extreme give to woman wanton and riotous there be nothing commoner than adultery incest and sodomy notwithstanding the rigour of their law and penalty as for simple fornication there be nothing more ordinary they count it not a sin neither their wife nor daughter which be not marry make it no great matter to yield themselves to their friend and after which be very execrable to evacuate their fruit by make a abortion or destroy their child which be not legitimate the woman be strange impudent and the man be not less vicious but they can be more and very effeminate all their desire be to procure if they can some lechery receipt that they may better content their wife and be more strong to exercise their fornication I think they spend all their good on this hereof they continual speak and be very dissclute in their word and almost never stir from their wife of who they have plurality to three which be the cause that they can satisfy each of they also the air of the country be hot and exhale part of their spirit and courage and also their continual soften their flesh in the water and that the most part eat opium or Aphion as they call it which tipple intoxicate and dull they the woman as I have say careful hide their breast to speak of they they account very lascivious and dishonest to kiss they make as great a matter as to lie together although they be dissolute in their conversation yet they contain themselves before their parent and respect their presence but if a man happen to speak a word such as I have breast not to be speak of say to a woman before one or any of her kindred they will go hide themselves and be great offend against he he must therefore make they excuse and say that he know not that they be near of kin otherwise they will think that he do purposely and therefore complain to the justice that he may manifest which say these lascivious word in their presence that he hold they for good and honest people a man dare not enter into the place where a woman bathe herself or where she be retire her robe be off although they never take off the cloth which environ they and serve they for a coat but as I have say they esteem the breast as shameful part when a man and a woman be together and another person meet with he he must not demand of this man if she be his wife or daughter or sister for if it be his daughter and he shall ask if it be his wife he shall offend as if he accuse he of incest only he must demand if she be his kinswoman and he tell the degree of parentage or affinity as long as the woman have their term they bathe not and wash only their hand and mouth they change not their garment nor lie with their husband nor eat nor converse with any body when the woman go a visit in the night they must have a man to accompany they who go before visitation and when he perceive that any body come he say three time Gas that be take heed the man advertise by this quite the side of the way where the woman go make no semblance of see they nor of know they with great respect and if they be other woman they take each her side of the way and salute not except they be very familiar they never knock at the gate for there be no ring or Hammer nor call to be let into the house for the great gate of the court be always open till eleven of the clock in the evening wherefore they enter into the court which be near the door of the house which be also open and spread only with tapestry of Cotton cloth or other stuff and as they approach to this gate they cough palace guard nobility robe attire attendance exercise riches slay by the bengalan the government of the estate of the maldive be royal and very absolute and ancient the king. the king be fear and reverence and all depend of he in each of the thirteen canton be one principal who they call naybe these naybe or principal of the province naybe be priest and doctor of their law and have the oversight of all that concern religion and instruction of the people therein and exercise of justice and command the priest which be under they these atollon be subdivide into many land in each of which where there be not above forty and one man be a doctor call catibe superior in the religion catibe of that i will who have under he the particular priest of the mosque all which have care to nourish and instruct the people in the law and live of a certain portion of first-fruit which every one be bind to give they and of certain rent which the king give they accord to their degree their maintenance but particular the naybe beside the exercise of religion and authority which they have be institute to execute and do justice each in his government they be the only judge of the country as well in matter civil as criminal and if any one will have justice he must go find out the naybe or attend his come to the place for the naybe four time in the year go in circuit about the land each in his jurisdiction and make visitation as well for the religion of the priest as for justice this be their great revenue for then their duty be pay they moreover they receive store of present from many person whereof they be very greedy in all the maldive there be no judge but the thirteen naybe for the catibe of the land the thirteen naybe visitation and circuit and the priest of the mosque be but for a show over these naybe there be a superior which reside in the i will of male and be ever near his person which be call pandiare who be not only chief of the religion throughout all the realm but also sovereign judge so that after they have plead before the naybe if they the pandiare or chief judge will not stand to his sentence whether in matter civil or criminal they may appeal to the pandiare who all affair that offer themselves take advice of some naybe which be near he of the catibe grave man call Moucouris that be doctor and experience man which be not officer they give no judgement if they be not assist with four or five of these person at the least these Moucouris can say all the Alcoran by heart and all the other read it only beside diverse other science which they know they solemn invite they to learned man all their feast sermon and ceremony and be great honour and respect by all there be not above fifteen of they in all the land the pandiare be call cady in the arabic language also after the judgement of the pandiare one may complain to the king who command and make justice to be execute and this be by six signior his principal officer who manage the king. six counsellor of state. the most importune affair of state the pandiare be assist with two catibe of the i will of Male and by naybe of the Attollon beside some of those doctor go also to make the country and serve only their creditor or other person which lend they money to discharge they these be call Pemousere which be to say servant by borrow and they continue thus till they be acquit to great person and man of authority to have support and favour for when they belong to no body they be trouble by one or other the wife can pursue in justice the death of her husband but only the child of murder to bring up the child of the decease and teach they some trade or mystery when they be come to age they demand justice or remit and pardon the murderer without any after examination in matter of injury commit on the person of any particular the wrong must complain or otherwise the crime be abolish except the king will make justice to be execute without the other party but this be seldom the ordinary punishment be banishment into the desert land towards the south cut punishments off a principal member or the whip which be the common punishment but extraordinary cruel they be thong of great thick leather a fathom in length four finger in breadth and two in thickness hereof there be five or six tie together in a stock and handle of wood terrible whip with this they chastise malefactor and beat they so severe that they die often this be the ordinary punishment for the most part of the great crime as sodomy incest and adultery beside this punishment they cut off the woman hair that be take in adultery false witness and perjure person be thus punish and moreover condemn in a pecuniary mulct which adultery rape theft be dispose of to the poor a rape be punish as adultery and for the most part the ravisher be condemn to endow the woman or maid the steal of any thing of value with the cut off the hand if they commit any thing against the law they must make a kind of public penance they think they shall never come in paradise if they pay not and accomplish that which the law have appoint for the execution and chastise of malefactor they have no hangman but the devanit or sergeant do it for punishment with death although their law ordain few execute it for homicide yet the judge never condemn they to it all the while I be in the maldive I see none condemn to death by the ordinary judge they dare not do it except the king express command it which be seldom they say common that they must not put man to death so and if they shall execute all that merit death it will be a long time before the land shall be inhabit yet the king send his soldier and condemn and execute those as have deserve it for although justice be in the power of the doctor of the law yet the king be the only arbitrator and alone have power of life and death among other the king use one particular punishment on those which have offend he he make they lie on the ground upon their belly and their arm and leg to be hold by four man and after to be beat on their back with a staff or kind of cane call Rotan which come from Bengala this pull off the skin and the mark or brand endure and then the king send to distribute his merchandise throughout the isle to the rich at what price he will although they have no use of it take in exchange such merchandise as he have need of at a money long as a finger coin but much fold the king coin they in his island and imprint on they his name in arabic letter the other money be exotic coin and there go currant but they take they not but at just value and at equal weight and only the gold or silver all other sort of coin which be not of the country they reject for in India as there be many realm and signiory so great diversity of money of stamp and character not only of gold and silver but also of a other mettle call Calin which be white like tin and very hard pure and beautiful whereof they make great esteem in the Indies they have also iron money but this kind of money go only in the dominion of the prince that coin it the gold and silver of whatsoever stamp and character it be be currant through all kingdom accord to the just value which be of different value from we because silver be dear than here and gold base the king make no lesser coin than the Larin so that to effect their merchandise they cut the silver because there be then no knowledge of that country as now there be it may be credible that though the boat be small in respect of those huge sea yet the wind and water may bring they thither as we see Columbus second voyage Leon a new world find out colon. in the year 1493. the five and twenty of the month of October Christopher Columbus go back unto the antiles and from Cadiz he take his course have in his company seventeen ship and fifteen hundred man in they with his brethren Bartholomew Columbus and Diego Columbus with other knight gentleman man of law and religious man with chalice cross rich ornament and with great power and dignity from pope Alexander and the ten day after their set forth they arrive at the canary and from thence in five and twenty or thirty day they sail unto the antiles and the first island that they see stand in 14. degree towards the north due west from cape Verde on the coast of Africa they say that the distance from thence to the canary be eight hundred league the name they give it be Deseada that be the desire or wish island for the great desire which the company have Deseada discover ^as uirgine to come to sight of land. after that they discover many more which they name the uirgine which the natural of the country call the Caribas for that the man of that country be good warrior and shoot well in bow they poison their arrow with a herb whereof he that be hurt die bite himself like as a make dog do from these land and other they go unto the principal island there which they of the country do call boriquen and the spaniard call it saint John and thence to hispaniola or Isabel where they find all the man dead which there they have leave here the admiral leave the boriquen or s. John de Porto ri^^^ most part of the people to plant it and appoint his brethren to be governor there and so take two ship and go to discover the other side of the island of Cuba and from thence to jamaica all these land stand from 16. unto 20. degree of northerly latitude in the jamaica mean time that the admiral sail about his brethren and they that be leave with they be much trouble because the savage do rise against they so that Christopher Colon go back again into Spain to tell the king and queen of his adventure in the year 1494. and in the month of january there be a agreement make of the difference see sup. l. 2. c. 1. @. 7. which be between the two king of Spain and Portugal for the which agreement there be send out of Portugal Ruy and don John his son and the doctor ayres de Almada and for the king of Spain there be don Henry Henriques don John de cardenas and the doctor Maldonado all these meet in the town of Tordefillas and they divide the world from the north to the south by a meridian which stand west from the land the first line of partition the death of don John the second of cape Verde 300. league so that the one half which lie to the east shall belong unto Portugal and that which lie to the west to the king of Spain whereby notwithstanding liberty to travel be leave equal unto both in the year follow 1495. petition the king but with such effect that the king make no answer which with the Chinois be a denial and at last he write to the king that accord to his office he will send they out of the kingdom such except as remain in the royal city this he do but the magistrate of those city where we reside dissemble the matter except that persecution and martyrdom Nanquin adversary which apprehend two often whip after their cruel manner one or two die in prison by force of the torment many of the ethnike favour we but the christian magistrate Paulus Michael Leo do marvellous bestir themselves nor do any convert apostatise but beyond the china pusillanimity be both constant and cheerful in their suffering at last our Nanquin adversary bribe the eunuch with ten thousand piece of gold extort from the king that we shall be send back to their own but not which he seek their death we therefore honourable dismiss from pequin come to Canton those of Nanquin Jesuit dismiss from Pequin be send away tempestuous storm and terrible earthquake insomuch that both ship in the harbour have be overset and driu^n a shore by the fur of the one and house on the land disjoint and shake to piece by the fearful tremble of the other it be govern by a emperor who have threescore and five king under his command emperor and government 65. vassal they have but small and petty kingdom yet all of they challenge and assume to themselves that royal state and dignity which may well become the person of far more famous prince there be but five of the emperor privy counsel who common be such that for council wisdom policy and careful vigilencie in manage the state affair in prevent of treason and rebellion in execute of justice and continue of peace and quietness may be compare with many nay most in Christendom no man may make know any cause unto the emperor himself either by word of mouth or petition but every one must acquaint the counsel with his cause and if they approve it the emperor shall know of it if not you must be content to have it drown in oblivion the emperor live in great royalty and seldom magnificence go abroad either to hawk or hunt without a thousand follower at least to attend he he have but one wife and it be general report that he keep company with no other but chastity her only and if it be true as it be think he may in that respect be term the phoenix of all those part of the world as for those within his own dominion they be so far either from imitate or follow he that one be scarce content with a hundred woman and they be so shameless in that kind that they will boast of it and account it a glory unto they to make relation of the multitude of woman which they have have the use of this emperor have abundance of silver and gold and not only his riches coffer but whole storehouse be cram with coin he have some ball of gold which be bring to his court from Ozechya castle of that weight and magnitude that fifteen or sixteen man be scarce able to bear one of they all river do in a kind of thankful renumeration return their water to the sea because they take they from thence but the prince of japon do clean contrary for they receive nothing from the emperor and yet they give all to the emperor for they do even impoverish press (...) themselves by enrich he by present nay they strive and contend who may give jealousy the great and chief present and each of those several prince must always be either himself in person or his brother elder son or the chief nobleman within his realm at the emperor court the reason of it be not well know but it be pretend that it be do to keep the several kingdom in quiet and free from tumult treason and rebellion the emperor do ordinary requite his prince present after this manner he give they a feather for a goose some few kerrimoone or coat for gold silver or other precious and rare commodity and that they may not grow rich and of sufficient ability to make head against he policy to impoverish subject he suffer not their fleece to grow but shear they off by raise tax on they for the build of castle and the repair of fortification and yet they be not suffer to repair their own or any way to fortify themselves Ozechya be the most famous castle that the emperor have or that be within the empire it be Osaca or Ozechia and other castle of a extraordinary bigness and compass round with three several wall the castle of be likewise wall and moat have some few ordnance on it at Crates and Falkata there be likewise castle both wall and moat the circumference of each of they be near about two mile the chief nobleman of those kingdom have house within the castle wall to come and live there either at the king or their own pleasure within each of those castle there be a storehouse keep ordinary full of rice which may serve for their provision at all occasion and needs at Falkata there be a wood of pine tree near about three mile square neatness and temple which be all the summer time sweep and keep so clean that you shall hardly see any small twig bough or leaf under the tree and the tree stand so close together that you may solace and recreate yourself there at all hour of the day without any hurt or heat of the sun in the midst of it there be a great pagoda or church very rich adorn with gild image and all sort of curious carve work the people be general courteous affable and full of compliment they be very punctual custom o^ the people in the entertain of stranger and they will assoon lose a limb as omit one ceremony in welcome their friend they use to give and receive th^ empty cup at one the other band and before the master of the house begin to drink he^ will proffer the cup to every one of his guest make show to have they to begin though it be far from his intention they feed not much upon variety for fish rootes and Rice be their common junkate and if they chance to kill a hen duck or pig which be but seldom they will not like ch^^les eat it alone but their friend shall be sure partaker of it their ordinary drink be water and that be make most time hot in the same pot where they see their rice that so it may receive some thickness and substance from the rice they have strong wine and rack distil of Rice of which they will sometime drink large especial at their feast and meeting and be move to anger or wrath in the heat of their drink you may assoon persuade tiger to patience and quietness as they so obstinate and wilful they be in the fury of their impatience their law be very strict and full of severity afford no other kind of punishment but either death or banishment murder theft treason or the violation of any of the emperor proclamation or edict be punish with death so be adultery also if it be know and the party pursue but the d^uill their master in those action have teach they such clean conveyance that seldom or never be they apprehend they proceed both in controversy and criminal cause accord to the verdict of the produce witness and the sentence be once past t^ey will not revoake or mitigate the severity of it but if the party attach have deserve death they shall sure have it and for the manner they be either behead or crucify he kneel down on his knee and then come the executioner behind he and cut off his head with a Catan or their countrie-sword and his head be off the young cavalleer try their weapon on his limb and prove whether they can cut off a arm or leg at a blow the other have their arm and leg spread abroad on a cross which do they set the cross upright in the ground and then come one either with a lance or spear and run the party through the body where he hang until he rot off no man be suffer to take he down every one may change his name three time when he be a child when he be a youngman and when he be old some change their name more often every one as he please may make choice of his own name and they be common name either by the king or else by some noble or great-man with who they be chief in favour they have the use of write and print and have have the space of many year no man know certain how long they have seven sort of letter each single letter serve for a word and many of they in their place serve for six or seven and each alphabet have eight and forty letter and yet with all these letter they be not able to write our christian name they have not the true pronounciation of h. b. t. and some other letter and a chinese if his life lie on it can true pronounce d. they observe no sabbath but certain feast day accord to the moon as the first of the moon the 15. or 28. on these day they go to the church visit the sepulcher of the dead and use many foolish and apish ceremony which time will not permit i now to relate the nine day of the moon throughout the year they hold for accurse and therefore in that day they will not begin or undertake any work of consequence and importance they strict observe a fast on that day of the month in which their father or mother die which they do so precise keep that they will not touch or eat any thing that have blood kind sir if I have not in this satisfy you accord to your expectation yet I will assure you it be accord as the time and my wayward affair will now permit i I will entreat to heat from you and God willing as I have leisure I will more full declare unto you my particular observation of japon in the mean time I will pray for your health and good success in all your affair and godly enterprise from Wingham in Kent the 25. of November 1623. rest yours to use in what he may arthur hatch chap. 4 extract of master Caesar Fredrick his eighteen year indian observation in the year of our lord God 1563 I Caesar Frederick be in Venice and very the author go from Venice to Cyprus and Tripoli touch the way from Aleppo to Bagdet see sup. l. 9 c. 1. and 3 desirous to see the east part of the world take my journey to Aleppo and there I acquaint myself with merchant of Armenia and moor that be merchant and consort to go with they to Ormus and we depart from Aleppo and in two day journey and a half we come to a city call bir. thence to Babylon or Bagdet and so to Basora and Ormus Ormus have a Moor king of the race of the Persian who be create and make king by the the election of the king of Ormus captain of the castle in the name of the king of Portugal at the creation of this king I be there and see the ceremony that they use in it which be as follow the old king be dead the captain of the portugal choose another of the blood royal and make this election in the castle with great ceremony and when he be elect the captain swear he to be true and faithful to the king of Portugal as his lord and governor and then he give he the sceptre regal after this with great feast and pomp and with great company he be bring into the royal palace in the city this king keep a good train and have sufficient revenue to maintain himself without trouble of any because the captain of the castle do maintain and defend his right and when that the captain and he ride together he be honour as a king yet he can ride abroad with his train without the consent of the captain first have it behoove they to do this and it be necessary because of the great trade that be in this city their proper language be the persian tongue there I ship myself to go for Goa a city in the Indies in which passage the first city that you come to in the Indies be call Diu and be situate in a little island in the kingdom of Cambaia which be the great diu. strength that the portugal have in all the Indies yet a small city but of great trade because there they lade very many great ship for the straits of Mecca and Ormus with merchandise and these ship belong to the moor and christian but the moor can trade neither sail into those sea without the licence of the viceroy of the king of Portugal otherwise they be take and make good prize the merchandise that they lade these ship withal come from Cambaietta a port in the kingdom of Cambaia which they bring from thence in small barke^ Cambaietta because there can no great ship come thither by reason of the sholdnesse of the water thereabouts and these sholde be a hundred or fourscore mile about in a straight or gulf which they call Macareo which be as much to say as a race of a tide because the water there run out of that place without measure so that there be no place like to it unless it be in the kingdom Macareo great tide of Pegu where there be another Macareo where the water run out with more force than these do Cambaietta be situate on the sea side and be a very fair city the time that I be there the Citi^ be in great calamity and scarceness so that I have see the man of the country that be gentile take their child their son and their daughter and have desire the portugal to buy they and I have see they sell for eighr or ten larin a piece which may be of our money ten shilling or thirteen shilling four penny for all this if I have not see it I can not have believe that there shall be such a trade at Cambaietta as there be for in the time of every new moon and every full moon the small bark innumerable come in and out for at those time of the moon the tide and water be high than at other time they be these bark be lade with all sort of spice with silk of China with sandols with elephant tooth velvet of great quantity of which come from Mecca Chickinos which be piece of gold worth seven shilling a piece sterling with money and with diverse sort of other merchandise also these bark lade out as it be a infinite quantity of cloth make of bombast of all sort as white stamp and paint with great quantity of indigo dry ginger and conserve myrabolans dry and Boraso in paste great store of sugar great quantity of Cotton abundance of opium Ferida Puchio with many other sort of drug turban make in dui great stone like to corncolaes garnet agat Diaspry hematist and some kind of natural diamond during the time I dwell in Cambaietta I see very marvelous thing there be a infinite a marvelous fond delight in woman number of artificer that make bracelet call or bracelet of elephant tooth of diverse colour for the woman of the gentile which have their arm full deck with they and in this occupation there be spend every year many thousand of crown the reason whereof be this that when there die any whatsoever of their kindred then in sign and token of mourn and sorrow they break all their bracelet from their arm and present they go and buy new again because that they have rather be without their meat then without their bracelet there come every year to Chau from cochin and from cananor ten or fifteen great ship lade with great nut cure and with sugar make of the self same nut call Giagra the tree where on these nut do grow be call the palmer tree and through out all the Indies and especial from this place to Goa there be great abundance of they and it be like to the date tree in the whole world there be not a tree more profitable and of more goodness than this tree be neither do man reap so much benefit of any other tree as they do of this there be not any part of it but serve for some use and none of it be worthy to be burn with the timber of this tree they Coco tree and profit thereof they (@) plentiful in the ^^es of the (@) make ship without the mixture of any other tree and with the leave thereof they make sail and with the fruit thereof which be a kind of nut they make wine and of the wine they make sugar and Placetto which wine they gather in the spring of the year out of the middle of the tree where continual there go or run out white liquor like unto water in that time of the year they put a vessel under every tree and every evening and morning they take it away full and then distil it with fire it make a very strong liquor and then they put it into butt with a quantity of Zibibbo white or black and in short time it be make a perfect wine after this they make of the nut great store of oil of the tree they make great quantity of board and quarter for building of the bark of this tree they make cable rope and other furniture for ship and as they say these rope be better than they that be make of hemp they make of the bow bedsted after the Indies fashion and Scavasches for merchandise the leave they cut very small and weave they and so make sail of they for all manner of ship or else very fine mat and then the first rind of the nut they stamp and make thereof perfect Ockam to calk ship great and small and of the hard bark thereof they make spoon and other vessel for meat in such wise that there be no part thereof throw away or cast to the fire when these mat be green they be full of a excellent sweet water to drink and if a man be thirsty with the liquor of one of the mat he may satisfy himself and as this nut ripen the liquor thereof turn all to kernel in the year of our lord 1567. I go from Goa to bezeneger the chief city of the kingdom of Narsinga eight day journey from Goa within the land in the company of two other merchant which carry with they three hundred arabian horse to that king because the horse of that country be of a small stature and at the go out of Goa the horse pay custom two and forty pagody for every horse which pagody may be of sterling money six shilling eight penny they be piece of gold of that value so that the arabian horse a very good sale for horse be of great value in those country as 300. 400. 500 and to 1000 ducat a horse the city of bezeneger be sack in the year 1565. by four king of the moor which be of great power and might the name of these four king be these follow the first be call Dialcan * * bezeneger Idalcan Xamalucco etc. a most unkind and wicked treason against their prince this they have for give credit to stranger rather than to their own native people the second Zamaluc the three Cotamaluc and the four Uiridy and yet these four king be not able to overcome this city and the king of bezeneger but by treason this king of bezeneger be a gentile and have amongst all other of his captain two which be notable and they be moor and these two captain have either of they in charge threescore and ten or fourscore thousand man these two captain be of one religion with the four king which be moores wrought mean with they to betray their own king into their hand the king of bezeneger esteem not the force of the four king his enemy but go out of his city to wage battle with they in the field and when the army be join the battle last but a while not the space of four hour because the two traitorous captain in the chief of the fight with their company turn their face against their king and make such disorder in his army that as astonish they set themselves to flight thirty year be this kingdom govern by three brethren which be tyrant the which keep the rightful king in prison it be their use every year once to show he to the people and they at their pleasure rule as they list these brethren be three captain belong to the father of the king they keep in prison which when he die leave his son very young and then they take the government to themselves the chief of these three be call and sit in the royal throne and be call the king the second be call and he take the government on he the three be call bengatre and he be captain general of the army these three brethren be in this battle in the which the chief and the last be never hear of quick nor dead only Temiragi^ flee in the battle have lose one of his eye when the news come to the city of the overthrow the sack of the city in the battle the wife and child of these three tyrant with their lawful king keep prisoner flee away spoil as they be and the four king of the moor enter the city bezeneger with great triumph and there they remain six month search under house and in all place for money and other thing that be hide and then they depart to their own kingdom because they be not able to maintain such a kingdom as that be so far distant from their own country when the king be depart from bezeneger this return to the city and then begin for to repopulate it and send word to Goa to the merchant if they have any horse to bring they to he and he will pay well for they and for this cause the aforesaid two merchant that I go in company withal carry those horse that they have to bezeneger also this tyrant make a order or law that if any merchant have any of the horse that policy to entrap man be take in the aforesaid battle or war although they be of his own mark that he will give as much for they as they will and beside he give general safe conduct to all that shall bring they when by this mean he see that there be great store of horse bring thither unto he he give the merchant fair word until such time as he see they can bring no more then he license the merchant to depart without give they any thing for their horse which when the poor man see they be desperate and as it be mad with sorrow and grief I rest in bezeneger seven month although in one month I may have discharge all my business for it be necessary to rest there until the way be clear of thief which at that time range up and down and in the time I rest there I see many strange and beastly deed do by the gentile first when there be any noble man or woman dead they burn their body and if a marry man die his wife must burn herself alive for the love of her husband and with the body of her husband so that when any man die his wife will take a month leave two or three or as she will to burn herself in and that day be come wife burn with their husband describe wherein she ought to be burn that morning she go out of her house very early either on horseback or on a elephant or else be bear by eight man on a small stage in one of these order she go be apparel like to a bride carry round about the city with her hair down about her shoulder garnish with jewel and flower accord to the estate of the party and they go with as great joy as bride do in Venice to their nuptial she carry in her left hand a lookingglass and in her right hand a arrow and sing through the city as she pass and say that she go to sleep with her dear spouse and husband shee be accompany with her kindred and friend until it be one or two of the clock in the afternoon a description of the burn place than they go out of the city and go along the river side call Nigondin which run under the wall of the city until they come unto a place where they use to make this burn of woman be widow there be prepare in this place a great square cave with a little pinnacle hard by it four or five step up the foresay cave be full of dry wood the woman be come thither accompany with a great number of people which come to see the feast and dance when they shall mourn thing than they make ready a great banquet and she that shall be burn eat with as great joy and gladness as though it be her wedding day and the feast be end than they go to dance and sing a certain time accord as she will after this the woman of she own accord command they to make the fire in the square cave where the dry wood be and when it be kindle they come and certify she thereof then present she leave the feast and take the near kinsman of her husband by the hand and they both go together to the bank of the foresay river where she put off all her jewel and all her clothes and give they to her parent or kinsfolk and cover herself with a cloth because she will not be see of the people be naked she throw herself into the river say oh wretch wash away your sin come out of the water she roll herself into a yellow cloth of fourteen brace long and again she take her husband kinsman by the hand and they go both together up to the pinnacle of the square cave wherein the fire be make when she be on the pinnacle she talk and reason with the people recommend unto they her child and kindred before the pinnacle they use to set a Mat because they shall not see the fierceness of the fire yet there be many that will have they pluck away show therein a heart not dissolute resoluteness fearful and that they be not afraid of that sight when this silly woman have reason with the people a good while to her content there be another woman that take a pot with oil and sprinkle it over her head and with the same she anoint all her body and afterward throw the pot into the furnace and both the woman and the pot go together into the fire and present the people that be round about the furnace throw after she into the cave great piece of wood so by this mean with the fire and with the blow that she have with the wood throw after she she be quick dead and after this there grow such sorrow and such mourn wh^ they shall rejoice lamentation among the people that all their mirth be turn into howl and weep in such wise that a man can scarce bear the hear of it I have see many burn in this manner because my house be near to the gate where they go out to the place of burn and when there die any great man his wife with all his slave with who he have have carnal copulation burn themselves together with he also in this kingdom I have see amongst the another fashion for poor wife to die with their husband base sort of people this use and order that the man be dead he be carry to the place where they will make his sepulchre and set he as it be upright then come his wife before he on her knee cast her arm about his neck with embrace and clasp he un^ill such time as the mason have make a wall round about they and when the wall be as high as their neck there come a man behind the woman and strangle she then when she be dead the workman finish the wall over their head and so they lie bury both together in the year of our lord God 1567. for the ill success that the people of bezeneger have in that their city be sack by the four king the king with his court go to dwell in a castle eight day journey up in the land from bezeneger call Penegonde also six day journey from bezeneger be the place where they get diamond I be not there but it be tell i Penegonde that it be a great place compass with a wall and that they sell the earth within the wall for so much a squadron and the limit be set how deep or how low they shall dig those diamond that be of a certain size and big than that size be all for the king it be many year ago since they get any there for the trouble that have be in that kingdom the first cause of this trouble be because the son of this have put to death the lawful king which he have in prison for which cause the baron and nobleman in that kingdom will not acknowledge he to be their king and by this mean there be many king and great division in that kingdom and the city of bezeneger be not altogether destroy yet the house stand still but empty and there be dwell in they nothing as be report but tiger and other bezeneger 24. mile about wild beast the circuit of this city be four and twenty mile about and within the wall be certain mountain the house stand wall with earth and plain all save the three palace of the three tyrant brethren and the pagode which be idol house these be make with lime and fine marble I have see many king court and yet have I see none in greatness like to this of bezeneger I say for the order of his palace for it have nine gate or port first when you go into the place where the king do lodge there be five great port or gate these be keep with captain and soldier then within these there be four lesser gate which be keep with porter without the first gate there be a little porch where there be a captain with five and twenty soldier that keep watch and ward night and day and within that another with the like guard where thorough they come to a very fair court and at the end of that court there be another porch as the first with the like guard and within that another court. and in this wise be the first five gate guard and keep with those captain and then the lesser gate within be keep with a guard of porter which gate stand open the great part of the night because the custom of the gentile be to do their business and make their feast in the night rather than by day the city be very safe from thief for the Portugal merchant sleep in the street or under porch for the great heat which be there and yet they never have any ham in the night at the end of two month I determine to go for Goa in the company of two other Portugal merchant which be make ready to depart with two palanchine or little litt^rs which be very commodious for the way with eight Falchines which be man hire to carry the palanchine eight for a palanchine four at a time they carry they as we use to carry Barrowes and I buy i two bullock one of they to ride on and the other to carry my victual and provision for in that country man ride on bullock with panel as we man ride on bullock and ^^avell with they on the way te^me they girt and bridle and they have a very good commodious pace from bezeneger to Goa in summer it be eight day journey but we go in the midst of winter in the month of july and be fifteen day come to Ancola on the sea coast so in eight day I have lose my two bullock for he that carry my victual be weak and can not go the other when I come unto a river where be a little bridge to pass over I put my bullock to swim and in the midst of the river there be a little island unto the which my bullock go and find pasture there he remain still and in no wise we can come to he and so perforce I be force to leave he and at that time there be much rain and I be force to go seven day a foot with great pain and by great chance I meet with Falchines by the way who I hire to carry my clothes and victual we have great trouble in our journey for that every day we be take prisoner by reason of the great dissension in that kingdom and every morning at our departure we must pay four or five page a man and another trouble we have as bad as this that when as we come into a new governors country as every day we do although they be all tributary to the king of bezeneger yet every one of they stamp a several coin of copper so that the money that we take this day will not serve the next at length by the help of God we come safe to Ancola which be a country of the queen of Gargopam tributary to the king of bezeneger the merchandise that go every year from Goa to the merchandise that come in and out to bezeneger every year the apparel of those people bezeneger be arabian horse velvet damask and satin Armesine of Portugal and piece of China saffron and scarlet and from bezeneger they have in Turkey for their commodity jewel and pagody which be ducat of gold the apparel that they use in bezeneger be velvet satin damask Scarlet or white bombast cloth accord to the estate of the person with long hat on their head call Colae make of velvet satin damask or scarlet gird themselves in stead of girdle with some fine white bombast cloth they have breech after the order of the turk they wear on their foot plain high thing call of they Aspergh and at their ear they have hang great plenty of gold. return to my voyage when we be together in Ancola one of my companion that have nothing to lose take a guide and go to Goa whither they go in four day the other Portugal not be dispose to go tarry in Ancola for that winter the winter in those part of their winter be our summer the Indies begin the fifteen of May and last unto the end of October and as we be in Ancola there come another merchant of horse in a palanchine and two Portugal Soldier which come from Zeilan and two carrier of letter which be christians bear in the Indies all these consort to go to Goa together and I determine to go with they and cause a pallanchine to be make for i very poor of cane and in one of they cane I hide privy all the jewel I have and accord to the order I take eight Falchines to carry i and one day about eleven of the clock we set forward on our journey and about two of the clock in the afternoon as we pass a mountain which divide the territory of Ancola and Dialcan I be a little behind my company be assault by eight thief four of they have sword and target and the other four have bow and arrow when the Falchines that carry i understand the noise of the assaule they let the pallachine and i fall to the ground and run away and leave i alone with my clothes wrap about i present the thief be on my neck and rifle i they strip i stark naked and I feign myself ficke because I will not leave the pallanchine and I have make i a little bed of my clothes the thief seek it very narrow and subtle and find two purse that I have well bind up together wherein I have put my copper money which I have change for four pagody in Ancola the thief think it have be so many ducat of gold search no further then they throw all my clothes in a bush and hie they away and as God will have it at there departure there fall from they a handkerchief and when I see it I rise from my pallanchine or couch and take it up and wrap it together within my pallanchine then these my Falchines be of so good condition that they return to seek i whereas I think I shall not have find so much goodness in they because they be pay their money aforehand as be the use I have think to have see they no more before there come I be determine to pluck the cane wherein my jewel be hide out of my couch and to have make i a walk staff to carry in my hand to Goa think that I shall have go thither on foot but by the faithfulness of my Falchines I be rid of that trouble and so in four day they carry i to Goa in which time I make hard fare for the thief leave i neither money gold nor silver and that which I do eat be give i of my man for God sake and after at my come to Goa I pay they for every thing royal that I have of they from Goa I depart for cochin which be a voyage of three hundred mile and between these two city be many hold of the portugal as onor mangalor four small fort of the portugal barzelor and Cananor the hold or fort that you shall have from Goa and cochin that belong to the portugal be call onor which be in the kingdom of the queen of Bart^cella which be tributary to the king of bezeneger there be no trade there but only a charge with the captain and company he keep there and pass this place you shall come to another small castle of the portugal call mangalor and there be very small trade but only for a little rice and from thence you go to a little fort call barzelor there they have good store of rice which be carry to Goa and from thence you shall go to a city call Cananor which be a harquebus shoot distant from the chief city that the king of Cananor have in his kingdom be a king of the gentile and he and he be very naughty and malicious people always have delight to be in war with the portugal and when they be in peace it be for their interest to let their merchandise pass there go out of this kingdom of Cananor all the great store of pepper ginger honey ship lade with great nut great quantity of Archa which be a fruit of the bigness of nutmeg which fruit they eat in all those part of the Indies and beyond the Indies with the leaf of a herb which they call bettell the which be bettell be a very profitable herb in that country like unto our ivy leaf but a little lesser and thin they eat it make in plaster with the lime make of oistershel and through the Indies they spend great quantity of money in this composition and it be use daily which thing I will not have believe if I have not see it the customer get great profit by these herb for that they have custom for they when this people eat and chew this in their mouth it make their spittle to be red like unto blood and they say that it make a man to have a very good stomach and a very sweet breath but sure in my judgement they eat which be these the great store of silk that come from China and the great store of sugar which come from Bengala the marry citizen pay not any custom for these two commodity for all other commodity they pay four custom to the king of cochin rate their good at their own pleasure those which be not marry and stranger pay in cochin to the king of Portugal eight per of all manner of merchandise this king of cochin be of a small power in respect of the other king of the Indies for he can make but seventy thousand man of arm in his camp he have a great number of gentleman which he call Amochi and some be call Nairi these two sort of man esteem not their Amochi and Nairi life any thing so that it may be for the honour of their king they will thrust themselves forward in every danger although they know they shall die these man go naked from the girdle up ward with a cloth roll about their thigh go barefooted and have their hair very long and roll up together on the top of their head and always they carry their buckler or target with they and their sword naked these Nairi have their wife common amongst themselves and when any of they go into the house of any of these woman he leave his sword and target at the door and the time that he be there there dare not any be so hardy as to come into that house the king child shall not inherit the kingdom after their father because they hold this opinion that perchance they be not beget of the king their father but of some other man therefore they accept for their king one of the son of the king sister or of some other woman of the blood royal for that they be sure they be of the blood royal the and their wife use for a bravery to make great hole in their ear and so big and wide that it be incredible hold this opinion that the great the hole be the more huge huge ear noble they esteem themselves I have leave of one of they to measure the circumference of one of they with a thread and within that circumference I put my arm up to the shoulder clothe as it be so that in effect they be monstrous great thus they do make they when they be little for than they open the care and hang a piece of gold or lead thereat and within the open in the hole they put a certain leaf that they have for that purpose which make the hole so great the ship every year depart from cochin to go for Portugal on the five day of December note the and another year in another place of the same sea. when the time of this fish draw near than they send very good diverse that go to discover where the great heap of oyster be under water and right against that place where great store of oyster be there they make or plant a village with house and a Bazaro all of stone which stand as long as the fish time last and it be furnish with all thing great umber of they go out and anchor in fifteen or eighteen fathom of water which be the ordinary depth of all that coast. when they be at anchor they cast a rope into the sea and at the end of the ^ope they make fast a great stone and then there be ready a man that have his nose and his ear well stop and anoint with oil and a basket about his neck or under his left arm than he go down by the rope to the bottom of the sea and as fast as he can he fill the basket and when it be full he shake the rope and his fellow that be in the bark hale he up with the basket and in such wise they go one by one until they have lade their bark with oyster and at evening they come to the village and then every company make their mount or heap of oyster one distant from another in such wise that you shall see a great long row of mount or heap of oyster and they be not touch until such time as the fish be end and at the end of the fish every company sit round about their mount or heap of oyster and fall to open of they which they may easy do because they be dead dry and brittle and if every oyster have pearl in these pearl be prise accord to the carat which they weigh every carat be 4. grain and these man that prize they have a instrument of copper with hole in it which be make by degree for to sort the pearl withal manar they it will be a very good purchase but there be very many that have no pearl in they when the fish be end than they see whether it be a good gather or a bad there be certain expert in the pearl who they call which set and make the price of pearl accord to their carract beauty and goodness make four sort of they the first sort be the round pearl and they be call Aia of Portugal because the portugal do buy they the second sort which be not round be call Aia of Bengala the three sort which be not so good as the second they call Aia of Canara that be to say the kingdom of bezeneger the four and last sort which be the least and worst sort be call Aia of Cambaia thus the price be set there be merchant of every country which be ready with their money in their hand so that in few day all be buy up at the prize set accord to the goodness and carract of
