black elephant be he never so great and sure there be wonderful fair and great and some be nine cubit in height and they do report that the king have above five thousand elephant of war beside many other which be not teach to fight this king have a very large place wherein he take the wild elephant it stand about take of elephant a mile from Pegu build with a fair court within and be in a great grove or wood and there be many huntsman which go into the wilderness with she elephant for without the she they be not to be take and they be teach for that purpose and every hunter have five or six of they and they say that they anoint the she elephant with a certain ointment which when the wild elephant do smell he will not leave she when they have bring the wild elephant near unto the place they send word unto the town and many horseman and footman come out and cause the she elephant to enter into a straight way which do go to the palace and the she and he do run in for it be like a wood and when they be in the gate do shut afterwards they get out the female and when the male see that he be leave alone he weep and cry and run against the wall which be make of so strong tree that some of they do break their tooth with run against they then they prick he with sharp cane and cause he to go into a strait house and there they put a rope about his middle and about his foot and let he stand there three or four day without eat or drink and then they bring a female to he with meat and drink and within few day he become tame the chief force of use of they in battle the king be in these elephant and when they go into the war they set a frame of wood upon their back bind with great cord wherein sit four or six man which fight with gun bow and arrow dart and other weapon and they say that their skin be so thick that a pellet of a harquebusse will scarce pierce they except it be in some tender place their weapon be very bad they have gun but shoot very bad in they dart and sword short without point the king keep a very great state when he sit abroad as he do every day twice all his nobleman which they call shemme sit on each side a good distance off and a great guard king sit twice a day without they the court yard be very great if any man will speak with the king he be to kneel down to heave up his hand to his head and to put his head to the ground three time when he enter in the middle way and when he come near to the king and then he sit down and talk with the king if the king like well of he he sit near he within three or four pace if he think not well of he he sit further off when he go to war he go very strong at my be there he go to in the country of king power a city in siam siam with three hundred thousand man and five thousand elephant thirty thousand man be his guard. these people do eat root herb leave dog cat rat serpent and snake they refuse almost nothing when the king ride abroad he ride with a great guard and many nobleman oftentimes upon a elephant with a fine castle upon he very fair gild with gold and sometime upon a great frame like a hors-lite which have a little house upon this manner of carriage on man shoulder be use in Peru and in Florida it cover over head but open on the side which be all gild with gold and set with many ruby and saphire whereof he have infinite store in his country and be carry upon sixteen or eighteen man shoulder this coach in their language be call Serrion very great feast and triumph be many time before the king both of man and woman this king have little force by sea because he have but very few ship he have house full of gold and silver and bring in often but spend very little and have the mine of ruby and saphire and spinelle near unto the palace of the king there be a treasure wonderful rich the which because it be so near he do not account of it and it stand open for all man to see in a great wall court with two gate which be always open there be four house gild very rich and cover with lead in every one of they be Pagodes or image of huge stature and great value in the first be the picture of a king in huge idol gold with a crown of gold on his head full of great ruby and saphire and about he there stand four child of gold. in the second house be the picture of a man in silver wonderful great as high as a house his foot be as long as a man and he be make sat with a crown on his head very rich with stone in the three house be the picture of a man great than the other make of brass with a rich crown on his head in the four and last house do stand another make of brass great than the other with a crown also on his head very rich with stone in another court not far from this stand four other pagode or idol marvelous great of copper make in the same place where they do stand for they be so great that they be not to be remove they stand in four house gild very fair and be themselves gild all over save their head and they show like a black mortan their expense in gild of their image be wonderful the king have one wife and above three hundred concubine by which they say he have fourscore or fourscore and ten child he sit in judgement almost every day they use no speech but give up their supplication write in the leave of a tree paper of the long leaf of a tree with the point of a iron big than a bodkin these leave be a ell long and about two inch broad they be also double he which give in his supplication do stand in a place a little distance off with a present if his matter be like of the king accept of his present and grant his request if his suit be not like of he return with his present for the king will not take it in India there be few commodity which serve for Pegu except opium of Cambaia paint cloth of saint Thome or of Masulipatan and white cloth of Beng^la which be spend there in great quantity they bring thither also much cotton yarn red colour with a root which a excellent colour with a root call Saia they call Saia which will never lose his colour it be very well sell here and very much of it come yearly to Pegu. by your money you lose much the ship which come from Bengala saint Thome and Masulipatan come to the bar of Nigrais and to cosmin to Martavan a port of the sea in the kingdom of Pegu come many ship from malacca lade with sandall Porcelanes and other ware of China and with Camp^^r^ of borneo and pepper from Achen in sumatra to Cirion a port of Pegu come ship from Mecca with woollen cloth scarlet velvet woollen cloth and scarlet sell in Pegu. opium and such like there be in pegu eight broker who they call tareghe which be bind to sell your good at the price which they be worth and you give they for their labour two in the hundred and they be bind to make your debt good because you sell your merchandize upon their word if the broker pay you not at his day you may take he home and keep he in your house which be a great shame for he and if he pay you not present you may take his wife and child and his slave and bind they at your door and set they in the sun for that be the law of the country their current money in these part be a kind of brass the money of Pegu. which they call Gansa wherewith you may buy gold silver ruby musk and all other thing the gold and silver be merchandise and be worth sometime more and sometime less as other ware be this brazen money do go by a weight which they call a Biza^ and common this Biza after our account be worth about half a crown or somewhat less the merchandise which be in Pegu be gold silver ruby saphire spivell musk Benjamin or frankincense the several merchandize or Pegu. long pepper tin lead copper Lacca whereof they make hard wax Rice and wine make of Rice and some sugar the elephant do eat the sugar cane or else they will make very much and they consume many cane likewise in make of their varellae or idol temple which be in great number both great and small they be make round like a sugar lose some be as high as a the form of their temple or varellae church very broad beneath some a quarter of a mile in compass within they be all earth do about with stone they consume in these varellae great quantity of gold for that they be all gild aloft and many of they from the top to the bottom and every ten or twelve year they must be new gild because the rain consume off the gold for they stand open abroad if they do not consume their gold in these vanity it will be very plentiful and good cheap in Peg^ about two day journey from Pegu there be a Varelle or Pagode which be the pilgrimage of the pegues it be call d^go^ne and be of a wonderful bigness and all gild from the foot to the top and there be a house by it wherein the tallipoy which be their priest do the tallipoy or priest of Pegu. preach this house be five and fifty pace in length and have three pawn or walk in it and forty great pillar gild which stand between the walk and it be open on all side with a number of small pillar which be likewise gild it be gild with gold within and without beautiful temple there be house (@) round about for the pilgrim to lie in and many goodly house for the tallipoy to preach in which be full of image both of man and woman which be all gild over with gold. it be the fair place as I suppose that be in the world it stand very high and there be four way to it which all along be set with tree of first-fruit in such wise that a man may go in the shade above two mile in length and when their feast day be a man can hardly pass by water or by land for the great press of people for they come from all place of the solemn feast kingdom of Pegu thither at their feast in Pegu they have many tallipoy or priest which preach against all abuse many man resort unto they when they enter into their kiack that be to say their holy place or temple at the door there be a great larre of water with a cock or ladle in it and there they wash their foot and then they enter in and lift up their hand to their head first to their preacher and then to the sun and so sit down the tallipoy go very strange apparel with one Camboline the preach and apparel of the priest or thin cloth next to their body of a brown colour another of yellow double many time upon their shoulder and those two be gird to they with a broad girdle and they have a skin of leather hang on a string about their neck whereupon they sit bare head and bear foot for none of they wear shoe with their right arm bare and a great broad Sombrero or shadow in their hand to defend they in the summer from the sun and in the winter from the rain when the tallipoy or priest take their order first they go to school until they be twenty year old or more and then they come before a tallipoie appoint for that purpose who they call Rowli he be of the chief and most learned and he oppose Rowli or high priest. they and afterward examine they many time whether they will leave their friend and the company of all woman and take upon they the habit of a tallipoie if any be content than he ride upon a horse about the street very rich apparel with drum and pipe to show that he leave the riches of the world to be a tallipoie in few day after he be carry upon a thing like a horslitter which they call a serion upon ten or twelve man shoulder in the apparel of order how take a tallipoie with pipe and drum and many tallipoy with he and all his friend and so they go with he to his house which stand without the town and there they leave he every one of they have his house which be very little set upon six or eight post and they go up to they with a ladder of twelve or fourteen staff their house be for the most part by the high way side and among the tree and in the wood and they go with a great pot make house and beg of wood or fine earth and cover tie with a broad girdle upon their shoulder which come under their arm wherewith they go to beg their victual which they eat which be Rice fish and herb they demand nothing but come to the door and the people present do give they some one thing and some another and they put all together in their pot for they say they must eat of their alm and therewith content themselves they keep their feast by the moon and when it be new moon they keep their great feast and then the people send Rice observation of new moon and other thing to that kiack or church of which they be and there all the tallipoy do meet which be of that church and eat the victual which be send they when the tallipoy do preach many of the people carry they gift into the pulpit where they sit and preach and there be one which sit by they to take that which the people bring it be divide among they they have none other ceremony nor service that I can see but only preach I go from Peg^ to jamahey which be in the country of the langeiannes who we call jangome it be five and twenty day journey north-east from Pegu. in which journey I pass many fruitful and pleasant country the country be very low and have many fair river jamahey five and twenty day journey northeastward from Pegu. the house be very bad make of cane and cover with straw here be many wild buff and elephant jamahey be a very fair and great town with fair house of stone well people the street be very large the man very well set and strong with a cloth about they bare head and bear foot for in all these country they wear no shoe the woman be much fair than those of Pegu. here in all these country they have no wheat they make some cake of Rice hither to jamahey come many merchant out of China and bring great store of musk gold silver and many other thing of China work here be great store of victual they have such plenty that they will not milk the buffle as they do in all other place here be great store of copper and Benjamin in these country when the people be sick they make a vow to offer meat unto the devil if they escape and when they be recover they make a banquet with many pipe and drum and other instrument and dance all the night and their physic in the devil name friend come and bring gift fig arrecae and other fruit and with great dance and rejoice they offer to the devil and say they give the devil to eat and drive he out when they be dance and play they will cry and hallow very loud and in this sort they say they drive he away and when they be sick a tallipoie or two every night do sit by they and sing to please the devil that he shall not hurt they and if any die he be carry upon a great frame make like a tower with a cover all gild with gold make of cane carry with fourteen or sixteen man with drum and pipe and other instrument play before he to a place out of the town and there be burn he be accompany with all his friend and neighbour they burn (@) dead all man and they give to the tallipoy or priest many mat and cloth and then they return to the house and there make a feast for two day and then the wife with all the neighbour wife and her friend go to the place where he be burn and there they sit a certain time and cry and gather the piece of bone which be leave unburned and bury they and then return to their house and make a end of all mourn and the man and woman which be near of kin do shave their head which they do not use except it be for the death of a friend for they much esteem of their hair Caplan be the place where they find the ruby saphire and the spinelle it stand six Caplan be the place where the ruby and other precious stone be find day journey from Avarice in the kingdom of Pegu. there be many great high hill out of which they dig they none may go to the pit but only those which dig they in Pegu and in all the country of Avarice langeiannes siam and the Bramas the man wear bunch or little round ball in their privy member some of they we be two and some three they cut the skin and so put they in one into one side and another into the other side which they do when they be five and twenty or thirty year old and at their pleasure they take one or more of they out as they think good when they be marry the husband be for every child which his wife have to put in one until he come to three and then no more for they say the woman do desire they they be invent because they shall not abuse the male sex for in time past all those country be so give to that villainy that they be very scarce of people it be also ordain that the woman shall not have past three cubit of cloth in their neither clothes which they bind about they which be so straight that when they go in the street they show one side of the leg bear above the knee the bunch aforesaid Anthony Galuano write of these bals. captain Saris also and other be of diverse sort the least be as big as a little walnut and very round the great be as big as a little hen egg some be of brass and some of silver but those of silver be for the king and his nobleman these be gild and make with great cunning and ring like a little bell there be some make of lead which they call selwy because they ring but little and these be of lesser price for the poor sort the king sometime take his out and give they to his nobleman as a great gift and because he have use they they esteem they great they will put one in and heal up the place in seven or eight day the Bramas which be of the king country for the king be a brama have their leg or belly or some part of their body as they think good themselves make black with certain thing which they have they use to prick the skin and to put on it a kind of anile or black which do continue always and this be count a honour among they but none may have it but the Bramas which be of the king kindred these people wear no beard they pull out the hair on their face with little pinson make the people of Pegu wear no beard for that purpose some of they will let sixteen or twenty hair grow together some in one place of his face and some in another and pull out all the rest for he carry his pinson always with he to pull the hair out assoon as they appear if they see a man with a beard they wonder at he they have their tooth black both man and woman for they say a dog have his tooth white therefore they will black they the pegues if they have a suit in the law which be so doubtful that they can well determine trial of suit it put two long cane into the water where it be very deep and both the party go into the water by the pole and there sit man to judge and they both do dive under the water and he which remain long under the water do win the suit the ten of januarie I go from pegu to April be a other island among the janas where the woman travel and labour as our man do in England and the man keep house and go where they will the nine and twenty of march 1588. I return from malacca to Martavan and so to Pegu where I remain the second time until the seventeen of September and then I go to he return from malacca cosmin and there take ship and pass many danger by reason of contrary wind it please God that we arrive in Bengala in November follow where I stay for want of passage until the the three of February 1589. and then I ship myself for cochin in which Bengala voyage we endure great extremity for lack of fresh water for the weather be extreme hot and we be many merchant and passenger and we have very many calm and hot weather yet it please God that we arrive in ceylon the six of march where we stay five day to water and to furnish ourselves with other necessary provision this ceylon be a brave island ceylon very fruitful and fair but by reason of continual war with the king thereof all thing be very dear for he will not suffer any thing to be bring to the castle where the portugal be wherefore oftentimes they have great want of victual their provision of victual come out of Bengala every year the king be call Raia and be of great force for he come to Columbo which be the place where the portugal have their fort with a hundred thousand man and many elephant but they be naked people all of they yet many of they be good with their piece which be musket when the king talk with any man he stand upon one leg and set the other foot upon his knee with his sword in his hand it be not their order for the king to sit but to stand his apparel be a fine paint cloth make of cotton-wool about his middle his hair be long and bind up with a little fine cloth about his head all the rest of his body be naked his guard be a thousand man which stand round about he and he in the middle and when he march many of they go before he and the rest come after he they be of the race of the chingalaye which they say be the best kind of all the malabar their ear be very large for the great they be the more honourable they be large ear account some of they be a span long the wood which they burn be cinnamon wood and it smell very sweet there be great store of ruby saphire and spinelle in this island gem the best kind of all be here but the king will not suffer the inhabitant to dig for they lest his enemy shall know of they and make war against he and so drive he out of his country for they they have no horse in all the country NIcholas Pimenta the indian visitor in his letter to Claudius the general of the Jesuit relate his visitation-voyage from Goa in December 1597. n. letter to cochin first the occurrent wherein he have certify by letter in the viceroy ship or carrack which be rich lade be accidental and irrecoverable Carrick burn fire the ordnance thunder death and lightning manifold mischief to the rescuer he send from cochin a mission to Bengala Francis Fernandes and Dominicke another to Pegu Melchior Fonsera and Andrew the effect whereof appear in their letter Fernandes write from siripur in Bengala in januarie 1599 letter of Francis Fernandes the danger of their voyage by malabar pirate a three day tempest the shelf of Ganges before they arrive at G^llum two hundred and ten mile up that river where they leave one of their society which can mean write to teach that school endeavour to learn the Bengalan language and translate into it a tractate of christian religion in which be confute the gentile and mahometan error to which be add a short catechism by way of dialogue which the child frequent the school learn by heart and teach the servant in their family with the sign of the cross and other thing belong to Christianity they persuade they to erect a hospital buy a house and householdstuff to that purpose and reform the course of many which live in piracy and loose lust and in October depart thence to the great port six hundred mile from the small port or Porto Pequeno not without danger from tiger and thief in the midway in the kingdom of Chandecan Chandecan where they stay a month to reform disorder by lust and discord and baptize two hundred the king give they a place to build a church in and money to that purpose with liberty to preach the gospel in the wood of sometime more sometime less as there be soldier and sailor to be find when they go out they be but light lade only with certain pipe of wine and oil and some small quantity of merchandise other thing they have not in but ballast and victual for the company for that the most and great ware that be send into India be rial of eight because the principal factor for pepper do every year send a great quantity of money wherewith to buy pepper as also diverse particular merchant as be the least ware that man can carry into India for that in these rial of eight they gain at the least forty when the ship be out of the river and enter into the sea all their man be muster as well sailor as soldier and such as be find absent and leave on land be register in the book be mark by the purser that at their return they may talk with their surety for that every man put in surety and the good of such as be absent be find in the ship be present bring forth and prise and a inventory be make it be leave to be dispose at the captain pleasure the like be do with their good that die in the ship but little of it come to the owner hand imbesele and privy make away the master and pilot have for their whole voyage forth and home again each man a hundred and twenty milreye every milrey be worth in dutch money seven gilder and receive before hand each man four and twenty milreye beside that they have and other person which sail in the ship which have for their portion every day in victual each man alike as well the great as the least a pound and three quarter of biscuit half a can of wine a can of water a which be 32. pound of salt flesh the month some dry fish onion and garleeke be eat in the begin of the voyage as be of small value other provision as sugar honey raisins prune Rice and such like be keep for those which be sick yet they get but little thereof for that the officer keep it for themselves and spend it at their pleasure nor let much go out of their finger as for the dress of their meat weed Pots and pannes every man must make his own provision beside all this there be a clerk and steward for the king soldier that have their part by themselves as the sailor have this be the order and manner of their voyage when they sail unto the but when they return again they have no more but each man a portion of biscuit and water until they come to the cape Bona and from thence home they must make their own provision the soldier that be passenger have nothing else but free passage that be room for a chest under hatch and a place for their bed in the orloope and may not come away without the viceroy passport and yet they must have be five year soldier in the Indies before they can have licence but the slave must pay fraught for their body and custom to the king. the one and twenty of September we enter the river into the road under the land of bard of the town and island of Goa chief city of India the city of Goa be the metropolitan or chief city of all the oriental Indies where the chap. 28. portugal have their traffic where also the viceroy the archbishop the king counsel and chancery have their residence and from thence be all place in the oriental Indies govern and rule there be likewise the staple for all indian commodity whither all sort of merchant do resort come thither both to buy and sell and out of Arabia Armenia Persia Cambaia Bengala Pegu Sian malacca java Molucca China etc. the city and island of Goa lie under 15. degree on the north side and be distant from the equinoctial by the way that the portugal ship do come thither from Mossambique four hundred mile it be a island whole compass about with a river and be above three mile great it lie within the coast of the firm land so that the island with the sea coast of the firm land do both reach as far each as other into the sea. it be only separate from the firm land by a arm of the sea or of the river that run in by the north side of the town and so round about the island to the south side where it enter again into the sea and be in form almost like a halfmoon the river run even unto the town and be indifferent broad there be between the firm land and the island certain small land that be all inhabit by the natural bear countryman and on the other side of the town the river be there so small that in summer time by wade to the knee in water a man may pass it over on foot on the which side the island have a wall with certain bulwark which the portugal of late year have cause to be make to defend they from the firm land in time of war as it often happen for it have diverse time be besiege by Dialcan or Hidalca^ at the mouth and the entry of the river on the north side lie the land of bard which be high land under which land the portugal do anchor safe out of all danger and there they have a place to lade and unlade their ware this land of bard be also under the Portugal subjection and be full of village inhabit with people bard canarijn that be of the firm land lie above it call canarijn who for the most part be christians but observe their own manner of apparel which be to go all naked their privy member only cover this land be full of indian palm tree whereon the indian nut call do grow as also all the other land lie in the river this island of bard be separate from the firm land by a small river which be so little that it can almost be discern from the firm land. on the south side off the island of Goa where the river run again into the sea there come even out with the coast a land call Salsette which be also under the subjection of Salsette the portugal and be inhabit and plant both with people and fruit like the land of bard and be likewise part with a little river from the firm land. between this land of Salsette and the island of Goa he also some small land all full of indian palmetree and by the mouth or issue of the river lie a island which be call Goa ve^^a that be old Goa from whence there come no special thing neither be it much inhabit those land of bard and Salsette be by the king of Portugal let out to farm and the rent thereof be employ to the payment of the archbishop cloister priest and other the king officer yearly stipend which be grant they by special privilege and patent from the king. the island be very hilly and in some place so desert and rough that on some side man can hardly travel over land but with great labour to the town of Goa the island even to the sea side be full of village and inhabit by the canarijn which be the natural bear people of the land and do altogether line by work upon the land and by their palm tree the village and dwelling of these canarijn be most round about the island and on the water side or by small lake whereof there be some few within the island and the cause why they dwell thus be for that the palm tree will not grow in any other place but on low ground by the water special in sandy ground so that there be no palm tree to be find on the high land within the country unless it be upon sandy ground on the sea coast or river side on the east side of the town of Goa upward into the river about three mile from the town of bard lie a place where the portugal ship do anchor the river have some creek and a ship of two hundred ton or there abouts may easy discharge before the town but the portugal great ship must discharge themselves at bard which be do they may if they will free go and l^e before the town the town be well build with fair house and street after the Portugal manner but because of the heat they be somewhat low they common have their garden and orchard at the backside of their house full of all kind of indian first-fruit as also the whole island through they have many pleasant garden and farm with house to play in and tree of indian first-fruit whether they go to sport themselves and wherein the indian woman take great delight the town have in it all sort of cloister and church as Lisb^^ have only it want nun for the man can get the woman to travel so far where they shall be shut up and forsake Venus tothe the portugal justice and ordinance as well in worldly as spiritual cause they be all one as they be in Portugal they dwell in the town among all sor^s of nation as Indian heathen moor jew armenians gusarate Benianes Bramenes and of all indian nation and people which do all dwell and traffic therein every man hold his own religion without constrain any man to do against his conscience only touch their ceremony of burn the dead and the live of marry and other supperstion and devilish invention (@) they be forbid by the archbishop to use they open or in the island but they may free use they upon the firm land and secret in their house thereby to shun and avoid all occasion of dislike that may be give to christian which be but new baptize but touch the worldly policy or good government of the country and execute of justice as also for the rule of the townsman in the city it be common to they all and they be under the portugal law and he that be once christen and be after find to use any heathenish superstition be subject to the inquisition whatsoever he be or for any point of religion whatsoever inquisition the island have nothing of itself to nourish it withal but only some cattle hen goat dove etc. but very few because of the barrenness and evil situation of the place which be a most hilly barren and wild country and full of waste ground all their necessary as beast hen hog egg milk etc. come from Salsette and bard but most part out of the firm land corn Rice and other grain also oil and all other necessary come from other country and be bring in by the river as from Cambaia on the north side and from the coast of malabar and other place as in the description of the coast we have in part declare of wine call wine of palm tree they have enough and so much that they have to spare for other place they have but little fresh water but only one well call Banga^ijn which stand about a quarter of a mile without the city wherewith the whole town be serve which the slave fetch in pot and sell it in the town and be very good to drink for water to dress meat wash and do other thing withal they common have well within their house the land of itself be very stony and dry have a kind of red earth so that some italian alchemist have promise to get copper and gold out of the same which neither the king nor viceroy will ever consent unto fear lest the report of such treasure will be occasion of great mine dangerous trouble the portugal in India be many of they marry with the natural bear woman of the country chap. 29. of the custom of the portugal and such as be issue from they call Mesticos or half countryman as well of Goa as of all the oriental country and the child proceed of they be call Mesticos that be half-countriman these Mesticos be common of yellowish colour notwithstanding there be many woman among they that be fair and well form the child of the portugal both boy and girl which be bear in India be call Casticos and be in all thing like unto the portugal only somewhat differ in colour for they draw towards a yellow colour the child of those castico be yellow and altogether like the mesticos and the child of Mesticos be of colour and fashion like the natural bear countryman or decanijn of the country so that the posterity of the portugal both man and woman be in the three degree do seem to be natural Indian both in colour and fashion their living and daily traffic be to Bengala Pegu malacca Cambaia China and every way both north and south also in Goa there be hold a daily assembly or meeting together as well of the citizen and inhabitant as of all nation throughout India and of the country border on the same which be like the meeting upon the burse in Antwerp yet differ much from that for that hither in Goa there come as well gentleman as merchant and other and there be all kind of indian commodity to sell so that in a manner it be like a fair this meeting be only before noon every day in the year except sunday and holiday it begin in the morning at seven of the clock and continue till nine of the clock but not in the heat of the day nor after noon in the principal street of the city name the straight street and be call the Leylon which be as much to say as a outroop there be certain crier appoint by the city for the purpose which have of all thing to be cry and sell these go all the time of the Leylon or outroop all behangd about with all sort of gold chain all kind of costly jewel pearl ring and precious stone likewise they have run about they many sort of captive and slave both man and woman young and old which be daily sell there as beast be sell with we where every one may choose which like he best every one at a certain price there be also arabian horse all kind of spice and dry drug sweet gum and such like thing fine and costly coverlet and many curious thing out of Cambaia sinde Bengala China etc. and it be wonderful to see in what sort many of they get their living which every day come thither to buy ware and at another time sell they again and when any man die all his good be bring thither and sell to the last pennyworth in the same outroop whosoever they be yea although they be the viceroy good and this be do to do right and justice unto orphan and widow and that it may be sell with the first where every man may see it so that every year there be great quantity of ware sell within that city for that there die many man within the town by mean of their disorder live together with the hotness of the country the like assembly be hold in all place of India where the portugal inhabit there be some marry portugal that get their living by their slave both man and woman whereof some have 12. some 20. and some 30. for it co they but little to keep they these slave for money do labour for such as have need of their help some fetch fresh water and sell it for money about the street the woman slave make all sort of confecture and conserve of indian first-fruit much fine needlework both cut and wrought work and then their master send the fair and the young of they well dress up with their ware about the street to sell the same that by the neatness and beauty of the say woman slave man may be move to buy which happen more for the affection they have to the slave and to fulfil their pleasure with they then for any desire to the conserve or needle-worke for these slave do never refuse they but make their daily live thereby and with the gain that they by that mean bring home their master may well keep and maintain they there be other that use exchange of money and to buy money when it come as time serve to sell it again for they buy the rial of eight when the ship come from Portugal whereof some buy at the least ten or twelve hundred and keep they till the month of April which be the time when the ship sail to China for then be the rial of eight seek for to carry thither and be common worth five and twenty or thirty in the hundred profit and then they receive for they a certain money which at the same time be bring from Ormus call larrijn that come out of Persia which they buy for eight or ten in the hundred profit and keep they till the portugal on the month of September come thither and so deliver they again for twenty or five and twenty in the hundred profit in exchange for rial of eight as I say before for they must have these larrijn with they to cochin to buy pepper and other ware for that it be the best and most profitable money there be yet other sort of money call pagoda venetianer and Santhones which be gold all which they do likewise buy and sell so that there be many that do nothing else and become rich special he that have a good stock this exchange come most common from the spiritualty who do secret use it by other man mean without any let or hindrance some there be that live upon their rent which they have by their palm tree there be among they but two manner of people that be marry man and soldier for that all young man unmarried be name soldier which be the best name that a man can have not that the soldier be any way bind or under the commandment and regiment of any captain which throughout India be not use but when the portugal come into India out of Portugal and be arrive there every man go where he think best although in Portugal every man name that go in the ship be write and register which be do in this sort every man be write up both his name and surname with a note what pay they receive of the king whereof some bear the title of Fidalgo da Caza Rey Senor that be a gentleman of the king house which be the chief title there be other name Mozos Fidalgos which be also a honourable title and they be common gentleman son or by the king favour advance thereunto there be yet other that be name Cavalhiero Fidalgo which be not so much as the other two yet it be a honourable title and be the title of a knight who for some valiant act by he do be make knight which they do for a small matter for that if he do any act to be account of or be in a manner of such a action do present he be of a captain or a gentleman make a knight whereof they much boast themselves and it be now grow so common among they that very cook boy and other as mean as they be make knight there be other also that be name Mosos da camara do do Seruico which be servant to the king some of his chamber some of his account and some for his service this be the first title or degree of credit whereby through their good service they attain unto better and be more glorious of their title then of all the riches in the world there be also that be name Escuderos Fidalgos that be esquire which be likewise a degree of credit other be name which be man of honour and the poor among they which be not name by any title be set down for soldier which be the common and rascal sort these be every man pay their wage accord to their title and may each man in his quality by long service or some good action but most by favour rise to high degree for that accord to their title their service be reward the portugal which sail for India be thus register and write down the say register at their arrival there be deliver to be keep by one of the king officer thereunto appoint which every three year be likewise change as other officer be and be call the chief clerk of the Matricola general the portugal mestico and christian keep worshipful and bountiful house have common as it be say before five six ten twenty some more some less slave both chap. 30. of the portugal and mestico their house courtesy narriage and other custom and manner of India man and woman in their house every man accord to his estate and quality I mean marry man they be very clean and sweet in all thing belong to their house special in their linen for that every day they change shirt and smock both man and woman and their slave and servant likewise with other thing that they wear which they do because of the great heat in that land. the portugal be common serve with great gravity without any difference between the gentleman and the common citizen townsman or soldier and in their go courtesy and conversation common in all thing when they go in the street they step very soft and slow forward with a great pride and vainglorious majesty with a slave that carry a great hat or veil over their head to keep the sun and rain from they also when it rain they common have a boy that bear a cloak of scarlet or of some other cloth after they to cast over they and if be before noon he carry a cushion for his master to kneel on when he hear mass and their rapier be most common carry after they by a boy that it may not trouble they as they walk nor hinder their gravity when they meet in the street a good space before they come together they begin with a great maos to stoop with their body and to thrust forth their foot to salute each other with their hat in their hand almost touch the ground likewise when they come into the church where they have stool ready which their slave have prepare for they all that be by he that come in do stand up and with the same manner of bow their body do he great reverence and if it chance that any do he reverence as the manner be and that he to who it be do do not great esteem thereof so that he do he not the like courtesy they do altogether for that cause go after he and cut his hat in piece say that he have disgrace the party wherein it be not for they to ask wherefore they shall so do for it will be the great shame and reproach in the world unto they if they shall not revenge so great a injury and when they seek to be revenge of any man that have show they discourtesy or for any other cause whatsoever it be they assemble ten or twelve of their friend acquaintance or companion and take he wheresoever they find he and beat he so long together that they leave he for dead or very near dead or else cause he to be stab by their slave but if they desire not to kill he they baste he well about the rib and all his body over with a thick reed as big as a man leg which be call Bambus whereby for eight day after and more he have enough to do to keep his bed and sometime in that manner they leave he for dead this be their common custom and be never look unto or once correct also they use long bag of full of sand wherewith they will give such blow each upon other that therewith they will break each other limb and for ever after make they lame when any man go to visit another in his house although he which be visit be one of the principal gentleman of the city and the visitor but a simple soldier or some other man it be the manner that he which be visit come unto the door of his house with his hat in his hand and with great courtesy to receive he that come to visit he and so lead he up into his hall or chamber wherein he will speak with he where he offer he a chair to sit down and then he himself sit by he than he ask he what he will have which have understand he bring he down again to the door in the like sort and so with a bid he farewell and if he shall not do so or when he give he a stool shall give he one unline or one that be less or low then that he take for himself he that visit he will take it in evil part esteem it a great scorn and seek to be revenge on he for the same when they have any wedding and be marry whosoever they be if they have any wealth all the friend and neighbour come together every man on horseback and he that have not a horse will borrow one and be every man very co^^ly apparel at the least some fifty or a hundred horse little more or less as the person be of quality and so they ride altogether in good order unto the church with their servant and every man his hat for the sun the parent and friend in the hinder part and in the last row the bridegroom between two of they who they call gossip after they follow the bride between two Commeres each in their Pallamkin which be most costly make and after follow the slave both man and woman go in troop as if they run to hunt and so come to the church and be marry accord to the order use in the church of Rome they be in the same order bring home again and pass through the street the neighbour lean upon indian carpet look out of the window and throw Rose water upon the bride and bridegroom and other sweet smell water with rose and Sugar comfit or corne. in the mean time their slave play upon shawm and trumpet most pleasant and melodious to hear and come to the house where the bride and bridegroom dwell with great reverence and courtesy bow down their body they take their leaf of all the company which be all on horseback about the door and so the bride the bridegroom and the Commeres go up and sit with great gravity in a window and then begin the horseman that lead they to church in honour of the marry couple one after the other to run a course the gossip beginning first and the rest follow twice or thrice one after the other with continual play on shawm which be very common in India for that he which be of any wealth have they of his own within his house this be end they all pass before the window where the bride and bridegroom sit with a great reverence and so pass on all save the gossip for they go up to the bride and bridegroom and bid God give they ^oy then be there some comfit and marchpane bring forth to drink a cup of water withal and after some courteous salutation and congratulations to the new marry couple they take their leaf and depart so there remain with the bride and bridegroom but three or four of their near friend and kinsman for who there be a dinner prepare with little meat yet very costly which they pass over very light and not many word which do they present bring the bride to bed without any other ceremony or charge wherewith the marriage be do and end oftentimes it chance that they go to bed at the least two hour before sunsetting not have the patience to stay so long as we do in these country when a child be to be christen it be likewise in the same sort lead to church with horse and last of all come the father alone after who follow two man on foot the one with a great silver or gild vessel full of bread bake like crackling which in Portugal be call Rosquilhos and in the middle a great wax candle well make and gild thrust through with some piece of money of gold and silver for a offer to the priest that baptise the child and all over strew and cover with rose the other carry a great silver or gild saltseller in one of his hand and a lamp of the same stuff in his other hand each with rich and costly towel on their shoulder after that follow two pallamkin on the one side the on the other side the midwife with the child cover with a costly mantle make for the purpose and so the ceremony of baptism be end in the church it be again in the like sort bring home and be there they have the like manner of music and shawm run and leap with their horse before the window where the sit with the same ceremony as at the wedding this be the manner and custom of those that be marry and keep house but concern the soldier that be unmarried thus it be they go in the summer time into the armado lie on the water and be within the town and on the land they be very stately apparel and go very grave along the street with their slave or man hire for the purpose that bear a hat over they for the sun and rain for there be many Indian that be daily hire fort he purpose and have twelve Basarucos the day which be as much as two stivers or a stoter and they serve such as have no slave and that will not keep any to that end the soldier dwell at least ten or twelve in a house where they have among they a slay or hire indian or two which serve they and wash their shirt and have four or five beggarly pride stool with a table and every man a bed. their meat be Rice sod in water with some salt fish or some other thing of small value without bread and clear fountain water for their drink wherewith they be well please they have amongst they all one or two good suit of apparel all of silk as the manner be there and when one go abroad the other stay at home for in the house they have no need of clothes but sit whosoever they be in their shirt and a pair of linen breeches and so as it be naked by reason of the great heat for if some of they have occasion to go out twenty time in one day they must so often lend he their apparel and he must likewise put off his clothes as often as he come home again some soldier have a gentleman or captain to their friend which dare they money to apparel themselves withal to the end when summer time come they may be ready to go with they in fleet to sea as also to have their friendship by night and at other time to bear they company or to help they to be revenge of any injury by they receive as I say before for that he which in India have most soldier to his friend be most regard and fear so that to be short in this manner they do maintain themselves in common whereby they be able to come in presence of the best of the country many and most of they have their chief maintenance from the portugal and mestico wife as also the indian christian wife which do always bestow liberal reward and gift upon they to fulfil their unchaste and filthy desire which they know very well how to accomplish and secret bring to pass there be some likewise that get their live by their friend travel for they from place to place with some ware and merchandize and they be call chattijn these do give over and leave the office of a soldier in the fleet and the king service and now likewise they be all give to scrape and catch as well the viceroy governor and other as also the churchman and spiritualty little pass or esteem the common profit or the service of the king but only their particular profit make their account that the time of their abode be but three year wherefore they say they will not do otherwise then those that be before they do but say that other which come after they shall take care for all for that the king say they give they their office thereby to pay they for their service in time past the portugal mestico and indian-christian woman in India be little see abroad but chap. 31. of the manuer and custom of Portugal and mestico woman in India for the most part sit still within the house and go but seldom forth unless it be to church or to visit their friend which be likewise but very little and when they go abroad they be well provide not to be see for they be carry in a Pallamkin cover with a Mat or other cloth so that they can be see when they go to church or to visit any friend they put on very costly apparel with bracelet of gold and ring upon their arm all beset with costly jewel and pearl and at their ear hang lace full of jewel their clothes be of damask velvet and cloth of gold for silk be their pride the worst thing they do wear within the house they go bare head with a waistcoat call Baiu that from their shoulder cover their navel and be so fine that you may see all their body through it and downward they have nothing but a paint cloth wrap three or four time about their body these clothes be very fair some of they be very costly wrought with loome-worke and diverse figure and flower of all colour all the rest of the body be naked without any hose but only barefooted in a pair of moile or pantofle and the man in like sort this be their manner in the house both old and young rich and poor none except for they go forth but very little and then they be both cover and carry and what they need abroad that the slave both man and woman do fetch in the woman their feed eat no bread or very little nor yet the slave not that they refuse it for the dearness or want of bread for they have enough and great abundance but they be so use to eat rice that they desire no other which they see with water and eat it with some salt fish or a kind of salt fruit call Mangas or with some other composition both of fish and flesh with pottage which they pour upon it and so eat it with their hand for there they eat nothing with spoon and if they shall see any man do so they will laugh at he when they drink they have certain pot make of black earth very fine and thin much like those that we use in Holland for flower-pot have in the neck thereof a partition full of hole with a spout and these cruse be call Gorgoletta to this end that when they drink they may hold the pot on high and touch it not with their mouth but the water run from the spout fall into their mouth never spill drop which they do for cleanliness because no man shall put it to his mouth and when any man come out of Portugal and then begin to drink after their manner because he be not use to that kind of drink he spill it in his bosom wherein they take great pleasure and laugh at he call he Reynol which be a name give in jest to such as new come from Portugal and know not how to behave themselves in such grave manner and with such ceremony as the portugal use there in India so that at the first they be much whoop and cry at in the street until by use and practice they have learn the indian manner which they quick do the man be very jealous of their wife for they jealousy will never bring any man into their house how special a friend soever he be that shall see their wife or their daughter unless it be some gossip or other marry man with his wife in company when they will go together to some place to sport and solace themselves they be always well guard by their slave both man and woman both for their safety and service if any man come to the door to ask for the master of the house present their wife and their daughter run to hide they and so leave the man to answer he that stand at the door likewise they suffer no man to dwell within their house where the woman and daughter be how near kinsman sooner he be unto they be once fifteen year of age nor their own son but have certain chamber and place beneath or beside their house where they lie and may in no sort come among the woman and thither they send they their meat and other provision for it have oftentimes be see in those country that the nephew have lie by his aunt and the brother by the brother wife and the brother with his sister whereof I have know some that have be take with the manner and that both they and the woman have be slay by the husband the woman be very luxurious and unchaste luxury and filthy lusts. for there be very few among they although they be marry but they have beside their husband one or two of those that be call soldier with who they take their pleasure which to effect they use all the slight and practice they can devise by send out their slave and bawd by night and at extraordinary time over wall hedges and ditch how narrow soever they be keep and look unto they have likewise a herb call Deutroa Deutroa which bear a seed whereof bruise out the sap they put it into a cup or other vessel and give it to their husband either in meat or drink and present therewith the man be as though he be half out of his wit and without feeling or else drink do nothing but laugh and sometime it take he sleep whereby he lie like a dead man so that in his presence they may do what they will and take their pleasure with their friend and the husband never know of it in which sort he continue four and twenty hour long but if they wash his foot with cold water he present revive and know nothing thereof but think he have sleep there be many man poison by their wife if once they be move for they know how cunning poisoner to make a certain poison or venom which shall kill the person that drink it at what time or hour it please they which poison be prepare they make it in such sort that it will lie six year in a man body and never do he hurt and then kill he without miss half a hour time they make it also for one two or three year month or day as it please they best as I have see it in many and there it be very common there be likewise many woman bring to their end by mean of their husband and slay when soever they take they in adultery or that they do but once suspect they which if they do present they cut their throat and bring three or four witness to testify that strange man enter into their house by night at unaccustomed time or else by day and have their pleasure of their wife or in other sort as they will devise it whereby they be present discharge of the crime accord to the law and ordinance both of Spain and Portugal and present may marry with another wife this notwithstanding be no mean to make the woman fear or once to leave their filthy pleasure although there be every year many woman without number so dispatch and make away by their husband and it be so common with they that no man think it strange or once wonder thereat because of the custom the woman also for their part say and flat affirm that there can be no better death then to die in that manner say that so they be sacrifice for love which they think to be a great honour unto they the woman be by nature very clean and neat as well in their house as in apparel for that although all whatsoever she put on her body every day be both white clean and neatness fresh yet they have a manner every day to wash themselves all the body over from head to foot and sometime twice a day in the morning and at evening and as often as they ease themselves or make water or else use the company of their husband every time they do wash themselves be it a hundred time a day and a night they be no great worker but idleness and costliness much delight in sweet herb and in perfume and frankincense and to rub their body and their forehead with sweet sanders and such like wood which with water they do steep or break in piece also the whole day long they do nothing but sit and chaw leave or herb call bettele with chalk and a certain fruit call Arrequa whereof in another place among fruit and herb I will speak more this Arrequa some of it be so strong that bettele and Arrequa it make man almost drink and whole out of sense although in show and in taste it be almost like wood or rootes these three thing they sit all the whole day chaw in their mouth like ox or cow chaw the cud they let the sap go down into their throat and spit the rest out of their mouth whereby they make their mouth so red and blackish that to such as know it not it be strange to see all which with their wash frankincense and rub with sanders they have learn and receive of the indian heathen which have have those custom of long time and yet till this day use they they say it preserve the tooth and keep they sound good for the maw and against a stink mouth and evil breath insomuch as they be so use to chaw it that wheresoever they go or stand they must always have of those leave carry with they and the woman slave do likewise go always chaw and be so use thereunto that they very think that without it they can not live for their common work be to sit all day when their husband be out of door behind the Mat which hang at the window always chaw the herb Bettele see those that pass by in the street and no man see they but as any man pass by which like they and they will let they have a sight they lift up the Mat whereby they do the passenger a great favour and with that manner of show themselves and cast look they make their beginning of love which by their slavish woman they bring to effect to the which end they have all devilish device that possible may be invent for that both night and day they do practice nothing else but make it their only work and to make nature more lively to abound and move they thereunto they do use to eat those Betteles and Chaulke and in the night it stand by their bed side this they eat whole handful of clove pepper ginger and a bake kind of meat call chachunde which be mix and make of all kind of spice and herb and such like meat all to increase their lechery and they be not content therewith but give their husband a thousand herb for the same purpose to eat they not know thereof thereby to fulfil their pleasure and to satisfy their desire which can not by any mean be satisfy they be likewise much use to take their pleasure in bath by swim therein which they can very well do for there be very few of they but they will easy swim over a river of half a mile broad every three year there be a new viceroy send into India and sometime they stay long as it please the king but very few of they he continue in Goa in the hall of his palace chap. 32. of the viceroy of Portugal and of his government in India stand the guard and in the great hall where his council sit be paint all the viceroy that have govern in India since the first discovery and conquest thereof and as they new come their picture be likewise place there these viceroy have great revenue they may spend give and keep the king treasure which be very much and do with it what please they for it be in their choice have full and absolute power from the king in such sort that they gather and hoard up a mighty quantity of treasure for that beside their great allowance from the king they have great present and gift bestow upon they for it be the custom in those country when any viceroy come new over that all the king border about Goa and that have peace and friendship with the portugal do then send their ambassador unto he to confirm their league with great and rich present therewith likewise to bid the viceroy welcome which amount to a great mass of treasure these present in this sort give the Jesuit by their practice have obtain of the king and for a time enjoy they at Jesuit go to the world end for the world their pleasure look very narrow unto they that they may not be deceive until long time since a viceroy name don taide earl of Atougia come thither and refuse to let they have they say that the king be in Portugal know not what be give he in India and that those present be give unto the viceroy and not to the king and say the king have no power to give they to the Jesuit so that he keep they for himself which the Jesuit take in evil part and say the viceroy be a heretic yet from his time ever since Jesuit heresy and ter. the viceroy have use to keep they for themselves they say and it be find to be most true that the first year of the viceroy time he have enough to do to repair and furnish his house and to know the manner and custom of the country without any further trouble of himself the second year to gather treasure and to look unto his particular profit for the which cause he come into India the three and last year to prepare himself and set all thing in order that he be not overtake or surprise by the new viceroy when he come but that he may return into Portugal with the good which he have scrape together the same be to be understand of all the captain in the fort and of all other officer in India in the town and island of Goa be resident many heathen moor which be Mahumetans chap. 33. of the heathen Indian and other stranger dwell in Goa variety of religion of their religion see more at large in my pilgrimag lib. 5. Jew and all strange nation border thereabout every one of they use several custom and superstion in religion the moor eat all thing except swine flesh and die be bury like the jew but the heathen as decanijn gusarate and Canaras and other Indian be dead be burn to ash and some woman be alive be burn with they such as be gentleman or nobleman and the wife of the Bramenes which be their idolatrous priest also for the merchant some of they eat all thing except cow or buffle flesh which they esteem to be holy. other eat not any thing whatsoever that have either life or blood in it as those of Gusarata and the banianes of Cambaia which observe Pythagoras law most of they pray unto the sun and moon yet they do all acknowledge a god that make create and rule all thing and that after this life there be another wherein man shall be reward accord to their work but they have idol and image which they ugly idol and idolatry more ugly call pagode cut and form most ugly and like monstrous devil to who daily they offer and say that those holy man have be live among they whereof they tell so many miracle as it be wonderful and say that they be intercessor between they and god. the devil oftentimes answer they out of those image who they likewise know and do he oracle great honour by offer unto he to keeph friendship with he and that he shall not hurt they they have a custom when any maid be to be marry and that they will honour their pagode for the more credit to the bridegroom they bring the bride with great triumph and music before their pagode which be make with a pin of ivory bone to who the near devilish custom for bride friend and kinswoman of the bride together with the bride do go and by force make the image to take the bride maidenhead so that the blood remain still upon the image for a remembrance thereof and then after other devilish superstition and ceremony have make their offering they bring the bride home where she be deliver to the bridegroom he be very joyful and proud that their pagode have honour he so much and call he of so hog-god much labour they have for the most part a custom to pray unto the first thing they meet withal in the morning and all that day after they pray unto it be it hog or any other thing and if in the morning they go out they chance at the first sight to see a crow whereof there be great number in India they will not go forth of their door all that day no not for all the good in the world for they esteem it a evil sign and a unlucky day they pray likewise to the new moon and when she first appear they fall upon their knee and salute she with great devotion there be among they certain people call jogos which be such as we jogue friar or hermit call hermit and those do they esteem for holy man these man live a very strict life with great abstinence and make the common people believe many strange thing they have likewise many soothsayer and witch which use juggle and travel through the out country have about they many live snake which they know how to bewitch and be shut up in little basket they pull they out and make they dance turn and wind at the sound of a certain instrument whereon they play and speak unto they they wind they about their neck arm and leg kiss they with a thousand other device only to get money they be all for the most part very skilful in prepare of poison wherewith they do many strange thing and easy poison each other their dwelling and house be very little and low cover with straw without window and very low and narrow door so that a man must almost creep upon his knee to go in their householdstuff be mat of straw both to sit and homely householdstuff lie upon their table table-clothe and napkin be make of the great indian figleaf they serve they not only for table sheet and other linen but also for dish wherein they put their meat which you shall likewise see in the grocer and pothecary shop to put and wrap in all thing whatsoever they have within their shop as we do in paper they likewise join they together in such sort that they can put both butter oil and such liquid stuff therein and also whatsoever come to hand to dress their meat they have certain earthen pot wherein they see Rice and make hole in the ground wher^^n they stamp it or beat it with a wooden pestle make for the purpose and they be so miserable that they buy the rice in the husk as it grow on the ground and some of they have Rice sow behind their house to serve their necessary use they use to drink out of a copper kanne with a spout whereby they let the water fall down into their mouth and never touch the pot with their flea-bane lip their house be common straw with kow-dung which they say kill flea they be very clean on their body for every day they wash themselves all their body over as often as they ease themselves or make water both man and woman like the moor and mahometans they wash themselves with the left hand because they eat with the right hand and use no spoon they do keep and observe their ceremony and superstition with great devotion for they never go forth without pray when they travel by the way they the devil never hinder the quantity but the quality of devotion for falsehood make it he whereof he be ambitious have on every hill cliff hole or den their pagode and idol in most devilish and deform shape cut and hew out of the stone and rock with their furnace hard by they and a cistern not far from they which be always full of water and every one that pass by wash their foot therein and so fall down before their idol some set before he for a offer fruit Rice egg hen etc. as their devotion serve and then come the Bramene their priest and take it away and eat it make the common people believe that the pagode have eat it when they will make a voyage to sea they use at the least fourteen day before they enter into their ship to make so great a noise with sound of trumpet and to make fire that it may be hear and see both by night and day the ship be hang about with flag wherewith they say they feast their pagode that they may have a good voyage the like do they at their return for a thanksgiving fourteen day long and thus they use to do in all their feast affair marriage childbirth and at other time of the year as sow and mow etc. the heathenish Indian that dwell in Goa be very rich merchant and traffic much there be one street within the town that be full of shop keep by those heathenish Indian that not only fall all kind of silk satin damask and curious work of Porceline from China and other place but all manner of ware of velvet silk satin and such like bring out of Portugal which by mean of their broker they buy by the great and sell they again by the piece or else wherein they be very cunning and natural subtle there be also another street where the Benianes of Cambaia dwell that have all kind of ware out of Cambaia and all sort of precious stone and be very subtle and cunning to bore and make hole in all kind of stone pearl and corral on the other side of the same street dwell other heathen which sell all sort of bedstead stool and such like stuff very cunning cover overwith lack most pleasant to behold and they can turn the lack into any colour that you will desire there be also a street full of gold and silver smith that be heathen which make all kind of work also diverse other handicraft man as copper-smith carpenter and such like occupation which be all heathen and every one a street by themselves there be likewise other merchant that deal all by great with corn Rice and other indian ware and merchandise as wood and such like some of they farm the king rent and revenue so that they be skilful every way to make their profit there be also many heathen broker very cunning and subtle in buy and sell and with their tongue to plead on both side there be in Goa many heathen physician which observe their gravity with hat carry over they for the sun like the portugal which no other heathen do but only ambassador or some rich merchant these heathen physician do not only cure their own nation and countryman but the portugal also for the viceroy himself the archbishop and all the monk and friar do put more trust in they then in their own countryman whereby they get great store of money and be much honour and esteem the countryman in the village round about Goa and such as labour and till the land be most christian but there be not much difference among they from the other heathen for that they can hardly leave their heathenish superstition which in part be permit they and be do to draw the other mongrel christians heathen to be christen as also that otherwise they will hardly be persuade to continue in the christian faith. there be in every place of the street exchanger of money by they call Xaraffos which be all christian jew they be very ready and expert in all manner of account and in know of all sort of money without who help man dare not receive any money because there be much counterfeit money abroad which be hard to be know from the good be it not for these Xaraffos which can discern it with half a eye the indian heathen have a custom that no man may change nor alter trade or occupation but must use his father trade and marry man daughter of the same occupation trade or deal trade-constancy which be so near look unto that they be divide and set apart each occupation by itself as country and nation be and so they call one another for if they speak to a man they ask he of what trade he be whether he be a goldsmith barber merchant grocer fisherman or such like they give no householdstuff with their daughter but only jewel and pay the charge of the wedding the son inherit all their good the time and season of the year be as follow winter begin on the last of April throughout the whole coast which be call India from Cambaia to the cape comorin chap. 34. of the time of the year in India and of their disease etc. and come with a western wind which blow out of the sea upon the coast the beginning thereof be with thunder and lightning and after that a steadfast and continual rain which last night and day till the month of September and then winter end with thunder and lightning and by reason of that continual rain it be call winter as also because at that time they can travel on the sea but in warm weather when fruit time come on it be then right summer for the time which in India be call summer because of the clearness and dryness of the weather be the cold and the wholesome and then there blow east wind so that the night be then very cool and somewhat sharp and then there be no special kind of first-fruit in season but such as grow continual all the year against the winter come every man make his provision of victual and all other necessary like as in a ship that be to make a voyage of five or six month also all their ship be bring into the river and unfurnished of tackle and every thing be take out of they they be cover with mat otherwise they will rot with the rain which be so steadfast and continual all the winter that many time diverse house by reason of the great moistness do fall unto the ground and as soon as winter begin there drive into the mouth of the haven great bank and shoal of sand which stop it up so that neither ship nor boat can either go out or in and the sea both there and along the coast make so great a roar and noise that man can neither hear nor see also the water of the river of Goa which run about the island in winter by mean of the land-water that by the continual rain fall from the hill be clean fresh water and of a red colour which in summer be clean contrary and like sea-water by reason of the concourse it have with the sea. in the month of September when winter end the bank of sand do fleet and vade away out of the river so that not only small ship may come in and go out but also the great Portugal ship of sixteen hundred ton may free enter without a pilot for it be deep enough and without danger in winter it be a heavy and melancholic be there for there be no other exercise to be use but only to sit in their shirt with a pair of linen breech and go and pass the time away with their neighbour in play and such exercise for that throughout the whole town there be no other do the woman and mestico take great pleasure in the winter time when it rain with their husband and slave to go into the field or some garden whether they carry good store of victual and there in their garden have many cistern or pond of water wherein they take their delight to swim and to bathe themselves in this time most of their indian fruit be in season the summer begin in September and continue till the last of April and be always clear sky and fair weather without once or very little rain then all the ship be rig and make ready to sail for all place as also the king army to keep the coast and to convoy merchant and then the east wind begin to blow from off the land into the sea whereby they be call Terreinhos that be to say the land wind they blow very pleasant and cool although at the first by change of the weather they be very dangerous and cause many great disease which do common fall in India by the change of the time these wind blow always in summer begin at midnight and continue till noon but constancy of wind they never blow above ten mile into the sea from off the coast and present after one of the clock until midnight the west wind blow which come out of the sea into the land and be call Uirason these wind be so sure and certain at their time as though man hold they in their hand whereby they make the land very temperate otherwise the heat will be unmeasurable it be likewise a strange thing that when it be winter upon the coast of India that be from din winter and summer within few mile in the same height to the cape comorin on the other side of the cape comorin on the coast call Choramandel it be clean contrary so that there it be summer and yet they lie all under one height or degree and there be but seventy mile by land between both coast and in some place but twenty mile and which be more as man travel over land from cochin to saint Thomas which lie on the same coast of Choramandel and come by the hill of ballagatte where man must pass over to go from the one coast unto the other on the one side of the hill to the top thereof it be pleasant clear sun shine weather and go down on the other side there be rain wind thunder and lightning as if the world shall end and be consume which be to be understand that it change from the one side to the other as the time fall out so that on the one side of the hill it be winter and on the other side summer and it be not only so in that place and country but also at Ormus on the coast of Arabia Felix by the cape of rosolgatte where the ship lie it be very still clear and pleasant water and fair summer time and turn about the cape on the other side it be rain and wind with great storm and tempest which with the time of the year do likewise change on the other side and so it be in many other place of the oriental country the sickness and
