disease in Goa and throughout India which be common come most with the change of the time and the weather as it be say before there reign a sickness call Mordexijn which steal upon man and handle they in such sort that it weaken a man and make he cast out all that he have in his body and many time his life withal this sickness be very common and kill many a man whereof they hardly or never escape the bloody flux be there likewise very common and dangerous as the plague with we they have many continual fever which be burn ague and consume man body with extreme heat whereby within four or five day they be either whole or dead this sickness be common and very dangerous and have no remedy for the portugal but let blood but the Indian and heathen do cure themselves with herb as sander and other such like ointment wherewith the ease themselves this sickness consume many portugal every year some because they have little to eat and less to drink of any meat or drink that be nourish and use much company of woman because that land be natural to provoke they thereunto as also the most part of the soldier by such mean have their live and their maintenance which oftentimes co they both life and limb for although man be of iron or steel the unchaste life of a woman with her unsatiable lust be able to grind he to powder and sweep he away like dust which co many a man life as the king hospital can well bear witness wherein they lodge whensoever they be sick where every year at the least there enter five hundred live man and never come forth till they be dead and they be only portugal for no other sick person may lodge therein I mean such as be call white man for the other Indian have a hospital by themselves in this hospital they be very well look unto by the Jesuit and gentleman whereof every month one of the best be choose and appoint who personal be there by they and give the sick person whatsoever they will desire and sometime spend more by four or five hundred ducat of their own purse than the king allowance reach unto but return to our matter of sickness pock and pile with other secret disease they be in those country very common and not hide or conceal for they think it no shame more than to have any other disease they heal they with the root China there be some that have have they at the least three or four time and be not any thing at all shun or dislike for the same but dare both boast and brag thereof it be not any thing perilous for the body insomuch that they have rather have they and fear they less than any of the foresay disease the plague have never be in India neither be it know unto the Indian but poison witch craft and such like whereby some lose their health and some their life be their daily exercise and very common with they the stone gravel and rapture reign much among they special among marry man by reason of the great quantity of water that they drink be give to all pleasure and riotousness enjoy all what their heart desire sit always with their belly open in their shirt in a gallery recreate themselves with the wind which cool they sometime have a slave to scratch and pare their nail and foot another the head the three hold a fan to drive away the fly this be the common use for two hour after noon where likewise they take a afternoon sleep and ever as they have thirst they bring he a dish of conserve or other com^ets that the water shall not work too much in his body but taste the better with such and the like exercise they do pass the day till night come on so that common they have all swell belly like Bacchus whereby the soldier and other Indian call they Barrigois that be belly or great belly the day both summer and winter be there all of a length not much difference only in the change they have about a hour difference the sun rise at six and set at six when it be noon common they have the sun in the middle of the element just over their head and it give shadow although it stretch somewhat out as the sun take his course in Goa you may see both the pole of the world the north and south star stand not far above the horizon the Bramenes be the honest and most esteem nation among all the indian heathen chap. 36. of the Indian call Bramenes which be the minister of the pagoda and indian idol and of their manner of life for they do always serve in the chief place about the king as receiver steward ambassador and such like office they be likewise the priest and minister of the pagoda or devilish idol they be of great authority among the indian people for that the king do nothing without their counsel and consent and that they may be know from other man they wear upon their naked body from the shoulder cross under the arm over their body down to the girdle or the cloth that be wrap about their middle three or four string like seal thread whereby they be know which they never put off although it shall cost they their life for their profession and religion will not permit it they go naked save only that they have a cloth bind about their middle to hide their privy member they wear sometime when they go abroad a thin cotton linen gown call Cabaia light cast over their shoulder and hang down to the ground like some other Indian as Benianes gusarate and decanijn upon their head they wear a white cloth wound twice or thrice about therewith to hide their hair which they never cut off but wear it long and turn up as the woman do they have most common round ring of gold hang at their ear as most of the Indian have they eat not any thing that have life but feed themselves with herb and rice neither yet when they be sick will for any thing be let blood but heal themselves by herb and ointment and by rub their body with sanders and such like sweet wood in Goa and on the sea coast there be many Bramenes which common do maintain themselves with sell of spice and other apothecary ware but it be not so clean as other but full of garbage and dust they be very subtle in writing and cast account whereby they make other simple Indian believe what they will touch the point of their religion wherein the common people believe they to be prophet whatsoever they first meet withal in the street at their go forth that do they all the day after pray unto the woman when they go forth have but one cloth about their body which cover their head and hang down unto their knee all the rest of the body be naked they have ring through their nose about their leg toe neck and arm and upon each hand seven or eight ring or bracelet some of silver and gilt if they be of wealth and ability but the common people of glass which be the common wear of all the indian woman when the woman be seven year old and the man nine year they do marry but they come not together before the woman be strong enough to bear child when the Bramenes die all their friend assemble together and make a hole in the ground wherein they throw much wood and other thing and if the man be of any account they cast in sweet sander and other spice with rice corn and such like and much oil because the fire shall burn the strong which do they lay the dead Bramenes in it then come his wife with music and many of her near friend all sing certain praise in commendation of her husband life put she in comfort and encourage she to follow her husband and go with he into the other world then she take all her jewel and part they among her friend and so with a cheerful countenance she leap into the fire and be present cover with wood and oil so she be quick dead and with her husband body burn to ash and if it chance as not very often it do that any woman refuse to be burn with her husband than they cut the hair clean off from her head and while she live she must never after wear any jewel more and from that time she be despise and account for a dishonest woman these Bramenes observe certain fast day in the year and that with so great abstinence that they eat nothing all that day and sometime in three or four day together they have their pagode and idol who minister they be whereof they tell and show many miracle and say that those pagode have be man live upon earth and because of their holy life and good work do here in this world be for a reward thereof become holy man in the other world as by their miracle by the devil perform have be manifest unto they and by their commandment their form and shape be make in the most ugly and deform manner that possible may be devise such they pray and offer unto with many devilish superstition and steadfast believe that they be their advocate and intercessor unto god. they believe also that there be a supreme God above which rule all thing and that man soul be immortal and that they go out of this world into the other both beast and man and receive reward accord to their work as Pythagoras teach who disciple they be the gusarate and Banianes be of the country of Cambaia many of they dwell in Goa chap. 37. of the gusarate and Banianes of Cambaia Diu Chau cochin and other place of India because of their trade and traffic in merchandise which they use much with all kind of ware as corn Cotton linen Anil Rice and other ware special all kind of precious stone wherein they have great skill they be most subtle and expert in cast of account and write so that they do not only surpass and go beyond all jew and other nation thereabouts but also the portugal and in this respect they have no advantage for that they be very perfect in the trade of merchandise and very ready to deceive man they eat not any thing that have life or blood in it neither will they kill it for all the good in the world how small or unnecessary soever it be for that they steadfast believe that every live thing have a soul and be next after man to be account of accord to Pythagoras law and know it must die and sometime they do buy certain fowl or other beast of the christian or portugal which they mean to have kill and when they have buy they they let they flee and run away they have a custom in Cambaia in the highway and wood to set pot with water and to cast corn and other grain upon the ground to feed bird and beast withal and throughout Cambaia they have hospital to cure and heal all manner of beast and bird therein whatsoever they ail and receive they thither as if they be man and when they be heal they let they fly or run away whither they will which among they be a work of great charity say it be do to their even neighbour and if they take a flea or a louse they will not kill it but take or put it into some hole or corner in the wall and so let it go and you can do they no great injury then to kill it in their presence for they will never leave entreat and desire with all courtesy not to kill it and that man shall not seem to commit so great a sin as to take away the life of that to who God have give both soul and body yea and they will offer much money to a man to let it live and go away they eat no radish onion garlic nor any kind of herb that have any colour of red in it nor egg for they think there be blood in they they drink not any wine nor use any vinegar but only water they be so dangerous of eat and drink with other man which be not their countryman that they will rather starve to death then once to do it it happen one live six day with the english and neither do eat or drink see lib. 3. c. 14. oftentimes that they sail in the portugal ship from Goa to cochin to sell their ware and to traffic with the portugal and then they make their provision for so long time as they think to stay upon the way which they take aboard with they and thereupon they feed and if the time fall out long than they make account of their water and provision be all spend as it happen when I sail from Goa to cochin they have rather die for hunger and thirst then once to touch the christian meat they wash themselves before they eat as the Bramenes do as also every time when they ease themselves or make water they be of a yellow colour like the Bramenes and somewhat white and there be woman among they which be much white and clear of complexion than the Portugal woman they be form and make both in face limb and in all other thing like man of Europe colour only except their apparel be a thin white gown upon their naked body from the head to the foot and make fast on the side under their arm their shoe of red leather sharp at the toe and turn up like hook their beard shave like the turk save only their moustachio they wear on their head a white cloth three or four time wrap about like the Bramenes and under their hair a star upon their forehead which they rub every morning with a little white sander temper with water and three or four grain of rice among it which the Bramene also do as a superstitious ceremony of their law. their body be common anoint with sanders and other sweet wood which they do very much use as also all the Indian their woman be apparel like the Bramenes wife they eat like the mahometan and all other Indian upon the ground in their house or assembly they sit on the ground upon mat or carpet and always leave their shoe without the door so that they be always barefoot in their house wherefore common the heel of their shoe be never pull up to save labour of unty or undo they they have a thousand other heathenish superstition which be not worth the rehearsal the Canaras and decanijn be of the country of Decam common call ballagate lie chap. 38. of the Canaras and d (...) s. behind Goa many of they dwell in Goa their apparel be like the gusurate and Benianes except their shoe which they wear like antic with cut toe and fasten above upon their naked foot which they call alparcas they wear their beard and hair long as it grow without cut but only turn it up and dress it as the Benianes and Bramenes use to do and be like they for colour form and make they eat all thing except cow hog and buffle flesh and fish. they account the ox kow or buffle to be holy which they have common in the house with they and they besmear stroke and handle they with brutish and stink holy all the friendship in the world and feed they with the same meat they use to eat themselves and when the beast ease themselves they hold their hand under their tail and so throw the dung away in the night time they sleep with they in their house and to conclude use they as if they be reasonable creature whereby they think to do God great service in their eat sit in the house wash make clean and other ceremony and superstition they be altogether like the Bramenes gusurate and Banianes in their marriage they contract each with other at seven year and at eleven or twelve year they be marry and dwell together when they be to be marry they begin fourteen day before to make a great sound with trumpet drum and fire which continue day and night for all those fourteen day with so great a noise of song and instrument that man can neither hear nor see on the wedding day all the friend and kindred on both side do assemble together and sit upon the ground round about a fire and go seven time about it utter certain word whereby the wedding be do they give their daughter no householdstuff but only some jewel as bracelet earring and such like of small value wherewith their husband must be content for the daughter be no heir but the son inherit all but they keep and maintain their daughter and sister till they marry when they die they be likewise burn and some of their wife with they but not so many as of the Bramenes every one of they follow his father occupation and marry with the daughter of such like trade which they name kindred they have their fast day and ceremony like the Bramenes for they be as the laity and the Bramenes as the spiritualty the minister priest and prophet of their idol they hire and farm the custom and rent of the portugal and the king revenue in the land of bard Salsette and the island of Goa so that oftentimes for any question or strife they must appear in law where they always come without council or attorney and know so well how to place their word accord to the law of Portugal not only temporal but spiritual that they be able to set down and show where it stand write as well as any counsellor can do and make their petition and request without any man advice that the portugal do wonder at their ready wit as I have oftentimes find in they when they be to take their oath to bear witness with any man they be set oath within a circle make of ash upon the pavement where they stand still lay a few ash on their bear head hold one hand on their head the other on their breast and then in their own speech swear by their pagode that they will tell the truth without dissimulation whatsoever shall be ask they for that they certain believe they shall be damn for ever if as than they shall not say the truth but conceal it the canarijn and corumbijn be the countryman and such as deal with till the land chap. 39 of the canariin and corumbiin of India fish and such like labour these be the most contemptible and the miserable people of all India and live very poor maintain themselves with little meat they eat all kind of thing except cow ox buffle hog and hen flesh their religion be like the decanijn and Canaras for they be all of one country and custom little differ they go naked their privy member only cover with a cloth the woman go with a cloth bind about their middle beneath their navel and hang down to the middle of their thigh and the other end thereof they cast over their shoulder whereby half their breast be cover they be in a manner black or of a dark brown colour many of they be christian because their chief habitation and dwell place be on the seaside in the country border upon Goa for that the palmtree do grow upon the sea coast or upon the bank by river side the rice be sow upon low ground which in winter time be cover with water Rice ground wherewith those canarijn do maintain themselves these bring hen fruit milk egg and other such like ware into the town to sell. they dwell in little straw house the door whereof be so low that man must creep in and out their householdstuff be a Mat upon the ground to sleep upon and a pit or hole in the ground to beat their rice in with a pot or two to seethe it in and so they live and gain so much as it be a wonder for common their house be full of small child which crawl and creep about all naked until they be seven or eight year old and then they cover their privy member when the woman be ready to travel childbirth with child they be common deliver when they be all alone and their husband in the field as it fortune upon a time as I and some other of my friend go to walk in the field and into the village where the canarijn dwell and have thirst I go to one of the canarijns house to ask some water therewith to refresh we and because I be very thirsty I stoop down and thrust my head in at the door ask for some water where I espy a woman alone within the house tie her cloth fast about her middle and before she have a wooden trough by the portugal call Gamell^ full of water where she stand and wash a child whereof as then she have new be deliver without any help which have wash she lay it naked on the ground upon a great indian fig leaf and desire i to stay and she will present give i water when I understand by she that she have as then new be deliver of that child without any help I have no desire to drink of her water but go unto another to ask water and perceive the same woman not long after go about her house as if there have be no such matter and the child be bring up in that manner clean naked nothing do unto they but only wash and make clean in a little cold water and do in that sort prosper and come up as well as man will wish or as any child within these country can do with all the tend they have and live many time until they be a hundred year old without any headache or toothache or lose any of their tooth they we be only a tusk of hair on the top of their head which they suffer to grow long the rest of their hair be cut short they be very expert in swim and dive they row up and down the river in boat call almadias whereof some of they be hew out of a piece of wood and so narrow that a man can hardly sit in they and it chance oftentimes that they turn over and over twice or thrice before they pass the river and then they leap out into the water and turn they up and so pour out the water they get into they again they be so miserable that for a penny they will endure to be whip and they eat so little that it seem they live by the air they be likewise most of they lean and weak of limb of little strength and very coward whereby the portugal do they great outrage and villainy use they like dog and beast in their marriage and death they observe the manner of the decanijn and Canaras as also in their religion and ceremony when the man be dead his body be burn and the woman cut her hair off and break all her jewel although they be but few and small for they be most of glass there be many arabian and abexijns in India the arabian observe Mahomet law chap. 40. of the arabian and abcxiins dwell in India and the abexijn some be mahometan some christian after their manner for they be of Prester john land the abexijn that be christian have on their face four burn mark in manner of a cross one over their nose in the middle of the forehead between both their eye on each of their cheek one between their eye and their ear and one under their neither lip down to the chin these abexijn and arabian such as be free do serve in all India for sailor and seafaring man the portugal although they serve for sailor in the pride of Portugal sailor portugal ship that come into India and have never be other in Portugal but sailor yet be they ashamed to live in that order and think it a great discredit unto they together with a great diminish of their authority and estimation which they account themselves to hold in India so that they give themselves out for master of ship and by their captain be also call pilot and chief boatswaine but not low for if they shall descend but one step low it will be a great blot and blemish unto they all their life after which they will not endure for any thing in the world these abexijn and arabian serve for small money and be hire be very lowly and subject so that oftentimes they be beat and smite not as slave but like dog which they bear very patient not once speak a word they common have their wife and child with they in the ship wherein they be hire which continual stay with they what voyage soever they make and dress their own meat which be Rice sod in water with salt fish among it the cause why the woman sail in the ship be for that in summer and not else their ship go to sea when they always have calm water and fair weather with good wind they have common but one Portugal or two for captain master and pilot and they have a chief boatswain which be a arabian which they call Mocadon and he be ruler of the arabian and abexijns that be sailor who he have under his subjection even as if they be his slave or subject this Mo^adon be he that condition and make bargain with the owner of the ship to have so many sailor and he receive the monethlie money for their wage and account with the sailor particular but for government of the ship he have not to do neither trouble himself therewith the ship when they sail use no cask for water because there be not any throughout all India nor any make there save only such as come out of Portugal and use in the Portugal ship but in stead of pipe they use a great four corner wooden cistern that stand by the main mast at the very foot thereof upon the keel of the ship which be very well pitch and make fast wherein they lade as much water as they think will serve they for their voyage the captain master or pilot merchant and passenger have every man their meat by themselves and their water in great indian pot call Martavans the black people or caffare of the land of Mosambique and all the coast of Ethiopia chap. 41. of the black people of Mosambique which be call caffare and of their manner and custom see of these sup. 9 c. 12 and within the land to the cape Speranza go all naked although those of Mosambique that be the woman do a little cover themselves which they do by mean of the daily conversation they have with the portugal some have all their body raze and sear with iron and all figure like raze satin and damask wherein they take great pride think there be no fair people than they in all the world so that when they see any white people that wear apparel on their body they laugh and mock at they think we to be monster and ugly people and when they will make any devilish form and picture than they invent one after the form of a white man in his apparel there be among they that file there tooth as sharp as needle which they likewise esteem for a great ornament there be some of they that be become christian since the portugal come thither but there be no great pain take about it in those country because there be no profit to be have as also that it be a infectious and unwholesome country and therefore the Jesuit be wary enough not to make any house or habitation therein for they see no great profit to be reap note of jesaites there for they as they do in India and the land of japan and in other place where they find great quantity of riches with the sap whereof they increase much and fill their bee-hive therewith to satisfy their thirsty and insatiable desire they have a custom among they that when they go to war against their enemy if they win the battle or overthrow each other he that take or kill most man be hold and account for the best and brave man among they and much respect and to witness the same before their king of as many as they have slay or take prisoner they cut off their privy member that if they be let go again they may no more beget child which in process of time may mischief they and then they dry they well because they shall not rot which be so dry they come before their king with great reverence in the presence of the principal man in the village and there take these member so dry one by one in their mouth and spit they on the ground at the king foot which the king with great thanks accept and the more to reward and recompense their valour cause they all to be take up and give to they again for a sign and token of honour whereby ever after from that time forward they be account as knight and they take all those member wherewith the king have thus honour they and tie they all upon a string like a bracelet or chain and when a costly kind of chain for woman to wear they marry or go to any wedding or feast the bride or wife of those knight do wear that chain of man member about their neck which among they be as great a honour as it be with we to wear the golden fleece from Mosambique great number of these caffare be carry into India and many time they sell a man or woman that be grow to their full strength for two or three ducat when the portugal ship put in there for fresh water and other necessary than they be dear in time of poverty or dearth the father may sell their child as it happen in my time that there be such a dearth and scarcity of victual in the firm land and country border upon Goa that the man of India come to Goa and outstretch place where the portugal be resident to sell their child in great number and for small price to buy they victual I have see boy of eight or ten year give in exchange for five or fix measure of rice and some for three or four ducat the piece and some come with their wife and child to offer themselves to be slave so that they may have meat and drink to nourish their body and because the portugal have traffic in all place as we have be in many it be the cause why so many be bring out of all country to be sell for the portugal do make a live by buy and sell of they as they do with other ware the Malabares be those that dwell on the sea-coast between Goa and the cape Comorijn chap. 42. of the Malabares and Nayros in India with their manner and custom southward from Goa where the pepper grow they have a speech by themselves and their country be divide into many kingdom they go all naked only their privy member cover the woman likewise have but a cloth from their navel down to their knee all the rest be naked they be strong of limb and very arrogant and proud of colour altogether blackie yet very smooth both of hair and skin which common they anoint with oil to make it shine they wear their hair as long as it will grow tie on the top or crown of their head with a lace both man and woman the lap of their ear be open and be so long that they hang down to their shoulder and the long and wide they be the more they be esteem among they and it be think to be a beauty in they of face body and limb they be altogether like man of Europe without any difference but only in colour the man be common very hairy and rough upon the breast and on their body and be the most lecherous and unchaste nation in all the orient so that there be very few woman child among they of seven or eight year old that have their maidenhead they be very ready to catch one from another though it be but for a small penny in their house they be not very curious their house and householdstuff differ not much from the ca^^rijns and corumbijn of Goa their idolatry ceremony and superstition be like the heathen of these Malabares there be two manner of people the one be nobleman or gentleman call Nayros which be soldier that do only wear and handle Nayros arm the other be the common people call Polyas and they may wear no weapon nor bear any arm the Nayros must in all place where they go or stand wear such arm as be appoint for they and always be ready at the king commandment to do he service some of they do always bear a naked rapier or courtelas in their right hand and a great target in their left hand those target be very great and make of light wood so that when they will they can cover their whole body therewith they be so well use thereunto that they esteem it nothing to bear they and when they travel on the way they may be hear a great way off for that they common make a great knock with the hilt of their rapier against the target because they will be hear there be some that carry a bow and a venomous arrow upon their shoulder wherein they be very expert other carry long pike some piece with the match ready light and wound about their arm and have the best lock that possible may be find in all Europe which they know so well how to use that the portugal can have no advantage against they wheresoever they go they must always have their arm with they both night and day not any of they be marry nor may not marry during their life but they may free lie with the nayros daughter or with any other that like they what woman soever they be yea though they be marry woman when the Nayro have a desire thereunto he enter into a house where he think good and set his arm in the street without the door and go in and dispatch his business with the good wife or the daughter the door stand wide open not fear that any man shall come in to let he for whosoever pass by and see the nayros arm stand at the door although it be the goodman himself he go by and let he make a end and have do he take his arm and depart thence and then the husband may come to the house without make any word or once move question about it in that manner they go where they will and no man may deny they as these Nayros go in the street they use to cry Po Po which be to say take heed look to yourselves or I come stand out of the way for that the other sort of people call Polyas that be no Nayros may not once touch or trouble one of they for if any of the Polyas shall stand still and not give they place whereby he shall chance to touch their body he may free thrust he through and no man ask he why he do it and when they be once touch by any Polyas or by any other nation except Nayros they must before they eat or converse with other Nayros wash and cleanse their body with great ceremony and superstition likewise they must not be touch by any christian or any other man and when the portugal come first into India at cochin it be conclude to pacify the matter and to keep peace and quietness among they that two man shall be choose one for the Nayros and the other for the portugal that shall fight body to body and he that shall be overthrow that nation shall give place unto the other this be do in the presence of both nation and the Portugal overcome the Nayro who he slay whereupon it be agree that the Nayros shall give place unto the Portugal and stand aside until he be past wheresoever they meet the Nayros wear the nail of their hand very long whereby they show that they be gentleman because the longness of the nail do let and hinder man from work or do any labour they say likewise that they do it the better and fast to gripe a thing in their hand and to hold their rapier which some portugal and mestico do likewise use and hold the same opinion with the Nayros whereof there be many in India which let their nail grow for the same cause the principall or chief of those Nayros which be leader or captain of certain number of Nayros wear a gold or silver bracelet or ring about their arm above their elbow as also their governor ambassador and king whereby they be know from other man for otherwise they go all naked also their king ruler and other captain and leader when they go abroad be guard and accompany by other Nayros they be very good and stout soldier and will set upon a man very fierce they be also veriefull of revenge so that whensoever they fight against their enemy either by water or by land and that they chance to be thrust into the body with a pike they be not present therewith content to he down but if they can speedy pluck the pike forth they will not spare to pull it forth with both their hand and draw it through their body therewith to set upon they that give they the wound and to be revenge on they the king may not judge nor execute those Nayros open for if they have deserve death he cause they by other Nayros to be put to death the daughter of the Nayros may not have the company of any man but only of Nayros although secret they have the company of many portugal and christian but if the Nayros once perceive it or find they in the deed do they may kill they without further question in every place where they dwell they have a pit or weil dig wherein they do hold water which stand open in the way where every man pass by wherein every morning when they rise they wash themselves all over begin first at the foot and so rise up to the head as well man as woman without be ashamed to be see of such as go by or look upon they and the king himself likewise which water be so green slimy and stink that a man can not choose but stop his nose as he go by it and they certain believe that whensoever they shall forget to wash themselves in that water that they shall then be whole unclean and full of fin and this wash or make clean must not be do in any run water but it must be in a holy water place where the water stand in a pit or well and by their Bramenes conjure with many word and ceremony otherwise it be of no virtue but whole unprofitable for their idolatrous service they be like the other heathen and be burn when they be dead their son may not be their heir because they have no wife but use all woman where heir and when they will doubt which be their own son for the Bramenes also have the king wife at their pleasure and do he great honour when it please they to lie with their queen their heir be their sister son for they say although they doubt of their father yet they know their sister be the mother of they thus much touch the Nayros and gentleman or soldier the other common people of the Malabares call Polyas be such as be the country husbandman and labourer man of occupation fisher and such like those be much contemn Polyas and despise they live miserable and may wear no kind of weapon neither yet touch or be conversant with the Nayros for as the Nayros go on the street and they hear he call they step aside bow their arm and stoop with their head down to the ground not dare so much as once look up before the Nayros be pass in other thing they observe the custom of the other Indian for that every man follow the occupation of his elder and may not change it for any thing there be great number of moor and jew in all place of India as at Goa cochin and within the land. in their house and apparel they follow the manner of the land chap. 43. of the moor and jew in India wherein they be resident amongst the Indian they have their church synagogue and wherein they use all ceremony accord to their law but in the place where the portugal inhabit and govern it be not permit unto they to use they open neither to any indian although they have their family and dwell house and get their living and deal one with the other but secret in their house they may do what they will so that no man take offence thereat without the town and where the portugal have no commandment they may free use and exercise their ceremony and superstition every one as like he best without any man to let or deny they but if they be find open do it in the portugal town and jurisdiction or that they have any point of christian ceremony mingle among they both man and woman die for it unless they turn unto the christian eaith they be most white of colour like man of Europa and have many fair woman there be many of they that come out of the country of Palestina and jerusalem thither and speak over all the exchange very perfect and good spanish the moor likewise have their mesquito wherein they pray and above the church they have many seller and gallery where they learn their child their principle of religion before they go to church they wash their foot for the which purpose they have always a cistern with water stand without the church and leave their Alparcos which be their shoe stand at the church door before they go in and be in the church they fall flat on the ground upon their face and so with their arm and hand lift up make many counterfeit face they be also circumcise like the jew and eat no hogs-flesh and when they be dead they be bury in their church they have not any image but only some stone or round pillar stand upright with certain chaldean letter out of their Koran grave upon they as I and a friend of i chance to go out of the town we be destron to see their mahometical church and their manner of service which be deny we by the keeper of the door that bid we put off our shoe but because we will not he say it be not lawful for we to enter in that sort into the church but to let we see it he suffer we to stand within the door and open some of the window that we may see what be within it then the Portugal ask he for their god and their saint which they use to pray unto because he see the church empty as I say before then the Moor answer he that they use not to pray to stock and stone but to the live God which be in heaven and say that the proud Portugal christians and the heathen be all of one religion for that they pray to see the proof hereof sup. pag. 28. image make of wood and stone and give they the glory which only appertain to the live God with the which answer the Portugal be so angry that he begin to chide so that there have grow a great quarrel have it not be for i in the kingdom of Narsinga or the coast call Choramandel there stand a pagode that chap. 44. of their pagode be very great exceed rich and hold in great estimation have many pilgrimage and visitation make unto it from all the country border about it where every year they have many fair feast and procession and there they have a wagon or a cart which be so great and heavy that three or four elephant can hardly draw it and this bring forth at fair feast and procession at this cart hang likewise many cable or rope whereat also all the country people both man and woman of pure devotion do pull and hale in the upper part of this cart stand a tabernacle or seat wherein fit the idol and under it sit the king wife which after their manner play on all instrument make a most sweet melody and in that sort be the cart draw forth with great devotion and procession there be some of mad zeal they that of great zeal and pure devotion do cut piece of flesh out of their body and throw they down before the pagode other lay themselves under the wheel of the cart and let the cart run over they whereby they be all crush to piece and press to death and they that thus die be account for holy and devout martyr and from that time forward devil martyr be keep and preserve for great and holy relic beside a thousand other such like beastly superstition which they use as one of my chamber fellow that have see it show i and it be also well know throughout all India upon a time I and certain portugal my friend have licence from the viceroy be at a banquet and meeting about five or six mile within the firm land and with we we have certain decanijn and natural bear Indian that be acquaint with the country the chief cause of our go be to see their manner of burn the dead Bramene and his wife with he be alive because we have be advertise that such a thing be to be do and there among other strange device that we see we come into some village and place inhabit by the Indian where in the way and at every hill stony rock or hole almost within a length we find a carve pagode or rather devil and monster in hellish shape at the last we come into a village where stand a great church of stone wherein we enter and find nothing in it but a great table that hang in the middle of the church with the image of a pagode paint therein so misshape and deform that more monstrous be never see for it have many horn and long tooth that hang out of his mouth down to the knee and beneath his navel and belly it have another such like face with many horn and tusk upon the head thereof stand a triple crown mitre not much unlike the pope triple crown so that in effect it seem to be a monster such as be describe in the apocalypse it hang before a wall which make a partition from another chamber in manner of a quire yet be it close make up without window or any place for light in the middle whereof be a little narrow close door and on both side of the door stand a small furnace make within the wall wherein be certain hole or lattice thereby to let the smoke or savour of the fire to enter into that place when any offer shall be make whereof we find some there as Rice corn fruit hen and such like thing which the Indian daily offer but there come so filthy a smoke and stink out of the place that whosoever go near it be almost ready to choke the say place be all black smeerie and foul therewith before this door be shut in the middle of the church there stand a calf of stone whereon one of our company leap and laugh begin to cry out which the Bramene that keep the church perceive begin to call and cry for help so that present many of the neighbour run thither to see what the cause may be but before the throng of people come we deal so well with the Bramene acknowledge our fault and say it be unadvised do that he be well content and the people go home again then we desire the Bramene to open we the door that stand shut which after much entreaty he yield unto offer first to throw certain ash upon our forehead which we refuse so that before he will open we the door we be force to promise he that we will not enter further in then to the door the door of their or rather be open it show within like lip like lettuce like a lime-kill be close vault round about over the head without either hole or window to cast in light but only at the door neither be there any light in all the church but that which come in at the door we enter by within the say cell or vault there hang at the least one hundred burn lamp in the middle whereof stand a little altar and cover over with cloth make of cotton-wool and over that with pure gold under the which as the Bramene tell we sit the pagode be of clean gold of the bigness of a puppet or a baby sell in fair hard by the church without the great door stand within the earth a great four corner or square cistern hew out of free stone with stair on each side to go down into it full of green filthy and stink water wherein they wash themselves when they mean to enter into the church to pray from thence we go further and still as we go in every place we find Pagodes hew out of hard stone and stand in their hole of such lively shape and figure as we tell you before these stand in the way under certain coverture without the church and have hard by each of they a small cistern of water cut o^^ of the stone to wash their foot with half a indian nut that have a handle and hang there to take up water withal and this be ordain for traveller that pass by who common at every one of those pagode do fall down and make their prayer and wash their foot in those cistern by the say pagode common do stand two little furnace with a calf or kow of stone before the which they set their offering which be of such thing as be to be eat every man as his devotion serve which they think the pagode eat in the night but it be take away by the Bramene we find in every place such offering stand but we have little desire once to taste thereof it look so filthy and as we have sufficient behold their misshape figure and monstrous image we return again into the village wherein we see the stone church because the Bramene have advertise we that the same day about evening the pagode shall be carry in procession to sport itself in the field and to fetch a circuit which we desire to see and about the time which he appoint they ring a little bell which they have get of the christian wherewith all the people begin to assemble and take the pagode out of his diabolical cell which with great reverence they set in a Palamkin bear by the chief man of the town all the rest with great devotion follow after with their usual noise and sound of trumpet and other instrument wherewith they go a reasonable way round about a field and then bring he to the stone cistern where wash he very clean although he be very filthy stink they carry he again into his cell leave he shut herein withal his lamp to make good cheer and have make a foul smoke and stink about he and every man leave his offer behind he they go home to their house leave the Bramene alone who in stead of the pagode make good cheer at their cost with his wife and family there be over all India great store of cattle as ox cow sheep hog goat kid and such like and very good cheap and in great abundance although the flesh be not chap. 45. of all the kind of beast cattle and fowl in India cow oxen. mutton hog sheep tail of so good a ^aste as that in Europe which proceed from the heat of the country and therefore it be not much esteem a man may buy the best kow in Goa for five or six pardawe ox be there little kill to eat but be most keep to till the land all other thing as hog sheep and goat be sell after the rate mutton be little esteem of and not much use to be eat for it be forbid to such as be sick and the hog flesh be much better and sound which be rather permit unto sick person than mutton there be sheep in that country of five quarter in quantity for that the tail be as great and have as much flesh upon it as any of the quarter there be many buffle but nothing good to be eat unless it be by poor people but their milk be very good and be very well sell and ordinary eat buffle and their milk for you shall see the slave and canarijn in great number all day go about the street to sell the milk of buffle and goat and excellent sweet cream and fresh butter in small piece they make likewise some small white cheese but they be very salt and dry wild cheese wild beast boar some hare coney heart and hind be there also to be find but not many cock capon pheasant and dove be there in great abundance and good cheap in the island of Goa and there about ar^ sparrow and some other small bird yet not many but on the coast few small bird great bat and hurtful I have hear that they breed and have many young as rat with we crow bold of cochin and malabar ^^ere be very few sparrow nor any such like small bird there be in India many bat and some of they so great that it be incredible to tell they do great mischief to tree fruit and herb whereby the canarijn be constrain ^o set man to watch in their tree and yet they can hardly rid they away the Indian eat they and say they be as good meat as a partridge there be a most wonderful number of black crow which do much hurt and be so bold that oftentimes they come fly in at their window and take the meat out of the dish as it stand upon the table before they that be set down to eat and as I myself sa^e write above in a chamber of the house the window be open one of those crow fly in at the window and pick the cotton but of my inkhorn and blot all the paper that lie on my table do what I can to let he they fit common upon the buffle back and peek off their hair so that you shall find very few buffle that have any hair upon their back and therefore to avoid the crow they get themselves into marsh and warry place where they stand in the water up to the neck otherwise they can never be rid of they there be likewise great number of rat and some as big as young pig so that the cat da^^ not touch they sometime they dig down the house for that they undermine great rat the wall and foundation through and through whereby many time the howl fall down and be spoil there be another sort of rat that be little and reddish of hair they be call sweet smell rat for they have a smell as for that man may set nothing whatsoever it be that be to be eat or fatty nor yet their clothes nor linen but you shall present find at the least a thousand upon it and in the twinkle of a eye they will present consume a loaf of bread wherefore it be the manner throughout India to make all the cupboard wherein they keep their victual and chest where their linen and apparel lie with four foot or pillar and under every foot or pillar a stone or wooden cistern full of water and place the cupboard or chest in the middle of the room not near the wall whereby they can come at it otherwise it will be spoil and if they do never so little forget to pour water into the cestern if it be but a while present there will be so many pismire crawl all over it that it be wonderful so that it seem to be a curse or plague of God send upon that country there be some likewise that use such cistern of water under their bedstead because they will not be trouble with they as they lie in their bed and also under their table some man which keep Canary bird or such small soul that be bring thither from Portugal or out of Turkey and Persia for their pleasure be force to set they on a stick or perch make for the purpose with a cistern of water under it otherwise it will present be kill by the pismire and though it hang in the top of the house yet they will come at it if it have a string to hold it by the soldier and poor people that have not the mean to buy cupboard with Cesternes put the bread and other victual which they leave which be not overmuch in a cloth tie on knot and hang it on a nail the Indian report for a truth that they have try it those elephant of other country do (@) and honour to the elephant of Seylon the most service that they us^ they for in India be to dra^ their pipe butt pack and other good and to ship they all which they do with elephant they be keep at the king charge and he that need they speak to their keeper and agree with they for a price to have their labour then the keeper get upon the neck of the elephant and thrust his foot under his ear have a hook in his hand which he stick on his head where his stone lie that be to say above between both his ear which be the cause that they be so well able to rule they and come to the thing which they be to draw they bind the fat or pack fast with a rope that he may feel the weight thereof and then the keeper speak unto he whereupon he take the cord with his snout and wind it about his tooth and thrust the end into his mouth and so draw it hang after he whither they desire to have it if it be to be put into a boat than they bring the boat close to the shore of the key and the elephant put it into the boat himself and with his snout gather stone together which he lay under the fat pipe or pack and with his tooth strike and thrust the pack or vessel to see if it lie fast or not it will draw any great shot or other iron work or metal be make fast unto it be it never so heavy they draw fust small galley and other great boat as carvel and such like as easy out of the water upon the land as if no man be in they so that they serve their turn there even as our sled or cart with horse do here to carry our ware and merchandise their meat be Rice and water they sleep like cow ox horse and all fourfooted beast and bow their knee and all their member as other beast do in winter when it begin to rain than they be unquiet and altogether mad so that their keeper can rule they and then they be let some whither out of the town to a great tree and there tie unto it by the leg with a great iron chain where they carry he meat and so he lie in the open air as long as he be mad which be from April to September all the winter time when it rain and then he come to himself and begin to serve again as tame that a man may lie under his belly so you do he no hurt but he that hurt he he must take heed for they never forget when any man do they injury until they be revenge they be very fearful of a rat or mouse and also of the pismire because they fear they will creep into their snout they be likewise afraid of gunshot and of fire unless by length of time they be use unto they when they have the company one of the other the male elephant stand upon the high ground and the female somewhat low as they go along the way although you see they not you may hear they a far off by the noise of their foot and clap of their ear which they continual use they be as swift in go almost as a horse and be very proud and desirous of honour when there be any great feast or holiday keep in Goa with solemn procession common the elephant go with they the young before and the old behind and be all paint upon their body with the arm and cross of Portugal and have every one five or six trumpeter or player upon the shawm fit upon they that sound very pleasant wherewith they be as well please and go with as great gravity and in as good order as if they be man it happen in Goa that a elephant shall draw a great Fust out of the water unto the land which fust be so great and heavy that he can not do it alone so that they must have another to help he whereupon the keeper chide he use many hard word say that he be idle and weak and that it will be a everlasting shame for he that they must fetch another to help he wherewith the elephant be so desperate that he thrust away his fellow which be bring to help he and begin fresh again to draw with so great force more than he be well able to do that with extreme labour he burst and fall down stark dead in the place at such time as I be to make my voyage from cochin to Portugal the rudder of our ship be out of order so that it must of force be bring on land to make it fit again and so it be draw to the river side at the stern of the boat which the elephant shall draw on land upon two board that it may slide up and because it be heavy as the rudder of a ship of fourteen hundred or sixteen hundred ton require as also that the elephant be as yet but young and not grow to his full strength so that he can not draw it out alone yet he do the best he can but see he can not do it he fall on his foreleg and begin to cry and weep that the tear run out of his eye and because many of we stand upon the shore to behold this fight the keeper begin to chide he and with hard word to curse he because he shame he thus in presence of so many man not to be able to draw up such a thing but what strength or labour soever the elephant use he can not do it alone but when they bring another elephant to help he they both together draw it half out of the water so that it lay partly upon the board the first elephant perceive that with his head and tooth thrust the other elephant away and will have no more help but draw it out himself they be likewise very thankful and mindful of any good do unto they when new year day come their keeper use of common custom to ask new year gift of the viceroy the archbishop and other governor and gentleman and then the elephant come to the door and bow their head down and when anything be give they kneel on their knee with great lowliness and thankfulness for the good deed so do unto their keeper which they think to be do unto themselves they use as they pass by such house to bow their head at the door as also when they pass by the church door and by cross which their master teach they they have a custom that they go often into the market where herb be sell as reddish Letrice colewort and such like stuff and those that be liberal to the elephant do use to throw something before he among the rest there be one herb wife which always use to throw something of her ware before the elephant now when the time come on that the elephant grow mad as I say before they use to go with they three or four day or a week about the street before they bind they up be as then but half mad to ask something of every body for the feed of the mad elephant in the winter time and go thus about the street the master be not able to rule he for he run about with his head downward and by his roar give the people warning to beware and when he find or see no man nee leap and overthrow whatsoever he meet withal whereby he make great sport and pastime much like to the bait of ox in Spain which never cease until one two or more of they be slay the like rule be keep with the mad elephant in India it chance in this run about that the elephant run through the street and in haste at unaware come into the market throw down all that be in his way whereat every man be abash and leave their ware run to save themselves from be over run by the elephant and by mean of the noise and press of people they fall one over another as in such case be common see among they be this woman that always use to give the elephant something to eat which have a little child in the market lie by she in a basket and by the hasty rise up and throng of the people the woman run into a house not have time to snatch up her child and take it with she and when the elephant be alone in the market place where he roar up and down overthrow all thing that be before he he come by the child that as I say lie still in the market and as every man look special the mother which cry out and very think that the elephant have take it and cast it on his shoulder and spoil it as he do all other thing he on the contrary notwithstanding all his madness be mindful of the good will and liberality of the child mother daily use unto he take up the child handsome and tender with his Snout and lay it soft upon a stall by a shop side which do he begin again to use the same order of stamp cry and clap as he have do at the first to the great wonder of all that behold it special to the ease and joy of the mother that have recover her child the better it be the piece and crumb that fall upon the ground they melt they together but that be not so good for it have filth and they beat the lac to powder and melt it and so mix all manner of colour upon it as they listen red black green yellow or any other colour and make piece thereof such as be sell here to seal letter withal see 71. earth within it it happen oftentimes that they find the pismire wing within the raw Lac. when the lac be raw as it come from the tree it be a darke-red-colour but be refine and cleanse they make it of all colour in India benjoin be a kind of stuff like frankincense and myrrh but more esteem for it serve for many medicine and other thing as when they make ball or piece of amber and musk they must always have benjoin with it to make it perfect it grow much in the kingdom of syan in the island of sumatra in the land of javas and the country of malacca they be high tree full of branch with leaf like Lemmon tree leave with a thick and high stem or stock in the middle from whence proceed the gum which be the benjoin when the tree be young than it yield the best benjoin which be blackish of colour and of a very sweet smell and be call benjoin de Boninas that be to say benjoin of the flower because of the perfect smell the second benjoin be call benjoin Amendoado that be benjoin of almond because it be mix with piece of white benjoin among the black like to almond that be cut in piece this benjoin be not so good because the white benjoin be of the old tree frankincense grow in Arabia it be the gum that flow out of the body of tree like benjoin ca. 72. main by the Indian be call bola it grow in the same that benjoin and frankincense do and come also out of Arabia but most out of the country of Abexin from the inward part of the country lie between Mosambique and the red sea which be call Prester john land. there be three sort of sander that be white yellow and red the white and the yellow which be the best come most out of the island of Tymor which lie by java this island have ca. 74. whole wood and wilderness of sander both of white and yellow and from thence it be carry throughout all India and other country and traffic much there with the red sanders grow most in the coast of Choramandel and Tanassarijn which be in the country of Pegu the tree of sander be like nut tree and have a certain fruit upon they like cherry at the first green and after black but of no taste nor any thing worth for it present fall off only the wood of the tree be account of which be the sander SNakewood be mostin the island of Seylon it be a low tree the root thereof be the snake-wood be of colour white show somewhat yellow very hard and bitter in taste it ca. 75. be much use in India they stamp and bruise it like sanders in water or wine and so drink it it be very good and well prove against all burn fever one ounce thereof bruise and mix with water be good against all poison and sickness as the colic worm and all filthy humour and coldness in the body and special against the sting of snake whereof it have the name it be first find by mean of a little beast call quill or Quirpele which be of bigness very like a ferret wherewith in those country they use to drive coney out of their hole and so catch they whereof in India they have many in their house which they play withal to pass the time away as also to kill their mouse and rat and to drive they away this beast by nature be a great enemy to the snake so that wheresoever she find any she fight with they and because it be often bite by the snake it know how to heal itself with this snake-wood whereof there be much in Seylon where also be many of those beast and great store of snake so that if it be never so sore bite have eat of this wood it be present heal as if it have never be hurt the aloe which in India be call calamba and Palo D'aguilla be most in malacca in the island of sumatra Camboia Zion and the country border on the same the tree be ca. 76. like olive tree and somewhat great when it be cut off it smell not so well because it be green for the dry it be the better it smell the best and that which smell most be the inner most part of the wood some of it be better than the rest which the Indian do present know how to find out the best and fine be call calamba and the other Palo Daguilla now to know which be the best you must understand that the wood that be very heavy with black and brown vein and which yield much oil or moistness which be find by the fire be the best and the great and thick it be the better it be and have the more virtue of this wood they make many costly thing and it have a special and precious smell so that it be great esteem special the calamba which if it be good be sell by weight against silver and gold. the Palo Daguilla next after the calamba be much account of there be another kind of Palo Daguilla which be call aquilla Brava or wild aquilla and be also much esteem for the Indian aquilla use it therewith to burn the body of their Bramenes and other man of account when they ^re dead and because it be costly therefore it be a great honour to those that be burn therewith the author proceed in a large discourse of other drug gem and indian occurrent which I have omit as it be to those that with we be bury in tomb of marble stone but it be not comparable to the other Palo Daguilla nor the calamba the wild aguill grow most in the island of Seylon and on the coast of Choramandel and the best Palo Daguilla and Calamba grow in malacca these costly wood be much use in India man towards he and joint the prosperity of his country for this benefit which he do to all that country in the invent money for they they call he general deranqun which be to say seal of money after the city of ormuz build in the coast of Persia and prosperous with many people and riches the king command his great man to go through the country of Magostan and every one shall take that which best take of who those country be nominate to this day and because the king that succeed Mahomet be mighty and good in their government they hold the country in their succession increase always in people and nobleness and their child that descend of they be such continual that the father in their life time give they the government of the kingdom and they rest in their old age it be the custom among these king because the memory of their forefather may not perish when they come to the ten generation they begin their denomination anew the ten custom of succession genealogy follow take the name of the ten before in sort that the first of the number of the ten be to take the name of the founder and so in order till the number of ten be end this order continue some year the reign go by a direct line afterwards this order and custom perish because that one for covetousness of reign do kill the other and many be make blind by other that will have the government of the kingdom but there be one great and notable thing in this kingdom that although there be many that reign tyrannous murder the lawful king yet unto this day there never reign any that be not of the blood royal only hormuz be in the side of Persia one that then reign be dead and have none of the blood royal in the country the goazill which be the governor of the kingdom the goazill do make himself king. at this time a son in cay have make himself king wherefore he raise present the siege from against cay and come with all the man he have to ormuz and assoon as he come he be receive of all with great contentment and feast Pinder have be before in east indies with those ship which the copany there take he be now in this persian business as I remember master of the London this I promise as a preface to the large ormusian relation follow namely the hart wherein master Richard Blithe be vice-admiral the roe Bucke rear admiral master Richard swan master of she and Christopher brown master of the egell be the four ship the five and twenty of march 1620. these four ship set sail from the down the four and twenty of April all four ship get into Saldan^ bay who latitude be 33. degree 57 minute and 29. degree 48. minute to the eastern of the lizart in Cornwall and it have 2. degree 27. minute westerly variation the same day arrive captain fitz-harbord with the exchange and unity who come from England in our company with three ship under his command and leave our company the four of April there be in the bay a english ship that come from surat name the lion captain Widdall in she also there be ten dutch ship bind for jaccatra the thirty of june our ship be water be the chief cause of put into that bay but former there have be plenty of ox and sheep to be buy for small value but by some abuse to the people there be nothing to be have except water by some neglect our continuance be until the 25. of july with much hazard and prejudice to our passage so ply for surat with purpose to have go within the island of s. Wilson chirurgeon contain many particular of the Ormus war and cause thereof as also of the most most admirable take of a great Portugal ship well man by a small english pinnace right worshipful my duty remember unto you sir I be glad to hear of your good health and welfare and shall be hearty glad to see you and all you the which I hope will be very short sir I be very much bind unto you that I know not how I shall make requital for the same in that in my absence you have show unto i that kindness for it which as at all other time I have find you the best friend that I have in the world I do give you a thousand thanks and will by god help make part requital for the same and I shall be ready at all time to do any thing for you that in i lie to the uttermost of my power or to any of you I will have write unto you concern our voyage but I can be so brief as to send it in a letter but I make no doubt but you will hear more of the passage thereof than I can certify or at least wise have hear already for there be letter send out of Persin over land to the company concern the take of Kishme castle and the city of Ormus wit^ the castle with the spoil of five ship and one great galley one ship burn and the rest sink the which I pray God may stand to the good like of you all for we have a terrible time in Ormus have pestilential fever with sudden death and among the portugal famine and that terrible contagious heat that in my day I never feel the like and such scent of dead body lie in the street without head be unburned and cat and dog eat they within o^st end be never the like see with infinite many fly and that the Persian will not let the dead body be bury we have such mortality among our man that we think we shall have perish all the ship before mention be they which word and of a excellent spirit he have live here in India many year he get commission of their king for three several design the first be to have sufficient ship and man with munition for the threefold commission root out of the english out of India the which he make no question to perform and do begin with captain shilling fleet but God be thank therein he fail as it fall out to his great grief and all our comfort the second thing that he be to perform be to erect a castle upon the island of kishme the which he do for when we come thither he have scarce furnish it he bring the frame thereof ready make in his ship and get it a shore with great resistance Kishme castle describe occasion of the war but so many as will not yield unto he he put to the sword and so many as will serve he he allow mean now the place where this castle be to be erect be about certain well of fresh water the which be for the use of Ormus because upon that island there be none now for the build of this castle they pull down a fine town with church and tomb only for the stone some of which he burn and make lime and with the other he make the castle wall of a great height and thickness with half moon and flanker native cause of indignation very artificial which in five month and a half he have finish a thing wonderful in so short a time to be effect and with a great deep dry moat round about he have erect on the castle 12. piece of great ordnance to the great annoyance of the persian army which have almost beleaguer it round only a small passage which they have towards the sea on either side of it beset with pallesadoe for the better go to their boat and frigate in safety though scarce able without great peril he mean to take the whole island of kishme in their own hand be a very fruitful place abound with all manner of fruit beast and fresh water where of the island of Ormus have none the portugal when they be first situate in Ormus do agree with the king of the sea-coast upon the main which be a kingdom of itself and since have be conquer of the persiant to pay to the aforesaid king certain tribute or custom upon every head of cattle pot of water and such like which do yearly amount unto a great sum of money which the portugal have not pay a long time at least this thirty year and have be demand it since the english have have trade here in Persia they have refuse to pay the same moreover they have get into their possession great quantity of silk which they have refuse to pay also for that reason the Persian will not let the portugal have cattle nor refresh from the main for it be death unto they that sell they any which be the reason of build the castle upon the island of Kishme now the portugal policy think it be good to have two string to his bow as this be one the other be this at Muskat a certain place which the portugal have upon Arabia they make a great feast and invite the king of Arabia unto the feast and violent b^ought he away unto Ormus and there make he king of the island and allow he certain custom yearly for his maintenance by this mean they have cattle and water sufficient in great quantity bring thither in arabian boat with fruit fish and all other thing which be every day sell in the market by report very plentiful likewise the arabian boat do fetch they water from kishme and be conduct with their galley and frigate against the Persian the king of Arabia be prisoner in the castle of Ormus unto the persian the portugal in these part will not let any commodity pass to and again upon the sea unless it be first bring unto Ormus and there to be custom upon loss thereof be take by their galley or frigate whereof they have here great store that carry piece of ordnance and other munition they trade to and fro in they and so be become master of the sea in these part the custom of Ormus do yearly amount as I have hear report to a hundred thousand pound beside rent and other duty which they tax the inhabitant with this town or city of Ormus be of great bigness the house all build of stone and seem a most famous thing to look upon from the ship with steeple and tower they have fair and large church in it strong and stately building the castle of Ormus be the fair large and strong that ever I see towards the town it have three wall one within another and well furnish with great ordnance of brass as cannon demi-canon Cannon-Pedro whole culverin and basilisk of 22. foot long now concern the three thing which be about the fish for pearl he have but little leisure by reason of these turmoil and war in not fish for pearl and burn all the fish town now they that have any boat be force to carry they up into the country to hide they from the portugal but when the Persian be to go over for Ormus the the portugal throat cut by the reason of their great hindrance in burn of their boat and town and slavery which they daily do sustain I will certify you concern the wonderful and strange manuer of the Richard take a Portugal ship that come from bumbasse she be a rich prize lade with elephant tooth turtle great ship take by a small small pinnace have but two piece filp or Philip chief cause of her
