agent for the east indian merchant trade in persia. at a consultation in Swally ride the fourteen of November 1621. commission be first consultation give by master Thomas Rastell precedent and the counsel of the merchant of surat to Richard Blithe and John weddell bind for jasques a persian port with five good ship and four pinnace whereof the London and pinnace shilling under captain blithe the jonas whale dolphin lion with their pinnace the rose Robert and richard under command of captain weddell to set sail with the soon opportunity towards port jasques and to keep together in such sort as they shall think fit for their defence against the common enemy and see the portugal have disturb their trade by the slaughter maym and imprison of their man and have make sundry assault against their ship that therefore it shall be lawful to they to chase and surprise whatsoever vessel pertain to the port and subject under the viceroy of Goa thereof to be accountable etc. and if they meet with any of decann^e Dabul Cha or any port belong to the Samorin of Calcutta to arrest they upon account of just pretence for good rob and spoil etc. without embezzle any part thereof that full restitution may be make after satisfaction on their part render a 6 part of good get from the Portugal to be distribute and their person to be reserve prisoner that in exchange our countryman by they miserable captive may be deliver to haste their lade and dispatch at jasque if possible within thirty day and see the reinforce enemy Ruy with his armada of six Galliones and other small vessel be attend on the persian coast in likelihood to assault their fleet that therefore it Ruy the Portugal admitall shall be lawful not defensive alone but offensive to await all advantage even in their own port if there be appearance of performance approve by general counsel warrantable to be undertake etc. in Costack road the six and twenty of December 1621. a consultation be hold aboard the jonas whereat be present John weddell Richard Blithe Edward Monoxe William second consultation baffin and many other the can or duke of Xiras have by his minister desire the aid of their ship against the common enemy the Portugal the article be translate into the persian tongue be dispee by Xareeali governor of the province of Mogustan towards the say duke who be then upon the way towards mina the sum whereof follow for so much as by several conference have with diverse and sundry of the Chan or duke of causesmove the english in those part and port to assist the persian first a secret force from the persian detain the english good on shore and not allow carriage as before which also will have break out to a open imbarge with danger likely to their person good and liberty second the open and often force and hostility whereof the former voyage testify from the Partugall they make a virtue of necessity article Xiras his minister and chief commander in the present war we have well observe they be full determine and resolve to require the aid of our ship and people in this intend expedition for the vanquish not only the Portugal armada but likewise for the take and surprise of the island and castle of ormuz and we be very confident they will use their endeavour to enforce we unto the say service by imbarge our good upon the shore which we have well understand by the governors refusal to furnish we with camel to bring our good from mina to the port Edward Monox late agent propound whether they may undertake that service or no. the proposition be well debate and the factor commission from surat warrant to right themselves of the great loss and hindrance sustain by the Portugal interrupt their peaceable trade both in India and Persia the last year attempt of Ruy against captain shilling fleet at jasques to the loss of that worthy commander and other his majesty subject be yet fresh and for so much as the persian now seek our aid and in manner foree it it be good to think on such condition as may be for the public benefit and not to omit this opportunity of a peaceable and profitable trade the same to be send unto the Chan in these article first in case God shall be please to deliver the island and castle of ormuz into the hand of the persian by our aid the moiety of the spoil and purchase of both to remain to the english the other moiety to the persian second the castle of ormuz to be deliver to the possession of the english with all the ordnance arm and munition thereto belong and the persian to build another for themselves at their own charge third the custom to be equal divide the english to be for ever custome-free four that all christian captive shall be at the english dispose the musselman at the persian five the persian to be at half the ship charge for victual wage wear and tear and to furnish they at his charge with sufficient powder and shot diverse other article be conclude to be present to the Chan after his come to mina master bell and master Monox the eight of januarie be send to he and entertain with a sumptuous banquet a great feast and triumph be also make for the joyful news of the king take in of a great country in Arabia and of Aweiza the chief city of that country the next day the duke send his Visier accompany with Sabander sultan and Xareearee persian victory in Arabia with answer to the former article the first be approve for the second the castle shall be equal possess by both till the king pleasure be know the three grant provide only that the king and duke good from India shall also pass custom-free to the four they make reservation of the two principal captain Ruy captain of Kishme castle and Simon de Mela captain of the castle of ormuz till the king pleasure know other article agree on and order also that no change of religion shall be admit on either side and charge of powder and shot to be divide the duke and master bell sign and present the english good be lade on the duke own camel on fire cost which before note no money can procure on the ten we turn to Costack we get aboard and acquaint the commander with the success of our journey which be divulge and make know amongst the several ship company it seem they consult together with one voice to refuse the business the London opposition company beginning fifty or sixty appear therein captain Blithe take much pain to suppress their disorder and in the end prevail with they they promise to go whither he will the other ship in a day or two be in like opposition allege it be no merchandize business nor be they hire for any such exploit nor can he tell whether it may not be a breach of the peace say a favourer of that religion till protest be make against each ship company what with fear to lose their wage and promise of a month pay they at last yield the nineteenth of januarie we set sail towards ormuz where we arrive the two and twenty and that night anchor in fight of the town about two league from the castle in expectation that the enemy armada consist of five galeon and some fifteen or twenty frigate will have come forth to fight with we but they hail so near the castle that we can not come at they which we perceive and understand that our vow enemy Ruy be in his new erect castle of Kishme the next day we address ourselves towards Kishme castle yield the say castle where we arrive in fit time to save both the life and reputation of the portugal not able long to hold out against the persian siege and willing rather to yield to we the first of February they yield both their person and castle after many meeting and treaty into our possession the four we set sail towards gombrone where we be royal gombrone feast by the duke who be discontent that Ruy be not deliver to he nor some of the moor contrary to my like especial for the moor the duke dissemble his discontent in regard of further need of our help at ormuz and after his feast ve all the english present accord to their quality the nine of February we set sail towards ormuz with about two hundred persian boat ormuz besiege great and small with two frigate in our company and in they five and twenty hundred or three thousand persian soldier of all sort and anchor that night about two league from the castle the next day before noon the Persian be all land and march in a confuse manner towards the city which they enter as far as the Mydan or market place without meet resistance which market place they find barricado against they and defend with shot and pike of the portugal but the Persian soon make way and the portugal like so many sheep take their heel into their castle one persian only which first enter be slay with a pike and he which slay he lose his head in the market place his heel be the city forsake too heavy to carry it away some eight or ten more find scatter in several house of the city be in the same place execute the persian general name culibeg at his first entrance into the city place his captain and soldier in several place of the city and proclaim upon pain of death every man to look to his quarter and none to fall on pillage which some infringe be severe execute he hang some cut off ear and nose of other and other he bastonadoe even for trifle yet within two or three day after shop and house be break open and every man weary with carry and recarry spoil all day and sleep so secure at night that easy the Portugal in a sally may have slay many the same night we enter I take possession of a very commodious house to settle a factory there which for convenience of room I think exceed any factory the company have but on the thirteen it prove too hot for i be set on fire in the night by one of the master mate of the whale with other his consort after I be in bed careless with candle rummage for pillage and fire a room in which be good give i by the general but the wind favour we so that the house be not consume when I consider the strength of the city and almost of every house be a little castle I can but marvel that the Portugal will so soon abandon the same strength of ormuz but it seeme^ they fear the persian will have intercept their way to the ormuz salt of itself and I know not what policy the general have to send away all the rice and our provision for victual and water whole to depend on the continent so that be a fleet of frigate have which be a pretty compliment where all his action show nothing less note the english enforce by present occasion to engage themselves in this war but we must be content to undergo all with patience yet be it not for our merchant and their good that be in the country and subject to whatsoever they will impose upon they we can remedy this business well enough and bring the unto another reckon but we be tie from that and therefore must of necessity be subject to accept the measure they please to lay upon we which I fear will prove unmeasurable ill yet they tell we all thing shall be to our own after salute the cavalier which be requite with like compliment with who I have some discourse of matter nothing pertain to the present occasion for that I will not presume to talk of that till the persian himself do first minister the occasion which be not before we have eat a persian collation of Pilaw etc. which be do the general demand the portugal what be their request or three treaty desire to which they answer the captain of the castle have give they instruction in write but his desire be they shall propound the same unto the duke himself if they may be permit to go unto he who be now at gombrone to which the general reply it be more than he dare do without first acquaint the duke therewith by which I well perceive they be only delay and distraction on both side and to gain time for effect their several design then the portugal proceed to their usual complain against Ruy as if Ruy as a private man and without order from the king his master have presume to do that which he have do and to excuse themselves demand what reason or justice it be to punish the father for the child offence beside the matter in itself be small only for a well of water or two to which the persian general reply again let the cause be what it will they have move war against the king of Persia and his subject for which their castle of Ormus must make satisfaction wherefore if without more bloodshed they will surrender their castle and come forth into the city they shall find good quarter and be well use to which the portugal make answer they have no commission from their captain to treat of any such matter with which they be dismiss notwithstanding the denial be make to the portugal request for go to the Chan yet the same night they have licence and be send unto he to treat their business with his excellency the certainty of the treaty I have no mean to know yet what I hear report shall be here insert first their demand be that the duke will vouchsafe to withdraw his siege from their castle and suffer they to enjoy the same as in former time in consideration whereof they will give he two hundred thousand tomans in hand and also the rent annual they have in former time give to the king of Ormus out of the revenue of the custom house which as have be report unto i be but one hundred and forty thousand rial of eight but some report they offer the Chan beside the of two hundred thousand tomans the second of April the persian with the aid of the english do blow up two other mine new breach with which be make a very fair and passable breach wherein they may have enter without any great difficulty but there be no assault give thereunto at all the passage of this business be well observe captain weddell and myself make our repair to the persian general to understand his purpose and resolution who to excuse the backwardness of his people in not assault the breach tell we it be very difficult and not to be enter of which we be content to give he the hear howbeit we be offer the contrary for that a english youth who be servant to the master of the jonas more bold than any persian go up the breach to the very top of the castle wall who tell we the way be as easy as to go up a bold boy pair of stair and spacious enough for many man to go up a breast wherefore we demand to know his resolution for further proceed who tell we within three day he will be fit for another mine and I believe it well for his mine be for gold not to make breach unless it be breach of promise unto we which he can do daily for of late they perform with we in just nothing yet all this can warn we to be circumspect to look unto ourselves the great hurt the Portugal do unto the persian in assault the castle be with powder pot wherewith many be scald and burn for prevention whereof the Chan have now send over store of coat and jacket make of leather which indeed be nothing so subject to take fire as be their calico coat bombast with Cotton wool but as the english proverb be the burn child dread the fire for notwithstanding their leather coat there be none so hardy to attempt the breach that be now make albeit much more easy to enter then the last be further then to pillage certain ball of Bastas and other stuff which be fall down from the baricado the portugal make for their defence against the Persian shoot in this adventure pitiful pillage one lose both his arm take away with a great shot by which mean he be fain to come back again without any Bastas or other pillage the five of April news be bring to the general of 100500. mane powder then arrive from bahrine the twelve ditto come a Portugal unto the persian general who escape out persian powder Portugal want and misery flux how cause of the castle and declare the great want and weak estate the soldier be in general insomuch that daily do die six seven or eight of the flux which be chief occasion through drink their corrupt water for the small quantity of water which they have in their cistern be grow so brackish and salt that it infect they all with the flux and beside the badness of it they be put to such strait allowance that many die with thirst beside for victual they have only rice and salt fish two very good preparative to a cup of good drink if they have it notwithstanding all which the persian defer yea I may say waste time in make new mine whereof he have no less than three in hand at this present as if he will blow up all the castle wall round about before he will make his entry the twelve at night one of our frigate namely the London be appoint to her too hot for their handle and therefore forsake she with what hurt to themselves I know not but of the London man be slay two outright and seven more hurt and wound and have not their black that row the frigate forsake they they will have put hard to have surprise the surpriser the fourteen ditto the persian spring another of his mine wherewith a very enterable breach be make but no assault give nor yet show of entry make but the troth be he be force to blow up the mine before his time for the Portugal from within the castle be come so near unto he that he be in doubt he will have defeat the frigate which fight with our single frigate above mention come from muscat wherein be the deeased don Francisco late captain of the castle his son who come purposely to fetch away his mother and other own consent deliver unto he who he promise shall have pardon for the error they have fall into to serve the portugal against their own king and country and that they shall also be provide for and have employment in the then intend expedition for Ormus which promise of his both to they and we in their behalf he persian perfidy seem to ratify by use some of the principal in our presence and grace they by other seem courtesy notwithstanding all which the next morning he cut off eighty of their head and those which he have make so fine in new vest to the number of five or six of the principal he send they over to coombrone to the duke by he to receive their fatal sentence which be not long defer but they be make to drink of the same cup their fellow have former drunken of mere senadine who be mortal enemy the seventeen ditto they spring another mine adjoin to the first mine be spring wherein be place about sixty barrel of powder which take not the effect which be expect for it fly out at the side and carry part of the wall out with it but strike nothing at all up upward whereby the first breach be very little better which be the thing the persian second assault aim at yet be it sufficient to give he encouragement to make his second assault which be do with at least two thousand soldier who very resolute run up the breach into a part of a bulwark which they may whole have possess that very instant have they not at first make such haste to run their resolution out of breath insomuch that only eight or ten portugal and a few negro make they only with their rapier to give ground and to retire themselves unto the very outward skirt of the bulwark where they have not room for forty m^^ to stand in the face of their enemy yet there they barracadod themselves which before they can effect to their purpose the Portugal ply two or three piece of ordnance from one of his flanker that say open unto they in such sort that they send some score of they to carry news unto their prophet Ali that more of his disciple will short be with he which accord be effect and proceed chief out of their own ignorance and dastardly cowardice for have they not make their stand in that place but enter pell-mell with the portugal into the castle with the loss of half those man they lose that day they may have gain the victory and with much less pain unto themselves who from that time the mine be blow up which be about nine of the clock before noon the whole day stand stocking together in the sun without either meat or drink which be sufficient to have kill half of they notwithstanding the portugal make very slender resistance the most that be do be by the negro who the portugal do beat forward to throw powder pot with which many of the Persian be pitiful scald and burn have I not see it I shall hardly have believe that such have be the gross ignorance of the persian that have two breach the one not much inferior to the other for his entrance that he will apply all his soldier to the assault of the one and none at all to the other beside have provide at least eighty or a hundred scale ladder never so much as bring one of they near unto the castle wall but such as their proceed be such be also like to be their success for his soldier hang in a cluster upon the breach just as a swarm of bee upon a tree or bush that want a hive or like a flock of sheep at a gap where none be so hardy to enter and the portugal to put they out of that pain glean away four five six sometime more at a shot insomuch that I can but pity they to see it the eighteen ditto the persian continue his assault but with more pain to himself Portugal poor estate then hurt unto the portugal the last height two captive negro make sign unto the persian that they be desirous to come unto they so the Persian let down rope unto they and so pluck they up unto they who declare that the captain of the castle have get a hurt on his head with a stone and how there be not above a hundred soldier in the castle able to manage their arm their water grow scant and daily worse and worse which also increase mortality amongst they how there be likewise difference among themselves be of different opinion some hold it best to adventure their escape by sea with those erigot they have other be contrary mind and hold it more honour to sell their life at the dear rate and defend their castle so long as they may and when they can no long then to put their woman and child with all their treasure into a house and blow they all up with gunpowder desperate counsel that the turk shall neither enjoy their wealth nor abuse their wife which do they will thrust themselves pell-mell with the Persian and so end their day the nineteenth ditto at euenbeing the three day the persian that have lie rest himself in the breach never offer to advance himself do then set forward whereby he get himself better footing and possess himself of all the bulwark and force the Portugal to forsake the same and retire himself further within the castle in which conflict many of the portugal be wound and scald with fire Pots wherein the persian be now as cunning as themselves though many of they have pay dear for their learning in the say conflict be likewise four portugal slay and their head bring before the general to witness the same wherein all the Persian be very well see for I do not think there be any hangman in all Germany yet this be the Persian praise that they be good swordman the turk fear to come to hand-blowe with they frigate escape that can go beyond they in that art for he no soon lay hold on his enemy but present at one blow with his sword off go his head and then with his knife he thrust a hole either in the ear or through one of the cheek and so thrust his finger in at the mouth and out at the hole in the cheek bring sometime two three or four of they before the general together in such sort that not a butcher in Eastcheap can do it better but if as common it happen that these head of their enemy so take in the war be send to the view of the king or Chan then be they no less cunning to slay off the skin of the whole head and face and stuff the same with straw like a football and so send they by whole sackful together this night one of the frigate that come from muscat for the donna make her escape and get away no doubt very rich freight her consort be chase in again which be likewise go that which escape be hale by the Arab boat that lie in wait to intercept their go use the watchword usual betwixt the english and arabs which be only ingre ingress which watchword have never be change nor once alter since our first attempt the business wherein both Persian and english be much to be blame for by the common use of that one watchword the portugal have come to the knowledge of it and have make good use of it to their own benefit which be their gain and our loss the twenty ditto at night the other frigate above mention offering to escape be take one watchword no watchword by the London man in her frigate and pinnace she be send to carry away the Almirante name Luis de Britto a kinsman of the viceroy of Goa who the captain of the castle will not suffer to depart wherefore the portugal which be take in she be fearful of the frigate take success of the castle and that it be not able long to hold out for safety of their own life be seven person hold it their best course to adventure their escape in the say frigate and in the night steal she away and be take as above mention the one and twenty ditto the persian make preparation and show as if at once they will make short work to possess themselves of the rest of the castle but where we expect to see they put the same in execution parley I perceive that they and the portugal be in parley together wherefore I address myself to know the cause of so sudden a alteration and as I be fit myself to go unto the persian general for that purpose I encounter a messenger from our english commander who send i word that a boat from the castle be go with a flag of truce aboard their ship and they desire my company aboard with they to understand what the business be and come aboard the London find two portugal with letter from the captain of the castle and from the Almirante contain viz. there have be such ancient friendship betwixt the portugal and the english that consider the war which at this present we have in this place we ought one to understand the other for it seem to i when I see the mine be make by the moor that only by your aid war be make against i with which one of my bulwark be get from i wherefore your worship will be please to do i the favour to be a mean to make peace betwixt i and those moor if the same shall stand with their and your good like provide it be in that manner that I lose not my credit neither yourselves leave to gain honour in a time so favourable unto you thus not else our lord keep you etc. Simon de Mela Perera this fort be so beset and oppress that the moor require we to deliver the same up on composition the which we will not do by any mean for when we shall be force to make composition we will call your worship for it be not reason we shall treat with moor where you be present for we hold it better to deliver our innocent woman and other unnecessary people to the rigour of our weapon then to the clemency of the moor and for that the knowledge hereof shall not be want to your worship I have write this beside what accompany the same from the captain and for what else you desire to know you may inform yourselves from this messenger to who you may give the some credit as unto my own person and so God keep your worship etc. the first of may 1622. v. s. Luis de Brito dareto the request of the portugal contain in their several letter on the other side be have to consideration and commiseration have of they as christian it be resolve to give they a comfortable answer unto their demand which in effect be as follow but want of time the business require expedition will not permit to keep copy of the say answer which be first unto the captain Simon melle to give he notice of the receipt of his letter and whereas the chief point therein be that we will be Terceras for they to procure they such condition of agreement with the Persian as that may be to the save of the life of so many christian soul as be with he in the castle our answer be that such have be our care to provide for they that it be in our own power to grant that request which we english clemency to the portugal be not only ready to do but likewise to show they any other courtesy or perform any christian duty towards they that may any way tend to their good therefore advise he to set down his demand and send the same unto we with as much brevity as be possible and to the like purpose and effect be our answer unto the almirant his letter with which the two messenger be dispee in one of our own barge who return with another letter both from the captain and almirant that viz. the necessity of the business so require the commander and myself will not lose so much time to write any other answer unto the say letter lest the persian shall take advantage of the opportunity and sudden press in upon they and put they all to the sword wherefore we address ourselves unto the persian general to be suitor unto he in the distress christian behalf that he will hold his promise with they of a faithful truce for two day in which time we may treat with they of such condition as shall be as well behooveful and beneficial for the persian as for ourselves and that there may be no more effusion of blood on either side at length myself and a persian gentleman with i be appoint offer as appear by this of Arabia by which your majesty will be force to make war and continual war by sea against this enemy for that by land you have no power to conquer he who be not content with the take away the firm land of this kingdom altogether with the isle of Barem and Kishme but further in confidence of his great number of boat have none to resist he have take from we Arabia which be the only remedy of this island of the truth of what have herein be speak your majesty ambassador don garcia de Sylva God send he well to your majesty shall be a good witness to who report I refer i and to all other which go from Kishme or qu^xome hence God keep your majesty Ormus the twelve of February 1621. Mamede Rey de Ormus to this letter I have add the translate copy of diverse other letter for the reader full more satisfaction the vice admiral his second letter illustriss s r I kiss the hand of your Ss. for write unto i and believe i I esteem english kindness acknowledge which upbraid the portugall ungratitude cause of this war the same as become a gentleman who adverse fortune in the war have no whit disanimate the captain have write unto you and all the portugall recommend themselves and do desire you and I for they that you well deal with they as christian and the nation who so many time have join in arm with they against the moor tomorrow shall you see in what manner they desire to be deal with all God keep you with all the rest of your company etc. May 1622. v. s. Luis de Brito bareto a certificate make by sundry portugall how the treasure jewel etc. belong to the king and his Vizeer of Ormus which be secret convey out of the castle of Ormus by the Persian we who name be hereunder write do certify our knowledge how that byram Aga with other turk by the commandment of their superior go unto the house of the Goasil within the fort to watch the good that there remain also the money and riches which be therein at the time when the fort be deliver up unto the english. and the same night many other turk by the trench of the bulwark name saint jago unseen of the english by the breach in the cistern adjoin to the say trench and also through the say trench convey much riches belong to the say go^^l and king of Ormus and also of their woman and kinsfolk in witness of the truth we have hereunder write our name Ormus the twenty five of may. 1622. perceive for some five or six day together for which cause on Monday be the eleven of january about ten of the clock in the morning there be a procession about the castle solemnize by the greek priest to the custom rite of circumcision of the jew resident in Constantinople and not in a synagogue as it be with the jew in other country this foresay amis for the love he bear to our english nation in the which he live till he be thirty year of age be at the time of my residence in Constantinople sixty as also for his good will sake which he bear to my foresay friend master William perch receive we with very courteous entertainment present unto we at a table in a fine little room where he place we diverse delicate dish and first-fruit with a cup of most excellent wine often welcome we with many hearty and wel-wishing speech while we be at breakfast diverse jew come into the room and sing certain hebrew song after which the child be bring to his father who sit down in a chair and place the child be now eight day old in his lap the whole company be desirous that we christian shall observe their ceremony call we to approach near to the child and when we come a certain other jew draw forth a little instrument make not unlike those small cisser that our lady and gentlewoman do much use do with the same cut off the or foreskin of the child and after a very strange manner unused I believe of the ancient hebrew do put his mouth to the child yard and sueke up the blood all his privity before he come into the room be besprinkle with a kind of powder which after the circumciser have do his business be blow away by he and another powder cast on immediate after he have dispatch his work the same also after his work be do take a little strong wine that be hold in a goblet by a fellow that stand near he and pour it into the child mouth to comfort he in the midst of his pain who cry out very bitter the pain be for the time very bitter indeed though it will be as they tell i cure in the space of four and twenty hour but those of any ripe year that be circumcise as it too often come to pass that christian which turn Turk as at forty or fifty year of age do suffer great pain for the space of a month the that be cut off be carry to the mother who keep it very precious as a thing of worth the twelve of August be Thursday the turk about eight of the clock at night illuminate lamp the steeple of their moskies with abundance of lamp over all Constantinople and galata as they do upon Mahomet birth day before mention by i as be the eve of their first sabbath in the month or moon of Regepf by way of preparation for their great feast of Ramazan which follow afterward which custom they observe every year upon the foresay day the eleven of September some of the learned turk that be skilful in their law observe that the contagion of the plague be late disperse over diverse place of the city have recourse to some of their Musulman book to the end they may inform themselves of some convenient and discreet course to be take for the prevention of the sickness and find in one of they that some thirty year since there be make a edict for the banish of all the dog dog banish to prevent pestilence out of the town as be principal instrument of scatter the plague by reason of their free pass up and down from one house to another they hold it meet to imitate that example and to do the like so that the matter be now propound to the grand signior it be at last determine that the dog shall be banish and for the better performance of the matter final they conclude thus that every christian and jew dwell in Constantinople shall by a day limit under the pain of forfeit four chiquin present a dog to the cad^e and take of he a Teskeria this be a turkish word that signify a the Visier make notable show upon the water before the grand signior with firework for there be sixteen boat that serve for the same purpose wherein pretty castle be contrive the people in which skirmish together at the least a hour spend such abundance of powder in their firework that I never see the like before send up diverse of their flash in the air as high as the high fire work steeple in Constantinople a sight most notable to observe so many boat with their firework encounter so long together in which space there be no cessation or intermission but that you shall sometime see four sometime six fiery steeple ascend into the air together with many burn line pass too and fro upon the water in diverse several form among the rest of these firework I observe some make upon the very shore itself with singular cunning resemble the shape of cypresse-tree a very please and delectable object to behold the twenty of September be Monday the jew of Constantinople and galata begin their feast of tabernacle which last till the eight and twenty of the same month that be Jew feast of tabernacle nine day just nine day in which they differ from the ancient Jew who be command by almighty God to spend only eight day in the colebration of their feast I talk with a jew concern the reason of this their difference who tell i that it be because be so far from jerusalem as in Constantinople they do not altogether so certain know the first day accord to the course of the moon as those jew that live in jerusalem and therefore for the better assurance of this matter they add a day to the number that God limit and appoint their forefather whereas the jew that live in jerusalem and the part of the holy land near thereabout by the course of the moon more certain know the precise time of the beginning do spend only eight day in their feast and no more again they do in another respect differ from God institution for he command only two day to be more solemn celebrate then the rest that be the first and the last but they celebrate two at the beginning and two also at the last but as of the former two the first day be the chief be keep with more solemnity than the second so also of the two late the last of all be more ceremonious observe then the former in this space they be much give to holiness rest from all labour during the whole nine day and they sometime eat and drink in their tabernacle which be make partly in their private house or the corner of some gallery belong thereto at the least if they have any and partly near to their synagogue they make the side of their tabernacle of reed of bulrush and cover they at the top with bay it be my hap to be in one of they that be make near to a synagogue also the nine day which be the last of their feast about four of the clock in the afternoon I be at their liturgy in one of their synagogue be admit synagogue-lyturgie irreverence to sit down among they I find the irreverence of the jew in Venice and of those of Constantinople to be like in the service of god. they neither uncover nor kneel the whole time of their prayer sometime they stand altogether and sometime they sit altogether for some quarter of a hour after the begin of the read of their law they wear nothing over their back but their ordinary apparel but then all of they put on their ephod both man and child which ephod be make of the same white stuff as the turkish turban be these hang over their back (...) odd and reach down to the middle part of their body after a loose manner than I think the ancient jew be wont to wear they for I read in the 2. sam. the 6. chapter and 14. verse that king David gird it about his middle when he dance before the ark but they hang it loose about their body this ephod many of they carry in a little scrip from their house and back again after the end of their liturgy when they sit at their devotion they use a most ridiculous and unseemly gesture for they always move their body up and down very strange the head be in a continual motion without any cessation after that they move their right side then their left and last their forepart forward which kind of wag of their body by interchangeable this Amboyna be a island lie near Seran of the circuit of forty league and give name Amboyna describe also to some other small hand adjacent it bear clove for gather and buy in whereof the english company for their part have plant five several factory the head and rendezvouz of all at the town of Amboyna and therein first master George muscham^e and afterward master Gabriel Tomerson their agent Seran the hollander have four fort the chief of all (@) at the say town of Amboyna and be very strong have four point or bulwark with their curtain and upon each of these point six great piece of ordnance mount most of they of brass the one side of this castle be wash by the sea and the other be dutch castle divide from the land with a ditch of four or five fathom broad very deep and ever fill with the sea. the garrison of this castle consist of about two hundred dutch soldier and garrison a company of free burgher beside these there be always a matter of three or four hundred mardikero for so they usual call the free native in the town ready to serve the castle at subject a hour warning there lie also in the road for the most part diverse good ship of the hollander as well for the guard of the place by sea as for the occasion of trassique this be the ship chief Rendevo^^ as well for the island of Banda as or the rest of Amboyna here the english live not in the castle but under protection there^^ in a house of their own in the town hold themselves safe as well in respect of the ^^cient bond of amity between both nation as of the strict conjunction make by the late treaty before mention they continue here foin two year converse and trade together with the hollander by virtue of the say treaty in which time there fall out sundry difference and debate between they the english complain that the hollander do not only lavish away much money in building and unnecessary expense upon the fort and other wise and bring large and unreasonable reckon thereof to the common account but also do for their part pay the garrison with victual and cloth of coromandel which they put off to the soldier at three or four time the value it cost they yet will not allow of the english company part of the same charge but only in ready money thereby draw from the english which ought to pay but one three part more than two three of the whole true charge hereupon and upon the like occasion grow some discontent and dispute and the complaint be send to jaccatra in the island of jan^ Maior to the council of defence of both nation there reside (@) who also jacatra now Baearia seat of the dutch government in the Indies not agree upon the point in difference send the same hither over into Europe to be decide by both company here or in default of their agreement by the king majesty and the lord the state general accord to a article of the treaty of the year 1619. on this behalf in the mean time the discontent between the english and the dutch about these and other difference continue and daily increase until at last there be a sword find to cut in sunder that knot at once which the tedious dispute of Amboyna and jaccatra can not untie and this be use in manner the bay of lot santos in the land of brasil be situate upon thirteen degree of southerly latitude a hundred league above P^ar^ambuco it be the place at which the governor the bishop and the auditor general of all the coast of brasil be resident this place be most inhabit it have three town the one be near to the Barra or come in and be call Villa which be the first that be build in this jurisdiction the second be the town call Saluador or saviour in english build by Thomas and four league thence Landwards in lie the village Paripe it have many sugar-mil although the inhabitant get their living for the most part by Cotton within the town be five church and one college of the jesuit of which be some eighty in the town the bay be some three league large and stretch some fifteen league landwards in it have many small land which yield great store of Cotton it be divide into several part and have many branch in which the inhabitant use small bark the bay be when the water be reasonable high in some place twelve eighteen and twenty fathom deep and lie inward north northwest on the corner of it be a castle build which be call saint Antonio near which lie a bank which reach a league into the sea southeastward when the wind blow very strong the water make there great noise but there be no danger for the ship see it be five or six fathom deep and the ground be land the corner on which saint Anthonio stand be but a league distant from the town the high ship land common just against the great church now for the take of the same by the dutch it be thus both relate and in picture also here omit describe the high and mighty state with the advice of his excellency the prince of Orange erect a west India company and prepare a navy of above thirty ship strong of which master jacob Wilkins be choose admiral and the lord of Dort appoint to be general this fleet put to sea the two and twenty of December in the last year 1623. and the island of saint Vincent which be one of the land of C^bo Verde be appoint to be the rendezvous all the ship of the fleet meet there except that in which the general be who come to Sierra Liona and the fleet have tarry there the space of five week it depart on the six and twenty day of march thence and come on the eight of May before the bay of santos in which he may have sail the same night but he tarry for good reason and consideration till it be day and use this stratagem or policy namely he put all the soldier on four of the great and best ship and cause their ensign on the other still to be display the same day he land fifteen hundred man with two light piece call dragon who go in the night time into a small wood which lie near to the town and the admiral command afterward that four ship shall sail direct to the town and lie against the battery which they do and come so near to it that they touch ground whereupon they shoot very fierce both upon the town and the battery from whence the enemy answer they in the same tune and shoot amongst other one of our captain name gedult (...) r. the captain Peter Fr^^ckson of Euchuys^^ behave himself amongst the rest very valiant to the great admiration of all they that see he and all the other use likewise there best endeavour but see that both the ordnance of the town and the battery play so cruel upon they they resolve to land some man with their boat to surprise the battery although it be defend by two hundred man and to make the ordnance unserviceable which charge be undertake by the vice-admiral Peter Petersson Heyn he go with eight boat or sloope which be well furnish with man musket skeane hammer and nail direct to the battery and as soon as our man mount upon the same the enemy flee through the water to the town whereupon our vice-admiral have nail the ordnance upon it and cast it down he return again with all his man to the ship without receive any damage by the ordnance of the town which be continual display against he clayes Gerritsson be not one of the least that show themselves in this enterprise the next day be the nine of May it be resolve that the town shall be assault on two ^des namely from the ship by the mariner and out of the wood by the soldier but the townsman have have the night before a alarm or two give unto they by reason of the soldier which be come into the wood as they learn they flee all out of the town with the archbishop and in the morning when our force think to scale the wall of the town there appear a old man who say that all the burgher be run away and open the gate at which time captain Vogelsanck of Amsterdam march first into the town with his company and the other follow he they beset the market and other passage and afterward when they mistrust no enemy they begin to pillage and every one get rich prize or booty of gold chain ducat rial of eight gild and silver rapier sword and dagger beside great store of rich apparel of which there be such abundance that every soldier be provide with it as if he be a captain they find likewise at their arrival the table yet cover in the cloister and many other place and fall to the meat and drink on they but because no excess shall be commit some hundred pipe or vessel of wine be present knock in piece all the house be almost all as palace and adorn and furnish with rich householdstuff of which every one take as much as he can carry when the pillage be do there be many inferior soldier that dare venture forty and fifty piece of eight rial which amount to four shilling and sixpence at a set or gain and there be many officer which have get fourteen thousand and fifteen thousand gilder for their own private booty and go with chain of gold about their neck whereby it appear that a man may even in one hour grow rich in those part the governor be with his servant and yet arm in his palace the vice-admiral cause governor take rich crucifix he to lay his arm down and take he as his prisoner among the other booty and prize that be find in the church there be a crucifix of silver some four foot long with the image of our saviour be make of gold and be a foot and a half long when all the tumult be cease and all thing be put in order namely on the twelve of May a preacher of Zealand give in the great church the almighty thanks for such a great victory and on the same day come the lord of Dort into the bay when he have wander some five week about it and in the mean time be the ship U^s or fox in english load with four hundred chest of sugar beside great store of tobacco and hide and be send thence the shipper of it namely the valorous claes Gerritsson u^s arrive the five and twenty of August with the same in the unite province and bring this good tiding to his countryman even before the departure of this shipper there arrive yet in the bay afore mention a small ship that come with the provedidor or Providor of the Jesuit with a great sum of money that be gather for they that be of his order and he be seize upon the money be present make prize on the castle which the enemy forsake be leave five and forty piece of brass there be also present order give for the demolish of the castle that be seat near the sea and for the fortification of the town the good which be take and the remainder of the prize be to be bring into the low-countries with other ship as soon as this tide come into the unite province there be on a sudden many soldier levy to go to the bay afore mention with a fleet that lie ready for the same purpose see that there be yet many other place to be take beside rich booty and prize
